nodes.label: Georg Bühler
variants: ゲオルグ・ビューラー
nodes.jawiki: ゲオルク・ビューラー
nodes.summary: Georg Bühler (1837–1898) was an Indologist and linguist who earned his doctorate at Göttingen under Theodor Benfey and Hermann Sauppe. He held chairs at Elphinstone College, Deccan College, the University of Mumbai, and the University of Vienna.

nodes.id: I:Grundriss der Indo-Arischen Philologie und Altertumskunde
nodes.label: Grundriss der Indo-Arischen Philologie und Altertumskunde
variants: Grundriss der Indo-Arischen Philologie und Altertumskunde
Grundriss der Indo-arischen Philologie und Altertumskunde
Grundriss der indo-arischen Philologie und Altertumskunde

nodes.label: Franz Kielhorn
nodes.summary: Franz Kielhorn (1840–1908) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and Albrecht Weber. He was Professor of Oriental Languages at Deccan College (1866) and Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Göttingen (~1881–1908).

nodes.label: Ernst Kuhn
nodes.image: Ernst Kuhn - Aufsätze zur Kultur- und Sprachgeschichte.jpg
nodes.description: German indologist, linguist, philologist and orientalist (1846–1920)
nodes.summary: Ernst Kuhn was an Indologist, linguist, and Central Asian scholar. He studied at Berlin, Heidelberg, Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth, Leipzig, and Halle-Wittenberg. He held posts at Heidelberg University (~1875–1877) and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1877–1920).

nodes.label: Lucian Scherman
nodes.summary: Lucian Scherman was a scholar of Indology and other fields. He studied at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1881–1885) and subsequently held a post there (~1893–1936).

nodes.label: Ernst Windisch
nodes.jawiki: エルンスト・ヴィンディシュ
nodes.summary: Ernst Windisch was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Leipzig University under Curtius, Ritschl, Zarncke, and Brockhaus. He held chairs at Heidelberg (1872) and Strasbourg (1875), and served at Leipzig University (1871–1918) and the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft (~1892–1918).

nodes.label: Leipzig University
variants: ライプツィヒ大学インド学・中央アジア学研究所
Department of Indology and Central Asian Studies, University of Leipzig

Sanskrit-Abteilung des Indogermanischen Forschungsinstituts der Königl. Sächsischen Forschungsinstitute zu Leipzig

nodes.label: Willem Caland
nodes.summary: Willem Caland (1859–1932) worked in Indology and linguistics. After studying at Leiden University (~1877–1882), he served at Leiden (1913–1914) and held the Chair of Sanskrit at Utrecht University (~1906–1929; Professor 1906–1917).

nodes.label: Bartholomäus Ziegenbalg
nodes.image: Bartholomäus Ziegenbalg monument in Tranquebar, Tamil Nadu, South India.jpg

Akademie der schönen Wissenschaften zu Paris
Institut de France. Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres

nodes.label: Alexander Johnston
nodes.summary: Alexander Johnston (1775–1849) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served on the Executive Council of Ceylon as chief justice and first member (c. 1811–1819) and was Vice-President of the Royal Asiatic Society (c. 1823–1849).

nodes.label: Abraham Hyacinthe Anquetil-Duperron
nodes.image: David d'Angers - Portrait d'Abraham-Hyacinthe Anquetil-Duperron (1731-1805), orientaliste.jpg
nodes.jawiki: アブラアム＝ヤサント・アンクティル＝デュペロン

nodes.label: Johann Bernoulli
nodes.summary: Johann Bernoulli was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Basel and served as a Mitglied at the Prussian Academy of Sciences from around 1764 to 1807.

nodes.label: James Rennell
nodes.summary: James Rennell (1742–1830) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served in the East India Company from 1762 to 1777 and joined the Bengal Engineers in 1764.

nodes.label: Nathaniel Brassey Halhed
nodes.description: Civilian of the British East India Company (1751-1830)
nodes.summary: Nathaniel Brassey Halhed (1751–1830) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied at Harrow School and worked as an official for the East India Company from circa 1771 to 1785.

nodes.label: University of Oxford
variants: オックスフォード大学
オックスフォード大學
Faculty of Oriental Studies, University of Oxford

nodes.label: Charles Wilkins
nodes.jawiki: チャールズ・ウィルキンズ
nodes.summary: Charles Wilkins was an Indologist and a founding member of the Asiatic Society. He served as Oriental Librarian for the East India Company and as Librarian for the India Office Library and Records circa 1801–1836.

nodes.label: Henry Thomas Colebrooke
nodes.jawiki: ヘンリー・トーマス・コールブルック
nodes.summary: Indologist Henry Thomas Colebrooke (1765–1837) studied under Citrapati. He served in the Bengal Civil Service, Fort William College (1782–1814), Sadar Diwani Adalat, and the Supreme Council of Bengal, later directing the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland (~1823–1837).

nodes.label: William Jones
nodes.jawiki: ウィリアム・ジョーンズ (言語学者)
nodes.description: Anglo-Welsh philologist and scholar of ancient India (1746–1794)
nodes.summary: William Jones (1746–1794) was an Indologist and linguist educated at Harrow and Oxford. He became Chief Justice at the Supreme Court of Judicature at Fort William (1783) and founded the Asiatic Society in 1784.

nodes.id: I:Supreme Court of Judicature at Fort William
nodes.label: Supreme Court of Judicature at Fort William
Robert Chambers
nodes.summary: Robert Chambers was an Indology scholar who studied at Lincoln College (~1754–1758). He held posts at the University of Oxford (~1766–1773), the Supreme Court of Judicature at Fort William (~1789–1798), and the Asiatic Society (~1797–1798).

nodes.label: John Shore
nodes.summary: Active in Indology and history/archaeology, Shore succeeded William Jones and served as president of the Asiatic Society.

nodes.label: William Carey
variants: ウィリアム・ケアリー
nodes.jawiki: ウィリアム・ケアリー (宣教師)
nodes.description: English Baptist missionary and Particular Baptist minister (1761-1834)
nodes.summary: William Carey (1761–1834) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Golok Nath Sharma (~1796–1801). He founded the Serampore Mission Press and was Professor of Sanscrit, &c. at Fort William College in 1801.

nodes.label: Otto von Böhtlingk
nodes.jawiki: オットー・フォン・ベートリンク
nodes.summary: Otto von Böhtlingk worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University, under Franz Bopp (~1835–1839), and under Christian Lassen (~1839–1841). He was a member of the Russian Academy of Sciences (1842) and held a post at Jena (~1868–1885).

nodes.label: Charles Rieu
nodes.summary: Charles Rieu studied at Geneva and Bonn, learning under Jean Humbert, Christian Lassen, G. W. Freytag, and Johannes Gildemeister. Working in Indology, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and linguistics, he held posts at the British Museum and Cambridge.

nodes.label: George Thibaut
nodes.summary: George Thibaut worked in Indology and studied under Albrecht Weber in 1867. He served as Direktor at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1879–1888), Principal at Muir Central College (~1895–1906), and held a post at the University of Calcutta (~1907–1914).

nodes.label: Horace Hayman Wilson
nodes.jawiki: ホーラス・ヘイマン・ウィルソン
nodes.summary: Indologist Horace Hayman Wilson (1786–1860) served as Assay Master at the Kolkata Mint (1816–1833) and Boden Professor of Sanscrit at Oxford (1833–1836). He was also an East India Company librarian and Director of the Royal Asiatic Society (1837).

nodes.label: Monier Monier-Williams
nodes.jawiki: モニエル・モニエル＝ウィリアムズ
nodes.summary: Monier Monier-Williams was an Indologist and linguist who studied at King's College School, Balliol College, and University College, Oxford, under Horace Hayman Wilson. He taught at East India Company College and Cheltenham College before serving as Oxford's Boden Professor of Sanskrit.

nodes.label: Sanskrit College and University
variants: Department of Postgraduate Training and Research, Sanskrit College, Calcutta

nodes.label: Vans Kennedy
nodes.description: Scottish major-general of the British Army

nodes.label: James Prinsep
nodes.jawiki: ジェームズ・プリンセプ
nodes.summary: James Prinsep (1799–1840) worked in Indology, history, archaeology, and linguistics. He was Assistant to the Assay Master at the India Government Mint in Kolkata (1819) and a member of the Asiatic Society (1832–1838), succeeding Horace Hayman Wilson in 1833.

nodes.label: Arthur Schopenhauer
nodes.jawiki: アルトゥル・ショーペンハウアー
nodes.summary: Arthur Schopenhauer was a philosopher who studied at Ernestinum Gotha (~1807), the University of Göttingen (1809), and Humboldt University of Berlin (1811). He held a post at the University of Berlin (Humboldt University of Berlin) from circa 1820 to 1831.

nodes.label: Paul Regnaud
nodes.summary: Paul Regnaud (1838–1910) was an Indologist, linguist, and philosopher. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études from circa 1869 to 1876 and held a post at the University of Lyon from circa 1879 to 1908.

nodes.label: École Pratique des Hautes Études
variants: École des Hautes Études in Paris
高等研究実習院第4部門
フランス國立高等研究院
École Pratique des Hautes Études, SHP
École Pratique des Hautes Études (EPHE, PSL University, Paris)

nodes.label: John Muir
nodes.summary: John Muir was an Indologist who studied at East India Company College and the University of Bonn. He served in the Bengal Civil Service (1828–1853) and later founded and held a post at the University of Edinburgh.

nodes.label: Johannes Klatt
nodes.summary: Johannes Klatt was an Indologist who studied under Albrecht Weber (~1869–1872) and at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1872–1873). He served as custos of the Indian department at the Berlin State Library (~1874–1892).

nodes.label: Albrecht Weber
nodes.jawiki: アルブレヒト・ヴェーバー
nodes.summary: Albrecht Weber was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Breslau, Bonn, and Berlin under scholars including Stenzler, Lassen, and Kuhn. He held several posts at Humboldt University of Berlin and the Prussian Academy of Sciences.

nodes.label: Ignazio Guidi
nodes.summary: Ignazio Guidi (1844–1935) was a linguistics and history scholar. He studied at Sapienza University of Rome (~1864–1869) and later held an academic post there from ~1877 to 1919.

nodes.label: Emilio Teza
nodes.description: Italian translator, indo-europeanist, romanist, orientalist and linguist
nodes.summary: Emilio Teza (1831–1912) was an Italian linguist and Indologist who studied under Anton Boller (~1851–1854). He held posts at the University of Bologna (~1860–1861), the University of Pisa (~1861–1887), and the University of Padua (~1887–1911).

nodes.label: Ram Mohan Roy
nodes.image: Portrait of Raja Ram Mohun Roy, 1833.jpg
nodes.jawiki: ラーム・モーハン・ローイ
nodes.description: Indian religious, social, and educational reformer, and humanitarian
nodes.summary: Ram Mohan Roy (1772–1833) was a scholar in religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. He founded Presidency University, Kolkata in 1816 and also founded the Brahmo Samaj.

nodes.label: Louis-Mathieu Langlès
nodes.jawiki: ルイ＝マチュー・ラングレス
nodes.description: French academic, philologist, linguist, translator, author, librarian and orientalist
nodes.summary: A scholar of sinology, linguistics, and Indology, Louis-Mathieu Langlès studied under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. He served as Chief Keeper of Manuscripts at the Bibliothèque nationale de France and as Administrateur and Persian chair holder at INALCO (~1795–1824).

nodes.label: Henry Pitts Forster
nodes.summary: Henry Pitts Forster (1766–1815) worked in Indology and linguistics. He served in the Bengal Civil Service (~1783–1815) and was Master of the Calcutta Mint at the India Government Mint, Kolkata (~1803–1815).

nodes.label: Johann Gottfried Herder
nodes.jawiki: ヨハン・ゴットフリート・ヘルダー

nodes.label: Friedrich Schlegel
nodes.jawiki: フリードリヒ・シュレーゲル
nodes.description: German poet, critic and scholar, editor
nodes.summary: Friedrich Schlegel worked in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He studied at Göttingen and Leipzig, and later under Alexander Hamilton and Antoine-Léonard de Chézy. He held posts at Jena (~1799–1801), Cologne (~1804–1807), and TU Dresden.

nodes.label: Bibliothèque nationale de France
variants: Bibliothèque Impériale, Département des Manuscrits Orientaux

East India Company's College at Haileybury
Honourable East India Company's College, Haileybury
Hon. East India Company's College, Haileybury

nodes.label: August Wilhelm Schlegel
nodes.jawiki: アウグスト・ヴィルヘルム・シュレーゲル
nodes.description: German poet, translator, critic, and writer (1767–1845)
nodes.summary: August Wilhelm Schlegel was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at the University of Göttingen under Christian Gottlob Heyne (~1786–1791) and under Antoine-Léonard de Chézy (1814). He held posts at the University of Jena (~1796–1801) and University of Bonn (1818).

nodes.label: William Robertson
nodes.description: British historian, minister of religion, and principal of the University of Edinburgh (1721-1793)
nodes.summary: William Robertson (1721–1793) was a historian and Indologist. He studied at the University of Edinburgh from around 1735 to 1741 and later held a post there from around 1762 to 1793.

nodes.label: Arnold Hermann Ludwig Heeren
nodes.summary: Arnold Hermann Ludwig Heeren was a German historian and archaeologist. He studied at the Athenaeum (~1776–1779) and the University of Göttingen (~1779–1784), where he subsequently served as a professor from circa 1787 to 1842.

nodes.label: Peter von Bohlen
nodes.summary: Peter von Bohlen (1796–1840) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Halle-Wittenberg, Bonn under Georg Wilhelm Freytag, and Berlin under Franz Bopp, before becoming außerordentlicher Professor at the University of Königsberg in 1826.

nodes.label: Othmar Frank
nodes.summary: Othmar Frank (1770–1840) worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and philosophy. After studying in Paris and London, he held professorships at the University of Bamberg (~1804–1807), University of Würzburg (~1821–1826), and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (1826).

nodes.label: Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich
variants: ミュンヘン大学大学院

nodes.label: University of Paris
variants: Institut de Civilisation Indienne of the Sorbonne
Institut de Civilisation Indienne of the University of Paris
Institute de Civilisation Indienne of the Sorbonne
Institute of Indian Civilization of the University of Paris

nodes.label: Franz Bopp
nodes.summary: Franz Bopp (1791–1867) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Karl Joseph Hieronymus Windischmann, Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy, and Antoine-Léonard de Chézy, and at London and Göttingen. He served as Chair of Sanskrit at Humboldt University of Berlin (1821–1867).

nodes.label: Friedrich Windischmann
nodes.summary: Friedrich Windischmann was an Indologist and Iranian studies scholar. He studied at Munich and Bonn (PhD ~1832–1833) under Christian Lassen, later holding posts at Munich (~1836–1858) and as vicar general for the Archdiocese of Munich and Freising (~1848–1861).

nodes.label: Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy
nodes.jawiki: アントワーヌ＝イザーク・シルヴェストル・ド・サシ
nodes.summary: Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy (1758–1838) was a scholar of linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history. He held long-term posts at ENLOV (1795–1838), the Collège de France (1806–1838), and served as president of the Société Asiatique.

nodes.label: Antoine-Léonard de Chézy
nodes.jawiki: アントワーヌ＝レオナール・ド・シェジー
nodes.summary: Antoine-Léonard de Chézy (1773–1832) studied under Louis-Mathieu Langlès and Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. An Indologist, he worked at the Bibliothèque nationale de France, taught Persian at INALCO, and became Professor of Indian Language at the Collège de France (1815–1832).

nodes.label: Collège de France
variants: コレージュ・ド・フランス
コレジュ・ド・フランス
Institut de Civilisation Indienne du Collège de France

nodes.label: University of Göttingen
variants: Seminar für Indologie und Buddhismuskunde of the University of Göttingen
Seminar für Indologie und Buddhismuskunde, Universität Göttingen

nodes.label: Wilhelm von Humboldt
nodes.jawiki: ヴィルヘルム・フォン・フンボルト
nodes.description: Prussian philosopher, government official, diplomat, and educator (1767–1835)
nodes.summary: Wilhelm von Humboldt worked in linguistics, Indology, and philosophy, studying at Frankfurt an der Oder, Göttingen, and Jena. He founded Humboldt University of Berlin in 1810 and held a post there the same year.

nodes.label: Ernst Siecke
nodes.description: born:1846|died:1935|; Siecke, Ernst (Ernst Ludwig Albert Karl), 1846-; Siecke, Ernst Ludwig Albert Karl, 1846-1935

nodes.label: Alexandre Langlois
nodes.summary: Alexandre Langlois (1788–1854) was an Indologist. He studied under Antoine-Léonard de Chézy from around 1815 to 1832 and was a member of the Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres from around 1835 to 1854.

nodes.label: Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat
nodes.jawiki: ジャン＝ピエール・アベル＝レミュザ
nodes.summary: Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat was a sinologist and linguist who studied at INALCO. He held a professorship in Chinese at the Collège de France from 1815 to 1832, and taught scholars including Stanislas Julien and Eugène Burnouf.

nodes.label: Jean-Louis Burnouf
nodes.summary: Jean-Louis Burnouf studied at Collège d'Harcourt and under Antoine-Léonard de Chézy. A linguist, he held posts at Lycée Louis-le-Grand, University of Paris, Collège de France (1817–1844), and École Normale Supérieure (~1826–1844).

nodes.label: Eugène Burnouf
nodes.jawiki: ウジェーヌ・ビュルヌフ
nodes.summary: Eugène Burnouf (1801–1852) was a French Indologist and linguist who studied under Antoine-Léonard de Chézy (~1822–1832). He served as secretary of the Société Asiatique (1826, 1832) and taught at the Collège de France (1832–1852).

nodes.label: Christian Gottlob Heyne
nodes.summary: Christian Gottlob Heyne was a scholar of linguistics and history/archaeology. After studying at Leipzig University (~1748–1752), he held a post at the University of Göttingen from circa 1763 to 1812.

nodes.label: Christian Lassen
nodes.jawiki: クリスチャン・ラッセン (東洋学者)
nodes.summary: Christian Lassen was an Indologist and linguist who studied under August Wilhelm Schlegel at the University of Bonn (~1823–1827). He served at Bonn as an außerordentlicher Professor (1830) and ordentlicher Professor of Old Indian Language and Literature (1840–1876).

nodes.label: Paul Deussen
nodes.summary: Paul Deussen (1845–1919) was an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Christian Lassen at the University of Bonn and at Humboldt University of Berlin. He served as a professor at the University of Kiel from circa 1889 to 1919.

nodes.label: Otto Strauss
nodes.summary: Otto Strauss worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied under Paul Deussen from circa 1904 to 1911 and served as a professor at the University of Kiel from circa 1920 to 1935.

nodes.label: Georg Wilhelm Freytag
nodes.jawiki: ゲオルク・フライターク
nodes.summary: Georg Wilhelm Freytag (1788–1861) was a scholar of linguistics. He studied at the University of Göttingen and under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy, holding posts at the University of Göttingen (~1811–1815) and the University of Bonn (~1819–1861).

nodes.label: University of Königsberg
variants: ケーニヒスベルク大学

nodes.label: Theodor Goldstücker
nodes.jawiki: テーオドール・ゴルトシュテュッカー
nodes.summary: Theodor Goldstücker worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Königsberg under Peter von Bohlen and Karl Rosenkranz, Bonn under Christian Lassen, and under Eugène Burnouf. He held a chair in Sanskrit at University College London and the University of London (~1852–1872).

nodes.label: Friedrich Rückert
nodes.jawiki: フリードリヒ・リュッケルト
nodes.description: German poet, translator, and professor of Oriental languages (1788–1866)
nodes.summary: Friedrich Rückert specialized in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Würzburg, Heidelberg, and under Franz Bopp, and later served as professor at Erlangen-Nuremberg (1826) and Berlin (1841–1849).

nodes.label: University of Erlangen-Nuremberg
variants: International Research Consortium of "Fate, Freedom, and Prognostication in East Asia and Europe"

nodes.label: Johann Wilhelm Andreas Pfaff
nodes.summary: Johann Wilhelm Andreas Pfaff, an Indologist, studied at the University of Tübingen (~1791–1797). He held posts at the Imperial University of Dorpat (~1803–1809), University of Würzburg (~1809–1817), and University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1818–1835).

nodes.label: Adolf Holtzmann the Elder
nodes.summary: Adolf Holtzmann the Elder was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Othmar Frank, Johann Andreas Schmeller, and Eugène Burnouf. From 1852 to 1870, he served as Professor of German Literature and Sanskrit at Heidelberg University.

nodes.label: Johann Andreas Schmeller
nodes.summary: Johann Andreas Schmeller (1785–1852) was a linguist who held positions at the Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1826–1852) and the Bavarian State Library (~1829–1852).

nodes.label: Heidelberg University
variants: South Asia Institute of Heidelberg University

nodes.label: Salomon Lefmann
nodes.summary: Salomon Lefmann was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Franz Bopp (~1858–1864). He later served in the Sanskrit Extraordinariat at Heidelberg University (~1870–1907).

nodes.label: University of Freiburg
variants: Confucius Institute at the University of Freiburg

nodes.label: Friedrich August Rosen
nodes.summary: Friedrich August Rosen (1805–1837) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Franz Bopp (~1824–1826). He held posts as Professor of Oriental Languages at University College London (~1828–1836) and Professor of Sanskrit at the University of London (1834).

nodes.label: Adolf Friedrich Stenzler
nodes.jawiki: アドルフ・フリードリヒ・シュテンツラー
nodes.summary: Adolf Friedrich Stenzler was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Berlin, Greifswald, Bonn, and Paris under Bopp, Schlegel, and Lassen. He became Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Breslau in 1833 and Wrocław University Library sub-librarian (1834–1872).

nodes.label: Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer
nodes.summary: Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer (1801–1888) was a linguist who founded the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft. He completed his studies at Leipzig University (~1819–1824) and subsequently held a post there from around 1835 until 1888.

nodes.label: Ferdinand Benary
nodes.summary: Ferdinand Benary was a scholar of linguistics and religious studies. He studied under Franz Bopp (~1824–1827) and became an associate professor in the theological faculty at the Humboldt University of Berlin in 1831.

nodes.label: Agathon Benary
nodes.summary: Agathon Benary was a linguist who studied at Göttingen, Halle-Wittenberg, and under Franz Bopp. He held professorships at Köllnisches Gymnasium and Humboldt University of Berlin from around 1833 to 1860.

nodes.label: Bernhard Hirzel
nodes.summary: Bernhard Hirzel was an Indologist who studied at the University of Göttingen (~1830–1832) and under Franz Bopp (~1832–1835). He served as a Dozent at the University of Zurich from around 1833 to 1839.

nodes.label: Hermann Brockhaus
nodes.summary: Hermann Brockhaus (1806–1877) was an Indologist, linguist, and Iranian specialist who studied at Leipzig and under August Wilhelm Schlegel. He served as Professor Extraordinarius at Jena (1839) and Professor of East Asian Languages at Leipzig (1848, 1872–1877).

nodes.label: University of Zurich
variants: Völkerkundemuseum of the University of Zurich

nodes.label: Johann Christoph Adelung
nodes.jawiki: ヨハン・クリストフ・アーデルング
nodes.summary: Johann Christoph Adelung was a linguist who studied at the Kloster Berge school and the University of Halle-Wittenberg from circa 1752 to 1754.

nodes.label: Johannes Gildemeister
nodes.summary: Johannes Gildemeister studied at Göttingen under Heinrich Ewald and at Bonn under Georg Wilhelm Freytag and Christian Lassen. He was professor on the theological faculty at Marburg (~1845–1859) and later professor at Bonn (~1859–1890) in Indology and linguistics.

nodes.label: Colin Mackenzie
nodes.image: Colonel Colin Mackenzie and his Indian pandits by Thomas Hickey.jpg

nodes.label: William Ward
nodes.description: English pioneer Baptist missionary, author, printer and translator

nodes.label: George Turnour
nodes.jawiki: ジョージ・ターナー (歴史家)

nodes.label: John Wilson
nodes.description: Christian missionary, orientalist, and educator in Maharashtra, India (1804-1875)
nodes.summary: Wilson was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1819–1828). He served as president of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (~1835–1842).

nodes.label: Asiatic Society of Mumbai
variants: Bombay Branch of the Royal Asiatic Society

nodes.label: Brian Houghton Hodgson
nodes.image: Brian Houghton Hodgson by Louisa Starr-Canziani.jpg
nodes.jawiki: ブライアン・ホートン・ホジソン
nodes.summary: Brian Houghton Hodgson (1800–1894) was an Indologist and Tibetologist who studied at East India Company College, Fort William College, and Haileybury. He served as Assistant Resident (1820) and Resident (~1833–1843) at the Court of Nepal and British Residency.

nodes.label: Charles Masson
nodes.description: British East India Company soldier and explorer (1800–1853)

nodes.label: Eugène Jacquet
nodes.summary: Eugène Jacquet (1811–1838) was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat from circa 1828 to 1832 and under Eugène Burnouf from circa 1832 to 1838.

nodes.label: Daniel Wright
nodes.description: Scottish surgeon and physician; resided in Nepal

nodes.label: William Wright
nodes.summary: William Wright (1830–1889) was a scholar of linguistics and religion who studied at the University of St Andrews. He held posts at University College London, the British Museum, and the University of Cambridge, including Adams Professor of Arabic.

nodes.label: Hendrik Kern
nodes.summary: Hendrik Kern was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at Utrecht, Leiden, and under Albrecht Weber, and served as a professor at Leiden University from 1865 to 1903.

nodes.label: Bunyiu Nanjio
nodes.summary: Bunyiu Nanjio was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology. He studied at Oxford (~1879–1884) under Friedrich Max Müller and Arthur Anthony Macdonell. He served as Professor at the University of Tokyo (~1889–1906) and President of Otani University (~1914–1923).

nodes.label: Edward Byles Cowell
nodes.image: Portrait of Edward Byles Cowell by Charles Edmund Brock-1905.jpg
nodes.summary: Edward Byles Cowell studied at Oxford under Horace Hayman Wilson. An Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar, he was Principal of Sanskrit College (1858–1864), taught history at Presidency University, and served as Professor at Cambridge (1867, 1887).

nodes.label: Julius Eggeling
nodes.summary: Julius Eggeling was an Indologist who studied at Breslau and Berlin under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and Albrecht Weber. He served as Secretary of the Royal Asiatic Society (1869–1875) and taught Sanskrit at University College London and the University of Edinburgh (~1875–1914).

nodes.label: Robert Alexander Neil
nodes.image: R A Neil-R H Lord recto.tif

nodes.label: Alexander Csoma de Kőrös
nodes.jawiki: ケーレシ・チョマ・シャーンドル
nodes.summary: Alexander Csoma de Kőrös was a scholar of Tibetology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Göttingen and under traditional teachers in Ladakh, later serving as sub-librarian at the Asiatic Society (circa 1837–1842).

nodes.label: Jules Barthélemy-Saint-Hilaire
nodes.description: French philosopher, journalist, statesman, and possible illegitimate son of Napoleon I of France (1805-1895)
nodes.summary: Jules Barthélemy-Saint-Hilaire (1805–1895) was a scholar in philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Bourbon College and Lycée Louis-le-Grand. He held posts at the Collège de France (1838–1852) and the Académie des Sciences Morales et Politiques (~1839–1895).

nodes.id: I:Académie des Sciences Morales et Politiques
nodes.label: Académie des Sciences Morales et Politiques
variants: Académie des Sciences morales et politiques

nodes.label: Jules Mohl
nodes.summary: Jules Mohl worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and Sinology. He studied at Tübingen and under Silvestre de Sacy and Abel-Rémusat. He became a professor at Tübingen (1826) and later Professor des Persischen at the Collège de France (1847–1876).

nodes.label: Stanislas Julien
nodes.jawiki: スタニスラス・ジュリアン
nodes.summary: Stanislas Julien was a sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat at the Collège de France. He succeeded Abel-Rémusat in 1832, serving at the Collège de France as professor and administrator until 1873.

nodes.label: Robert Lenz
nodes.summary: Robert Lenz was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at Tartu Governorate Gymnasium and the Imperial University of Dorpat (1825–1828). He was Professor of Sanskrit at Saint Petersburg State University from ~1835 to 1836.

nodes.label: Saint Petersburg State University
variants: Faculty of Oriental Languages at St. Petersburg
Faculty of Oriental languages at St. Petersburg

nodes.label: Gaspare Gorresio
nodes.image: Gaspare Gorresio, post 1869 - Accademia delle Scienze di Torino 0015 B.jpg
nodes.summary: Gaspare Gorresio (1808–1891) was an Indologist who studied under Eugène Burnouf in 1834. He held posts at the University of Turin (~1852–1859) and served as a librarian at the Royal Library of Turin (~1859–1891).

nodes.label: Émile Burnouf
nodes.summary: Émile Burnouf worked in Indology and linguistics, studying at the École Normale Supérieure, the French School at Athens, and under Jean-Louis and Eugène Burnouf. He held a professorship at the University of Nancy and its Faculté des lettres (~1854–1867).

nodes.label: Théodore Pavie
nodes.image: Théodore Pavie (1811–1896), Orientalist, friend of the artist MET 31523.jpg
nodes.summary: Théodore Pavie (1811–1896) was a scholar of Indology and Sinology. He studied under Eugène Burnouf, whom he succeeded at the Collège de France (1852–1857), and later held a post at the Catholic University of the West (circa 1875–1896).

nodes.label: Adolphe Régnier
nodes.summary: Adolphe Régnier was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Eugène Burnouf (~1838–1844). He held posts at the Palace of Fontainebleau and served as Professor of Latin Eloquence at the Collège de France (~1857–1864).

nodes.label: Félix Nève
nodes.summary: Félix Nève (1816–1893) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Eugène Burnouf (~1838–1840) and Christian Lassen (~1840–1841) before becoming a professor at KU Leuven in 1841.

nodes.label: Abel Bergaigne
nodes.summary: Abel Bergaigne was a French Indologist and linguist who studied under Michel Bréal (~1867–1869). He held posts as a répétiteur at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1869–1888) and taught at the University of Paris (~1877–1888).

nodes.label: Theodor Benfey
nodes.jawiki: テーオドール・ベンファイ
nodes.summary: Theodor Benfey was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Göttingen (~1824–1826). He spent his career there as Privatdozent (1834), Lehrmeister (1848), and Ordinarius (1862–1881).

nodes.label: Friedrich Max Müller
nodes.jawiki: フリードリヒ・マックス・ミュラー
nodes.description: German-born British philologist, orientalist and indologist (1823–1900)
nodes.summary: Friedrich Max Müller worked in Indology, linguistics, and religious studies. He studied at Leipzig, Berlin, and Paris under Hermann Brockhaus, Eugène Burnouf, Franz Bopp, and others. He spent his career at Oxford from 1850, becoming professor in 1854.

nodes.label: Joseph Toussaint Reinaud
nodes.summary: Joseph Toussaint Reinaud worked in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology, having studied under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. He held posts at INALCO from 1838, the Société Asiatique from 1852, and the Bibliothèque nationale de France from 1854.

nodes.label: Heinrich Ewald
nodes.description: German orientalist, theologian, and Biblical exegete (1803–1875)
nodes.summary: Heinrich Ewald (1803–1875) worked in linguistics, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Göttingen under Johann Gottfried Eichhorn, and held professorships at Göttingen (1824–1837, 1848–1867) and the University of Tübingen (1838–1848).

nodes.id: I:Zeitschrift für die Kunde des Morgenlandes
nodes.label: Zeitschrift für die Kunde des Morgenlandes
variants: Zeitschrift für die Kunde des Morgenlandes

nodes.label: Ernst Trumpp
nodes.jawiki: エルンスト・トランプ
nodes.summary: Ernst Trumpp worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied under Rudolf von Roth (~1847–1850) and served as a professor at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich from ~1873 to 1885.

nodes.label: August Schleicher
nodes.jawiki: アウグスト・シュライヒャー
nodes.summary: August Schleicher worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Leipzig, Tübingen, and Bonn under scholars including Heinrich Fleischer, Heinrich Ewald, and Christian Lassen. He taught at the University of Bonn, Charles University, and the University of Jena.

nodes.label: Moritz Abraham Stern
nodes.jawiki: モーリッツ・アブラハム・シュテルン
nodes.summary: Moritz Abraham Stern was a linguist who studied at Heidelberg University and the University of Göttingen under Carl Friedrich Gauss. He was a faculty member at the University of Göttingen from 1830 to 1884.

nodes.label: Rudolf von Roth
nodes.jawiki: ルドルフ・フォン・ロート
nodes.summary: Rudolf von Roth was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Tübinger Stift under Heinrich Ewald and under Eugène Burnouf. He held a professorial post at the University of Tübingen from 1848 until 1895.

nodes.label: William Dwight Whitney
nodes.jawiki: ウィリアム・ドワイト・ホイットニー
nodes.summary: William Dwight Whitney (1827–1894) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Williams, Yale, Berlin, and Tübingen under Salisbury, Weber, Roth, and Bopp. He was a professor of Sanskrit at Yale (1853–1894) and served as president of the AOS.

nodes.label: James Tod
nodes.description: 1782-1835, English officer of the British East India Company and an Oriental scholar
nodes.summary: James Tod worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He held posts with the East India Company (~1799–1822) and served as Librarian at the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland (~1823–1835).

nodes.id: I:Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland
nodes.label: Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland
variants: Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland

nodes.label: Adalbert Kuhn
nodes.jawiki: アーダルベルト・クーン
nodes.summary: Adalbert Kuhn, a scholar of linguistics and Indology, studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Franz Bopp (~1833–1837). He later served as Direktor of the Köllnisches Gymnasium (~1870–1881).

nodes.label: Andrzej Gawroński
nodes.summary: Andrzej Gawroński (1885–1927) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Lviv University (~1902–1903) and Leipzig University (~1904–1907). He held posts at Jagiellonian University (~1912–1916) and Lviv University (~1916–1927).

nodes.label: Stamford Raffles
nodes.image: George Francis Joseph - Sir Thomas Stamford Bingley Raffles.jpg
nodes.jawiki: トーマス・ラッフルズ

nodes.label: Gottlieb Siegfried Bayer
nodes.summary: Gottlieb Siegfried Bayer (1694–1738), a sinologist and historian, studied at the University of Königsberg under Christoph Theodosius Walther. He held posts at Königsberg and the Russian Academy of Sciences (from 1726) for classical antiquities and oriental languages.

nodes.label: Russian Academy of Sciences
variants: Akademie der Wissenschaften zu St. Petersburg
K. Akademie der Wissenschaften zu St. Petersburg
Imperial Academy of Sciences at St. Petersburg

nodes.label: Friedrich Bollensen
nodes.summary: Friedrich Bollensen was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied theology and Sanskrit under Heinrich Ewald at Göttingen (~1827–1830), later holding posts at Gatchina Orphanage (1834), Saint Petersburg State University (~1845–1860), and Kazan Federal University (1852–1856).

nodes.label: Wilhelm Geiger
nodes.jawiki: ヴィルヘルム・ガイガー
nodes.summary: Wilhelm Geiger was an Indologist, Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar, and linguist. He earned his PhD at Erlangen-Nuremberg under Friedrich von Spiegel, later holding posts at Neustadt, Munich, and Erlangen-Nuremberg.

nodes.label: Friedrich von Spiegel
nodes.jawiki: フリードリヒ・シュピーゲル
nodes.summary: Friedrich von Spiegel worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and Indology. He studied at Bonn under Christian Lassen, Hermann Brockhaus, and Heinrich Fleischer, and held a post at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1849–1890).

nodes.label: Heinrich Uhle
nodes.summary: Heinrich Uhle (1842–1925) was an Indology scholar who studied under Hermann Brockhaus from around 1860 to 1865. He later served as a professor at the Kreuzschule from around 1874 to 1907.

nodes.label: Eduard Sachau
nodes.summary: Eduard Sachau worked in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history/archaeology. After studying at Kiel and Leipzig (under Hermann Brockhaus), he held posts at Vienna, Frederick William University Berlin, and as Director of the Seminar for Oriental Languages.

nodes.label: Hermann Camillo Kellner
nodes.summary: Hermann Camillo Kellner (1839–1916) was an Indologist who studied under Hermann Brockhaus (~1860–1865). He served as a Gymnasialprofessor at Gymnasium zu Zwickau from ~1866 to 1904.

nodes.label: Richard Fritzsche
nodes.summary: Richard Fritzsche (born 1851) was an Indologist who studied under Hermann Brockhaus. He held the post of Rektor at Gymnasium Schneeberg.

nodes.label: University of Marburg
variants: マールブルク大学大学院

nodes.label: Niels Ludvig Westergaard
nodes.image: Niels Ludvig Westergaard by Budtz Müller.jpg
nodes.jawiki: ニルス・ルズヴィ・ヴェスタゴー
nodes.summary: Niels Ludvig Westergaard worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at Østre Borgerdyd school and the universities of Copenhagen, Bonn, Paris, London, and Oxford. In 1845, he became Professor für Indisch-orientalische Philologie at the University of Copenhagen.

nodes.label: Albert Hoefer
nodes.summary: Albert Hoefer worked in Indology and linguistics. He served as a professor at the University of Greifswald from circa 1840 to 1883 and founded the Zeitschrift für die Wissenschaft der Sprache in 1845.

nodes.id: I:Zeitschrift für die Wissenschaft der Sprache
nodes.label: Zeitschrift für die Wissenschaft der Sprache
variants: Zeitschrift für die Wissenschaft der Sprache

nodes.label: Johann Gottfried Ludwig Kosegarten
nodes.summary: Johann Gottfried Ludwig Kosegarten was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Greifswald (~1808–1812). He held posts at the University of Jena (~1817–1824) and as professor at Greifswald (~1824–1850).

nodes.label: Siegfried Goldschmidt
nodes.summary: Siegfried Goldschmidt (1844–1884) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at the University of Tübingen in 1867 and under Albrecht Weber (1864) and Rudolf von Roth (~1864–1869).

nodes.label: Anton Eduard Wollheim da Fonseca
nodes.image: PPN663949858 Bildnis von Anton Eduard Wollheim Dafonseca.jpg
nodes.summary: Anton Eduard Wollheim da Fonseca (1810–1884) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin from circa 1827 to 1831 and later served there as Privatdozent for oriental languages in 1849.

nodes.label: Richard Pischel
nodes.jawiki: リヒャルト・ピシェル
nodes.summary: Richard Pischel was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and Albrecht Weber. He held posts at Breslau, Kiel, Halle-Wittenberg, and Humboldt University of Berlin (1902–1908), alongside the Prussian Academy of Sciences.

nodes.label: Alfred Hillebrandt
nodes.summary: Alfred Hillebrandt (1853–1927) was an Indologist. He studied at the University of Breslau (~1871–1875) under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1875–1876). He served as professor at the University of Breslau (~1883–1922).

nodes.label: Adalbert Bezzenberger
nodes.summary: Adalbert Bezzenberger was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Göttingen (~1869–1874) under Theodor Benfey and at LMU Munich (~1872–1873). He held a post at the University of Göttingen (~1874–1880).

nodes.label: Hermann Oldenberg
nodes.jawiki: ヘルマン・オルデンベルク
nodes.summary: Hermann Oldenberg (1854–1920) was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1871–1875). He held professorships at Berlin (~1878–1889), the University of Kiel (~1889–1908), and the University of Göttingen (~1908–1920).

nodes.label: Jacob Wackernagel
nodes.jawiki: ヤーコプ・ヴァッカーナーゲル
nodes.summary: Jacob Wackernagel was a linguistics and Indology scholar who studied at the University of Göttingen under Theodor Benfey (~1872–1874). He held professorships at the University of Basel (1881–1902) and the University of Göttingen (~1902–1915).

nodes.label: Leo Meyer
nodes.summary: Leo Meyer was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Göttingen and Berlin under Theodor Benfey, Franz Bopp, and Moriz Haupt. He held posts at the University of Göttingen (ca. 1856–1865) and the Imperial University of Dorpat (ca. 1865–1898).

nodes.label: Hermann Collitz
nodes.summary: Hermann Collitz (1855–1935), a scholar of linguistics and Indology, studied at Johanneum Lüneburg and under Theodor Benfey at Göttingen. He served as professor at Bryn Mawr College (1885–1907) and Johns Hopkins University (1907).

nodes.label: Friedrich Bechtel
nodes.summary: Friedrich Bechtel worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Göttingen under Theodor Benfey and August Fick (~1873–1876), later holding posts at Göttingen (~1878–1895) and the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1895–1924).

nodes.label: Berthold Delbrück
nodes.jawiki: ベルトルト・デルブリュック
nodes.description: German comparative linguist and Sanskrit scholar (1842–1922)
nodes.summary: Berthold Delbrück was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied under August Friedrich Pott and Albrecht Weber. He held posts at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (1867) and the University of Jena (1870–1913).

variants: University of Copenhagen, Department of Asian Studies
Institute of Oriental Studies, University of Copenhagen
Center for Subjectivity Research at the University of Copenhagen
Danish National Research Foundation: Center for Subjectivity Research, University of Copenhagen

variants: ルーヴァン・カトリック大学東洋学科

nodes.label: August Leskien
nodes.jawiki: アウグスト・レスキーン
nodes.summary: August Leskien was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Leipzig, Kiel, and Jena, learning under Georg Curtius and August Schleicher. He held posts at Jena and Göttingen before serving as a professor at Leipzig University (~1870–1916).

nodes.label: Leopold von Schroeder
nodes.summary: Leopold von Schroeder (1851–1920) was an Indologist who studied at Dorpat/Tartu, Leipzig, Jena, and under Rudolf von Roth. He held posts at the University of Tartu (~1882–1894), the University of Innsbruck (~1896–1899), and the University of Vienna (~1899–1920).

nodes.label: Anton Schiefner
nodes.summary: Anton Schiefner was a scholar of Tibetology, linguistics, and Indology. He studied law at Saint Petersburg State University (~1835–1840) and served as Bibliothekar at the Russian Academy of Sciences from around 1852 to 1879.

nodes.label: Carl Cappeller
nodes.summary: Carl Cappeller was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Franz Bopp and Albrecht Weber, as well as Königsberg, Leipzig (PhD), and Jena (Habilitation). In 1875, he became a professor at the University of Jena.

nodes.label: Karl Rosenkranz
nodes.jawiki: ヨハン・カール・ローゼンクランツ
nodes.summary: Karl Rosenkranz was a philosopher who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1824–1826), Heidelberg University (~1826–1827), and the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1827–1828). He held a post at the University of Halle-Wittenberg from around 1828 to 1833.

nodes.label: University of Tübingen
variants: Seminar für Indologie und Vergleichende Religionswissenschaft, Universität Tübingen

nodes.label: Martin Haug
nodes.summary: Martin Haug was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Tübingen and Bonn under Rudolf von Roth and Theodor Benfey. He held posts at Bonn, Heidelberg, Deccan College (~1859-1866), and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1868-1876).

nodes.label: Karl Friedrich Geldner
nodes.jawiki: カール・フリードリヒ・ゲルトナー
nodes.summary: Karl Friedrich Geldner studied Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies at Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth and at Leipzig under Hermann Brockhaus and Ernst Windisch. He held posts at Tübingen, Halle-Wittenberg, Humboldt University of Berlin, and Marburg.

nodes.label: Bruno Lindner
nodes.summary: Bruno Lindner was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied under Rudolf von Roth (~1874–1878). He held a post at Leipzig University from ~1879 to 1925.

nodes.label: Richard von Garbe
nodes.summary: Richard von Garbe was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Rudolf von Roth and Bhagavata Acharya. He later succeeded Roth at the University of Tübingen, serving as chairholder from 1895 to 1927.

nodes.label: Maurice Bloomfield
nodes.jawiki: モーリス・ブルームフィールド
nodes.summary: Maurice Bloomfield (1855–1928) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied under William Dwight Whitney and Charles Rockwell Lanman, earned his PhD at Johns Hopkins University, and was appointed professor there in 1881.

nodes.label: Julius Grill
nodes.summary: Julius Grill was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at the University of Tübingen and under Rudolf von Roth and Adalbert Kuhn. He held professorships at the Seminaries of Maulbronn and Blaubeuren (~1874–1904) and Tübingen (1888).

nodes.label: Adolf Kaegi
nodes.summary: Adolf Kaegi was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied under Rudolf von Roth around 1872–1874. He served as a professor at the University of Zurich from approximately 1883 to 1914.

nodes.label: Heinrich Zimmer
nodes.summary: Heinrich Zimmer (1851–1910) was a linguist and Indologist who studied in Strasbourg and Berlin under Roth, Goldschmidt, Weber, Scherer, and Windisch. He held posts at Greifswald (~1881–1901), Berlin (~1901–1910), Heidelberg University, and Columbia University.

nodes.label: Theodor Aufrecht
nodes.summary: Theodor Aufrecht worked in Indology and linguistics, studying at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1842–1847), where he became Privatdozent in 1850. He was Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Edinburgh (1862) and Professor at the University of Bonn (1875–1889).

variants: Zeitschrift für Vergleichende Sprachforschung auf dem Gebiete des Deutschen, Griechischen und Lateinischen

nodes.label: Beitrage zur Vergleichenden Sprachforschung auf dem Gebiete der Arischen, Celtischen und Slawischen Sprachen
variants: Beiträge zur Vergleichenden Sprachforschung auf dem Gebiete der Arischen, Celtischen und Slawischen Sprachen

nodes.label: Beitrage zur Kunde der indogermanischen Sprachen
variants: Beiträge zur Kunde der indogermanischen Sprachen

nodes.label: Wilhelm Schulze
nodes.summary: Wilhelm Schulze specialized in linguistics and Indology. He held posts at the University of Marburg (~1892–1895), the University of Göttingen (~1895–1902), and as professor at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1902–1932).

nodes.label: Johannes Schmidt
nodes.jawiki: ヨハネス・シュミット
nodes.summary: Johannes Schmidt studied under August Schleicher at Jena and Albrecht Weber at Bonn. A linguist and Indologist, he held posts at Bonn (~1868–1873) and Graz (~1873–1876), before serving as professor at Berlin (~1876–1901).

nodes.label: Gottfried Hermann
nodes.image: Gottfried Hermann, von Carl Christian Vogel von Vogelstein.jpg
nodes.summary: Gottfried Hermann (1772–1848) was a German linguist. He studied at Leipzig University (~1786–1793) and the University of Jena (~1793–1794), and subsequently held a post at Leipzig University from around 1798 to 1848.

nodes.label: Moriz Haupt
nodes.summary: Moriz Haupt was a scholar of linguistics who studied at Leipzig University under Gottfried Hermann. He subsequently held academic posts at Leipzig University from around 1837 to 1851 and at Humboldt University of Berlin from around 1853 to 1874.

nodes.label: Anton Westermann
nodes.summary: Anton Westermann was a German scholar in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Leipzig University (~1823–1828) and spent his career there as a faculty member from around 1834 to 1869.

nodes.label: Reinhold Klotz
nodes.summary: Reinhold Klotz (1807–1870) was a linguist who studied at Leipzig University from circa 1826 to 1829. He later held a post at Leipzig University from circa 1832 to 1870, where he taught Friedrich Max Müller.

nodes.label: Friedrich Wilhelm Joseph von Schelling
nodes.image: Friedrich Wilhelm Joseph Schelling, 1848 daguerreotype - cropped.jpg
nodes.jawiki: フリードリヒ・シェリング
nodes.summary: Friedrich Wilhelm Joseph von Schelling was a philosopher who studied at the Tübinger Stift, Tübingen, and Leipzig. He held professorships at Jena (1798), Würzburg (~1803–1806), Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1820–1827), Munich (~1827–1841), and Berlin (~1841–1846).

nodes.label: Hermann Brunnhofer
nodes.summary: Indologist Hermann Brunnhofer (1841–1916) studied under Albrecht Weber and succeeded Franz Kielhorn. He taught at Goldingen Gymnasium (~1875–1881) and served as Titularprofessor at the University of Bern (1901–1914).

nodes.label: Moriz Winternitz
nodes.jawiki: モーリッツ・ヴィンターニッツ
nodes.summary: Moriz Winternitz was an Indologist who studied at the University of Vienna under Georg Bühler and under Friedrich Max Müller. He taught at the German University in Prague, Charles University, and Visva-Bharati University.

nodes.label: James R. Ballantyne
nodes.summary: James R. Ballantyne (1813–1864) was an Indology and philosophy scholar educated at Edinburgh under James Michael and Francis Johnson. He taught at the Scottish Naval and Military Academy, headed Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and was librarian at the India Office Library.

nodes.label: Sampurnanand Sanskrit University
variants: Sarasvati Bhavan Library, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University

nodes.label: Jean-Baptiste Biot
nodes.jawiki: ジャン＝バティスト・ビオ
nodes.summary: Jean-Baptiste Biot studied at Collège Louis-le-Grand, École polytechnique, and École Nationale des Ponts et Chaussées. He worked in sinology and history/archaeology, holding posts in the French Revolutionary Army, Bureau des Longitudes, Collège de France, and Science Faculty of Paris.

nodes.label: Ebenezer Burgess
nodes.description: United States missionary to the Mahrattas, in western India

nodes.label: Christian Karl Josias von Bunsen
nodes.summary: Christian Karl Josias von Bunsen was a scholar in linguistics, religious studies, and history/archaeology. He completed his studies at the University of Marburg (~1808–1809) and the University of Göttingen (~1809–1812).

nodes.label: Ludwig Noiré
nodes.image: Plate 13 Ludwig Noiré, Photograph album of German and Austrian scientists (cropped).png
nodes.jawiki: ルートヴィヒ・ノワレ

nodes.label: Louis Havet
nodes.summary: Louis Havet worked in linguistics and other fields, studying at EPHE under Michel Bréal and Abel Bergaigne (~1868–1874). He was later appointed to a post at the Collège de France, serving from 1885 to 1925.

nodes.label: Kenjiu Kasawara
nodes.summary: Kenjiu Kasawara (1851–1883) was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Oxford in 1879, studying under Friedrich Max Müller from 1879 to 1882 and Arthur Anthony Macdonell around 1880 to 1882.

nodes.label: Heinrich Wenzel
nodes.summary: Heinrich Wenzel (1855–1893) worked in Indology and Tibetology. He studied at Jena, Tübingen, Leipzig, and under Heinrich August Jäschke, Léon Feer, and Georg von der Gabelentz, later completing his Habilitation at Leipzig University in 1887.

nodes.label: Heinrich August Jäschke
nodes.jawiki: ハインリヒ・アウグスト・イェシュケ

nodes.label: Bruno Liebich
nodes.summary: Bruno Liebich was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Franz Kielhorn (~1883–1886). He served as Professor Ordinarius at the University of Breslau (~1891–1921) and held a post at Heidelberg University (~1921–1928).

nodes.label: Archibald Edward Gough
nodes.description: (1845-1915) British educationalist, translator, editor and academic administrator
nodes.summary: Archibald Edward Gough was an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Monier Monier-Williams (~1863–1866). He held posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1868–1878), Presidency University, Kolkata (~1878–1895, 1914), and served as Principal of Aliah University (~1881–1895, 1914).

nodes.label: John Pickford
nodes.summary: John Pickford was an Indologist who studied under Monier Monier-Williams. He later served as a professor at the University of Madras.

nodes.label: University of Madras
variants: Department of Sanskrit, University of Madras
Department of Sanskrit at the University of Madras
Radhakrishnan Institute for Advanced Study in Philosophy, University of Madras
Radhakrishnan Institute for Advanced Study in Philosophy
Department of Sanskrit in the University of Madras
Centre of Advanced Study in Philosophy, University of Madras

nodes.label: Ralph T. H. Griffith
nodes.summary: Ralph T. H. Griffith (1826–1906) was an Indologist who studied at The Queen's College, Oxford, under Horace Hayman Wilson (~1845–1849). He succeeded James R. Ballantyne and served as Principal at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1883).

nodes.label: Robert Needham Cust
nodes.summary: Robert Needham Cust was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at Eton College (~1834–1840) and Haileybury and Imperial Service College (~1840–1842). He served in the Bengal Civil Service from ~1843 to 1867.

nodes.label: J. Talboys Wheeler
nodes.description: British historian and author known for his works on Indian history during the colonial era (1824–1897)
nodes.summary: J. Talboys Wheeler worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. After studying at the University of Oxford, he served as Assistant Secretary for the Government of India from circa 1862 to 1870.

nodes.label: Aliah University
variants: Madrassa, il Collegio maomettano di Calcutta

nodes.label: Presidency University, Kolkata
variants: Presidency College of the University of Calcutta

nodes.label: James Sutherland Cotton
nodes.summary: James Sutherland Cotton was an Indologist and historian. He studied at Magdalen College School, Brighton College (~1859–1862), Winchester College (~1862–1867), and Trinity College, Oxford (~1867–1871), and held a post at Queens' College, Cambridge (1871–1874).

nodes.label: William Wilson Hunter
nodes.jawiki: ウィリアム・ウィルソン・ハンター
nodes.summary: William Wilson Hunter (1840–1900) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Glasgow, Paris, and Bonn, he served in the Indian Civil Service (~1862–1887) and held a post at the University of Calcutta (~1882–1887).

nodes.label: Adolf Kirchhoff
nodes.summary: Adolf Kirchhoff was a scholar of linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at the Humboldt University of Berlin (~1842–1846) and later held a post there and at Frederick William University Berlin (~1865–1908).

nodes.label: Hermann Jacobi
nodes.summary: Indologist and linguist Hermann Jacobi (1850–1937) studied at Bonn, Berlin, and Calcutta. He held posts at Münster (~1876–1885), Kiel (~1885–1889), Cologne, Munich, and the University of Bonn (attested 1925).

nodes.label: Jarl Charpentier
nodes.summary: Jarl Charpentier was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Uppsala University and the University of Bonn under Karl Ferdinand Johansson and Hermann Jacobi. He served as an assistant professor at Uppsala University, later succeeding Johansson in 1927.

nodes.label: Bal Gangadhar Tilak
nodes.image: Young India; an interpretation and a history of the nationalist movement from within (1916) (14781987942).jpg
nodes.jawiki: バール・ガンガーダル・ティラク
nodes.description: Indian nationalist leader, writer and journalist (1856–1920)
nodes.summary: Bal Gangadhar Tilak worked in indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Elphinstone College (~1873-1874), Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1874-1877), and Government Law College, Mumbai (~1877-1879).

nodes.label: Reinhold Rost
nodes.image: Reinhold Rost, Porträt mit Signatur, um 1890.jpg
nodes.summary: Reinhold Rost (1822–1896) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Jena (~1842–1847). He served at The King's School Canterbury, St Augustine's College, the Royal Asiatic Society, and as Librarian for the India Office and India Office Library.

nodes.label: Heinrich Kiepert
nodes.description: German geographer, cartographer and university professor in Berlin (1818–1899)
nodes.summary: Heinrich Kiepert (1818–1899) was a scholar in history and archaeology who studied at Frederick William University Berlin in 1837. He held positions at the Landes-Industrie-Comptoir zu Weimar (1845–1852) and at Frederick William University Berlin in 1859.

nodes.label: Wilhelm Deecke
nodes.summary: Linguist Wilhelm Deecke studied at Leipzig, Frederick William University Berlin, and Katharineum under Albrecht Weber, Franz Bopp, and Moriz Haupt. He held posts at Katharineum (1852–1855) and Ernestinenschule (1855–1870).

nodes.label: Ghent University
variants: Centre for Buddhist Studies, Ghent University

nodes.label: Josef Schick
nodes.summary: Josef Schick (1859–1944) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Albrecht Weber. He held posts at Heidelberg University (c. 1890–1896) and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (c. 1896–1926).

nodes.label: Michael Viggo Fausbøll
nodes.jawiki: ヴィゴ・ファウスベル
nodes.description: Danish educator, translator, orientalist and linguist (1821–1908)
nodes.summary: Michael Viggo Fausbøll (1821–1908) was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Copenhagen (~1838–1847) and later held a post there (~1878–1902).

nodes.label: Emil Sieg
nodes.summary: Emil Sieg (1866–1951) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin and the University of Kiel. He held positions at Humboldt University of Berlin (1896–1908), the University of Kiel (~1909–1920), and the University of Göttingen (~1920–1935).

nodes.label: Walther Schubring
nodes.summary: Walther Schubring was an Indologist who studied under Ernst Leumann (~1903–1906). He later served as a professor at the University of Hamburg (attested 1958).

nodes.label: Ernst Leumann
nodes.jawiki: エルンスト・ロイマン
nodes.summary: Ernst Leumann was a scholar in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He served as a professor at the University of Strasbourg from ~1884 to 1919.

nodes.label: Luigi Suali
nodes.summary: Luigi Suali was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at the University of Bologna (~1900–1904) and under Hermann Jacobi (~1904–1906). He held a post at the University of Pavia from ~1907 to 1951.

nodes.label: Helmuth von Glasenapp
variants: ヘルムート・フォン・グラーゼナップ
nodes.summary: Helmuth von Glasenapp was an Indologist and scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He studied under Hermann Jacobi and Wanczura, and held posts as Privatdozent at Bonn and Berlin, followed by chairs at Königsberg (1928–1944) and Tübingen (1946–1959).

nodes.label: Yale University
variants: Yale University's Interdisciplinary Center for Bioethics
Department of East Asian Languages and Literatures at Yale University
Sheffield Scientific School at New Haven

nodes.label: Edward Elbridge Salisbury
nodes.summary: Edward Elbridge Salisbury worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Yale and in Europe under Woolsey, Burnouf, de Sacy, Garcin de Tassy, Bopp, and Lassen. He was Professor of Arabic and Sanskrit at Yale (1841–1854).

nodes.label: Charles Rockwell Lanman
nodes.image: Charles Rockwell Lanman Professor of Sanskrit Harvard.jpg
nodes.summary: Indologist and linguist Charles Rockwell Lanman studied at Yale, and under William Dwight Whitney and Rudolf von Roth. He taught at Johns Hopkins (circa 1876–1880) and served as Professor at Harvard University from 1880.

nodes.label: John Avery
nodes.summary: John Avery was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Amherst College, University of Tübingen, Humboldt University of Berlin, and under William Dwight Whitney. He later served as Professor of Greek at Grinnell College (1870–1877) and Bowdoin College (1877).

nodes.label: Ernst Haas
nodes.summary: Ernst Haas was an Indologist who studied at Berlin under Albrecht Weber, and at Bonn and Tübingen. He held posts at the British Museum (1866) and at University College London as Professor of Sanskrit (1875).

nodes.label: British Museum
variants: Department of Coins and Medals, the British Museum
Department of Oriental Printed Books and Manuscripts in the British Museum
Department of Oriental Antiquities, The British Museum

nodes.label: University College London
variants: Wellcome Trust Centre for the History of Medicine at University College London
Institute of Archaeology, University College London (UCL)
Institute of Archaeology, University College London
Wellcome Trust Centre for the study of the History of Medicine at University College London

nodes.label: Wilhelm Pertsch
nodes.summary: Wilhelm Pertsch specialized in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1853–1854) and under Albrecht Weber (1850) and Rudolf von Roth (~1854–1855).

nodes.label: Fritz Johaentgen
nodes.summary: Fritz Johaentgen was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Christian Lassen and Martin Haug.

nodes.label: Hermann Grassmann
nodes.jawiki: ヘルマン・グラスマン
nodes.summary: Hermann Grassmann (1809–1877) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Frederick William University Berlin. He taught at Marienstiftsgymnasium Stettin (1832–1834; 1852–1877 as professor), the Gewerbeschule (1834–1835), and Friedrich-Wilhelms-Gymnasium (1835–1852).

nodes.label: Alfred Ludwig
nodes.summary: Alfred Ludwig (1832–1912) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Vienna and Humboldt University of Berlin under Albrecht Weber, Moriz Haupt, Anton Boller, and Friedrich Müller. He served as professor at Charles University from 1860.

nodes.label: University of Vienna
variants: ウィーン大学インド学研究所
Institut für Indologie der Universität Wien

nodes.label: Friedrich Müller
variants: フリードリヒ・ミューラー
nodes.summary: Friedrich Müller was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at the Theresianum, University of Vienna, and Göttingen, studying under Anton Boller (~1853–1856). He worked at Austrian libraries and printing offices before becoming professor at Vienna (1869).

nodes.label: Anton Boller
nodes.summary: Anton Boller (1811–1869) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. His academic career was centered at the University of Vienna, where he served as Dozent and Professor from 1845, becoming Professor of Comparative Linguistics and Sanskrit in 1855.

nodes.label: Wilhelm Scherer
nodes.summary: Wilhelm Scherer was a scholar of linguistics who studied at the University of Vienna (~1858–1860). He later held posts at the University of Vienna (~1868–1872) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1877–1886).

nodes.label: University of Cambridge
variants: Mongolia and Inner Asia Studies Unit
Department of East Asian Studies of the University of Cambridge

nodes.label: Edward Granville Browne
nodes.jawiki: エドワード・グランヴィル・ブラウン
nodes.summary: Edward Granville Browne specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. After studying at Pembroke College, Cambridge (~1879–1882), he served as Adams Professor of Arabic at the University of Cambridge from ~1902 to 1926.

nodes.label: Franz Heinrich Trithen
nodes.summary: Franz Heinrich Trithen (1820–1854) was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Franz Bopp at Frederick William University and Humboldt University of Berlin. He worked at the British Museum (~1844–1848) and as Professor of Modern Languages at Oxford (~1848–1854).

nodes.label: Friedrich Haag
nodes.description: Swiss classical philologist, linguist and teacher (1846-1914)
nodes.summary: Friedrich Haag worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Zurich under Heinrich Schweizer-Sidler (~1865–1869, habilitation 1873), Berlin, and Göttingen, before serving as Dozent at Zurich (1873–1884) and professor at Bern (~1878–1914).

nodes.label: Heinrich Schweizer-Sidler
nodes.summary: Heinrich Schweizer-Sidler (1815–1894) was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied under Bernhard Hirzel from around 1835 to 1838 and held an academic post at the University of Zurich from around 1841 to 1894.

nodes.id: I:Evangelical Seminaries of Maulbronn and Blaubeuren
nodes.label: Evangelical Seminaries of Maulbronn and Blaubeuren
Georg Curtius
nodes.jawiki: ゲオルク・クルツィウス
nodes.summary: Georg Curtius (1820–1885) was a linguist who studied at Bonn under Ritschl and Lassen and at Berlin under Bopp. He held academic posts at Charles University and the University of Kiel before serving as professor at Leipzig University (~1862–1885).

nodes.label: Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl
nodes.summary: Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl was a scholar of linguistics. He studied at Leipzig and Halle-Wittenberg, and subsequently held posts at Halle-Wittenberg (~1829–1833), Breslau (~1833–1839), Bonn (~1839–1865), and Leipzig (~1865–1875).

nodes.label: Friedrich Zarncke
nodes.summary: Friedrich Zarncke was a scholar of linguistics. He studied at Leipzig University (~1843–1847) and later held academic posts at the University of Rostock (~1850–1852) and Leipzig University (~1852–1891).

nodes.label: Hermann Reich
nodes.description: German writer, literary scholar and classical philologist

nodes.label: Johannes Hertel
nodes.summary: Johannes Hertel studied at Leipzig University (PhD ~1891–1897). Specializing in Indology, he taught at Lessing-Gymnasium Döbeln (~1898–1920) and later held the chair for Indian philology at Leipzig University (~1920–1937), succeeding Ernst Windisch.

nodes.label: August Friedrich Pott
nodes.jawiki: アウグスト・フリードリヒ・ポット
nodes.summary: August Friedrich Pott was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Göttingen (~1821–1827) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1830–1833). In 1833, he was appointed Professor of General Linguistics at the University of Halle-Wittenberg.

nodes.label: Karl Brugmann
nodes.jawiki: カール・ブルークマン
nodes.summary: Karl Brugmann was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Georg Curtius from around 1868 to 1871. He held academic posts at the University of Freiburg (~1884–1887) and Leipzig University (~1887–1919).

nodes.label: Eugen Wilhelm
nodes.summary: Eugen Wilhelm (1842–1923) was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Indology. He studied under August Schleicher (~1860–1864) and served as a professor at the University of Jena from circa 1869 to 1923.

nodes.label: Carl Gaedicke
nodes.summary: Carl Gaedicke worked in Indology and linguistics. He completed his PhD at the University of Jena by 1877, having studied under Berthold Delbrück, Eduard Sievers, and Carl Cappeller.

nodes.label: Ferdinand de Saussure
nodes.image: Ferdinand de Saussure by Jullien Restored.png
nodes.jawiki: フェルディナン・ド・ソシュール
nodes.summary: Ferdinand de Saussure was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Geneva, Berlin, and Leipzig under Georg Curtius and Karl Brugmann. He held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1880–1891) and the University of Geneva (1891–1913).

nodes.label: Eduard Sievers
nodes.jawiki: エドゥアルト・ジーファース
nodes.summary: Eduard Sievers was a linguist who studied at Leipzig and Frederick William University Berlin. He held professorial posts at Jena (1871–1883), Tübingen (1883–1887), Halle-Wittenberg (1887–1892), and Leipzig (1892–1922).

nodes.label: Ernst Curtius
nodes.summary: Ernst Curtius was a historian and archaeologist who studied at the universities of Bonn (~1833–1834) and Göttingen (~1834–1837). He held posts at Frederick William University Berlin (~1844–1856), the University of Göttingen (~1856–1868), and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1868–1896).

nodes.label: Graziadio Isaia Ascoli
nodes.image: Graziadio Isaia Ascoli, post 1861 - Accademia delle Scienze di Torino 0066 B.jpg
nodes.jawiki: グラツィアディオ・イザイア・アスコリ
nodes.summary: Graziadio Isaia Ascoli (1829–1907) was a linguist and Indologist. In 1860, he became a professor at the Accademia Scientifico-Letteraria di Milano, and he founded the journal Archivio Glottologico Italiano.

nodes.id: I:Morphologische Untersuchungen auf dem Gebiete der indogermanischen Sprachen
nodes.label: Morphologische Untersuchungen auf dem Gebiete der indogermanischen Sprachen
variants: Morphologische Untersuchungen auf dem Gebiete der indogermanischen Sprachen

nodes.label: Hermann Osthoff
nodes.jawiki: ヘルマン・オストホフ
nodes.summary: Hermann Osthoff (1847–1909) worked in linguistics and Indology. He held academic posts at Leipzig University (~1875–1877) and Heidelberg University (~1877–1909), and founded the publication Morphologische Untersuchungen auf dem Gebiete der indogermanischen Sprachen.

nodes.label: Pietro Merlo
nodes.summary: Pietro Merlo was a linguist who studied at the University of Turin under Giovanni Flechia (~1869–1873). He later held a position at the University of Pavia (~1881–1888).

nodes.label: Michele Kerbaker
nodes.summary: Michele Kerbaker (1835–1914) worked in Indology and linguistics. He succeeded Giacomo Lignana in 1870 and held a post at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" from circa 1872 to 1907.

nodes.label: Giuseppe Bardelli
nodes.summary: Giuseppe Bardelli (1815–1865) was an Italian scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied under Giuseppe Caspar Mezzofanti, Eugène Burnouf, and Stanislas Julien, and served as Dozent for Coptic and Sanskrit at the University of Pisa (~1845–1859).

nodes.label: Giuseppe Caspar Mezzofanti
nodes.jawiki: ジュゼッペ・ガスパロ・メゾファンティ
nodes.summary: Giuseppe Caspar Mezzofanti (1774–1849) was an Italian linguist. He studied at the University of Bologna (~1786–1797) and subsequently held an academic post there from around 1797 to 1831, teaching Giuseppe Bardelli.

nodes.label: Fausto Gherardo Fumi
nodes.summary: Fausto Gherardo Fumi was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at the Scuola Normale Superiore's Classe di Lettere e Filosofia under Giuseppe Bardelli from approximately 1858 to 1862.

nodes.label: Carlo Giussani
nodes.summary: Carlo Giussani was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at the Scuola Normale Superiore (~1859–1863) under Giuseppe Bardelli, and later studied under Albrecht Weber (1863) and Rudolf von Roth (~1864–1865).

nodes.label: Francisco García Ayuso
nodes.image: 1897-05-30, La Ilustración Española y Americana, Francisco García Ayuso (cropped).jpg
nodes.summary: Francisco García Ayuso was a scholar in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich under Martin Haug between circa 1868 and 1871.

nodes.label: Ivan Minayev
nodes.summary: Ivan Minayev was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Saint Petersburg State University and under Albrecht Weber. He served as professor at Saint Petersburg State University (circa 1871–1890) and taught Sergey Oldenburg and Fyodor Shcherbatskoy.

nodes.label: Garcin de Tassy
variants: Joseph Héliodore Sagesse Vertu Garcin de Tassy
nodes.dewiki: Joseph Héliodore Sagesse Vertu Garcin de Tassy
nodes.summary: Garcin de Tassy (1794–1878) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Lycée Thiers and under Jean-Daniel Kieffer (~1817–1820). He served as Professor of Hindustani at INALCO and taught at the École nationale des langues orientales vivantes (~1828–1878).

nodes.label: Philippe-Édouard Foucaux
nodes.jawiki: フィリップ・エドゥアール・フーコー
nodes.summary: Philippe-Édouard Foucaux was a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies who studied under Eugène Burnouf. He served as Professor of Tibetan at INALCO from 1854 and Professor of Sanskrit at the Collège de France from 1857 to 1894.

nodes.label: Léon Feer
nodes.summary: Léon Feer was an Indologist and Tibetologist who studied under Philippe-Édouard Foucaux. He held posts at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales (1865), the Collège de France (1869–1872), and the Bibliothèque nationale de France (1872).

nodes.label: Michel Bréal
nodes.summary: Michel Bréal (1832–1915) was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at École Normale Supérieure, and under Franz Bopp and Albrecht Weber. He served as Professor at Collège de France (1866–1905) and Director at École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1868–1882).

nodes.label: Hermann Wilhelm Ebel
nodes.summary: Hermann Wilhelm Ebel (1820–1875) was a linguist who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1836–1838) and the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1838–1842) under August Friedrich Pott. He later held a post at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1872–1875).

nodes.label: Ernst Wilhelm Förstemann
nodes.jawiki: エルンスト・フェルステマン

nodes.label: Otto Blau
nodes.summary: Otto Blau worked in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Halle-Wittenberg under August Friedrich Pott from circa 1848 to 1851.

nodes.label: József Budenz
nodes.summary: Specializing in linguistics, József Budenz studied under Theodor Benfey at the University of Göttingen (~1855–1858). He later held a post at Eötvös Loránd University from circa 1872 to 1892.

nodes.label: August Fick
nodes.jawiki: アウグスト・フィック
nodes.summary: August Fick was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at the University of Göttingen under Theodor Benfey (~1852–1856). He held academic posts at the University of Göttingen (~1869–1887) and the University of Breslau (1888–1891).

nodes.label: Ferdinand Justi
nodes.summary: Ferdinand Justi specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at the University of Marburg (~1854–1856) and under Theodor Benfey (~1856–1859), later serving on the faculty at the University of Marburg (~1865–1907).

nodes.label: Ludwig Lange
nodes.summary: Ludwig Lange was a scholar of linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at Leipzig University and the University of Göttingen (~1843–1847) under Theodor Benfey, later holding posts at Göttingen, Charles University, the University of Giessen, and Leipzig University (~1871–1885).

nodes.label: Theodor Nöldeke
nodes.jawiki: テオドール・ネルデケ
nodes.summary: Theodor Nöldeke was a linguist and scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Göttingen under Theodor Benfey, Vienna, Berlin, and Leiden, and held academic posts at the University of Göttingen (~1861–1864) and the University of Kiel (~1864–1872).

nodes.label: John Peile
nodes.summary: John Peile was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at St. Bees School, Repton School, and Christ's College, Cambridge (~1856–1860), and later studied under Theodor Benfey (~1869–1870).

nodes.label: Émile Senart
nodes.summary: Émile Senart was an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and historian/archaeologist who studied under Theodor Benfey (~1867–1868). He served as president of the Société Asiatique from 1908 to 1928.

nodes.label: Carl Siegfried
nodes.summary: Carl Siegfried worked in Indology and religious studies, studying at Halle-Wittenberg (~1849–1852) and Bonn (~1852–1853) under Rudolf von Roth and Albrecht Weber (1849). He held posts at Schulpforta (~1865–1875), Jena (~1875–1903), and Trinity College Dublin as Professor des Sanskrit.

nodes.label: Julius Euting
nodes.summary: Julius Euting specialized in linguistics and history and archaeology. He studied at Eberhard-Ludwigs-Gymnasium, the Seminaries of Maulbronn and Blaubeuren, and Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth. He held posts at the BNU de Strasbourg (~1871–1909) and the University of Strasbourg (~1880–1912).

nodes.label: Matthias von Lexer
nodes.summary: Matthias von Lexer (1830–1892) was a linguist who studied under Albrecht Weber. He held posts at the University of Freiburg (circa 1864–1868), University of Würzburg (circa 1868–1874), and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (circa 1874–1892).

nodes.label: Sophus Bugge
nodes.summary: Sophus Bugge was a linguist who studied under Albrecht Weber in 1858. He held an academic post at Uppsala University and taught Sten Konow.

nodes.label: Angelo De Gubernatis
nodes.summary: Angelo De Gubernatis (1840–1913) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Turin and Humboldt University of Berlin under Albrecht Weber. He held professorships at the University of Florence (1863–1891) and Sapienza University of Rome (1890).

nodes.label: Henri Gaidoz
nodes.summary: Henri Gaidoz was a scholar in linguistics and religious studies. He studied at Lycée Louis-le-Grand and under Albrecht Weber in 1865.

nodes.label: Ramkrishna Gopal Bhandarkar
nodes.summary: Ramkrishna Gopal Bhandarkar (1837–1925) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Martin Haug and at Elphinstone College, University of Mumbai, and University of Göttingen. He was a professor at Deccan College (~1882–1893) and Elphinstone College (attested 1907).

nodes.label: Heinrich Hübschmann
nodes.summary: Heinrich Hübschmann (1848–1908) was a scholar of linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Jena (~1868–1872) and under Martin Haug (~1871–1872), later holding a post at Leipzig University (~1876–1877).

nodes.label: Julius Jolly
nodes.summary: Julius Jolly was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Berlin under Albrecht Weber and also under Martin Haug. From 1872 to 1923, he held posts at the University of Würzburg, becoming Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology in 1886.

nodes.label: University of Florence
variants: Istituto dei Studi Superiori in Florenz

nodes.label: Sapienza University of Rome
variants: Università degli Studi di Roma "La Sapienza"

nodes.label: James Burgess
nodes.summary: James Burgess (1832–1916) worked in Indology and history and archaeology. He founded The Indian Antiquary (1872) and Epigraphia Indica (1892), succeeded Alexander Cunningham in 1885, and served multiple times as head of the Archaeological Survey of India.

nodes.label: Robert Caesar Childers
nodes.summary: Robert Caesar Childers was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at Wadham College and under Yataramulle Dhammarama, later serving as Professor of Pali and Buddhist Literature at University College London and University of London (~1872–1876).

nodes.label: Augustus Frederic Rudolf Hoernle
nodes.summary: Augustus Frederic Rudolf Hoernle worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He served as director of Aliah University (~1881–1899) and was secretary of the Asiatic Society in 1891.

nodes.label: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar
nodes.description: Philosopher, academic, writer, translator, entrepreneur, social reformer and philanthropist (1820-1891)
nodes.summary: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Sanskrit Collegiate School and Sanskrit College and University, where he later served as Direttore from around 1851 to 1858.

nodes.label: Austrian Academy of Sciences
variants: kaiserl. Akademie der Wissenschaften in Wien
オーストリア科学アカデミー
Austrian Academy of Sciences in Vienna

Institute of Social Anthropology, Austrian Academy of Sciences
