variants: Mission an der Küste von Malabar

nodes.label: Thomas William Rhys Davids
nodes.jawiki: トーマス・ウィリアム・リス・デイヴィッズ
nodes.description: British scholar of the Pāli language (1843–1922)
nodes.summary: Thomas William Rhys Davids (1843–1922) worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied under Waskaduwe Subhuti, Yataramulle Dhammarama, and Adolf Friedrich Stenzler at the University of Breslau, later holding posts at UCL and the University of Manchester.

nodes.label: Marcel Mauss
nodes.summary: Marcel Mauss was a scholar of religious studies and other fields who studied at the University of Bordeaux (~1890–1895). He held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1900–1940) and the Collège de France (1931–1942).

nodes.label: Wilhelm Grube
nodes.jawiki: ヴィルヘルム・グルーベ
nodes.summary: Wilhelm Grube worked in sinology and linguistics, studying under Vasily Vasiliev and Georg von der Gabelentz, and at Leipzig University. He held an extraordinary professorship at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1892–1908).

nodes.label: Karl Florenz
nodes.jawiki: カール・フローレンツ
nodes.summary: Karl Florenz specialized in Japanology, Indology, and linguistics. He held posts as professor at the University of Tokyo from around 1889 to 1914 and at the University of Hamburg from around 1914 to 1934.

nodes.label: Fitzedward Hall
nodes.summary: Fitzedward Hall was an Indologist who studied at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute (~1840–1842) and Harvard University (~1842–1846). He later held a post at King's College London from circa 1862 to 1869.

nodes.label: Arthur Berriedale Keith
nodes.summary: Arthur Berriedale Keith was a Scottish Indologist and linguist who studied at Edinburgh and Balliol College, Oxford, under A. A. Macdonell. He worked at the Colonial Office (~1901–1914) before serving as Regius Professor at Edinburgh (~1914–1944).

nodes.label: Junjirō Takakusu
nodes.description: Japanese Buddhist studies scholar and Indologist
nodes.summary: Junjirō Takakusu was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku, Tokyo, and Oxford, learning under Max Müller, Winternitz, and Lévi. He held posts at Tokyo, Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, Osaka University of Foreign Studies, and Toyo University.

nodes.label: Otto Stein
nodes.summary: Otto Stein was an Indology scholar who studied at the philosophy faculty of the German University of Prague from circa 1913 to 1921 under Moriz Winternitz.

nodes.label: J. Estlin Carpenter
nodes.summary: J. Estlin Carpenter was a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied at the University of London from circa 1860 to 1866. He later held an academic post at the University of Oxford from circa 1886 to 1915.

nodes.label: Robert Chalmers
nodes.description: British civil servant, and Pali and Buddhist scholar (1858-1938)
nodes.summary: Robert Chalmers was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at Oriel College (~1877–1881) and served as Master of Peterhouse, Cambridge (~1924–1931).

nodes.label: Richard Morris
nodes.summary: Richard Morris was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at Battersea Training College (~1852–1854) and held posts at King's College School (~1869–1890) and the Royal Masonic School for Boys (1875).

nodes.label: Edmund Hardy
nodes.summary: Edmund Hardy worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, studying at Heidelberg (~1872–1875) and Humboldt University of Berlin. He was Professor of Philosophy at Freiburg (1885–1893) and professor of Indian languages and comparative religions at Fribourg (~1893–1898).

nodes.label: Dines Andersen
nodes.summary: Dines Andersen was a Danish scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Copenhagen (~1879-1892) under Vilhelm Thomsen, Karl Verner, and Michael Viggo Fausbøll, later serving there as professor of Indian philology (1903-1927).

nodes.label: W. H. D. Rouse
nodes.summary: W. H. D. Rouse was a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. He completed his education at Cheltenham College and Christ's College, Cambridge around 1882 to 1886.

nodes.label: Caroline A. F. Rhys Davids
variants: C. A. F. リス・デヴィッズ
nodes.summary: Caroline A. F. Rhys Davids worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. She studied at University College London and under Thomas William Rhys Davids, lectured at the University of Manchester and SOAS, and served as President of the Pali Text Society (~1923–1942).

nodes.label: Sylvain Lévi
nodes.summary: Sylvain Lévi specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at Lycée Charlemagne and EPHE, he held chairs at the University of Paris, EPHE, Collège de France, and Maison Franco-Japonaise.

nodes.label: Louis de La Vallée Poussin
variants: ラ・ヴァレー・プーサン
L・ドゥ・ラ・ヴァレー・プーサン
nodes.summary: Louis de La Vallée Poussin was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Charles de Harlez, Philippe Colinet, Victor Henry, Sylvain Lévi, and Hendrik Kern, later holding professorships at Ghent University (1894–1929) and Free University of Brussels (~1921–1938).

nodes.label: Godefroy de Blonay
nodes.description: Swiss linguist and member of the International Olympic Committee (1869-1937)

nodes.label: Henry Clarke Warren
nodes.summary: Henry Clarke Warren was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who founded the Harvard Oriental Series. He earned his B.A. at Harvard University (~1875–1879) and studied under Charles Rockwell Lanman at Johns Hopkins University in 1879.

nodes.label: Vincent Arthur Smith
nodes.image: The Early History of India by Vincent Arthur Smith.jpg
nodes.summary: Vincent Arthur Smith worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1871–1900) and later held a post at the University of Oxford (~1910–1920).

nodes.label: Sarat Chandra Das
nodes.image: Sarat Chandra Das, C.I.E. photo from Journey to Lhasa and Central Tibet (page 10 crop).jpg
nodes.jawiki: サラト・チャンドラ・ダス
nodes.description: Indian scholar of Tibetan language and culture (1849-1917)
nodes.summary: Sarat Chandra Das (1849–1917) was a scholar of Tibetology and Indology. He studied civil engineering at Presidency University, Kolkata, and received instruction from Ugyen Gyatso and Sengchen Lobzang Palden Chöpel.

nodes.label: Cecil Bendall
nodes.summary: Cecil Bendall (1856–1906) was a scholar of indology and buddhist studies who studied at Oxford and Cambridge, under Edward Byles Cowell and Theodor Benfey. He held posts at the British Museum, University College London, and Cambridge, where he was Professor of Sanskrit.

nodes.label: Unrai Wogihara
nodes.summary: Unrai Wogihara (1869–1937) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied under Junjirō Takakusu and with Ernst Leumann at the University of Strasbourg (~1899–1908). He later held posts at the University of Tokyo and Taisho University (~1926–1937).

nodes.label: Vasily Radlov
nodes.jawiki: ヴァシーリー・ラドロフ
nodes.summary: Vasily Radlov (1837–1918) was a linguist specializing in Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1854–1858) and held a post at the Kunstkamera (~1894–1918).

nodes.label: Alexander von Staël-Holstein
nodes.summary: Alexander von Staël-Holstein (1877–1937) was an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and sinologist. Educated at Dorpat, Berlin, Halle-Wittenberg, and Harvard, he held posts at Peking University (c. 1922–1928) and directed the Sino-Indian Institute (c. 1928–1937).

nodes.label: Masaharu Anesaki
nodes.summary: Masaharu Anesaki studied religious and Buddhist studies at the University of Tokyo (~1893-1896), under Friedrich Max Müller (~1900), and at the University of Kiel under Paul Deussen (~1900-1902). He was a professor at the University of Tokyo (1904) and lectured at Collège de France (~1919-1920).

nodes.id: P:G. A. van den Bergh van Eysinga
nodes.label: G. A. van den Bergh van Eysinga
variants: G. A. van den Bergh van Eysinga

nodes.label: Richard Fick
nodes.summary: Richard Fick (1867–1944) was an Indologist. He studied at the University of Kiel from circa 1885 to 1888 and later held a post at the University of Göttingen from circa 1921 to 1932.

nodes.label: University of Kiel
variants: Historisches Seminar, Asiatische Geschichte, Universität Kiel

nodes.label: Richard Schmidt
nodes.summary: Richard Schmidt was an Indologist who studied under Ernst Mehliß and completed his studies at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1888–1893).

nodes.label: Helmer Smith
nodes.summary: Helmer Smith was an Indologist, linguist, and Buddhist studies scholar. He held academic posts at Lund University from ~1921 to 1936 and at Uppsala University from ~1936 to 1947.

nodes.label: Louis Finot
nodes.summary: Louis Finot worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology after studying at the École des chartes (1884–1888). He was the first director of the École française d'Extrême-Orient (~1898–1904) and later held posts at the Collège de France (1920–1935).

nodes.label: Édouard Huber
nodes.summary: Édouard Huber was a scholar of sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology who studied at the University of Paris, INALCO, and the Collège de France (~1899–1901). He held a teaching post in Chinese at the École française d'Extrême-Orient (~1905–1914).

nodes.label: Kaikyoku Watanabe
nodes.summary: Kaikyoku Watanabe was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the University of Strasbourg (~1900–1907). He held posts at Toyo University and Taisho University (~1926–1933).

nodes.label: Max Lindenau
nodes.summary: Max Lindenau was an Indologist who completed his studies under Ernst Windisch at Leipzig University in 1913.

nodes.label: Ludwig Heller
nodes.summary: Ludwig Heller was an Indologist who studied at the University of Göttingen (~1887–1894). He later held a post at the University of Greifswald (~1897–1934).

nodes.label: Hermann Beckh
nodes.summary: Hermann Beckh (1875–1937) worked in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1900–1907) and subsequently held a post there from ~1908 to 1921.

nodes.label: Theodor Bloch
nodes.summary: Theodor Bloch was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Leipzig University (~1890–1892) under Ernst Windisch, and later studied under Georg Bühler (~1893–1895).

nodes.label: Hermann von Schlagintweit
nodes.summary: Hermann von Schlagintweit (1826–1882) worked in history, archaeology, and other fields. He studied at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1846–1849) and held a post at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1852–1854).

nodes.label: Georg Morgenstierne
nodes.dewiki: Georg Valentin von Munthe af Morgenstierne
nodes.jawiki: ゲオルク・モルゲンスティールネ
nodes.summary: Georg Morgenstierne (1892–1978) was a scholar in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Oslo and under Sten Konow, later holding a post at the University of Gothenburg (~1930–1937).

nodes.label: Sten Konow
nodes.summary: Sten Konow worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Richard Pischel, served as Government Epigraphist for India, and held professorships at the University of Oslo, University of Hamburg, and Visva-Bharati University.

nodes.label: Frederick William Thomas
nodes.summary: Frederick William Thomas (1867–1956) was an Indologist and Tibetologist educated at Trinity College, Cambridge. He served as Librarian at the India Office Library (~1903–1927) and Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford (1927–1937).

nodes.label: Tukaram Krishna Laddu
nodes.summary: Tukaram Krishna Laddu was an Indologist and linguist who completed studies at the University of Halle-Wittenberg by 1912. He held a post at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, attested in 1920.

nodes.label: Edward Denison Ross
nodes.image: Edward Denison Ross by John Lavery (1856-1941).jpg
nodes.jawiki: エドワード・デニソン・ロス
nodes.summary: Edward Denison Ross worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Tibetology, and history and archaeology. Educated at University College London (~1887–1891), he held posts there (~1896–1901), at the British Museum (1914), and served as head of SOAS (~1916–1937).

nodes.label: Satischandra Vidyabhusana
nodes.summary: Satischandra Vidyabhusana (1870–1920) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied under Sarat Chandra Das and earned a PhD from the University of Calcutta. He was Principal of Sanskrit College and held posts at Presidency University.

nodes.label: Ganganatha Jha
nodes.summary: Ganganatha Jha (1872–1941) was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Calcutta, Allahabad, and Sampurnanand Sanskrit universities. He worked at Darbhanga Raj Library (1893–1902), Muir Central College (1902), and served as Allahabad University's Vice-Chancellor (attested 1937–1939).

nodes.label: Edward Washburn Hopkins
nodes.summary: Edward Washburn Hopkins was an Indology, linguistics, and religious studies scholar. He studied at Columbia and Leipzig under Ernst Windisch and Albrecht Weber. He held professorships at Bryn Mawr College (1885–1895) and Yale University (1895–1926).

nodes.label: Arthur Coke Burnell
nodes.summary: Arthur Coke Burnell was an Indologist and linguist. Educated at Bedford School and King's College London (~1857–1860), he worked as an officer in the Indian Civil Service between circa 1860 and 1880.

nodes.label: Peter von Bradke
nodes.summary: Peter von Bradke was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at the Imperial University of Dorpat, University of Tübingen, Leipzig University, and University of Giessen, studying under Rudolf von Roth and Leo Meyer. He held a post at Giessen from 1886 to 1896.

nodes.label: Prafulla Chandra Ray
nodes.jawiki: プラフラ・チャンドラ・レイ
nodes.description: Bengali chemist, educationist, poet, historian, industrialist and philanthropist (1861–1944)
nodes.summary: Prafulla Chandra Ray worked in history and archaeology and Indology. Educated at Vidyasagar College, Presidency University, and the University of Edinburgh (~1882–1888), he held posts at Presidency University (1911–1916) and University College of Science, Technology & Agriculture (1916–1936).

nodes.label: George Melville Bolling
nodes.summary: George Melville Bolling worked in Indology and linguistics. After studying at Loyola University Maryland (~1887–1891) and Johns Hopkins University (~1891–1896), he held posts at Catholic University of America (1895–1913), Johns Hopkins (1913–1914), and Ohio State University (1914–1939).

nodes.label: Bapu Deva Sastri
nodes.description: Indian scholar in Sanskrit and mathematics and translator

nodes.label: Arthur Anthony Macdonell
nodes.jawiki: アーサー・アンソニー・マクドネル
nodes.summary: Arthur Anthony Macdonell was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Göttingen, Oxford, and Leipzig. He served as Deputy Professor and then Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford (1899), as well as a Fellow of Balliol College (~1899–1926).

nodes.label: LeRoy Carr Barret
nodes.summary: LeRoy Carr Barret was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He completed his studies at Washington and Lee University (ca. 1894–1898) and at Johns Hopkins University (ca. 1899–1903), where he studied under Maurice Bloomfield.

nodes.label: Franklin Edgerton
variants: フランクリン・エジャトン
nodes.jawiki: フランクリン・エジャートン
nodes.summary: Franklin Edgerton was an Indologist and linguist. After studying at Cornell, Munich, Jena, and Johns Hopkins (PhD under Maurice Bloomfield), he served as professor at the University of Pennsylvania (1913–1926) and Salisbury Professor at Yale University (1926, 1946).

nodes.label: Bernhard Geiger
nodes.summary: Bernhard Geiger specialized in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. Educated at the University of Vienna (~1900–1904), he held posts at Vienna (~1909–1938), the Tibetan-Iranian Institute (1938–1951), and Columbia University (~1947–1956).

nodes.label: Willibald Kirfel
nodes.summary: Willibald Kirfel (1885–1964) was an Indologist who studied under Hermann Jacobi at the University of Bonn from ~1904 to 1908. He succeeded Jacobi and served as librarian and Privatdozent at Bonn in 1920.

nodes.label: Alfons Fürst
nodes.summary: Alfons Fürst (born 1961) is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Tübingen from around 1982 to 1988 and held a post at the University of Münster around 2006.

nodes.label: Robert Zimmermann
nodes.summary: Robert Zimmermann (1874–1931) was an Indologist who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1907–1913). He held an academic post at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai, from around 1914 to 1930.

nodes.label: Leiden University
variants: Leiden University, Department of Indo-European Comparative Linguistics (VIET)
Kern Institute, Leiden University, the Netherlands
Kern Institute of Indology, Leiden University

nodes.label: Heinrich Lüders
nodes.jawiki: ハインリヒ・リューダース
nodes.summary: Heinrich Lüders (1869–1943) was an Indologist, linguist, and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at Göttingen under Franz Kielhorn. He held posts at Göttingen, Rostock, Kiel, and became Ordinarius für indische Philologie at Berlin in 1909.

nodes.label: Edward Joseph Thomas
nodes.summary: Edward Joseph Thomas worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of St Andrews, held a post at Cambridge University Library (~1909–1939), and was attested as a professor at the University of Cambridge in 1946.

nodes.label: Pe Maung Tin
nodes.native: ဖေမောင်တင်
nodes.summary: Pe Maung Tin was a scholar of Buddhist studies, linguistics, and Indology. He studied at the University of Yangon (~1904–1909) and the University of Calcutta (~1909–1911), later serving as Professor of Pali at the University of Yangon (~1912–1946).

nodes.label: Benimadhab Barua
nodes.description: Bengali Writer, Indologist, and pundit of Pali and Buddhism (1888-1948)
nodes.summary: Benimadhab Barua was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. After studying at several institutions, including the University of Calcutta (~1911–1913) and the University of London (~1914–1917), he held a post at the University of Calcutta from 1918 to 1948.

nodes.label: Hakuju Ui
nodes.image: Recent portrait of Dr. Hakuju Ui.jpg
nodes.summary: Hakuju Ui was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied under Junjirō Takakusu at the University of Tokyo and Richard von Garbe at Tübingen, later holding posts at Tokyo, Tohoku, Waseda, Komazawa, and Nagoya universities.

nodes.label: Theodore Stcherbatsky
nodes.summary: Theodore Stcherbatsky (1866–1942) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied under Ivan Pavlovich Minaev, Georg Bühler, and Hermann Jacobi. An attested member of the Russian Academy of Sciences in 1931, he taught numerous scholars.

nodes.label: Chimanlal Dahyabhai Dalal
nodes.description: Sanskrit scholar and librarian of the Central Library in Baroda

nodes.label: Ramesh Chandra Majumdar
nodes.summary: Ramesh Chandra Majumdar was an Indian historian and Indologist who studied at institutions including Ravenshaw, Presidency, and Calcutta universities. He held posts at the University of Calcutta (~1914–1921), the University of Chicago (~1958), and chaired the History of Bengal Publication Committee.

nodes.label: A. B. Gajendragadkar
nodes.summary: A. B. Gajendragadkar was an Indologist who served as a Senior Dakshina Fellow at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute and as a Lecturer on Sanskrit at Karnatak Arts College, Dharwad.

nodes.label: S. Kuppuswami Sastri
nodes.summary: S. Kuppuswami Sastri was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He was a professor at Presidency University, Kolkata, Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology at Presidency College, Chennai (~1914–1935), and later Dean and Honorary Professor at Annamalai University (~1935–1943).

nodes.label: Richard Jay Kohn
nodes.summary: Richard Jay Kohn was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1988, studying under Geshe Lhundub Sopa and Lama Tharchin Rinpoche.

nodes.label: University of Wisconsin-Madison
variants: Memorial Library at the University of Wisconsin
Buddhist studies department at the University of Wisconsin

nodes.label: Geshe Lhundub Sopa
nodes.death_place: Deer Park Buddhist Center and Monastery
nodes.summary: Geshe Lhundub Sopa (1923–2014) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Ganden Chokhor and Sera Jey monasteries under Lhundrub Thabkhe, Geshe Ngawang Rigsal, Geshe Ngawang Gendun, and Lhundrub Tsöndrü, later serving as a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison.

nodes.label: Dor Bahadur Bista
nodes.summary: Dor Bahadur Bista is a scholar in Tibetology and other fields. He studied at Tri Chandra College (~1950–1954) and served as a professor at Tribhuvan University (~1972–1990).

nodes.label: Tribhuvan University
variants: Centre for Nepal and Asian Studies of Tribhuvan University

nodes.label: Bruce McCoy Owens
nodes.summary: Bruce McCoy Owens works in religious studies and Indology. He held posts at Columbia University (attested 1988) and at Wheaton College as associate professor of anthropology (attested 2019).

nodes.label: Columbia University
variants: コロンビア大学大学院
Center for Buddhist Studies, Columbia University
Italian Academy for Advanced Studies in America at Columbia University

nodes.label: Christoph von Fürer-Haimendorf
nodes.summary: Christoph von Fürer-Haimendorf was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He held the Chair of Asian Anthropology at the University of London from circa 1951 to 1976 and was attested as a professor at SOAS in 1988.

nodes.label: David L. Snellgrove
nodes.summary: David L. Snellgrove was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Southampton, Queens' College, Cambridge, and under figures including Harold Walter Bailey and Walter Simon. He spent his career at the University of London and SOAS (~1950–1982).

nodes.label: Tadeusz Skorupski
nodes.summary: Tadeusz Skorupski specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. After earning his Ph.D. from the University of London in 1978, he held posts at SOAS University of London as professor (attested 1987–1996) and reader (attested 2005).

nodes.label: Michael Oppitz
nodes.summary: Michael Oppitz (born 1942) works in history, archaeology, and Tibetology. He held posts at the Wissenschaftskolleg zu Berlin (~1987–1988) and the University of Zurich (~1991–2008).

nodes.label: Mark Tatz
nodes.summary: Mark Tatz specialized in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of British Columbia under Leon Hurvitz, studied under traditional teachers including Tenzin Dragpa Chokyi Gyaltsen, and was a professor at CIIS (attested 1988).

nodes.label: Komazawa University
variants: 駒沢大学仏教学部仏教学科

nodes.label: Kazuo Hyodo
nodes.summary: Kazuo Hyodo (born 1948) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University and Otani University under Hajime Sakurabe. He served as an assistant professor at Otani University (~1983–2014) and served on the Otani Society committee.

nodes.label: Junsho Kato
nodes.summary: A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, Junsho Kato studied at KU Leuven, under Étienne Lamotte, Akira Hirakawa, and Hajime Nakamura, and earned a PhD from the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Nishogakusha University and Nagoya University.

nodes.label: Toyo Bunko
variants: 東洋文庫チベット研究室

nodes.label: Nobuyoshi Yamabe
nodes.summary: Nobuyoshi Yamabe is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Otani, Osaka, and Yale universities. He held positions at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College, Tokyo University of Agriculture, and Waseda University.

nodes.label: Shudo Ishii
nodes.summary: Shudo Ishii (born 1943) is a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar. He earned his BA at Komazawa University (~1961–1965), where he studied under Shigeo Kamata (~1961–1966), and later served as professor at Komazawa University (attested 1988–2016).

nodes.label: Noriaki Hakamaya
nodes.summary: Noriaki Hakamaya is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo. He taught primarily at Komazawa University and Komazawa Junior College, and visited the University of Wisconsin-Madison.

nodes.label: Stanley Weinstein
variants: スタンリー・ワインスタイン
nodes.jawiki: スタンリー・ワインスタイン
nodes.summary: Stanley Weinstein was a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and japanology who studied at Harvard University. He was a professor at the University of London (circa 1962–1968) and later served as emeritus professor at Yale University.

nodes.label: Jikido Takasaki
nodes.summary: Jikido Takasaki (1926–2013) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned PhDs from Savitribai Phule Pune University and the University of Tokyo, later serving as professor at Tokyo (1977–1987) and president of Tsurumi University (1992–2004).

nodes.label: Waseda University
variants: 早稲田大学大学院文学研究科
早稲田大学文学学術院

早稲田大学アジア太平洋研究センター
早稲田大学感性文化研究所

nodes.label: Kotatsu Fujita
nodes.summary: Kotatsu Fujita was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and Harvard. He taught at Hokkaido University (~1968–1991) and served as head of Sapporo Otani Junior College (~1991–1995).

nodes.label: Eshō Mikogami

nodes.label: Taiken Kimura

nodes.label: Ryugen Tanemura

nodes.label: Toru Tomabechi
nodes.summary: Toru Tomabechi is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University and the University of Lausanne, where he was an assistant in 1998, later holding senior researcher posts at two humanities institutes.

variants: ディヴァーカル・アーチャーリヤ

nodes.label: Matthew T. Kapstein
nodes.summary: Matthew T. Kapstein is a Tibetologist and philosopher who earned his PhD from Brown University. He held positions at the University of Chicago, Columbia University, and served as Director of Tibetan Religious Studies at the École Pratique des Hautes Études.

nodes.label: Birgit Kellner
nodes.summary: Birgit Kellner is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. She earned her doctorate at Hiroshima University under Shoryu Katsura, and has held posts at the University of Vienna and the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.

nodes.label: Susanne Mrozik
nodes.summary: Susanne Mrozik works in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned an M.T.S. at Harvard University, studying with Diana L. Eck, Stephanie W. Jamison, Margaret R. Miles, and doctoral supervisor Charles Hallisey. She held posts at Western Michigan University (attested 2002) and Mount Holyoke College (attested 2009).

nodes.label: Western Michigan University
variants: Department of Art, Western Michigan University, Kalamazoo

nodes.label: A. Charles Muller
nodes.jawiki: アルバート・チャールズ・ミュラー
nodes.summary: A scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology, Muller earned his PhD at Stony Brook University (1988) and studied at the University of Virginia (~1989–1993). He was a professor at Toyo Gakuen University (~1997–2008) and the University of Tokyo (~2008–2019).

nodes.label: Jan Nattier
nodes.summary: Jan Nattier studied at Indiana University and Harvard University, specializing in Buddhist studies, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Sinology. She held professorships at Macalester College, the University of Hawaii, Indiana University, Soka University, and Stanford University.

nodes.label: Indiana University
variants: Department of Central Eurasian Studies at Indiana University
Inner Asian and Uralic National Resource Center

nodes.label: University of Manchester
variants: マンチェスターのヴィクトリア大学

nodes.label: Walter Slaje
nodes.summary: Walter Slaje is an Indologist who studied at the University of Vienna from around 1974 to 1979. He served as a professor at the University of Halle-Wittenberg from circa 1999 to 2020.

nodes.label: Roland Steiner
nodes.summary: Roland Steiner is a scholar of Indology and Tibetology. He studied under Michael Hahn (attested 1990) and held an assistant professor post at the University of Marburg (attested 2002).

nodes.label: Dominik Wujastyk
nodes.summary: Dominik Wujastyk works in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of London and Oxford. His posts include the Wellcome Institute (~1984–2002), UCL (2002–2009), University of Vienna (2009–2015), and University of Alberta (2015).

nodes.label: Ute Hüsken
nodes.summary: Ute Hüsken (born 1965) is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies scholar. She completed her dissertation under Heinz Bechert at the University of Göttingen (~1988–1995) and held a post at Heidelberg University (~2003–2008).

nodes.label: Heinz Bechert
nodes.jawiki: ハインツ・ベッヘルト
nodes.summary: Heinz Bechert (1932–2005) was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Saarland University (~1956–1964), served as Director at the University of Göttingen (~1965–2000), and was a series editor at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences (~1973–2005).

nodes.label: Museum für Asiatische Kunst
variants: Museum für Indische Kunst der Staatlichen Museen zu Berlin - Preußischer Kulturbesitz
Museum für Indische Kunst der Staatlichen Museen zu Berlin – Preußischer Kulturbesitz
Museum für Indische Kunst in Berlin

nodes.label: Jeffrey Samuels
nodes.summary: Jeffrey Samuels specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under W. S. Karunatillake and earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under Karen C. Lang. In 2013, he was Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Western Kentucky University.

nodes.label: Karen C. Lang
nodes.summary: Karen C. Lang specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. She studied at Banaras Hindu University, the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives, and the University of Washington under David Seyfort Ruegg, later serving as professor at the University of Virginia.

nodes.label: W. S. Karunatillake
nodes.summary: W. S. Karunatillake worked in linguistics, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He served as a professor at the University of Kelaniya (attested 1997) and was Visiting Numata Professor of Buddhist Studies at Harvard University in 1998.

nodes.label: Kenyu Mitomo
nodes.summary: Kenyu Mitomo is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University and UC Berkeley under Akira Hirakawa and others. He held multiple leadership and professorial roles at Rissho University between ~1974 and 2016.

nodes.label: Minonori Nishimura
nodes.summary: Minonori Nishimura specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a PhD from Taisho University (~1971–1976) studying under Shunkyo Katsumata and Seiren Matsunami, served on its faculty (~1993–2018), and was a researcher at Sanko Research Institute (attested 2002).

nodes.label: Shunkyo Katsumata
nodes.summary: Shunkyo Katsumata (1909–1994) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1932–1935). He held a post at Toyo University and served at Taisho University (~1949–1986), where he became emeritus professor.

nodes.label: Koun Kajiyoshi
nodes.summary: Koun Kajiyoshi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and held a post at Taisho University from circa 1952 to 1974.

nodes.label: Shindai Sekiguchi
nodes.summary: Shindai Sekiguchi (1907–1986) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University (~1928–1933). He later held professorships at Hanazono University and Taisho University (~1957–1978).

nodes.label: Seiren Matsunami
nodes.summary: Seiren Matsunami specialized in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji (~1927–1930) and under Walther Schubring (~1936–1938). He held posts at Kyushu University (~1950–1966), Rissho University (~1966–1974), and Taisho University (attested 1972).

nodes.label: Yasuhiko Nagano
nodes.summary: Yasuhiko Nagano (born 1946) is a Tibetologist and linguist who studied at UC Berkeley (~1974–1978). He held posts at the Graduate University for Advanced Studies (~1998–2011) and the National Museum of Ethnology, becoming professor emeritus in ~2011.

nodes.label: Soshu Nishioka
nodes.summary: Soshu Nishioka is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as a professor at Shitennoji University, attested in 2000 and 2015.

nodes.label: Satoru Harada
nodes.summary: Satoru Harada (b. 1947) works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies and earned an MA from the University of Tokyo. He held posts at the Toyo Bunko, the Eastern Institute, and as a professor at Kokushikan University.

nodes.label: Hajime Kitamura
nodes.summary: Hajime Kitamura (1923–2003) was a linguist and Tibetologist who studied at the University of Tokyo under Tokan Tada. He held posts at NINJAL, the Toyo Bunko, Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, Reitaku University, and the Centre for East Asian Cultural Studies.

nodes.label: Tokan Tada
nodes.summary: Tokan Tada was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Sera Monastery (1913–1923). He later taught at Tohoku University (circa 1931–1945) and held a post at the University of Tokyo (circa 1945–1953).

nodes.id: I:National Institute for Japanese Language and Linguistics
nodes.label: National Institute for Japanese Language and Linguistics
Akira Suganuma
nodes.summary: Akira Suganuma was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at Toyo University (~1959–1962). He spent his career at Toyo University (~1962–2005) as assistant, associate professor, professor, and president (1991–1994).

nodes.label: Kyoshun Todo
nodes.summary: Kyoshun Todo (1916–2002) was a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts at Bukkyo University, where he served as an assistant professor (attested 1962) and as a professor (attested 1988–1992).

nodes.label: Narimoto Tamayama
nodes.summary: Narimoto Tamayama (1916–2004) worked in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He served as a professor at Taisho University, with posts attested in 1974 and 1988.

nodes.label: Xianlin Ji
nodes.description: Chinese academic, linguist, historian, translator and university teacher (1911-2009)
nodes.summary: Xianlin Ji studied at Tsinghua University (1930–1934) and the University of Göttingen (1935–1941), working in Indology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Göttingen (1937) and Peking University, where he became Life Professor in 1980.

nodes.label: Florin Deleanu
variants: デレアヌ フロリン
nodes.jawiki: デレアヌ フロリン
nodes.summary: Florin Deleanu is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Waseda University and the University of Hamburg (PhD under Lambert Schmithausen). His appointments include professorships at Kansai Medical University (~1999–2002) and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~2002).

nodes.label: Zhongxin Jiang
nodes.summary: Zhongxin Jiang was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Peking University under Xianlin Ji (~1960–1965). Jiang held posts at Peking University, the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1980–2002), and Soka University (~1999).

nodes.label: Chinese Academy of Social Sciences
variants: The Chinese Academy of Social Sciences
中国社会科学院哲学研究所
中国社会科学院亜州太平洋研究所
Institute for Chinese Literature of the Academy of Social Sciences in Beijing
Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, Beijing
Academy of Social Sciences in Beijing

nodes.label: Hiroshi Kanno
nodes.summary: Hiroshi Kanno works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1971–1982) and served as director at Soka University (~1987–2023) and the International Research Institute for Advanced Buddhology (~2002–2009).

nodes.label: Noriyuki Kudo
nodes.summary: Noriyuki Kudo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed postgraduate studies at Bukkyo University. He held positions at Bukkyo University, Soka University, and the International Research Institute for Advanced Buddhology.

nodes.label: Akira Yuyama
nodes.summary: Akira Yuyama was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied under Hirakawa, Tsuji, Basham, and de Jong. He served at ANU (1965–1973), directed the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (~1976–1996), and was a professor at Soka University (~1996–2021).

nodes.label: Michael Zimmermann
variants: ミヒャエル・ツィンマーマン
nodes.summary: Michael Zimmermann (born 1966) works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, earning his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen and others. His posts include the Nepal Research Centre (2002), Stanford University (2003), and University of Hamburg Director (attested 2009–2015).

nodes.label: Michihiko Yajima
nodes.summary: Michihiko Yajima (born 1963) is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied as a graduate student at the University of Tokyo (attested 1981) and held posts there (attested 1992) and as a professor at Tsurumi University (attested 2003–2008).

nodes.label: Tsurumi University
variants: 鶴見大学佛教文化研究所
鶴見大学仏教文化研究所

nodes.label: Reimon Yuki
nodes.summary: Reimon Yuki (1902–1992) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1923–1927). He served as professor at the University of Tokyo (~1953–1963) and held posts at Kyoto Women's and Ryukoku universities.

nodes.label: Katsumi Mimaki
nodes.summary: Katsumi Mimaki studied at Kyoto University, INALCO, University of Paris, and Sorbonne Nouvelle University. A scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, he held research and professorial posts at Kyoto University from 1976 to 2011 and taught numerous students.

nodes.label: Masaaki Nohin
nodes.summary: Masaaki Nohin is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Gadjin Nagao. He served as an assistant professor (attested 1999–2003) and professor (attested 2013–2014) at Ryukoku University.

nodes.label: Osamu Hayashima
nodes.summary: Osamu Hayashima (born 1946) specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Having studied under Noritoshi Aramaki and researched at the University of Hamburg, he held professorships at Nagasaki University, Shiga University of Medical Science, and Ryukoku University.

nodes.label: Akifumi Naito
nodes.summary: Akifumi Naito is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University and under Gadjin Nagao. He held posts at the Research Institute of Shin Buddhism, Ryukoku University, Kyoto Women's University, and Gyoshin Buddhist Academy.

nodes.label: Yuhiko Katsuzaki
nodes.description: Japanese bhikku and Buddhist studies scholar
nodes.summary: Yuhiko Katsuzaki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University from around 1964 to 1973. Katsuzaki later served as president (学長) of Taisho University from around 2010 to 2015.

nodes.label: Yoshihiko Sakurai
nodes.summary: Yoshihiko Sakurai specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at Ryukoku University (attested 2001) and later held posts there as a part-time lecturer (attested 2003) and as a researcher at Kyogaku Dendo Kenkyu Senta (attested 2003).

nodes.label: Nobuyuki Kaji
nodes.summary: Nobuyuki Kaji is a scholar of Sinology and philosophy who studied at Kyoto University. He taught at Koshien Junior College, Nagoya University, Osaka University, Koyasan University, Doshisha University, and Ritsumeikan University.

nodes.label: Kosho Kawamura
nodes.summary: Kosho Kawamura is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Toyo University (~1948–1952) under Giyu Nishi, Nichijin Sakamoto, Shunkyo Katsumata, Koshiro Tamaki, and Yoshiro Tamura. He later held several academic posts at Toyo University (~1957–1994).

nodes.label: Kosei Mizutani
nodes.summary: Kosei Mizutani was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University and Bukkyo University (~1948–1952). He served at Bukkyo University as an assistant professor (~1961–1970) and later as president (~1981–1989).

nodes.label: Hiroo Kashiwagi
nodes.summary: Hiroo Kashiwagi works in Buddhist studies. He completed doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo (~1958–1963) and held posts as professor at Matsusaka University (~1982–2000) and president of Matsusaka Women's Junior College (~1988–1996).

nodes.label: Jason Birch
nodes.summary: Jason Birch is an Indologist and scholar of religious studies. He studied at the University of Sydney and the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson and Peter Oldmeadow, later holding research posts at Oxford and SOAS University of London.

nodes.label: Gareth Sparham
nodes.summary: Gareth Sparham (born 1948) works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics and earned his PhD at the University of British Columbia under Ashok Aklujkar (~1984–1989), later teaching at UBC and the University of Michigan.

variants: Centre for Studies of Curriculum and Instruction
Centre of Chinese Research, Institute of Asian Research
Department of Asian Studies at UBC

nodes.label: University of Calgary
variants: Department of Religious Studies, University of Calgary

nodes.label: Padmanabh S. Jaini
nodes.summary: Padmanabh S. Jaini was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He held a professorship at the University of California, Berkeley, where he was attested as professor between 1977 and 2002, and as professor emeritus in 2016.

nodes.label: Hiroshima University
variants: 広島大学大学院文学研究科

広島大学大学院社会科学研究科

nodes.label: Akira Sadakata
nodes.summary: Akira Sadakata is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1955–1959) under Akira Hirakawa and Hajime Nakamura, and at the University of Paris (1963). He served as associate professor and professor at Tokai University (~1971–2007).

nodes.label: Étienne Lamotte
variants: エティエンヌ・ラモット
エティエンヌ・ラモート
nodes.summary: Étienne Lamotte was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied under Louis de La Vallée Poussin, Carlo Formichi, Sylvain Lévi, Alfred Foucher, Paul Demiéville, Marcelle Lalou, and Jean Przyluski, holding major posts at KU Leuven and Université catholique de Louvain.

nodes.label: Hubert Durt
nodes.summary: Hubert Durt specialized in Buddhist studies, having studied under Étienne Lamotte (~1958–1965). He served as editor-in-chief and Professor at EFEO, director of the Hōbōgirin Institute (~1980–2001), and Professor at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~1996–2010).

nodes.label: Mitsuji Fukunaga
nodes.summary: Mitsuji Fukunaga was a sinologist and philosopher who studied at Kyoto University (~1939–1942). He held academic posts at the University of Kitakyushu (~1953–1961), the University of Tokyo (~1961–1970), Kyoto University (~1970–1982), and Kansai University (~1982–1989).

nodes.label: Yoshitaka Iriya
nodes.summary: Yoshitaka Iriya (1910–1998) was a Sinology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1933–1936). He held posts at Nagoya University (~1957–1968), Kyoto University (attested 1967–1969), Kyoto Sangyo University (~1974–1981), and Hanazono University (~1981–1986).

nodes.label: Shinjo Kawasaki
nodes.summary: Shinjo Kawasaki is a Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology scholar who studied at Columbia University and under teachers including Hajime Nakamura. He held posts at the Toyo Bunko, University of Tokyo, University at Buffalo, University of Tsukuba, and Taisho University.

nodes.label: Kangei Okamoto
nodes.summary: Kangei Okamoto (1899–1948) was a Buddhist studies and history/archaeology scholar. He studied at the University of Paris and under Takamatsu Yoshie, and later held a post at the Tokyo National Museum.

nodes.label: Takamatsu Yoshie
nodes.summary: Takamatsu Yoshie studied at Matsumoto Fukashi High School, Tōkyō Senmon Gakkō (~1900-1903), Waseda University, and the University of Paris (~1916-1920). He held a post at Waseda University from ~1906 to 1940.

nodes.label: Satoshi Hiraoka
nodes.summary: Satoshi Hiraoka works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Bukkyo University and the University of Michigan under Shozen Kumoi, Takao Kagawa, and Luis Oscar Gómez. He held posts at Bukkyo University, Kyoto Bunkyo Junior College, and Kyoto Bunkyo University.

nodes.label: Kyoto Bunkyo University
variants: 京都文教大学人間学部
京都文教大学総合社会学部

nodes.label: Yoshifumi Honjo
nodes.summary: Yoshifumi Honjo is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Kyoto University (~1970–1975) under Hajime Sakurabe. His career includes posts at Kyoto University, Kobe Women's University, Bukkyo University, Otani University, and Anshin-in.

nodes.label: Shizuka Sasaki
nodes.summary: Shizuka Sasaki (born 1956) is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1975–1985) under Jikido Takasaki. He served as Professor of Indian Buddhism at Hanazono University from circa 1992 to 2021.

nodes.label: Stephen L. Jenkins
nodes.summary: Stephen L. Jenkins specialized in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Harvard University, supervised by Masatoshi Nagatomi and Charles Hallisey, and served as Professor of Religious Studies at California State Polytechnic University, Humboldt.

nodes.label: Masatoshi Nagatomi
nodes.description: Japanese professor of Buddhist studies at Harvard University
nodes.summary: Masatoshi Nagatomi (1926–2000) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University and Harvard University, where he later served as a professor from circa 1969 to 1996.

nodes.label: Malcolm David Eckel
nodes.summary: Malcolm David Eckel is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned his doctorate at Harvard (~1975–1980) under Masatoshi Nagatomi. He held faculty posts at Harvard (~1980–1990, ~1998–2002) and Boston University (~1990).

nodes.label: Donald S. Lopez Jr.
nodes.summary: Donald S. Lopez Jr. works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, held posts at Middlebury College (~1979–1989), and joined the University of Michigan in 1990.

nodes.label: Charles Hallisey
nodes.summary: Charles Hallisey studied at Colgate, Harvard, UPenn, and the University of Chicago. A religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar, he taught at Loyola University Chicago (circa 1988–1996), Harvard University, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison.

nodes.label: Seiji Kimura
nodes.summary: Seiji Kimura works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Komazawa University (attested 1986), where he also held a post (attested 1990), and later served as a lecturer at Komazawa Junior College (attested 1995).

nodes.label: Ernst Steinkellner
nodes.summary: Ernst Steinkellner specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied under Erich Frauwallner at the University of Vienna (~1955–1963), later serving as a director at the University of Vienna and the Institute for Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.

nodes.label: Helmut Krasser
nodes.summary: Helmut Krasser was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He held posts at the University of Vienna (~1989–2014) and the Austrian Academy of Sciences (~1989–2014), and was director of the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.

nodes.label: Gerhard Oberhammer
variants: G. オーバーハンマー
nodes.summary: Gerhard Oberhammer worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Innsbruck, studied under Erich Frauwallner and V. Raghavan, and held posts at Utrecht University (1961) and the University of Vienna (from 1964).

nodes.label: Keio University
variants: Keio Institute of Cultural & Linguistic Studies (慶應大學言語文化研究所)
Keio Institute of Cultural & Linguistic Studies

nodes.label: Yohei Kawajiri
nodes.summary: Yohei Kawajiri is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He has held positions as a research associate at Chikushi Jogakuen University (attested 2008–2013) and as a JSPS special research fellow (attested 2011).

nodes.label: André Padoux
nodes.summary: André Padoux (1920–2017) was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Paris. He directed the Institut Français Frankfurt (~1959–1964) and held CNRS posts from 1959, becoming Directeur de Recherche in 1982.

nodes.label: Bettina Bäumer
nodes.summary: Bettina Bäumer is an Indology, philosophy, and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Salzburg and under Lakshman Joo. She served as Director of the Alice Boner Institute and Abhinavagupta Research Library, Professor at the University of Vienna, and Fellow at IIAS.

nodes.label: Alexis Sanderson
nodes.summary: Alexis Sanderson (born 1948) is an Indologist and scholar of religious studies and philosophy. After studying at Balliol College and with Lakshman Joo, he held fellowships and posts across Oxford, including Professor and fellow at All Souls College (c. 1992–2015).

nodes.label: Dominic Goodall
nodes.summary: Indologist Dominic Goodall completed his D.Phil. at Oxford (-1995) under Alexis Sanderson and also studied under Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan. He served as a lecturer at EPHE (2005) and held a professorship at the EFEO starting in 2000.

nodes.label: Judit Törzsök
nodes.summary: Judit Törzsök is an Indologist who studied at Eötvös Loránd University and the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. She held posts at the University of Lille (~2001–2017) and became professor at the École Pratique des Hautes Études in 2018.

nodes.label: Alex Watson
nodes.summary: Alex Watson works in Indology and philosophy. Educated at Oxford and SOAS, he completed his doctorate under Alexis Sanderson and Harunaga Isaacson, later holding posts at Wolfson College, Harvard University, and Ashoka University.

nodes.label: Isabelle Ratié
nodes.summary: Isabelle Ratié is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at Paris 1, EPHE, and under Alexis Sanderson. She held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences, Leipzig, University of Paris, Sorbonne Nouvelle (2014–2025), and Collège de France (2025).

nodes.label: University of Lucknow
variants: Abhinavagupta Institute of Aesthetics and Śaiva Philosophy

nodes.label: Kei Kataoka
nodes.summary: Kei Kataoka (born 1969) is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo (PhD 1992–2001 under Hiroshi Marui) and National Sanskrit University (~1999–2001). His posts include Wolfson College, Oxford (1998–1999) and Kyushu University (~2007).

nodes.label: Shigeo Kamata
nodes.summary: Shigeo Kamata (1927–2001) specialized in Buddhist studies and sinology, studying at Komazawa University (~1948–1951) and the University of Tokyo (~1953–1958). He served at Tokyo (~1961–2001; professor ~1972–1988), Aichi Gakuin University, Matsugaoka Bunko, and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Edward Winslow Bastian
nodes.summary: Edward Winslow Bastian works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Banaras Hindu University and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (PhD -1980 under Geshe Lhundub Sopa), also studying under Geshe Lobsang Tenzin, Geshe Lobsang, and Geshe Lobsang Donyo.

ベナレス・ヒンドゥ大学

Department of Dravyaguna, Faculty of Ayurveda, Banaras Hindu University

nodes.label: Samdhong Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Samdhong Rinpoche works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. Educated at Drepung and Gyuto monasteries, he served as principal (~1971–2001) and director (1988) of the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, among other institutional leadership roles.

nodes.label: Geshe Lobsang Tenzin
variants: Gyurme Kensur Rinpoche Geshe Lobsang Tenzin
nodes.summary: Geshe Lobsang Tenzin is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He held an attested post at Sera Monastery in 1980 and served as abbot of Gyume Tantric College as attested in 1987.

nodes.label: Rizong Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Rizong Rinpoche was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Tenzin Gyatso, the 14th Dalai Lama. He served as abbot of Gyume Tantric College from around 1979 to 1985.

nodes.label: Seitatsu Matsunami
nodes.summary: Seitatsu Matsunami is an Indology and Tibetology scholar. He served as an assistant at the University of Tokyo and as a professor at Taisho University (attested 1992).

nodes.label: Norio Koyama
nodes.summary: Norio Koyama is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Shinshu University and under Seitatsu Matsunami. He became a professor at Taisho University circa 2008.

nodes.label: David P. Jackson
nodes.summary: David P. Jackson is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Washington (BA, MA, PhD under David Seyfort Ruegg), he held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences, University of Vienna, and University of Hamburg (~1988–2007).

nodes.label: University of Washington
variants: ワシントン大学文学部東洋学科
Far Eastern and Russian Institute, University of Washington
Inner Asia Research Project, University of Washington, Seattle

nodes.label: John E. Cort
nodes.summary: John E. Cort is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1974–1982) and Harvard University (~1982–1989), and was appointed Professor at Denison University circa 1993.

nodes.label: Paul Dundas
nodes.summary: Paul Dundas (1952–2023) was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. Educated at the University of Edinburgh, he later served as a professor there from circa 1976 until 2017.

nodes.label: Christoph Emmrich
nodes.summary: Christoph Emmrich is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Heidelberg University by 2004 and has held posts at Heidelberg (attested 2001) and the University of Toronto as Assistant Professor.

nodes.label: Shubhachandra
nodes.summary: Shubhachandra is an Indologist who served as a professor at Karnatak University (attested 2001) and held a post in the Department of Jainology and Prakrits at the University of Mysore (attested 2002).

nodes.label: Jayandra Soni
nodes.summary: Jayandra Soni is a scholar in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He earned Ph.D.s from Banaras Hindu University (~1975–1978) and McMaster University (~1982–1987), and served as a lecturer at the University of Marburg (~1991–2012).

nodes.label: Royce Wiles
nodes.summary: Royce Wiles is a scholar of Indology. He earned his PhD by 2000 from the Australian National University, where he also held an academic post.

nodes.label: Derek F. Maher
nodes.summary: Derek F. Maher works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Evergreen State College and the University of Virginia, completing his Ph.D. under Jeffrey Hopkins. He lectured at Virginia and UNC Greensboro, and co-directed the Religious Studies Program at East Carolina University.

nodes.label: Georges Dreyfus
nodes.summary: Georges Dreyfus works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics and the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, later holding posts at the University of Virginia (~1991–1992) and Williams College (~1992).

nodes.label: William Magee
nodes.summary: William Magee specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, held a professorship there around 1992, and later taught at Dharma Drum Buddhist College and Chung-Hwa Institute.

nodes.label: Jules Brooks Levinson
nodes.summary: Jules Brooks Levinson works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, earning his PhD from the University of Virginia in 1994 under Jeffrey Hopkins. He founded the Light of Berotsana Translation Group (1999) and taught at Hamline University (attested 1996).

nodes.label: Richard B. Martin
nodes.summary: Richard B. Martin (1937–2004) was an Indologist and Tibetologist. He worked at the University of Virginia as a professor (attested 1983–1991) and as a South Asian bibliographer (attested 2003).

nodes.label: Charles D. Orzech
nodes.summary: Charles D. Orzech works in religious studies, sinology, and buddhist studies. He completed his dissertation at the University of Chicago, served as chair of Religious Studies at UNC Greensboro (attested 1998–2006), and was a fellow at the National Humanities Center (2009–2010).

nodes.label: Seizan Yanagida
nodes.summary: Seizan Yanagida was a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar. He studied at Hanazono University (~1942–1948) and later held posts at Hanazono University (~1960–1976), Kyoto University (attested 1986–1988), and Chubu University (~1986–1992).

nodes.label: Richard Gombrich
variants: リチャード・F・ゴンブリッチ
nodes.summary: Richard Gombrich (born 1937) is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He earned a D.Phil. at Oxford under Robert Charles Zaehner, having also studied under Gananath Obeyesekere and Walpola Rahula, and served as Boden Professor at Oxford and Balliol College.

nodes.label: Gananath Obeyesekere
nodes.summary: Gananath Obeyesekere (1930–2025) studied at the University of Washington (~1958–1964) in religious and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the University of California, San Diego (~1972–1980) and Princeton University (~1980–2000).

nodes.label: Walpola Rahula
nodes.summary: Walpola Rahula was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ceylon under G. P. Malalasekera, Calcutta, and Paris under Paul Demiéville. He held an academic post at the University of Oxford from circa 1974 to 1977.

nodes.label: Sodo Mori
nodes.summary: Sodo Mori specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1957–1968) and served as professor at Aichi Gakuin University (attested 1993–1997), lecturer at Toyo and Taisho universities, and Pali Text Society representative in Japan (attested 1985).

nodes.label: Norihiko Tanaka
nodes.summary: Norihiko Tanaka is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Osaka Kyoiku University from circa 1964 to 1968. He served as a professor at Bukkyo University from circa 1995 to 2015.

nodes.label: Shunzo Onoda
nodes.summary: Shunzo Onoda is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a D.Lit. from Bukkyo University by 1993 and served there as an associate professor (attested 1996) and later as professor (attested 2005).

nodes.label: Mark L. Blum
nodes.summary: Mark L. Blum works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He held an assistant professorship at the State University of New York (attested 2005) and was an associate professor at the University at Albany, SUNY (attested 2006).

nodes.label: Jushu Nakasone
nodes.summary: A scholar of Buddhist studies, Jushu Nakasone held posts at Bukkyo University as a part-time lecturer (attested 2005) and at Kyoto Bunkyo Junior College (attested 2020).

nodes.label: Toshinori Ochiai
nodes.summary: Toshinori Ochiai is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He held posts as professor at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~1996–2019) and Kacho Junior College, and directed a manuscript research institute.

nodes.label: Daishun Ueyama
nodes.summary: Daishun Ueyama was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Akira Fujieda (~1960–1970). He held posts at Ryukoku University, serving as assistant professor (~1970–1980) and later as president in 1983.

nodes.label: Akira Fujieda
nodes.summary: Akira Fujieda was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1931–1935) and later served as a section head (班長) there from ~1949 to 1974.

nodes.label: Paul B. Donnelly
nodes.summary: Paul B. Donnelly works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. He studied under doctoral supervisor Geshe Lhundub Sopa and traditional teachers Geshe Yeshe Thabkhe and Lobsang Gyatso, and held a post at Northern Arizona University.

nodes.summary: Hōkei Izumi (1884–1947) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Otani University, where he later served as a professor (attested 1930).

nodes.label: Shoshin Fukihara
nodes.summary: Shoshin Fukihara (1907–1975) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Otani University, Horyu-ji, and under Susumu Yamaguchi and Join Saeki, later holding posts at Otani University, Doho University, and Otani University Junior College.

nodes.label: Hoyo Watanabe
nodes.summary: Hoyo Watanabe (born 1933) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (~1952–1960). He spent his career at Rissho University as a professor of Buddhist studies (~1974–2003) and served as dean of the faculty (attested 1984–1985).

nodes.label: Yosho Nomura
nodes.summary: Yosho Nomura (1916–1997) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Rissho University (~1936–1939) and later served there as a professor (~1963–1987) and director (~1981–1987).

nodes.label: Koken Sasaki
nodes.summary: Koken Sasaki (1931–2008) studied Buddhist studies and sinology at Rissho University (~1950–1960). He spent his career at Rissho University as an assistant professor (~1971–1977), department chair (~1977–2001), and director and professor (attested 2000).

nodes.label: Senkei Sakawa
nodes.summary: Senkei Sakawa is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Rissho University until around 1965 and served there as a professor in the Department of Buddhism, attested between 1981 and 1985.

nodes.label: Enshu Kurumiya
nodes.summary: Enshu Kurumiya (b. 1942) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a PhD from the Australian National University in 1974 and served as professor of Buddhist studies at Rissho University (attested 1981–1985).

nodes.label: K. L. Dhammajoti
nodes.summary: K. L. Dhammajoti (born 1949) specializes in Buddhist studies, having studied under Yin Shun and Y. Karunadasa at the University of Kelaniya. He held posts at Kelaniya, the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, and the University of Hong Kong.

nodes.summary: Yin Shun was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Taixu and at Minnan, Wuchang, NTNU, and Taisho University. He held teaching posts at Minnan, Wuchang, Shandao Temple, and NCKU, and served as president of the Hong Kong Buddhist Association.

nodes.label: Shi Huifeng
nodes.summary: Shi Huifeng is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied under K. L. Dhammajoti. He held academic posts at the University of Hong Kong and Fo Guang University, where he was a professor (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Daniel Veidlinger
nodes.summary: Daniel Veidlinger (born 1970) is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under Steven Collins, served as research associate at Chiang Mai University (1999), and held a post at California State University, Chico (2006).

nodes.label: Steven Collins
nodes.summary: Steven Collins specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his D.Phil. at Oxford under Richard Gombrich, Margaret Cone, and Michael Carrithers, later holding posts at Bristol (~1980–1991), Indiana (~1987–1991), and Chicago (1991).

nodes.label: Hideo Mineshima
nodes.summary: Hideo Mineshima (1927–2013) was a philosophy and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University. He held professorships at Waseda University (~1968–1998, attested 1999), Bunkyo Gakuin University, and Sanko Research Institute (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Zenno Ishigami
nodes.summary: Zenno Ishigami worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Taisho University (~1949–1953), where he later served as professor (~1976–2000), and was a researcher at the Sanko Research Institute (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Susumu Otake
nodes.summary: Susumu Otake is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at the University of Tsukuba (~1992–2001) under Makio Takemura. He held part-time lecturer posts at Kyoto University (~2008), Hanazono University (~2008–2013), and Bukkyo University (~2012–2013).

nodes.label: Dan Arnold
nodes.summary: Dan Arnold is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology who studied at Carleton College and the University of Chicago. He has held positions at McGill University, the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, and the University of Chicago (~2003).

nodes.label: Barbara Stoler Miller
nodes.summary: Barbara Stoler Miller was an indologist who studied at Barnard, Columbia, and the University of Pennsylvania (PhD, ~1964-1968) under W. Norman Brown and Royal W. Weiler. She served as Assistant Professor of Oriental Studies at Barnard College (~1968-1993).

nodes.label: Robert A. F. Thurman
nodes.summary: Robert A. F. Thurman is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Harvard University (~1967–1972) and held posts at Amherst College (1973) and Columbia University (1988).

nodes.label: Albrecht Wezler
nodes.summary: Albrecht Wezler was an Indologist who studied at the University of Tübingen under Paul Thieme. He served as Director at the University of Hamburg and Director General of the Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project (1982–2002).

nodes.label: Wilhelm Halbfass
nodes.summary: Wilhelm Halbfass was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He held posts at the University of Göttingen (~1967–1970), the University of Pennsylvania (~1973–2000), the University of Hamburg (1981–1982), and the Wissenschaftskolleg zu Berlin (~1990–1991).

nodes.label: Satoru Noriyama
nodes.summary: Satoru Noriyama works in Buddhist studies and Indology and studied under Eshō Mikogami. He held teaching posts at Osaka University of Foreign Studies (attested 1995) and Ryukoku University (attested 2003 and 2013).

nodes.label: David B. Gray
nodes.summary: David B. Gray specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He earned his Ph.D. at Columbia University under Robert A. F. Thurman and Ryuichi Abe. He was a fellow at Rice University and Associate Professor at Santa Clara University (attested 2008–2017).

nodes.label: Ryuichi Abe
nodes.summary: Ryuichi Abe (born 1954) specializes in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He studied at Keio, SAIS, and Columbia, serving as professor at Columbia (~1996–2005) before becoming Edwin O. Reischauer Institute Professor at Harvard University (~2005).

nodes.label: Gary A. Tubb
nodes.summary: Gary A. Tubb (born 1950) is an Indologist who studied under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He held faculty posts at Harvard University (attested 1999), Columbia University (attested 2007), and the University of Chicago (attested 2011).

nodes.label: Ryushin Uryuzu
nodes.summary: Ryushin Uryuzu (1932–2015) specialized in Buddhist studies. He studied at Ryukoku University (~1951–1958) and held posts at the Tibetan Tripitaka Research Center (attested 1962) and Kyoto Women's University (professor, attested 1982).

nodes.label: Yasunori Ejima
nodes.summary: Yasunori Ejima (1939–1999) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his degrees at the University of Tokyo and researched at the University of Göttingen. He served as professor at the University of Tokyo and president of the Japanese Association of Indian and Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Fernando Tola
nodes.summary: Fernando Tola was an Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the National University of San Marcos. He held posts at the University of Buenos Aires (~1964–1984) and served as director of the Instituto de Investigaciones Budistas (~1989–2017).

nodes.label: Carmen Dragonetti
nodes.summary: Carmen Dragonetti was an Indologist and scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at the National University of San Marcos. She served as vice director of the Instituto de Investigaciones Budistas (~1988–2018), with visiting roles at IIBS (1989) and Nyingma Institute (1996).

nodes.label: Tsugunari Kubo
nodes.summary: Tsugunari Kubo (1936–2019) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1956–1967). He lectured at Rissho University and served as president of Reiyūkai and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Shoju Inaba
nodes.summary: Shoju Inaba (1915–1990) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He was a professor at Otani University (~1957–1980) and served as a part-time lecturer at Nagoya University.

nodes.label: Kogi Kudara

nodes.label: Michitoshi Barada
nodes.summary: Michitoshi Barada works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Jien Abe and J. R. Joshi, as well as at Savitribai Phule Pune University (1997), and held research posts at Otani University (attested 1992) and the Eastern Institute (attested 2000–2003).

nodes.label: V. Raghavan
nodes.summary: V. Raghavan (1908–1979) was an Indologist who completed his Ph.D. under S. Kuppuswami Sastri at the University of Madras (1931–1934). He spent his academic career at the University of Madras, serving in the Sanskrit Department and as its head.

nodes.label: Juro Watanabe
nodes.summary: Specializing in Indology and philosophy, Juro Watanabe studied under Gerhard Oberhammer and held a post at the University of Tsukuba, attested from 1989 to 1990.

nodes.label: Kiyotaka Yoshimizu
nodes.summary: Kiyotaka Yoshimizu specializes in Indology and philosophy, having studied under Gerhard Oberhammer (~1984–1989) and as a graduate student at the University of Tokyo. Yoshimizu held posts at Hokkaido University, Toyo Bunko, and as professor at Tohoku University (~2006–2020).

nodes.label: Atsushi Uno
nodes.summary: Atsushi Uno was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at Kyoto University and Banaras Hindu University under T. R. V. Murti and others. He taught at Shuchiin, Kyoto, and Tokai universities, Hiroshima University (1974–1986), and Kindai University (attested 1988–1989).

nodes.label: Raghunath Giri
nodes.summary: Raghunath Giri was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Vamacharana Bhattacharya and taught Atsushi Uno. He served as a department head (科長) at Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith.

nodes.label: Keisho Tsukamoto

nodes.label: Noriaki Inoue
nodes.summary: Noriaki Inoue is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University from circa 1949 to 1953. He later served as a professor at Taisho University from circa 1975 to 1999.

nodes.label: Hideo Sakurai

nodes.label: Takushu Sugimoto

nodes.label: Hisashi Sato
nodes.summary: Hisashi Sato was a Tibetology and history scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1934–1937). He taught Katsumi Mimaki and Tsuguhito Takeuchi, and held professorships at Kyoto University (~1964–1977), Toyo University (~1977–1984), Komazawa University, and a post at Bukkyo University.

nodes.label: Tatsuo Nishida
nodes.summary: Tatsuo Nishida (1928–2012) worked in linguistics, Tibetology, and Sinology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1948–1953), where he later served as a professor (attested 1996).

nodes.label: Helmut Hoffmann
nodes.summary: Helmut Hoffmann was an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied under Heinrich Lüders, Giuseppe Tucci, and Ferdinand Diederich Lessing, later holding professorships at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (1948) and Indiana University (1969–1980).

nodes.label: Christopher I. Beckwith

nodes.summary: Christopher I. Beckwith is a linguist and scholar of Tibetology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Ohio State and Indiana University under Helmut Hoffmann and Thubten Jigme Norbu, later holding academic appointments at Indiana University.

nodes.label: Takao Moriyasu
nodes.summary: A scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and history, Moriyasu studied at the University of Tokyo (~1967–1976) and Osaka University (~1991–1992). He held posts at Kobe City University of Foreign Studies, Kanazawa University, and Osaka University (professor ~1992–2013).

nodes.label: Tokio Takata
nodes.summary: Tokio Takata is a scholar of Sinology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Kyoto University (circa 1968–1976) and later held a post there from circa 1988 to 2014.

nodes.label: Shinshu Kusumoto
nodes.summary: Shinshu Kusumoto specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning a PhD from Hiroshima University in 2001 under doctoral supervisor Shoryu Katsura. He also studied under Hideyo Ogawa, Hiromi Yoshimura, Kazufumi Oki, Osamu Hayashima, and Tomoyuki Uno.

nodes.label: Hideyo Ogawa
nodes.summary: Hideyo Ogawa is an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Hiroshima University (~1974–1982). Ogawa continued at Hiroshima University as an assistant professor (~1987–1996) and as Professor of Indian Philosophy (~1996–2019).

nodes.label: Yoshihito Muroji
nodes.summary: Yoshihito Muroji is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He earned a PhD from the University of Hamburg (1992) under Lambert Schmithausen and held posts at Kyoto University, Koyasan University (attested 1995–2012), and Shiga University of Medical Science (attested 2014–2015).

nodes.label: Robert Kritzer
nodes.summary: Robert Kritzer is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned his Ph.D. at UC Berkeley under Padmanabh S. Jaini in 1995. He served as an associate professor at Kyoto Notre Dame University (attested 1999–2017).

nodes.label: Hiromi Yoshimura
nodes.summary: Hiromi Yoshimura works in Buddhist studies and Indology. Yoshimura held positions at Ryukoku University as a full-time lecturer (attested 1987) and later in 2006.

nodes.summary: Toshihiko Kimura is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religious studies who studied at Tohoku University (~1959–1963). He held posts at Tokai Gakuin University, Tohoku University, and Shitennoji University.

nodes.label: Shinkan Murakami
nodes.summary: Shinkan Murakami studied Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy at Tohoku University (~1958–1963, ~1978–1979) under teachers including Ensho Kanakura and Hakuyu Hadano. He served as professor at Tohoku University (attested 1982–2000) and at Seiwa Gakuen College (~1996–2003).

nodes.label: Shujun Motegi

nodes.label: Tsultrim Kelsang
nodes.summary: Tsultrim Kelsang (1939–) is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the International Buddhist Association (attested 1973), Otani University (attested 1984 as lecturer, 1999–2002 as professor), and Ryukoku University (2015).

nodes.label: Kiyotaka Kimura
nodes.summary: Kiyotaka Kimura (born 1940) specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. nodes.label: Koyu Tamura

nodes.summary: Hara Prasad Sastri worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He served as Principal of Sanskrit College and University (attested 1905) and as Joint Philological Secretary at the Asiatic Society (attested 1905–1911).

nodes.label: Hartmut-Ortwin Feistel
nodes.summary: Hartmut-Ortwin Feistel worked in Indology. He served as head at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 1989) and held a post in the Oriental Department at the Berlin State Library (attested 1992–1994).

nodes.summary: Shobha Rani Dash specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. She was an open-call researcher at Ryukoku University in 2010 and a lecturer at Otani University (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Makoto Yoshimura

nodes.label: Ryogon Fukuhara
nodes.summary: Ryogon Fukuhara was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (~1928–1933) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1938–1941), where he also lectured. He served as a professor at Ryukoku University (~1957–1978).

nodes.label: Noboru Karashima

Educated at the University of Tokyo (~1954-1961), he held faculty posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1964-1974), the University of Tokyo (~1974-1994), Taisho University (~1994-2004), and the Open University of Japan (~1994-1998).

nodes.summary: Taijun Inokuchi specialized in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held posts as lecturer (attested 1963) and committee member (attested 1973–1987) at Ryukoku University, and representative of The Society for the History of Buddhism (attested 1988).

nodes.label: Yusen Kashiwahara
nodes.summary: Yusen Kashiwahara was a scholar of Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He studied at Otani University and served there as a professor (~1957–1987).

nodes.label: Shuyu Kanaoka
nodes.summary: Shuyu Kanaoka (1927–2009) worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1948–1954) and held professorships at Ryukoku University (~1961–1963) and Toyo University (assistant professor ~1958–1967; professor ~1967–1984).

nodes.label: Hiromu Kitanishi
nodes.summary: Hiromu Kitanishi was a Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology scholar. He studied at Otani University (~1946–1950) and later served there as professor (~1966–1991).

nodes.label: Masahiro Kusunoki
nodes.summary: Masahiro Kusunoki specialized in religious and Buddhist studies, studying at Tohoku University (~1947-1953). He served as professor at Tohoku University (~1968-1985) and held leadership roles in the Tohoku Association of Indian and Religious Studies and the Japanese Association for Religious Studies.

nodes.label: Yoshiro Tamura
nodes.summary: Yoshiro Tamura (1921–1989) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1946–1949). He held professorial posts at Toyo University, the University of Tokyo, Rissho University, and the University of Chicago.

nodes.label: Joryu Chiba
nodes.summary: Joryu Chiba (1921–2008) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Ryukoku University and served there as a professor from circa 1958 to 1995.

nodes.label: Kyosho Hayashima
nodes.summary: Kyosho Hayashima (1914–1999) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. Attested as a lecturer at Yokohama City University and associate professor at Toyo University in 1962, he later served as professor at the University of Tokyo (attested 1980) and taught Shinjo Kawasaki.

nodes.label: Yukei Matsunaga

nodes.label: Satoshi Hayashima
nodes.summary: Satoshi Hayashima specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at Ryukoku University (attested 2013) and served there as a lecturer (attested 2015–2017).

nodes.label: Michihiko Komine
nodes.summary: Michihiko Komine (born 1945) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University. He served there as an assistant (attested 1978–1980) and professor (attested 2014–2015), and was board chairman of the Japanese Association for Esoteric Buddhist Studies (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Shun'ei Matsushita
nodes.summary: Shun'ei Matsushita is a Buddhist studies scholar who served at Otani University as a term-limited assistant professor until 2013 and as a part-time lecturer (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Koshiro Tamaki
nodes.summary: Koshiro Tamaki was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1937–1940). He held posts at Toyo University, Tohoku University, Nihon University, and the University of Tokyo.

nodes.summary: Nobuo Otsuka specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Taisho University from circa 1983 to 1988 and served as a researcher there, attested in 1995.

nodes.label: Takayasu Kimura
nodes.summary: Takayasu Kimura specialized in Indology and Buddhist studies, completing doctoral studies at Taisho University. He held positions as a researcher at the Buzan-ha Institute of Modern Mission (attested 1995) and lecturer at Taisho University (attested 1995).

nodes.label: Keiya Noguchi
nodes.summary: Keiya Noguchi (born 1954) specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology, completing doctoral studies at Kyoto University (~1980–1985). Noguchi held positions at Shuchiin University (attested 1995–2005) and Taisho University, including institute director (attested 2017).
