nodes.label: Shinya Moriyama
nodes.summary: Shinya Moriyama (born 1972) works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He completed a master's at the University of Tokyo (~1996–1998) and a doctorate at the University of Vienna (~2002–2006), later joining Shinshu University (~2009).

nodes.label: Hiroshi Marui
nodes.summary: Hiroshi Marui is an Indology and philosophy scholar educated at the University of Tokyo and Savitribai Phule Pune University, studying under Albrecht Wezler. He served at the Eastern Institute, Musashino University, and long-term as associate professor at the University of Tokyo.

nodes.label: Atsushi Kanazawa
nodes.summary: Atsushi Kanazawa is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held posts as a lecturer at Meteorological College (attested 1986–1989) and as an assistant professor at Komazawa University (attested 1996–2003, 2012).

nodes.label: Yoichi Fukuda
nodes.summary: Yoichi Fukuda is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as a full-time researcher at Toyo Bunko (attested 1986–1991) and as a professor at Otani University (attested 2003 and 2015).

nodes.label: Péter-Dániel Szántó
nodes.summary: Péter-Dániel Szántó works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University and Balliol College under Alexis Sanderson, and held posts as a Fellow at All Souls College, Oxford, and Eötvös Loránd University.

nodes.label: William M. Gorvine
nodes.summary: William M. Gorvine is a scholar in Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Connecticut College and the University of Virginia, completing his PhD under David Germano in 2006.

nodes.label: Sara L. McClintock
nodes.summary: Sara L. McClintock works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. Educated at Columbia, CIHTS, Lausanne, and Harvard (PhD 2002 under Tom J. F. Tillemans), she has held posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and Emory University.

nodes.label: A. K. Ramanujan
nodes.summary: A scholar of linguistics and Indology, Ramanujan studied at the University of Mysore, Maharaja's College, Mysore (~1946–1950), and Indiana University (~1959–1963). He taught at Baroda College (~1958–1959), the University of Chicago (~1962–1993), and Harvard University (~1987–1988).

nodes.label: Elliot Sperling
nodes.summary: Elliot Sperling (1951–2017) was a Tibetologist and historian. He studied at Queens College (~1969–1973) and earned his PhD at Indiana University (~1976–1983) under Helmut Hoffmann and Lynn A. Struve, later serving on the faculties of Harvard University and Indiana University (~1987–2015).

nodes.label: Takashi Ogawa
nodes.summary: A specialist in Buddhist studies and Sinology, Takashi Ogawa studied at Komazawa University (~1980–1986) and Peking University (~1986–1988). He became an assistant professor at Komazawa University around 1991.

nodes.label: Kyoko Fujii
nodes.summary: Kyoko Fujii studied at the University of Tokyo (~1967–1977). A scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology, she held professorships at Yokohama City University (1990), Hamamatsu University (1996), Hokkaido University (~1998–2008), and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~2008–2019).

nodes.label: Kenryo Minowa
nodes.summary: Kenryo Minowa is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1979–1989). He held positions at Rissho University, Eastern Institute, Aichi Gakuin University (~1999–2010), and became a professor at the University of Tokyo in 2010.

nodes.label: Shogo Watanabe
nodes.summary: Shogo Watanabe (born 1953) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Toyo University (~1973–1982), where he later served on the faculty (attested 1991) and as professor (~2002–2019).

nodes.label: Takanori Kimura
nodes.summary: Takanori Kimura, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studied at Komazawa University. He served as research assistant at the University of Tokyo (~1973-1978), lecturer at Yamaguchi University (attested 1996), and head priest at Kaichoji (attested 2003).

nodes.label: Toshihide Mori
nodes.summary: Toshihide Mori is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied under Shoko Takeuchi. In 1995, he held a post as a part-time lecturer at Chikushi Jogakuen University.

nodes.label: Kaiten Nukariya
nodes.description: Religious scholar and ordained Zen Buddhist monk
nodes.summary: Kaiten Nukariya studied Buddhist studies and philosophy at Keio, Komazawa, and under Ryodo Nukariya. He lectured at Harvard (~1913–1914) and held posts at Komazawa University, including head teacher (1919) and first president (1925–1934), as well as Soto-shu University (~1921–1934).

nodes.label: Nathmal Tatia
nodes.summary: Nathmal Tatia (1916–2002) worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He earned a Doctor of Literature at the University of Calcutta under Satkari Mookerjee and Sukhlal Sanghvi, and served as Director of the Jain Vishva Bharati Institute.

nodes.label: Yasuro Abe
nodes.summary: Yasuro Abe (born 1953) is a scholar of Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who studied at Wako University. He held professorships at Otemae University, Nagoya University (~2003–2018), and Osaka University (attested 2004).

nodes.label: Shunpei Ueyama

nodes.label: Gustav Roth
nodes.summary: Gustav Roth (1916–2008) studied Indology and Buddhist studies at Munich and Patna University under scholars including Paul Thieme. He held posts at the University of Göttingen, the Australian National University, and served as Director of Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (1982–1985).

nodes.label: Reinhold Grünendahl
nodes.summary: Reinhold Grünendahl is an Indologist. He held posts at the Free University of Berlin (attested 1983) and the Göttingen State and University Library (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Petra Kieffer-Pülz

nodes.label: Sen Wang
nodes.summary: Sen Wang was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Peking University from around 1931 to 1936 and served as a professor at Minzu University of China from around 1952 to 1988.

nodes.label: Anantalal Thakur
nodes.summary: Anantalal Thakur (1916–2009) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He served as a professor at Mithila Research Institute (~1955–1974) and as Director of the Kashi Prasad Jayaswal Research Institute (1968–1971).

nodes.label: Tilmann Vetter
nodes.summary: Tilmann Vetter (1937–2012) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Vienna under Erich Frauwallner and Erich Heintel, and served as a professor at Leiden University from circa 1973 to 2002.

nodes.label: Minoru Kiyota
nodes.summary: Minoru Kiyota was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at UC Berkeley (~1946–1949) and the University of Tokyo (~1954–1963) under Reimon Yuki, Shinsho Hanayama, Hajime Nakamura, and Akira Hirakawa. He was a long-time professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1966–2013).

nodes.label: Yumi Nakamoto

nodes.summary: Ryosei Fukuda was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Toyo University (~1956–1960). nodes.summary: Ryojin Soga was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He held academic posts at Toyo University (~1916–1924) and Otani University (~1925–1967), and served as president of the Otani Society (~1961–1967).

nodes.label: Migmar Tsering

nodes.label: Joseph Hackin
nodes.summary: Joseph Hackin (1886–1941) was an archaeologist, Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar, and Buddhist studies specialist. Educated in Paris under Sylvain Lévi, he held posts at Musée Guimet, the French Archeological Delegation to Afghanistan, and EPHE.

nodes.label: Bunzaburo Matsumoto
nodes.summary: Bunzaburo Matsumoto worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1890–1893), where he later held a post (~1899–1906), before serving at Kyoto University from 1906 to 1929 and as professor (attested 1934).

nodes.label: Shoson Miyamoto
nodes.summary: Shoson Miyamoto (1893–1983) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1918–1921). He held posts at the University of Tokyo, Komazawa University (~1954–1973), and Waseda University (~1954–1964).

nodes.label: Giei Honda
nodes.summary: Giei Honda (1888–1953) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. After studying at Kyoto University, he served as a professeur adjoint there from 1934 to 1948 and also held a post at Rissho University.

nodes.label: Vidhusekhara Bhattacharya
nodes.summary: Vidhusekhara Bhattacharya was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. nodes.label: Giuseppe Tucci

nodes.summary: Giuseppe Tucci (1894–1984) studied at Rome, Calcutta, and Visva-Bharati. A specialist in Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies, he held posts at the University of Calcutta, Sapienza University of Rome, and served as president of IsMEO.

nodes.label: Shuntaro Matsuyama
nodes.summary: Shuntaro Matsuyama (1930–2014) was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1949–1953). He served as a professor at Joshibi University of Art and Design (~1971–1995) and held posts at Tama Art University and Kokugakuin University.

nodes.id: I:Joshibi University of Art and Design
nodes.label: Joshibi University of Art and Design
Rikizan Ishikawa
nodes.summary: Rikizan Ishikawa was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Komazawa University (~1962–1972), where he later served as lecturer (~1978) and Professor of Buddhist Studies until 1997.

nodes.label: Shuken Ito
nodes.summary: Shuken Ito (born 1947) is a scholar of Buddhist studies who did graduate studies at Komazawa University (attested 1973). He served at Komazawa University as research assistant (attested 1973–1978) and professor (attested 1994), and held a post at Aichi Gakuin University.

nodes.label: Masashi Nagai
nodes.summary: Masashi Nagai specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at Komazawa University (~1965-1974) and later served there as an assistant professor (~1981-2017).

nodes.label: Peter N. Gregory
variants: ビーター・N・グレゴリー
ピーター・N・グレゴリー
nodes.summary: Peter N. Gregory (b. 1945) works in Buddhist studies and sinology. After receiving his PhD from Harvard (1981) under Masatoshi Nagatomi, he held posts at the Kuroda Institute, University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, and Smith College.

nodes.label: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
variants: Japan House at the University of Illinois

nodes.label: Rosan Ikeda
nodes.summary: Rosan Ikeda is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Komazawa University, where he subsequently served as a professor from circa 1988 to 2012.

nodes.label: Ichiro Katayama
nodes.summary: Ichiro Katayama (born 1942) is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Komazawa University from ~1961 to 1965 and later served as a professor there from ~1985 to 2012.

nodes.label: Tatsugen Sato
nodes.summary: Tatsugen Sato (1924–2021) specialized in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He served on the faculty of Komazawa University (~1972–1995) as assistant professor and professor, with additional teaching posts at Ryukoku University (attested 1974) and Tokai University.

nodes.label: Morten Schlütter
variants: モルテン・シュルター
nodes.summary: Morten Schlütter, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology, studied at the University of Copenhagen, Komazawa University, and Yale University. He has taught at Yale, Komazawa, Victoria University of Wellington, UCLA, the University of Wisconsin-Madison, and the University of Iowa.

nodes.label: Shigeki Kudo
nodes.summary: Shigeki Kudo was a Buddhist studies scholar. He worked as an assistant at Kyoto University, an assistant professor at Shuchiin University, and an assistant professor at Shitennoji University (attested 1972–1973).

nodes.label: University of Calcutta
variants: Department of Ancient Indian History, Calcutta University
Council of Post-Graduate Teaching in Arts, Calcutta University
Centre of Advanced Study in AIHC, Calcutta University
Department of Ancient Indian History and Culture of the Calcutta University

nodes.label: Shin Kitada
nodes.summary: Shin Kitada is an indologist who completed doctoral studies at the University of Halle-Wittenberg. He held a post at the Eastern Institute (attested 2008–2010).

nodes.label: Dhammapāla
nodes.summary: Dhammapāla is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD from the University of Hong Kong under K. L. Dhammajoti. He later served as a guest assistant professor at the University of Hong Kong.

nodes.label: Yutaka Ochihara
nodes.summary: Indologist and linguist Yutaka Ochihara studied at Kyoto University (~1944–1947) and the University of Pennsylvania (1951–1954). He was an Associate Professor (1957) and Professor (1972–1986) at Kyoto University, and a Professeur étranger at Collège de France (1985).

nodes.label: Hideaki Nakatani
nodes.summary: Hideaki Nakatani is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University (1966) under Gadjin Nagao, under Yutaka Ochihara, and earned a PhD from Sorbonne Nouvelle University. He was a professor at Kobe Gakuin University (attested 2003).

nodes.label: Louis Renou
nodes.summary: Louis Renou was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the Faculty of Arts of Paris, Lycée Janson-de-Sailly, and under Antoine Meillet at ENLOV. He served as Director at the University of Paris (~1937–1966) and Membre de l'Institut (~1946–1966).

nodes.label: Vincent Eltschinger
nodes.summary: Vincent Eltschinger specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at Collège Saint-Michel and the University of Lausanne. He held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences, IKGA, University of Vienna (~2003–2015), and EPHE (Professor, ~2015).

nodes.label: Danielle Feller
nodes.summary: Danielle Feller is an Indology scholar who completed her PhD at the University of Lausanne by 2001 under doctoral supervisor Johannes Bronkhorst and studied under Ganesh Umakant Thite.

nodes.label: Yael Bentor
nodes.summary: Yael Bentor studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and Indiana University, completing doctoral work under Gregory Schopen in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Attested in 2000, she taught in the Department of Indian Studies at the Hebrew University.

nodes.label: David Shulman
nodes.description: Israeli-American indologist, historian of religion, and poet
nodes.summary: David Shulman is an Indologist who studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1967–1971) and the University of London (~1971–1976). He spent his academic career at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1976–2016), serving as Professor of Indian Studies and Comparative Religion (~1985–1995).

nodes.label: Lydia Aran
nodes.description: Professor emerita:Hebrew University of Jerusalem/scholar of Buddhism (1921–2013)

nodes.label: Thubten Jigme Norbu
nodes.image: Thubten Jigme Norbu, The Dalai Lama opens art exhibit in Tokyo, 1967 (cropped) (cropped).jpg
nodes.description: lama, writer, civil rights worker, university and college faculty member

nodes.label: Patrick Olivelle
nodes.description: Sri Lankan Indologist and Sanskrit scholar (born 1942)
nodes.summary: Indologist and religious studies scholar Patrick Olivelle studied at Oxford (~1968–1972) and the University of Pennsylvania (~1972–1974). He served as chairman at Indiana University (~1984–1991) and Chair of Asian Studies at the University of Texas at Austin (1991).

nodes.label: Gregory Schopen
variants: グレゴリー・ショペン
nodes.summary: Gregory Schopen (born 1947) is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He earned his PhD at the Australian National University under Jan Willem de Jong and Tissa Rajapatirana, holding posts at Brown, Texas, Indiana, Stanford, and UCLA.

nodes.label: Dan Martin
nodes.summary: Dan Martin is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed his Ph.D. at Indiana University (~1984–1991). He held positions at the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters, the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, and Carnegie Mellon University.

nodes.label: Khetsun Sangpo Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Khetsun Sangpo Rinpoche (1920–2009) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, studying under teachers including Dudjom Rinpoche and Chatral Sangye Dorje Rinpoche. He taught at Tokyo and Kyoto universities (1960–1970), founded the Nyingmapa Wishfulfilling Center (1971), and taught at the University of Virginia.

nodes.label: Shoren Ihara
nodes.summary: Shoren Ihara is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He held posts at Kyushu University (attested 1959–1977) and the Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 1996–1998), and taught Kunio Harikai and Hiromasa Tosaki.

nodes.label: Tokai Gakuen University
variants: 東海学園大学短期大学部

nodes.label: Ryoso Matsushita
nodes.summary: Ryoso Matsushita works in Buddhist studies. He studied under Daishun Ueyama and held a post as lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 1987).

nodes.label: Fukuoka Prefectural Human Rights Center
variants: 福岡県人権啓発情報センター

nodes.label: Yutaka Iwamoto
nodes.summary: Yutaka Iwamoto was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1931–1934), supervised by Toru Haneda and Hidenaka Tanaka. He held academic posts at Kyoto Tachibana University (~1977–1982) and Soka University (~1982–1988).

nodes.label: Istituto Italiano per l'Africa e l'Oriente
variants: Istituto Italiano per l'Africa e l'Oriente
Istituto Italiano per l’Africa e l’Oriente in Rome

variants: Dipartimento di Studi Asiatici, Università di Napoli “L'Orientale”
ナポリ東洋大學文學部

nodes.label: Mauro Maggi
nodes.summary: Mauro Maggi specializes in Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological studies. He earned his doctorate at the University of Naples "L'Orientale," worked as a researcher at the University of Hamburg (1990), and held posts at IsIAO and Sapienza University of Rome (attested 2018).

nodes.label: Tatsuhiro Saito
nodes.summary: Tatsuhiro Saito is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Kenyu Mitomo (attested 1996) and founded the Nikaya Buddhism Thought Study Group.

nodes.label: Yasuo Sano
nodes.summary: Yasuo Sano is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Kenyu Mitomo (attested 1996) and founded the Nikaya Buddhism Thought Study Group.

nodes.label: Toshio Sako
nodes.summary: Toshio Sako specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo and Columbia University, where Alex Wayman was his doctoral supervisor.

nodes.label: Anna-Pya Sjödin
nodes.summary: Anna-Pya Sjödin specializes in Indology and philosophy. She completed her PhD at Uppsala University in 2007, where her doctoral supervisors included Gunilla Gren-Eklund, Eli Franco, Jonardon Ganeri, K. Venugopalan, and Toshihiro Wada, with instruction from Klas Hagren and Barbro Eriksson.

nodes.label: Jonardon Ganeri
nodes.summary: Ganeri, a specialist in philosophy and Indology, studied at Cambridge and Oxford under Bimal Krishna Matilal. He held posts at Nottingham, Liverpool, Sussex, Monash (~2013–2015), NYU (~2013–2020), and the University of Toronto (~2020).

nodes.label: K. Venugopalan
variants: K・ヴェーヌゴーパラン

nodes.label: Toshihiro Wada
nodes.summary: Toshihiro Wada is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Vashishtha Narayan Jha in 1981. He served as an associate professor and held a post at Nagoya University from ~1990 to 2020.

nodes.label: Tadashi Tani
nodes.summary: Tadashi Tani, a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy, completed doctoral studies at Waseda University under Yuichi Kajiyama and studied at Kyoto University (1995). He was a professor at Kochi College (attested 1996–2000) and later lectured at several universities.

nodes.id: I:National Institute of Technology, Kochi College
nodes.label: National Institute of Technology, Kochi College
variants: 高知工業高等専門学校

nodes.label: Ryudo Fujii
nodes.summary: Ryudo Fujii specializes in Indology and philosophy. He studied under Albrecht Wezler and Harunaga Isaacson, and held posts at JSPS (attested 2003), Kokushikan University (attested 2010), and Kyoto Women's University (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Karl Jettmar
nodes.summary: Karl Jettmar worked in history, archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held posts at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz from around 1958 to 1964 and at Heidelberg University from around 1964 to 1986.

nodes.label: Gérard Fussman
nodes.summary: Gérard Fussman (1940–2022) studied at École Normale Supérieure (~1960–1964) and worked in Indology, history and archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He succeeded Jean Filliozat and served as a professor at the Collège de France (~1984–2011).

nodes.label: Ahmad Hasan Dani
nodes.description: Pakistani intellectual, archaeologist, historian, and linguist (1920–2009)
nodes.summary: Ahmad Hasan Dani was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Banaras Hindu University and the University of London under Altekar, Wheeler, and Codrington. He held posts at Dhaka, Peshawar, SOAS, and Quaid-i-Azam University.

nodes.label: Klaus Müller-Deis
variants: クラウス・ミューラーダイス

nodes.label: Gessho Sasaki
nodes.summary: Gessho Sasaki (1875–1926) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University from circa 1896 to 1900. He subsequently held an academic post at Otani University from circa 1901 to 1926.

nodes.label: Koichi Hokazono
nodes.summary: Koichi Hokazono (born 1944) specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyushu University (PhD) and the University of Bonn, and held posts at The International University of Kagoshima (professor, attested 1991–2000) and Kyushu University (attested 1995).

nodes.label: Ryuken Sato
nodes.summary: Ryuken Sato (1930–2018) was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as professor emeritus at Taisho University (attested 2014) and advisor at the Kawasaki Daishi Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Akitoshi Saito
nodes.summary: Akitoshi Saito is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He served at Taisho University, where he is attested as a professor in 1982 and as professor emeritus in 2014.

nodes.label: Chisan Denpoin
variants: 真言宗智山派智山伝法院

nodes.label: Institute for Zen Studies
variants: Research Institute for Zen Culture (Zen Bunka Kenkyūsho)

nodes.label: Yumi Katayama
nodes.summary: Yumi Katayama specializes in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. She was a PhD student at Hiroshima University (attested 2007) and studied under supervisor Kenyu Mitomo (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Geshe Lobsang Tharchin
nodes.summary: Geshe Lobsang Tharchin (1921–2004) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his studies at Sera Monastery, earning his Lharampa Geshe degree by 1953, and also studied at Gyume Tantric College.

nodes.label: Meiji Yamada
nodes.summary: Meiji Yamada is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (attested 1962). He also served as a professor there (attested 1963, 2007).

nodes.label: Frank-Richard Hamm
nodes.summary: Frank-Richard Hamm was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He earned his doctorate at the University of Hamburg under Walther Schubring, later teaching at Hamburg (~1954–1964) before becoming Professor of Indology at the University of Bonn in 1965.

nodes.label: Daniel Cozort
nodes.summary: Daniel Cozort (born 1953) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Virginia (~1982–1989) under Jeffrey Hopkins and taught at Bates College (~1987–1988) and Dickinson College (~1988–2021).

nodes.label: Thubten Yeshe
nodes.summary: Thubten Yeshe (1935–1984) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Sera Monastery under Geshe Lhundub Sopa and Trijang Rinpoche, and held posts at the University of Virginia (1982) and Middlebury College (1982).

nodes.label: Geshe Palden Drakpa
nodes.summary: Geshe Palden Drakpa specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He was a visiting scholar at the University of Virginia in 1987 and served as librarian at Tibet House in New Delhi, attested between 1987 and 2004.

nodes.label: Shaoyong Ye
nodes.summary: Shaoyong Ye is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his doctoral studies at Peking University in 2009 under Qing Duan and served there as an Associate Professor (attested 2010–2016).

nodes.label: Qing Duan
nodes.description: Chinese scholar of Indian and Iranian languages; Professor of Indo-Iranian Studies and Boya Chair Professor of Peking University
nodes.summary: Qing Duan worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Peking University and the University of Hamburg, and served as a Professor at Peking University (~1987–2022), where she taught Shaoyong Ye.

nodes.label: Zhaohua Yang
nodes.summary: Zhaohua Yang works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He held posts at Stanford University (attested 2007) and Columbia University (attested 2018).

nodes.label: Shinsho Hanayama
nodes.summary: Shinsho Hanayama (1898–1995) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1918–1921). He taught Buddhism there (~1935–1959) and held posts at Toyo University and Kokugakuin University.

nodes.label: Naoshiro Tsuji
nodes.summary: Naoshiro Tsuji (1899–1979) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo and Oxford. He served as Professor and Chair of Sanskrit at the University of Tokyo (1927–1960) and later directed the Toyo Bunko (~1974–1979).

nodes.label: Paul Hacker
nodes.summary: Paul Hacker (1913–1979) was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Bonn, Heidelberg, Frankfurt, and Berlin. He held posts at the University of Münster, Mithila Research Institute, the University of Bonn, and the University of Pennsylvania.

nodes.label: Université catholique de Louvain
variants: Institut Orientaliste de l'Université Catholique de Louvain
Institut Orientaliste of the University of Louvain

nodes.id: I:Wiener Studien zur Tibetologie und Buddhismuskunde
nodes.label: Wiener Studien zur Tibetologie und Buddhismuskunde
variants: Wiener Studien zur Tibetologie und Buddhismuskunde

nodes.label: Michael Friedrich
nodes.summary: Michael Friedrich is a scholar in sinology and Buddhist studies. He succeeded Friedrich Alexander Bischoff and served as a professor at the University of Hamburg from approximately 1994 to 2023.

nodes.label: Jowita Kramer
nodes.summary: Jowita Kramer is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who studied at the University of Hamburg and LMU Munich. She held positions at Oxford, LMU Munich, Heidelberg, UC Berkeley, Göttingen, and EPHE.

nodes.label: Masaru Akimoto
nodes.summary: Masaru Akimoto is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He held appointments, including professor in the Faculty of Contemporary Social Studies, at Kyoto Women's University (attested 2002, 2015).

nodes.label: Sergey Oldenburg
nodes.jawiki: セルゲイ・オルデンブルク
nodes.description: Russian scholar of Sanskrit and Buddhism (1863-1934)
nodes.summary: Sergey Oldenburg was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Ivan Minayev at St. Petersburg University. He held posts at Saint Petersburg State University, the Russian Academy of Sciences, Asiatic Museum, and the Institute of Oriental Studies.

nodes.label: George R. Elder
nodes.summary: George R. Elder is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at Columbia University under doctoral supervisor Alex Wayman (attested 1978).

nodes.label: Ikuhisa Takigawa
nodes.summary: Ikuhisa Takigawa (born 1968) is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University. In 2002, he held part-time lecturer posts at both Waseda University and Tokai University.

nodes.label: Thomas A. Tweed
nodes.summary: Thomas A. Tweed (born 1954) is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who completed his PhD at Stanford University under William R. Hutchison and others. He was Professor of Religious Studies at UNC Chapel Hill from around 1993 to 2008.

nodes.label: William A. Clebsch
nodes.description: American church historian, developer of religious studies, and university professor (1923-1984)

nodes.label: Robert E. Buswell Jr.
nodes.summary: Robert E. Buswell Jr. is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his Ph.D. at UC Berkeley (~1979–1985) and studied under Kusan Sunim, Gerald James Larson, Lewis Lancaster, and others. He served as professor at UCLA (attested 1986–1994, ~1993).

nodes.label: Luis Oscar Gómez
variants: Luis O. GÓMEZ ルイス・ゴメス
nodes.description: Puerto Rican buddhologist, translator and psychologist
nodes.summary: Luis Oscar Gómez worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning degrees at the University of Puerto Rico, Yale University under Stanley Insler, and the University of Michigan. He held professorships at Michigan (~1976–2008) and directed the Mangalam Research Center (~2010–2017).

nodes.label: Van Austin Harvey
nodes.image: Van A. Harvey and a dog.jpg

nodes.label: Gordon D. Kaufman
nodes.summary: Gordon D. Kaufman (1925–2011) was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Northwestern University (~1947–1948) and Yale Divinity School (~1948–1955), and held a faculty post at Harvard University from around 1963 to 1995.

nodes.label: Carl Bielefeldt
nodes.summary: Carl Bielefeldt specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied under Shunryu Suzuki and completed his PhD at UC Berkeley (~1970–1980). He served on the editorial board at Stanford University (~1980–2013) and was a member of the Numata Center (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Kurtis R. Schaeffer
nodes.summary: Kurtis R. Schaeffer is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Washington under Collett Cox and Richard Salomon and at Harvard under Leonard van der Kuijp, later holding posts at Alabama and Virginia.

nodes.label: Trungram Gyaltrul Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Trungram Gyaltrul Rinpoche (1968–) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at Harvard University (~1997–2004), where he studied with Thomas Burke and doctoral supervisor Leonard van der Kuijp.

nodes.label: Chishō Namai
nodes.summary: Chishō Namai (1947–) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served at Koyasan University as a professor (attested 1996) and later as president (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Satkari Mookerjee
variants: サトカリ・ムカージー

nodes.label: John Brough
nodes.summary: John Brough was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at Edinburgh under Arthur Berriedale Keith and Cambridge under Harold Walter Bailey. He held posts at the British Museum, SOAS, University of London, and Cambridge (1967–1984).

nodes.label: Chitai Takenaka
nodes.summary: Chitai Takenaka (1945–) is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He completed a Master of Letters at Kyoto University in 1968, later serving as an assistant professor at Hanazono University (1979–1983) and professor at Tokoha University (attested 1989).

nodes.label: Hideki Kiyoshima
nodes.summary: Hideki Kiyoshima is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Delhi and held an attested post as a lecturer at Kindai University (1989).

nodes.label: Jun Takashima
nodes.summary: Jun Takashima specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Minoru Hara and at Kyoto University. He later held posts at Aichi Prefectural University and Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, where he was a professor (2002–2021).

nodes.label: Motoichi Miyamoto
nodes.summary: Motoichi Miyamoto is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo from around 1968 to 1978 and served as an assistant professor at Kokugakuin University from around 1984 to 1993.

nodes.label: Muneo Tokunaga
nodes.summary: Muneo Tokunaga (1945–2016) was an Indology scholar who earned degrees from Kyoto University (~1969–1971) and Harvard University (PhD ~1974–1979). He taught at Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1981–1989) and served as assistant professor (~1989–1997) and professor (~1997–2009) at Kyoto University.

nodes.label: Yasumasa Sekine
nodes.summary: Yasumasa Sekine (born 1949) specializes in religious studies and Indology, having studied at Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1967–1971). His career includes posts at Japan Women's University, Gakushuin Women's College, the University of Tsukuba, and Kwansei Gakuin University (~2014).

nodes.label: Nobuyuki Watase
nodes.summary: Nobuyuki Watase is an Indologist who completed his master's studies at Kyoto University around 1966–1969. He served as an associate professor (circa 1977–1985) and professor (circa 1985–2012) at Tokai University.

nodes.label: Katsuhiko Kamimura
nodes.summary: Katsuhiko Kamimura was an Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo under Minoru Hara, and with V. Raghavan. He held posts at Kokugakuin University (~1973–1980) and the University of Tokyo (~1980–2003), and taught Mizuho Okita and Yuko Yokochi.

nodes.label: Michio Yano
nodes.summary: Michio Yano (born 1944) works in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1963–1972) and Brown University under David Pingree (~1978–1980), and served as a professor at Kyoto Sangyo University (~1974–2010).

nodes.label: Issei Suzuki
nodes.summary: Issei Suzuki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University and later held a post there as professor (教授).

nodes.label: Ryoshu Michihata
nodes.summary: Ryoshu Michihata (1903–1993) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Otani University (~1925–1928), where he later held a post (~1949–1973), before serving as professor at Kyoto Koka Women's University (~1973–1983).

nodes.label: Mizumaro Ishida
nodes.summary: Mizumaro Ishida was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor at Tokai University, attested in 1976 and 1987.

nodes.label: Rosemarie Fuchs
nodes.summary: Rosemarie Fuchs is a specialist in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied under Katia Holmes and Khenpo Tsültrim Gyamtso Rinpoche, and served as a member of the Marpa Translation Committee (attested 2000).

nodes.label: Tenzin Dorjee
nodes.summary: Tenzin Dorjee is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Geshe Lobsang Tsephel, Geshe Sonam Rinchen, and Geshe Dawa. He worked as a translator at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives and General Secretary at Pullahari Monastery.

nodes.label: Allen Wright Thrasher
nodes.summary: Allen Wright Thrasher (b. 1946) is an Indologist who completed his doctorate under Daniel H. H. Ingalls (~1968–1977) and studied with traditional teachers in India. He held a position at the Library of Congress from around 1985 to 2013.

nodes.label: Daniel H. H. Ingalls
nodes.summary: Daniel H. H. Ingalls (1916–1999) was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at Harvard University (~1932–1941) under Willard Van Orman Quine and Walter Eugene Clark, later serving as Harvard's Wales Professor of Sanskrit (~1958–1983; emeritus ~1983–1999).

Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute
Deccan College Post-graduate and Research Institute

nodes.label: Stefan Anacker
nodes.summary: Stefan Anacker was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Wisconsin–Madison from circa 1964 to 1970 under the supervision of Alex Wayman.

nodes.label: T. V. Venkatachala Sastry
nodes.description: Kannada writer, lexicographer, grammar expert, critic and editor
nodes.summary: T. V. Venkatachala Sastry is a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He held a post at Osmania University (~1964–1968) and served as professor at the University of Mysore from ~1968 to 1994.

variants: Institute of Kannada Studies, University of Mysore
Department of Jainology and Prakrits, University of Mysore

nodes.label: Jacques May
nodes.summary: Jacques May (1927–2018) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He served as editor-in-chief for Hōbōgirin and the École française d'Extrême-Orient (~1968–1981) and as a professor at the University of Lausanne (~1974–1992).

nodes.label: Richard Hugh Robinson
nodes.summary: Richard Hugh Robinson specialized in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at Alberta, SOAS, and London under Edward Conze, David L. Snellgrove, Arthur Waley, and David Friedman. He taught at Toronto (1954) and became a professor at Wisconsin-Madison in 1961.

nodes.label: Kyojun Shimizutani
nodes.summary: Kyojun Shimizutani (1891–1979) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Taisho University. He later held a post at Taisho University and served as head priest (貫主) of Senso-ji from around 1952 to 1979.

nodes.label: Manabendu Banerjee
nodes.summary: Manabendu Banerjee is an Indologist who served as DSA Sanskrit Co-ordinator at Jadavpur University (attested 2003) and Secretary of the Asiatic Society. He also taught Reeta Bhattacharya.

nodes.label: John D. Dunne
nodes.summary: John D. Dunne is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. Educated at Amherst, CIHTS, Harvard Divinity School, and Harvard, he taught at Antioch, CIHTS, Harvard, University of Wisconsin-Madison (1999), and Emory University (~2005–2014).

nodes.label: Margaret R. Miles
nodes.summary: Margaret R. Miles is a scholar of religious studies and history. After studying at San Francisco State University and the Graduate Theological Union, she held faculty posts at Harvard Divinity School (~1978–1996) and Harvard University (attested 1999).

nodes.label: James W. Benson
nodes.summary: James W. Benson is an Indologist and linguist who taught James McHugh and Susan J. Rosenfield. He held posts as Assistant Professor in Sanskrit at Harvard University (attested 1999–2003) and at Wolfson College, Oxford (attested 2004).

variants: 東京女子大学文理学部

nodes.label: Leela Aditi Wood
nodes.summary: Leela Aditi Wood works in archaeology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Michigan by 2005 under Luis Oscar Gómez and Martin J. Powers, and held a post at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute.

nodes.label: Walter M. Spink
nodes.summary: Walter M. Spink worked in history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Amherst College, he held posts at Brandeis University (~1956–1961) and served as Professor at the University of Michigan (attested 2005).

nodes.label: Thomas E. Crow
nodes.summary: Thomas E. Crow (born 1948) is a historian and archaeologist. Educated at Pomona College, he held posts at the University of Michigan from around 1986 to 1990 and at New York University around 2007.

nodes.label: Marvin Eisenberg
nodes.summary: Marvin Eisenberg was a history and archaeology scholar. He studied at the University of Pennsylvania (~1939–1943) and Princeton University (~1946–1954), and held a post at the University of Michigan (~1949–1993).

nodes.label: Cyrus Stearns
nodes.summary: Cyrus Stearns is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD from the University of Washington (-1996) under Leonard van der Kuijp. He has served as a translator for the Tsadra Foundation.

nodes.label: Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima
variants: Sde gzhung Rin po che, Kun dga' bstan pa'i nyi ma
nodes.image: Buddhist scholars - Dezhung Rinpoche III seated on a stool, Chris Wilkinson, student seated at the feet of his lama, wearing Buddhist robes, malas, likely Seattle, Washington, USA (16134833232) (cropped).jpg
nodes.summary: Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Gatön Ngawang Lekpa, Ngawang Nyima, and Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse Rinpoche, and participated in a research project at the University of Washington from 1960 to 1972.

nodes.label: Chogye Trichen Rinpoche
variants: Bco brgyad Khri chen Rin po che, Ngag dbang legs bshad rgya mtsho
Bco brgyad Khri chen Rin po che
nodes.summary: Chogye Trichen Rinpoche (1920–2007) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He became the Eighteenth Chogye Trichen at Nalendra Monastery in 1928, studied under teachers including Geshe Tsechok and the 13th Dalai Lama, and taught multiple scholars.

nodes.label: Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche
variants: Dil mgo Mkhyen brtse Rin po che, Rab gsal zla ba
nodes.description: Buddhist Vajrayana master, scholar, poet, and teacher (1910–1991)
nodes.summary: Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Shechen Gyaltsap Gyurme Pema Namgyal, Khenpo Shenga, and Dzongsar Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö (~1926-1959).

nodes.label: Jong-Nam Choi
nodes.summary: Jong-Nam Choi is a Buddhist studies scholar who attended Shitennoji University and completed a PhD at the University of Hamburg by 1998 under Lambert Schmithausen, also studying with S. A. Srinivasan, Albrecht Wezler, and David Seyfort Ruegg.

nodes.label: David Seyfort Ruegg
nodes.summary: David Seyfort Ruegg was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at EPHE and the University of Paris (~1953–1961), and held professorships at Leiden (1966–1972), Washington (1972–1984), Hamburg (1983–1990), and SOAS (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Edward Garrett
nodes.summary: Edward Garrett works in linguistics and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at UCLA (~1996–2001) under Carson Schütze and Dominique Sportiche, and undertook postdoctoral study under Anna Szabolcsi. He held research assistant posts at UCLA (1996–2000) and the University of Virginia (2000–2001).

nodes.label: Carson Schütze
nodes.summary: Carson Schütze is a linguist who studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology from 1992 to 1997. He held a post at the University of California, Los Angeles in 1997.

nodes.label: Dominique Sportiche
nodes.summary: Dominique Sportiche is a linguist who studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (~1979–1984). He held a post at the University of California, Los Angeles, beginning around 1988.

nodes.label: Anna Szabolcsi
nodes.summary: Anna Szabolcsi is a linguist who studied at Eötvös Loránd University (1972–1976). She later held faculty positions at the University of California, Los Angeles (~1990–1998) and New York University (~1998).

nodes.label: Naomi Appleton
nodes.summary: Naomi Appleton works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. She earned her D.Phil. at Oxford under Christopher Minkowski and David Gellner. She held a postdoctoral fellowship at Cardiff University and a Chancellor's Fellowship at the University of Edinburgh (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Lancaster University
variants: Department of Religious Studies in Lancaster
The Institute for Philosophy and Public Policy, Lancaster University

nodes.label: Laurie L. Patton
nodes.summary: Laurie L. Patton specializes in Indology and religious studies. Educated at Harvard (ca. 1979–1983) and the University of Chicago (ca. 1983–1991), she held posts at Emory University (ca. 1996–2011), Duke University (ca. 2011–2015), and Middlebury College (ca. 2015).

nodes.label: Anna Aurelia Esposito
nodes.summary: Anna Aurelia Esposito specializes in Indology. She earned an MA at the University of Tübingen in 1998, studied Indology and Cultural Anthropology at Heidelberg University, and served as Assistant Professor of Indology at the University of Würzburg (attested 2012–2015).

nodes.label: Jonathan Geen
nodes.summary: Jonathan Geen is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He earned his doctorate at McMaster University under Phyllis Granoff by 2001 and taught at McMaster University, Butler University, and the University of Rochester.

nodes.label: Phyllis Granoff
nodes.summary: Phyllis Granoff is an indologist and scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. Educated at Radcliffe College and Harvard (PhD ~1969–1973), she held professorships at McMaster University (~1976–2004) and Yale University (~2004–2020), among other posts.

nodes.label: McMaster University
variants: Department of Religious Studies at McMaster

nodes.label: Myoshin Fujitake
nodes.summary: Myoshin Fujitake (born 1956) is a Buddhist studies scholar. Fujitake has served as Professor of Shin Buddhist Studies at Otani University and was a committee member of the Otani Society (attested 2000).

nodes.label: Ryusei Keira
nodes.summary: Ryusei Keira specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his doctoral studies under supervisor Tom J. F. Tillemans at the University of Lausanne, finishing his thesis by 2003.

nodes.label: Koichi Shinohara
nodes.summary: Koichi Shinohara (born 1941) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He was a professor at McMaster University (~1972–2004) and later held positions at the University of Toronto Mississauga (attested 2004) and Yale University (~2004).

nodes.id: I:Okura Institute for the Study of Spiritual Culture
nodes.label: Okura Institute for the Study of Spiritual Culture
Hidetoshi Yoshizawa
nodes.summary: Hidetoshi Yoshizawa is a Buddhist studies scholar. He held positions at Taisho University as a researcher (attested 1998–2008) and as a chief research fellow (attested 2017).

nodes.label: University of Texas at Austin
variants: The University of Texas at Austin

nodes.label: Hiroko Matsuoka
nodes.summary: Hiroko Matsuoka works in Indology and philosophy. She was a doctoral student at Hiroshima University (attested 2006) and held a post at Leipzig University (attested 2016).

nodes.label: Yasuhiro Sueki
nodes.summary: Yasuhiro Sueki (born 1952) specializes in Buddhist studies and completed short-term study under George Baumann at Tübingen University Library. He held posts at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (~1979–1996) and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~1996).

nodes.label: Michael Torsten Much
nodes.summary: Michael Torsten Much (born 1953) is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology who studied under Ernst Steinkellner (attested 1991). He has held a post as a fellow at the University of Hamburg.

nodes.label: Helmut Tauscher
nodes.summary: Helmut Tauscher is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Ernst Steinkellner. He held a professorship at the University of Vienna (attested 2010–2015) and served as a Numata visiting professor at Leiden University.

nodes.label: Zeff Bjerken
nodes.summary: Zeff Bjerken works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He studied at UC Santa Barbara and the University of Michigan (PhD, 2001) under Donald S. Lopez Jr., and held a post at the College of Charleston (attested 2001).

nodes.label: T. Griffith Foulk
nodes.summary: T. Griffith Foulk is a Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology scholar. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan (~1978–1987) under Luis Oscar Gómez, later teaching there (~1987–1995) and at Sarah Lawrence College (~1995–2012).

nodes.label: Lopon Tenzin Namdak
nodes.summary: Lopon Tenzin Namdak (1927–2025) studied at Menri Monastery and under Sangye Tenzin and Gangru Tsultrim Gyaltsen. A specialist in Tibetology and religious studies, he founded Menri and Triten Norbutse monasteries, serving as Lopon at both.

nodes.label: Makoto Nagai
nodes.summary: Makoto Nagai was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo from around 1904 to 1907. He held positions at the University of Tokyo (~1920–1942) and Toyo University (~1943–1954), and taught Giyu Nishi.

nodes.label: Takashi Hidaka
nodes.summary: Takashi Hidaka is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He served as an open-call researcher at the Buddhist Art Resource Center in 2012 and as a part-time lecturer at Otani University (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Rajendra Chandra Hazra
nodes.summary: Rajendra Chandra Hazra (1904–1982) was an Indologist who completed his doctoral studies under Sushil Kumar De. He held posts at Jagannath University (1931), the University of Dhaka (1939–1949), and Sanskrit College and University (1951–1972).

nodes.label: Ramchandra Narayan Dandekar
nodes.summary: Ramchandra Narayan Dandekar (1909–2001) was an Indologist who studied at Mumbai and Heidelberg. He held posts at Fergusson College (~1932–1950), Savitribai Phule Pune University (~1949–1974), and served as Secretary at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (~1939–1993).

nodes.label: Izumi Hoshi
nodes.summary: Izumi Hoshi is a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics who studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1986 to 1995. She served as an associate professor at the Tokyo University of Foreign Studies from circa 2001 to 2017.

nodes.label: Michiyo Hoshi
nodes.summary: Michiyo Hoshi (born 1941) is a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics. She held posts at the Research Institute for Languages and Cultures of Asia and Africa and at Toyo Bunko (attested 2003).

nodes.label: Temba Gyaltsen
variants: テンバ・ギェンツェン

nodes.label: Jitsuaki Oshika
nodes.summary: Jitsuaki Oshika (b. 1919) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Tohoku University and served as a professor at Toyo University, attested in 1980–1981.

nodes.label: Esho Sasaki
nodes.summary: Esho Sasaki is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. Sasaki held posts as an associate professor at Ikenobo Junior College (attested 1979) and professor at Kyoto Women's University (attested 1991).

nodes.label: Ronald Y. Nakasone
nodes.summary: Ronald Y. Nakasone is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (circa 1975–1980). He held posts at the Institute of Buddhist Studies around 1987 and the Pacific School of Religion (attested 1996).

nodes.label: Hirofumi Isoda
nodes.summary: Hirofumi Isoda is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at Tohoku University (~1963–1966). He served at Tohoku University as lecturer (~1969–1974) and associate professor (~1974–2002), and is attested as professor emeritus at Shimane University (1974).

nodes.label: Werner Abraham
nodes.summary: Werner Abraham was a linguist who studied at the University of Vienna from 1962 to 1965. He held a post at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich in 2002.

nodes.label: Tarab Tulku
nodes.summary: Tarab Tulku (1934–2004) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as a curator at the Royal Danish Library (~1967–1998) and held a post at the University of Copenhagen (~1968–1998).

nodes.label: Hartmut Buescher
nodes.summary: Hartmut Buescher works in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Chandrabhal Tripathi and held posts at the University of Copenhagen and the Royal Danish Library.

nodes.label: Burkhard Quessel
nodes.summary: Burkhard Quessel is a scholar of Tibetology who studied at the University of Hamburg, where he was attested as a member in 1997. He later served as a curator at the British Library, attested from 2002 to 2012.

nodes.label: Kenneth G. Zysk
nodes.summary: Kenneth G. Zysk is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He earned an M.A. at UC Santa Barbara and a Ph.D. at Australian National University, holding posts at UCLA, Eastern Michigan University (attested 1989), and the University of Copenhagen (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Christian K. Wedemeyer
nodes.summary: Christian K. Wedemeyer is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. He earned degrees from Wesleyan University and Columbia University (PhD ~1992–1999 under Robert A. F. Thurman) and has served as Professor at the University of Chicago since circa 2003.

nodes.label: Ole Holten Pind
nodes.summary: Ole Holten Pind (1945–2018) worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He completed his doctoral degree at the University of Vienna under Ernst Steinkellner by 2009 and served as a professor at the University of Hamburg.

nodes.label: John Ronald Newman
nodes.summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology, Newman completed his Ph.D. at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1987 under Geshe Lhundub Sopa. He was an assistant professor of Asian religions at the New College of Florida (attested 1996–2000).

nodes.label: Kyogaku Dendo Kenkyu Senta
variants: 浄土真宗本願寺派教学伝道研究センター

nodes.label: Yasuhiro Ueno
nodes.summary: Yasuhiro Ueno is a Buddhist studies scholar who pursued doctoral studies at Kyoto University (attested 2003–2004). He served as a commissioned researcher at Koyasan University (attested 2004).

nodes.label: Eric David Mortensen
nodes.summary: Eric David Mortensen works in Tibetology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Harvard University (attested 2003), where he was supervised by Leonard van der Kuijp, Michael Witzel, and Kimberley C. Patton.

nodes.label: Kimberley C. Patton
nodes.summary: Kimberley C. Patton (b. 1958) is a religious studies scholar who completed her dissertation at Harvard University (~1981–1992). She was an assistant professor at Harvard around 1990 and an associate at the American School of Classical Studies at Athens in 1991.

nodes.label: Christopher S. George
nodes.summary: Christopher S. George, founder of the American Institute of Buddhist Studies, works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Columbia under Royal W. Weiler, learned from Padma Gyaltsen and Geshe Wangyal, and became a professor at IASWR.

nodes.label: Joe Bransford Wilson
nodes.summary: Joe Bransford Wilson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and the University of Virginia (PhD 1984), later teaching at Virginia (1981–1985) and UNC Wilmington (attested 1994–2001).

nodes.label: Grigorij Maksimovič Bongard-Levin
nodes.summary: Grigorij Maksimovič Bongard-Levin (1933–2008) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Central Asian studies. Educated at Moscow State University, where he later taught (~1978–2008), he also served at the Institute of Oriental Studies (~1956–2008).

nodes.label: Ryojun Mitomo
nodes.summary: Ryojun Mitomo is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as a professor at Rissho University Junior College (attested 1996) and as a professor in the Faculty of Social Welfare at Rissho University (attested 2001).

nodes.label: Raghu Vira
nodes.summary: Raghu Vira (1902–1963) was a scholar of Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of the Punjab (~1920–1924) and Leiden University (~1928–1930), and taught Lokesh Chandra.

nodes.label: Lokesh Chandra
nodes.jawiki: ローケーシュ・チャンドラ
nodes.summary: Lokesh Chandra (born 1927) is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology scholar. He studied under Raghu Vira, at University of the Punjab, and completed a PhD at Utrecht University (~1949–1950), serving as Secretary and Director at the International Academy of Indian Culture.

nodes.label: Richard F. Nance
nodes.summary: Richard F. Nance is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies who completed his PhD at the University of Chicago in 2004. He taught Cameron Bailey and became an assistant professor at Indiana University (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Makio Ueno
nodes.summary: Makio Ueno is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Otani University by 2009. He later held posts at Otani University, attested as an assistant professor (助教) from 2010 to 2012 and attested again in 2022.

nodes.label: Atsushi Ibuki
nodes.summary: Atsushi Ibuki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University and held a professorship at Toyo University (attested 2015).

nodes.id: I:Japanese Association for Esoteric Buddhist Studies
nodes.label: Japanese Association for Esoteric Buddhist Studies
Tomoyuki Komine
nodes.summary: Tomoyuki Komine is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University and held a post there as a part-time lecturer (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Ruriko Sakuma
nodes.summary: Ruriko Sakuma works in Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at Nagoya University, she held posts as a permanent researcher and director at the Eastern Institute and as a researcher at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute, both attested in 2015.

nodes.label: Daiju Sasaki
nodes.summary: Daiju Sasaki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University (~1996–2007). In 2015, he held posts as a part-time lecturer at Taisho University and as a full-time lecturer at Chisan Denpoin.

nodes.label: Fumio Shoji
nodes.summary: Fumio Shoji (b. 1979) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Rissho University (~1998–2007), where he later served as an assistant professor in the Faculty of Buddhist Studies (~2012).

nodes.label: Kenta Suzuki
nodes.summary: Kenta Suzuki is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied at Kyoto University (~1994–1998) and the University of Tokyo (~1998–2005). He became an associate professor at Hokkaido Musashi Women's Junior College around 2012.

nodes.label: Hokkaido Musashi Women's Junior College
variants: 北海道武蔵女子短期大学

nodes.label: Kimiaki Tanaka
nodes.summary: Kimiaki Tanaka (b. 1955) works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. After studying at the University of Tokyo (~1974–1983) and under Ratnakaji Bajracharya, he held posts at the University of Tokyo, Eastern Institute, Toho Gakuin, and Keio University.

nodes.label: Humanities Information Studies Institute
variants: 一般財団法人人文情報学研究所

nodes.label: Nobumasa Miyazaki
nodes.summary: Nobumasa Miyazaki specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a doctorate at the University of Tokyo (~2005-2011) and held posts at Toyo University (~2011-2014), Tokyo University of Agriculture (attested 2015), and the University of Tokyo (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Masahide Mori
nodes.summary: Masahide Mori specializes in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Nagoya University (~1985-1987) and under Tadeusz Skorupski at the University of London/SOAS (1988-1997). His academic posts include Koyasan University (1994), Nagoya University (~1996-2000), and Kanazawa University (~2000-present).

nodes.label: Kazuyoshi Hotta
nodes.summary: Kazuyoshi Hotta works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He pursued doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo and served the University of Tokyo Young Buddhist Association (attested 2007), later holding a term-limited assistant professorship at Otani University (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Steven Neal Weinberger
nodes.summary: Steven Neal Weinberger specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Amherst College and the University of Virginia, completing his PhD under Jeffrey Hopkins alongside numerous traditional teachers, and held a post at Virginia (attested 2006).

nodes.label: Sakya Trizin
nodes.summary: Sakya Trizin is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Khenpo Appey, Tritsho Khenpo Rinchen, and the 14th Dalai Lama, Tenzin Gyatso.

nodes.label: Ralf Kramer
nodes.summary: Ralf Kramer (born 1971) is a Tibetologist. He studied at the University of Hamburg under David P. Jackson and at the University of London, and served as Aris Librarian for Tibetan & Himalayan Studies at Bodleian Libraries (~2003).

nodes.label: Achim Bayer
nodes.summary: Achim Bayer is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who completed his MA under David P. Jackson and his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen (2005). He was a research associate at LMU Munich (2004–2006).

nodes.label: Lore Sander
nodes.summary: Lore Sander (1936–2023) specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, having studied under Ernst Waldschmidt. She served as Curator at the Museum für Asiatische Kunst and held posts at Humboldt, Munich, and Free University of Berlin.

Department for the Study of Religions, Freie Universität Berlin

nodes.label: Hoshu Mitsuhara
nodes.summary: Hoshu Mitsuhara (1916–2004) was a Buddhist studies scholar who served on the faculty at Koyasan University, where he was attested as professor in 1982 and emeritus professor in 2004.

nodes.label: Hans T. Bakker
nodes.description: b. 1948; teaches Sanskrit, Philosophy, and Indian Religions, U. of Groningen
nodes.summary: Hans T. Bakker works in Indology and religious studies. He studied under Jacob Ensink and served at the University of Groningen from ~1982 to ~1995, later working as a curator at the British Museum (~2014–2019).

nodes.label: Arjo Vanderjagt
nodes.summary: Arjo Vanderjagt is a philosopher who studied at Franklin Academy, Prattsburgh Central School, and the University of Groningen (1971–1981). He held academic posts at Radboud University (1976–1979), Utrecht University (2007), and the University of Groningen (1994–2009).

nodes.label: Seiji Kumagai
nodes.summary: Seiji Kumagai specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He completed his PhD at Kyoto University (~2003–2008) and became an associate professor there around 2014.

nodes.label: Takatsugu Hayashi
nodes.summary: Hayashi worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at the University of Delhi (attested 1996). He held posts at Tohoku University (attested 1997), Sendai College (associate professor attested 2008), and Hosen Gakuen College (professor attested 2015).

nodes.label: Yoshio Kawakatsu
nodes.summary: Yoshio Kawakatsu (1922–1984) worked in Sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1945–1948) and under Paul Demiéville (~1958–1961), and he held an academic post at Kyoto University from ~1952 to 1984.

nodes.label: Shin'ichi Hisamatsu
nodes.summary: Shin'ichi Hisamatsu (1889–1980) studied philosophy and Buddhist studies at Kyoto University (~1915–1918) under Kitaro Nishida and Shozan Ikegami. He held posts at Ryukoku University (~1919–1949), Kyoto University (1935–1949), Hanazono University (~1949–1963), and Harvard University (1958).

nodes.label: Serinity Young
nodes.summary: Serinity Young was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. She earned her Ph.D. from Columbia University in 1990 under Alex Wayman and studied under Vidya Dehejia, later working at the American Museum of Natural History and Southern Methodist University in 2000.

nodes.label: Carole McGranahan
nodes.summary: Carole McGranahan is a scholar of Tibetology, history, and archaeology. She studied at Colgate University and earned her PhD at the University of Michigan (2001) under Nicholas B. Dirks and Ann Laura Stoler, later holding posts at the University of Colorado Boulder.

nodes.label: Ann Laura Stoler
nodes.summary: Ann Laura Stoler works in history, archaeology, and other fields. She studied at Columbia University (~1972–1982) and later held academic posts at the University of Michigan (1989–2003) and The New School (2004).

nodes.label: Dawa Norbu
nodes.summary: Dawa Norbu was a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Delhi (~1970–1974) and UC Berkeley (~1976–1982), and held posts at San Francisco State University, the University of San Francisco, CIIS, and Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1984–2006).

nodes.label: Jawaharlal Nehru University
variants: Centre for Historical Studies, Jawaharlal Nehru University
Centre for South, Central, South-East Asian & South-West Pacific Studies

nodes.label: Samuel M. Grupper
nodes.summary: Samuel M. Grupper works in Iranian and Central Asian studies, sinology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Indiana University, studying under teachers Irving Yucheng Lo and Philip West.

nodes.label: Shoko Takeuchi
nodes.summary: Shoko Takeuchi (1910–1999) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University. He served as professor emeritus at Ryukoku University (attested 1987–1995, 2009) and taught Koyo Shimizu, Toshihide Mori, and Shodo Fujita.

nodes.label: Yasutoshi Murakami
nodes.summary: Yasutoshi Murakami is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University. He has held posts at Yamaguchi University, Koyasan University, and served as president of the Association of Esoteric Buddhist Studies (attested 2004).

nodes.label: Takatoshi Ito
nodes.summary: Takatoshi Ito worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He held a position as professor at Komazawa University (attested 1978–1981 and 1991).

nodes.label: Guangchang Fang
nodes.summary: Guangchang Fang is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He worked as a researcher at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences from around 1986 to 2004 and became a professor at Shanghai Normal University around 2004.

nodes.label: Michael J. Walsh
nodes.summary: Michael J. Walsh is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at the University of Cape Town (~1986–1989) and the University of California, Santa Barbara (~1991–1994), completing his doctorate under William F. Powell (~1994–2000).

nodes.label: Atsuuji Ashikaga
nodes.summary: Atsuuji Ashikaga studied at Doshisha University and under Ryosaburo Sakaki (~1920–1924). Working in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics, he served as a professor at Kyoto University (~1950–1965).

nodes.label: Yasuke Ikari
nodes.summary: Yasuke Ikari (born 1940) is an Indologist who studied under Masaaki Hattori and completed a PhD at the University of Chicago (~1969–1978). He held posts at Kindai University, Harvard University, and Kyoto University, where he became professor emeritus in ~2004.

nodes.label: T. R. Chintamani
nodes.summary: T. R. Chintamani was an Indology scholar who studied under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He served as Manager and Correspondent for the Journal of Oriental Research, Madras (~1927) and as Senior Lecturer in Sanskrit at the University of Madras (attested 1938–1951).

nodes.label: T. Chandrasekharan
nodes.summary: T. Chandrasekharan was an Indology scholar who studied as a pupil under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He served as Professor of History of Sanskrit Language and Literature at The Madras Sanskrit College (attested 1951), succeeding T. R. Chintamani.

nodes.label: Ryuichi Kogachi
nodes.summary: Ryuichi Kogachi (born 1970) is a Sinologist. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1989–1999) and held posts at the Kyoto University Research Centre for the Cultural Sciences (~2001) and Kyoto University (~2001–2007; associate professor ~2007).

nodes.label: Niigata University
variants: 新潟大学人文社会教育科学系

nodes.label: Shoshin Kuwayama
nodes.summary: Shoshin Kuwayama (b. 1938) works in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University (~1957–1961) and later served there as assistant professor (~1973–1989).

nodes.label: Kiyoshi Okano
nodes.summary: Kiyoshi Okano (born 1956) is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Bhikkhu Pāsādika. Okano has held posts at Kyushu University as associate professor (attested 2002) and professor (attested 2013–2024).

nodes.label: Bhikkhu Pāsādika
nodes.summary: Bhikkhu Pāsādika (born 1939) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who studied at Magadh University. His academic posts include Professor at the University of Marburg (~1993), as well as positions at Kassel and Bergen.

nodes.label: Akhu Gungthang Lodrö Gyatso
variants: Akhu gung thang blo gros tshang

nodes.label: Ho-chin Yang
nodes.summary: Ho-chin Yang is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at the University of Washington under Leonard van der Kuijp (attested 1994).

nodes.label: Susumu Shimazono

nodes.label: Shinjo Hinonishi

nodes.label: Shintaro Kitano
nodes.summary: Shintaro Kitano is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Kazunobu Matsuda (attested 2005). He was a researcher at Taisho University (attested 2005) and a part-time lecturer at Kyushu University (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Akira Mukai
nodes.summary: Akira Mukai is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed doctoral coursework at Hokkaido University. He served as an assistant at Hokkaido University (attested 1978) and as a professor at Hokkaido Musashi Women's Junior College (attested 1999).

nodes.label: Klaus Wille

nodes.label: Hironori Tanaka
nodes.summary: Hironori Tanaka is a scholar in Buddhist studies. Tanaka studied as a PhD student at Bukkyo University (attested 2015–2020) and also held an academic post there.

nodes.label: Yuto Kawamura
nodes.summary: Yuto Kawamura works in Indology and linguistics. He was a postdoctoral fellow at Kyoto University (2015–2018) and held posts at Hiroshima University (attested 2013–2020) and the University of Oxford (attested 2019).

nodes.label: Laura Harrington

nodes.label: Charles Goodman

nodes.summary: Allan Gibbard (b. 1942) is a philosopher who studied at Swarthmore College (~1960–1964) and Harvard University (~1965–1971). He held positions at the University of Chicago (~1969–1977), the University of Pittsburgh (~1974–1975), and the University of Michigan (~1977).

nodes.label: Kazuhiro Furuta
nodes.summary: Kazuhiro Furuta (born 1940) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He was affiliated with the Otani Society as editor and publisher (attested 1991) and served as dean at Otani University (attested 1998).

nodes.label: Stephen F. Teiser
nodes.summary: Stephen F. Teiser works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He studied at Oberlin College and Princeton University (PhD ~1981–1986), subsequently holding faculty posts at Middlebury College (~1986–1988) and Princeton University (~1988–).

nodes.label: Franciscus Verellen

nodes.label: Thomas Freeman Yarnall

nodes.label: Wayne Proudfoot

nodes.label: Mario D'Amato

nodes.label: Lynn A. Struve
nodes.summary: Lynn A. Struve is a scholar of Sinology and history/archaeology. She studied at the University of Washington (~1963–1967) and the University of Michigan (~1968–1976), and held a faculty post at Indiana University from ~1977 to 2010.

nodes.label: Yoshiyuki Kawazoe

nodes.summary: Harumi Hirano Ziegler is a scholar of Buddhist studies. She earned her MA (completed 1994) and PhD (completed 2001) from the University of California, Los Angeles, studying under doctoral supervisor Robert E. Buswell Jr.

nodes.summary: Tairyo Makita studied at Bukkyo University and Kyoto University (~1934-1939). In Buddhist studies and sinology, he served as professor at Kyoto University (~1957-1976), taught at Gifu Shotoku Gakuen University, and became president of Saitama Institute of Technology (attested 2001).

nodes.label: Samten Gyaltsen Karmay
nodes.summary: Samten Gyaltsen Karmay specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. After earning his MPhil and PhD at SOAS under David Snellgrove, he held posts at SOAS, CNRS (Directeur de Recherche from 1980), and served as president of the IATS (1996).

nodes.label: Klemens Karlsson

nodes.label: Ivette Vargas-O'Bryan
nodes.summary: Ivette Vargas-O'Bryan works in Buddhist, Tibetan, and religious studies. She earned a PhD from Harvard in 2003 under Leonard van der Kuijp, and held a fellowship post at Grinnell College.

nodes.label: Keiji Nishitani
nodes.summary: Keiji Nishitani (1900–1990) was a philosopher and religious studies scholar. He studied at Kyoto University (~1921–1924) under Kitaro Nishida, and held appointments at Kyoto University (~1935–1963) and Otani University (~1963–1971).

His academic posts included Fourth Higher School, Otani University, and Kyoto University, where he served as Professor of Philosophy (1912–1927).

nodes.label: Kenneth K. Inada
nodes.summary: Kenneth K. Inada (1923–2011) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He was a professor at the University at Buffalo (attested 1983–1999) and served as chair of the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research (1996–1999).

nodes.label: Todd A. Gibson
nodes.summary: Todd A. Gibson is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. He studied under György Kara and earned his PhD at Indiana University (attested 1991).

nodes.label: Jongcheol Lee
nodes.summary: Jongcheol Lee is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Seoul National University and completed a PhD at the University of Tokyo in 1994 under Yasunori Ejima. He held posts at the University of Mysore and the Academy of Korean Studies.

nodes.label: Thomas A. Forsthoefel
nodes.summary: Thomas A. Forsthoefel works in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Georgetown University, Loyola University Chicago, and the University of Chicago under Paul J. Griffiths, later serving as associate professor of religious studies at Mercyhurst University.

nodes.label: Katherine Janiec Jones
nodes.summary: Katherine Janiec Jones is an Indology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies scholar. She studied at Davidson College and earned her PhD at the University of Chicago under doctoral supervisor Paul J. Griffiths, also studying under William K. Mahony and Karl A. Plank.

nodes.label: W. Randolph Kloetzli
variants: W・ランドルフ・クレツリ
nodes.summary: W. Randolph Kloetzli earned a PhD at the University of Chicago in 1964 and studied under teachers including Paul Tillich and Mircea Eliade. He lectured at American University, George Washington University, and Dartmouth College.

nodes.label: Frank E. Reynolds
variants: フランク・レイノルド

nodes.label: J. A. B. van Buitenen
variants: J・A・B・ファン・ブイテネン
nodes.summary: J. A. B. van Buitenen was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at Utrecht University (~1946–1953) under Jan Gonda (~1948–1953). He held posts at Utrecht University (~1953–1956) and the University of Chicago (~1959–1979).

nodes.label: Paul Tillich
nodes.summary: Paul Tillich was a philosopher and religious studies scholar. He studied at Berlin, Tübingen, Breslau, and Halle-Wittenberg. His academic career included posts at Berlin (1918–1924), Frankfurt (1929–1933), Union Theological Seminary (1933–1955), Harvard (~1955–1962), and Chicago (~1962–1965).

nodes.label: Mircea Eliade
variants: ミルチア・エリアーデ
nodes.jawiki: ミルチャ・エリアーデ
nodes.description: Romanian-American historian, writer, philosopher and professor at the University of Chicago (1907–1986)
nodes.summary: Mircea Eliade was a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Bucharest and the University of Calcutta under Surendranath Dasgupta, later holding professorships at the University of Bucharest (~1933–1938), University of Paris (attested 1965), and University of Chicago (~1956–1986).

nodes.label: Dartmouth College
variants: Department of Religion at Dartmouth College

nodes.label: Eiichi Yamaguchi
variants: やまぐち えいいち
nodes.summary: Eiichi Yamaguchi works in the fields of Indology and philosophy. He was a graduate student at Kyushu University (attested 1986–1990) and later served as a research assistant there (attested 1991).

nodes.label: Gyosho Takahashi
nodes.summary: Gyosho Takahashi is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor at Minobusan University, attested in 1992 and 1996.

nodes.label: Toshiya Unebe
nodes.summary: Toshiya Unebe is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Musashi Tachikawa. He served as an associate professor in Indian Studies at Nagoya University (attested 2009).

nodes.label: Chizuko Yoshimizu
nodes.summary: Chizuko Yoshimizu works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. She studied at the University of Tokyo and University of Vienna, worked at Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 1991), and became a professor at University of Tsukuba (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Hiroshi Nemoto
nodes.summary: Hiroshi Nemoto works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. Nemoto earned an MA at Hiroshima University and later served as a professor there (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Kazuyoshi Kino
nodes.summary: Kazuyoshi Kino (1922–2013) specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Shudo Junior & Senior High School and the University of Tokyo (~1945–1948), holding posts at Hosen Gakuen College (~1965–1985) and Shogen Junior College.

nodes.label: Hōkai
nodes.summary: Hōkai (1768–1834) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Hōgetsu and Zuihe.

nodes.label: Masao Abe
nodes.description: Japanese Buddhist, professor in religious studies
nodes.summary: Masao Abe specialized in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Osaka City University and Kyoto University under Hajime Tanabe, Shin'ichi Hisamatsu, Keiji Nishitani, and Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki. He held professorships at Nara University of Education, Kyoto University, and Pacific School of Religion.

nodes.label: Siglinde Dietz
nodes.summary: Siglinde Dietz works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She completed her PhD under Michael Hahn at the University of Bonn in 1980 and held a post at the University of Göttingen (attested 1990).
