nodes.label: Shripad Krishna Belvalkar
nodes.description: Indian historian and scholar of Sanskrit
nodes.summary: Shripad Krishna Belvalkar (1881–1967) was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under Kashinath Bapu Pathak (~1902–1904). He served as General Secretary of the All-India Oriental Conference (~1920–1943) and Professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College (attested 1929).

nodes.label: Sojo Hirano
nodes.summary: Sojo Hirano was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as an assistant professor at Hanazono University (attested 1974) and as shike at Zuigan-ji (attested 1992–1996). He also taught Sonja Arntzen.

nodes.label: Hachiro Hasebe
nodes.summary: Hachiro Hasebe (born 1950) is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at Keio University (~1969–1973) and served as an associate professor at Komazawa University (~1993–2000).

nodes.label: Xuesong Zhang
nodes.summary: Xuesong Zhang studied at The Chinese University of Hong Kong under doctoral supervisor Xueyu (PhD attested 2008). Specializing in Buddhist and religious studies, Zhang was an associate professor at Renmin University of China, attested in 2015.

nodes.label: Hsing Yun
nodes.summary: Hsing Yun (1927–2023) worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Yin Shun and at the University of Hong Kong, founded Fo Guang Shan and University of the West, and held a post at National Taiwan University.

nodes.label: Taixu
nodes.summary: Taixu studied under Jichan (~1904-1907) in Buddhist studies. He founded the Minnan Buddhist Institute (1918; leader in 1927), Wuchang Buddhist Institute (1922), Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Institute (1930-1931), and Tianning Buddhist College (1931).

nodes.id: I:Tohoku Association of Indian and Religious Studies
nodes.label: Tohoku Association of Indian and Religious Studies
Takao Yamagata
nodes.summary: Takao Yamagata worked in religious studies, completing his studies at Tohoku University (~1952–1961). He held a post at Miyagi Gakuin Women's University (~1970–2002) and served as president of the Association for the Study of Indian Religions (attested 1997).

nodes.label: Alfred Foucher
nodes.jawiki: アルフレッド・フーシェ
nodes.summary: Alfred Foucher (1865–1952) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure in 1885 and held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1901–1928) and the University of Paris (~1907–1936).

nodes.label: Marcelle Lalou
nodes.summary: Marcelle Lalou was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Paris and under Sylvain Lévi, Jacques Bacot, Paul Pelliot, and Jean Przyluski. She held a post at École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1926–1967).

nodes.label: Jean Przyluski
nodes.description: French linguist and scholar of religion
nodes.summary: Jean Przyluski studied at the EPHE (~1913–1923), working in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He founded Bibliographie bouddhique and held posts at INALCO (1923), the EPHE (~1927–1930), and the Collège de France (~1930–1944).

nodes.label: Velcheru Narayana Rao
nodes.description: Indian author, critic, and literary translator

nodes.label: José Ignacio Cabezón
nodes.summary: José Ignacio Cabezón works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, having earned degrees from Caltech and the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa. He held posts at Iliff School of Theology, the University of Denver, and UC Santa Barbara.

nodes.label: Takanobu Takahashi
nodes.summary: Takanobu Takahashi worked in Indology and linguistics. He held posts at Shitennoji University and served as an associate professor at the University of Tokyo from ~1996 to 2017.

nodes.label: Tadashi Toda
nodes.summary: Tadashi Toda is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under teachers Keiki Higashimoto and Kogen Mizuno.

nodes.label: Kevin A. Vose
nodes.summary: Kevin A. Vose is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He completed his B.A. at Bates College and his M.A. and Ph.D. at the University of Virginia, studying under Jeffrey Hopkins and Ngawang Jinpa.

nodes.label: Ngawang Jinpa
nodes.summary: Ngawang Jinpa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Drepung Loseling Monastery. He taught Kevin A. Vose and Samdhong Rinpoche and was a professor at St. Joseph's College, Darjeeling, attested in 1995.

nodes.label: National Taiwan University
variants: Department of Philosophy, National Taiwan University
台灣大學音樂學研究所

nodes.label: Ryusho Onami
nodes.summary: Ryusho Onami (born 1926) is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied under Taishun Mibu and held a post as lecturer at Taisho University (attested 1985).

nodes.label: Helmut Eimer
nodes.summary: Helmut Eimer was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied under Frank-Richard Hamm (~1968–1973) and held a post as Dr. at the University of Bonn (attested 1991–2010).

nodes.label: Esho Yamaguchi
nodes.summary: Esho Yamaguchi is an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Kyoto University from circa 1938 to 1942. Yamaguchi held positions at Ritsumeikan University and served as a professor at Osaka University (attested 1980–1984).

nodes.label: Kazuo Osumi
nodes.summary: Kazuo Osumi (1932–2024) worked in history, archaeology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1951–1955) and held posts at Hokkaido University (~1973–1985) and Tokyo Woman's Christian University (~1985–2003).

nodes.label: Chandrabhal Tripathi
nodes.summary: Chandrabhal Tripathi (1929–1996) was an indologist who earned his PhD at the University of Göttingen under Ernst Waldschmidt (~1957–1960). He held posts at Göttingen, Cologne, Humboldt University of Berlin (attested 1985), and the Free University of Berlin (~1977–1994).

nodes.label: Romila Thapar
nodes.summary: Romila Thapar is a historian and Indologist who studied at Panjab University and the University of London under A. L. Basham. She held posts at the University of Delhi (~1963–1970) and Jawaharlal Nehru University (attested 2001).

nodes.label: Arthur Llewellyn Basham
nodes.summary: Arthur Llewellyn Basham was an Indologist and historian. After studying at SOAS under Lionel David Barnett, he held professorships at the University of London, SOAS (~1958–1965), Australian National University (~1965–1978), and the Asiatic Society (~1985–1986).

nodes.label: Masatoshi Konishi
nodes.summary: Masatoshi Konishi (1938–2020) was an Indology, history, and archaeology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1957 to 1965. He later held a post at Rikkyo University from circa 1972 to 2004.

nodes.label: Toshio Yamazaki
nodes.summary: Toshio Yamazaki (1916–1994) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He held posts at the Tokyo Institute of Technology and Hannan University, and was a professor at the University of Tokyo (~1957–1977) and Chuo University (~1977–1987).

nodes.label: Myles Dillon
nodes.description: Irish academic, historian, philologist and celticist (1900–1972)
nodes.summary: Myles Dillon (1900–1972) was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at University College Dublin (~1919–1922). He held academic posts at Trinity College Dublin, University College Dublin, University of Wisconsin-Madison, and the Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies (~1949–1972).

nodes.label: James Kenneth Powell II
nodes.summary: James Kenneth Powell II is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Northwestern, the University of Chicago, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (PhD, 1998). His teachers included David Tracy, Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Isshi Yamada, and David M. Knipe.

nodes.label: Chang-geun Hwang
nodes.summary: Chang-geun Hwang is a scholar of buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 2000, studying under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Minoru Kiyota, and Morten Schlütter.

nodes.label: Hugh B. Urban
nodes.summary: Hugh B. Urban is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies under Wendy Doniger, Bruce Lincoln, and Tony K. Stewart, and served as Associate Professor at Ohio State University (~2004–2008).

nodes.label: Bruce Lincoln
nodes.summary: Bruce Lincoln, specializing in religious studies, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, studied at Haverford and Chicago under Mircea Eliade (~1970–1976). He held posts at the University of Minnesota (~1976–1992) and the University of Chicago (~1992).

nodes.label: Jeffrey J. Kripal
nodes.summary: Jeffrey J. Kripal specializes in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Conception Seminary College (~1985–1989) and the University of Chicago (~1989–1993, PhD). In ~2002, he was Lynette S. Autrey Associate Professor in the Humanities at Rice University.

nodes.label: Tony K. Stewart
nodes.summary: Tony K. Stewart is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at Western Kentucky University (~1972–1976). He held posts at North Carolina State University (~1986–2011) and Vanderbilt University (~2011).

nodes.label: Joachim Prandstetter
nodes.summary: Joachim Prandstetter is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He completed his Magister degree at the University of Vienna by 1994, studying under Gerhard Oberhammer.

nodes.label: Ferdinand Diederich Lessing
nodes.image: Professor Ferdinand Deiderich Lessing, Univ. of California, Berkeley. 1952.jpg
nodes.summary: Ferdinand Diederich Lessing was a scholar of sinology, Tibetology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He served as a teacher at the Humboldt University of Berlin (~1925–1935) and at the University of California, Berkeley (~1935–1952).

nodes.label: Ronald M. Davidson
nodes.summary: Ronald M. Davidson works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned his PhD from the University of California, Berkeley in 1985, studying under numerous scholars including Padmanabh S. Jaini, and held a post at Fairfield University (attested 2002–2005).

nodes.label: Gil Fronsdal
nodes.summary: Gil Fronsdal (born 1954) is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned a PhD at Stanford University (~1989–1998) and held posts at the Sati Center for Buddhist Studies (~1997) and Insight Meditation Center (~2001).

nodes.label: Bernard Faure
nodes.jawiki: ベルナール・フォール
nodes.summary: Bernard Faure specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. After doctoral studies at the University of Paris and Paris Diderot University, he held posts at Cornell University (~1983–1987), Stanford University (~1987–2006), and Columbia University (~2006).

nodes.label: David W. Chappell
nodes.summary: David W. Chappell was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology who completed doctoral work at Yale University (~1968–1976). He served as a professor at the University of Hawaii (~1972–2002) and held a post at Soka University of America (~2002–2004).

nodes.label: Vesna A. Wallace
nodes.summary: Vesna A. Wallace (born 1952) is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies scholar who completed her doctorate at UC Berkeley. She held positions at UC Berkeley, the University of Oxford (until 2010), and UC Santa Barbara (attested 2007–2014).

nodes.label: Anthony Kennedy Warder
nodes.summary: Anthony Kennedy Warder (1924–2013) studied Indology and Buddhist studies at SOAS University of London under John Brough. He held faculty posts at the University of Edinburgh (circa 1955–1963) and the University of Toronto (circa 1964–1990).

nodes.label: Mitsuyo Demoto
nodes.summary: Mitsuyo Demoto is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University and held an affiliation at the University of Marburg (attested 2024).

nodes.label: Peter Skilling
variants: ピーター・スキリング
nodes.summary: Peter Skilling works in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning a PhD from École Pratique des Hautes Études by 2004. He founded the Fragile Palm Leaves Foundation and taught at Chulalongkorn University and École française d'Extrême-Orient (2009).

nodes.label: Kunio Harikai
nodes.summary: Kunio Harikai (born 1942) is an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Kyushu University under Seiren Matsunami and Shoren Ihara. He served as an associate professor at Saga Medical School (~1978–1996).

nodes.label: Futoshi Omae
nodes.summary: Futoshi Omae is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He served as a lecturer at Kyushu University (attested 1986–1991) and held a post at Shimane Prefectural Junior College (attested 1997).

nodes.label: Eki Nakayama
nodes.summary: Eki Nakayama is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University (attested 2020) and held a DC2 special research fellowship with the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (attested 2020).

nodes.label: Hisashi Matsumura
nodes.summary: Hisashi Matsumura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held posts at the Australian National University (attested 1982) and Kobe Shinwa University as an assistant professor (attested 1996).

nodes.label: Yoshinobu Kimoto
nodes.summary: Yoshinobu Kimoto (born 1950) is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Japanology. He held appointments as an assistant professor at Yonezawa Women's Junior College (attested 1989) and at Koshien Junior College.

nodes.label: Yonezawa Women's Junior College
variants: 山形県立米沢女子短期大学

nodes.label: Kazuo Oyamada
nodes.summary: Kazuo Oyamada (born 1952) specializes in Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Tamagawa University (~1971–1975) and held a post at Rissho University (~1995).

nodes.label: Koyo Shimizu
nodes.summary: Koyo Shimizu is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Shoko Takeuchi. He served as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University, attested in 1995.

variants: ネパール国立古文書館

nodes.label: Ernst Waldschmidt
nodes.summary: Ernst Waldschmidt was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Central Asian studies. He studied under Heinrich Lüders, August Hermann Francke, and Albert Grünwedel, and at Göttingen, later holding posts at the Göttingen Academy (1936) and Göttingen University (~1936–1965).

nodes.label: Kyushu Otani Junior College
variants: 九州大谷短期大学仏教科

nodes.label: Gerald James Larson
nodes.summary: Gerald James Larson worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at Union Theological Seminary and Columbia University, later holding posts at the University of California, Santa Barbara (~1970–1995) and Indiana University (~1995–2003).

nodes.label: Toshiki Osada
nodes.summary: Toshiki Osada specializes in linguistics and Indology, having studied at Hokkaido University (~1973–1977). He served as professor and project leader at the Research Institute for Humanity and Nature (~2003–2020) and at Kyoto University of the Arts (~2020).

nodes.label: Tomoyasu Oshima
nodes.summary: Tomoyasu Oshima specializes in Indology and linguistics. Attested in 2012, Oshima studied under Toshifumi Goto and held a part-time lecturer post at Kyoto University.

nodes.label: Naoko Nishimura
nodes.summary: Naoko Nishimura is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Toshifumi Goto and earned her PhD from Tohoku University in 2002. She later served there as a specialized researcher (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Sumitra Mangesh Katre
nodes.summary: Sumitra Mangesh Katre (1906–1998) worked in linguistics and Indology, earning a PhD from the University of London (~1928–1931). He held posts at Sir Parashurambhau College, Deccan College as Chair of Indo-European Philology (1942–1971), and the University of Texas at Austin.

nodes.label: Satoshi Naiki
nodes.summary: Satoshi Naiki specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from Kyoto University, where he served as an assistant professor at the Center for Cultural Heritage Studies (attested 2016–2020).

nodes.label: Koji Takahashi
nodes.summary: Koji Takahashi (1934–2023) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Bukkyo University (~1953–1957). He later served at Bukkyo University as an assistant professor (~1969–1978) and professor (~1978–2005).

nodes.label: University at Buffalo
variants: ニューヨーク州立大学バッファロー校
University of Buffalo, State University of New York
State University of New York at Buffalo
State University of New York at Buffalo Law School
University at Buffalo, The State University of New York

nodes.label: Sonam Gyatso
nodes.summary: Sonam Gyatso is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He worked as a research assistant at the Toyo Bunko and held a professorship at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Chijo Akamatsu
nodes.summary: Chijo Akamatsu (1886–1960) was a religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University (~1910–1913). He was appointed the first professor at Keijo Imperial University in 1927 and held a post at Yamaguchi University (~1949–1957).

nodes.label: Kazuhiko Yoshida
nodes.summary: Kazuhiko Yoshida (born 1955) specializes in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Sophia University, Kyoto University, and Cornell University under Jay Jasanoff. He held posts at Nagoya City University (~1989–1995) and as professor at Kyoto University (~1995–2020).

nodes.label: Tokuno Oda
nodes.summary: Tokuno Oda was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Fukui Prefectural Normal School, Otani University, and under Gaju Ikehara. He held teaching posts at Fukui Prefectural Normal School, Fukui Chugakko, and Toyo University.

nodes.label: Enryo Inoue
nodes.summary: Enryo Inoue (1858–1919) was a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Higashi Hongan-ji, Nagaoka High School, and the University of Tokyo (~1881–1885). He founded Toyo University and held a post there (~1887–1919).

nodes.label: Teun Goudriaan
nodes.summary: Teun Goudriaan is a scholar in the fields of Indology and religious studies. He held an academic post at Utrecht University, where he is attested as Professor Emeritus in 2000.

nodes.label: Sanjukta Gupta
variants: サンジェクタ・グプタ
nodes.summary: Sanjukta Gupta works in Indology and religious studies. After doctorates from Visva-Bharati University and Utrecht University under Jan Gonda, she held posts at Jadavpur, Utrecht (~1971–1986), and Oxford (~1986–2001).

nodes.label: Kojun Fukui
nodes.summary: Kojun Fukui (1898–1991) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. After studying at Waseda University (~1918–1923), he held a post there (~1944–1969) and later served as president of Taisho University (~1968–1972).

nodes.label: Takudo Ishikawa
nodes.summary: Takudo Ishikawa worked in Buddhist studies. He held posts as a researcher at the Jodo Shu Research Institute (attested 2005) and as a specially appointed full-time lecturer at Taisho University (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Kengo Harimoto
nodes.summary: Kengo Harimoto works in Indology. Harimoto earned a PhD from the University of Pennsylvania under Wilhelm Halbfass in 1999, and held posts at Mahidol University (attested 2020) and the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (attested 2021–2022).

nodes.label: Kenji Takahashi
nodes.summary: Kenji Takahashi is an Indologist who studied at Leiden University (2015–2016) under Peter Bisschop, Diwakar Acharya, and Yuko Yokochi. Takahashi held a JSPS-sponsored fellowship at the University of Naples Federico II (2019–2021).

nodes.label: Peter Bisschop
nodes.summary: Peter Bisschop is an Indology scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Groningen (-2004) under Hans T. Bakker and Harunaga Isaacson. He held posts at Wolfson College, Oxford, Edinburgh (2005–2010), and Leiden (attested 2011–2021).

nodes.label: Andrey Klebanov
nodes.summary: Andrey Klebanov specializes in Indology and linguistics. He completed his MA (2010) and PhD (2016) at the University of Hamburg under Harunaga Isaacson and Dominic Goodall, and served as a professor at Kyoto University, attested in 2019.

nodes.label: James L. Fitzgerald
nodes.summary: James L. Fitzgerald (b. 1948) is an Indologist. He held professorships at the University of Tennessee (attested 2004–2006) and at Brown University (attested 2019) as Das Professor of Sanskrit in the Department of Classics.

nodes.label: Ryosaburo Sakaki
nodes.summary: Ryosaburo Sakaki worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. Educated at Third Higher School and the University of Tokyo (~1893–1895), he lectured at Ryukoku University (1897) and became a professor at Third Higher School (1899) and Kyoto University (1908).

nodes.label: Gikyo Ito
nodes.summary: Gikyo Ito (1909–1996) specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at Kyoto University under Atsuuji Ashikaga and held posts at Osaka University of Foreign Studies and Kyoto Sangyo University.

nodes.label: Koji Kamioka
nodes.summary: Koji Kamioka (1938–2024) studied Iranian/Central Asian studies and linguistics at Kyoto University (~1957–1961) under Yutaka Ochihara. He held academic posts at Kyoto Sangyo University and Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (assistant professor, attested 1979).

nodes.label: Norihiko Uchida
nodes.summary: Norihiko Uchida specializes in linguistics and Indology and studied under Yutaka Ochihara. In 1962, he held posts at the Osaka University of Foreign Studies and the University of Tokyo.

nodes.label: Sensho Murakami
nodes.summary: Sensho Murakami was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Toyo University. He held posts at Sendan-Rin School, Toyo University, Otani University, and the University of Tokyo, where he was a professor from 1917 to 1922.

nodes.label: Takao Hayashi
nodes.summary: Takao Hayashi specializes in Indology and the history of science. He studied at Tohoku University (~1968-1977) and Brown University (~1979-1985) under David Pingree, later serving as Professor of History of Science at Doshisha University (~1989-2015).

nodes.label: Mizuho Okita
nodes.summary: Mizuho Okita is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. She studied at Tokai University and Gakushuin University under Katsuhiko Kamimura and doctoral supervisor Atsuhiko Yoshida, and served as a part-time lecturer at Meisei University (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Atsuhiko Yoshida
nodes.summary: Atsuhiko Yoshida is a scholar of religious studies and linguistics. He studied at Seikei University (~1951–1955) and the University of Tokyo (~1955–1960), and later held a post at Seikei University (~1974–1999).

nodes.label: Masanori Shono
nodes.summary: Masanori Shono specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He has held positions as an assistant professor at Osaka University (attested 2012) and as a researcher at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Michael Radich
variants: マイケル・ラディッチ
nodes.summary: Michael Radich is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD at Harvard University (~2001–2007) supervised by Robert M. Gimello, also studying at Kyoto University (2009). He held posts at Victoria University of Wellington (~2005–2017) and Heidelberg University (~2018).

nodes.label: Yumiko Ishihama
nodes.summary: Yumiko Ishihama is a scholar of Tibetology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Waseda University (~1980–1989) and held a post there around 1997.

nodes.label: Shinkai Sugawara
nodes.summary: Shinkai Sugawara (1925–2018) was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied at Waseda University (~1945–1951). He later held a post at Waseda University from around 1960 to 1996.

nodes.label: Jikai Fujiyoshi
nodes.summary: Jikai Fujiyoshi (1915–1996) specialized in Buddhist studies. He served as a professor at Rissho University and was attested as a member at Kyoto University in 1967.

nodes.label: Masao Shizutani
nodes.summary: Masao Shizutani specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and history/archaeology. He held assistant professor posts at Josai University and Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (attested 1974).

nodes.label: Ryodo Kudo
nodes.summary: Ryodo Kudo is a Buddhist studies scholar. He served as a researcher at Taisho University (attested 2015–2020) and as a part-time lecturer at Shukutoku University (attested 2020).

nodes.label: Lance E. Nelson
nodes.summary: Lance E. Nelson, an Indology, religious studies, and philosophy scholar, earned his doctorate at McMaster University (1986). He served as a professor at the University of San Diego (attested 1997) and taught James Blumenthal.

nodes.label: Sayaka Sonoda
nodes.summary: Sayaka Sonoda works in Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed her PhD at Toyo University under doctoral supervisor Shinobu Yamaguchi and committee member Shogo Watanabe.

nodes.label: Shinobu Yamaguchi
nodes.summary: Shinobu Yamaguchi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a PhD at Nagoya University in 1995. She taught Sayaka Sonoda and held a professorship at Toyo University (attested 2015).

nodes.id: I:Research Institute of Old Japanese Manuscripts of Buddhist Scriptures
nodes.label: Research Institute of Old Japanese Manuscripts of Buddhist Scriptures
Hiroshi Maruyama
nodes.summary: Hiroshi Maruyama works in Indology and related fields. Maruyama held positions as a professor at Osaka University and head of Ayurveda Kenkyūkai (both attested 1987).

nodes.label: Ayurveda Kenkyūkai
variants: アーユルヴェーダ研究会

nodes.label: Tsutomu Hatai
nodes.summary: Tsutomu Hatai was an Indologist attested in 1987 as head (会長) of Ayurveda Kenkyūkai, where he succeeded Hiroshi Maruyama.

nodes.label: Yasuhiro Okazaki
nodes.summary: Yasuhiro Okazaki is an Indologist and philosopher who earned a PhD at Hiroshima University under Atsushi Uno, Shoryu Katsura, and Hiroakira Ono. He held teaching posts at Hiroshima Prefectural Chiyoda, Kabe, and Takamiya high schools.

nodes.label: Otoya Tanaka
nodes.summary: Otoya Tanaka (1903–1989) was an Indologist. He studied under Naoshiro Tsuji at the University of Tokyo (~1924–1927) and later held an academic post at Chuo University (~1957–1974).

nodes.label: Kiyozo Kazama
nodes.summary: Kiyozo Kazama (born 1928) is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. Kazama studied at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji and at the University of Vienna, later holding posts at Hosei University, Nagoya University, and the University of Tokyo (~1970–1989).

nodes.label: Fujio Taniguchi
nodes.summary: Fujio Taniguchi specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed a PhD at Nagoya University (-1991) under Musashi Tachikawa, Yusho Miyasaka, and other teachers, and was attested as a lecturer at Chiba College of Health Science in 1991.

nodes.label: Geshe Sonam Rinchen
variants: Dge bshes bsod nams rin chen
nodes.summary: Geshe Sonam Rinchen (1933–2013) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies from circa 1968 to 1971 and served as a teacher at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives from circa 1978 to 2013.

nodes.label: Shinko Mochizuki
nodes.summary: Shinko Mochizuki (1869–1948) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Togai Soga and at Bukkyo University. He served at Shukyo University, including as president (1914–1928), and at Taisho University as professor, dean, and president (1930–1932).

nodes.label: Junkei Washio
nodes.summary: A scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology, Junkei Washio studied at Toyo University from circa 1887 to 1891. He later held posts at Toyo University, Sendan-Rin School, and Komazawa University.

nodes.label: Genchi Kato
nodes.summary: Genchi Kato (1873–1965) was a scholar of religious studies and Japanology. He completed his studies at the University of Tokyo from ~1896 to 1903 and held a post there from ~1907 to 1934.

nodes.label: Seigai Omura
nodes.summary: Seigai Omura specialized in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied at Tokyo University of the Arts (~1889–1893) and served as a professor at Tokyo School of Fine Arts (~1902–1927).

nodes.summary: Michio Kamikawa (born 1960) specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Ritsumeikan University (~1979–1989) and held a post at Aichi Prefectural University circa 2005.

nodes.label: Yoshitoyo Ohara
nodes.summary: Yoshitoyo Ohara (born 1968) works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He held appointments at Kyoto University (attested 2006) and Kyoto National Museum (attested 2016).

nodes.label: Akira Shimada
nodes.summary: Akira Shimada is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at the College of Art, Delhi, under Rajeev Lochan and Daud Ali. He held posts at the British Museum and the State University of New York.

nodes.label: Michael D. Willis
nodes.summary: Michael D. Willis, an Indologist and historian of Buddhist studies, studied at Victoria and Chicago. His career included posts at British Columbia, SUNY New Paltz, De Montfort, the British Museum (1994–2014), and the European Research Council (2014–2020).

nodes.label: Kōdō Yotsuya
nodes.summary: Kōdō Yotsuya is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed an MA at Komazawa University and earned a PhD from the University of Hamburg.

nodes.label: Alexander Wynne
nodes.description: British sanskritist and religious studies scholar, works on the history of Buddishm
nodes.summary: Alexander Wynne (born 1974) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed undergraduate studies at the University of Bristol (c. 1996–1999) and earned a DPhil at the University of Oxford (2000–2003) under Richard Gombrich.

nodes.label: Paul Williams
nodes.summary: Paul Williams is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at Sussex (~1969–1972) and Oxford (Wadham College, ~1972–1978). He served at Bristol (attested 1998–2016) and held a chair at Calgary (~2002).

nodes.label: David Pingree
nodes.summary: David Pingree was a scholar of Indology and history who studied at Harvard University (1950–1960). He held posts at Harvard, Chicago, the American University of Beirut, the Institute for Advanced Study, and served as a professor at Brown University (1971).

nodes.label: Otto Neugebauer
nodes.jawiki: オットー・ノイゲバウアー
nodes.summary: Otto Neugebauer worked in history and archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studying at Graz and Göttingen, he held posts at Göttingen, Copenhagen, Brown University, and the Institute for Advanced Study.

nodes.label: Eishun Fushimi
nodes.summary: Eishun Fushimi is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Hamburg (attested 1998) under David P. Jackson.

nodes.label: Hong Luo
nodes.summary: Hong Luo is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology scholar who was a doctoral student at Peking University. He has held posts at the China Tibetology Research Center and as a professor at Sichuan University.

variants: Institute of Religion at Sichuan University
Center for Tibetan Studies, Sichuan University

nodes.label: Peter Zieme
nodes.summary: Peter Zieme (b. 1942) specializes in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He held posts at the German Academy of Sciences at Berlin (~1965–1991), Berlin-Brandenburg Academy of Sciences and Humanities (~1992–2007), and Free University of Berlin.

nodes.label: Haiyan Hu-von Hinüber
nodes.summary: Haiyan Hu-von Hinüber is an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and sinologist. She studied at Peking University under Kemu Jin and Zhongxin Jiang, later holding posts at the University of Vienna and the University of Freiburg.

nodes.label: Vincent Tournier
nodes.summary: Vincent Tournier works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Leiden University and EPHE, and completed postdoctoral work under Seishi Karashima in 2008. He held an affiliation with the École française d'Extrême-Orient (attested 2021).

nodes.label: Taiki Mibu
nodes.summary: Taiki Mibu is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD from Ryukoku University by 2016 and served there as a part-time lecturer, attested in 2015.

nodes.label: Harushige Kōzu
nodes.summary: Harushige Kōzu (1908–1973) was a linguistics scholar who studied at the University of Oxford (~1937–1939). He held academic posts at the University of Tokyo (~1942–1969) and Musashi University (~1969–1973).

nodes.label: Toru Haneda
nodes.summary: Toru Haneda was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, Sinology, and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (circa 1903–1907) and held a post at Kyoto University from circa 1907 to 1945.

nodes.label: Shingen Takagi
nodes.summary: Shingen Takagi is an indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University under teachers including Gisho Nakano, Yusho Miyasaka, Ensho Kanakura, and Hakuyu Hadano. He served as assistant professor (attested 1970) and president (attested 1991–1995) at Koyasan University.

nodes.label: Gisho Nakano
nodes.image: 哲學系教授中野義照先生 (cropped).jpg
nodes.summary: Gisho Nakano (1891–1977) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Koyasan University and Kyushu University (~1925–1954), where he taught Shingen Takagi.

nodes.label: Ekai Kawaguchi
nodes.summary: Ekai Kawaguchi worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studying at Gyosei Shoin, Toyo University, Sera Monastery, and Central Hindu College under teachers including Hiroshi Tsuchiya and Sarat Chandra Das. He taught at Toyo University (1916), Taisho University (~1926–1934), and Toyo Bunko (1940).

nodes.label: Masakazu Tanaka
nodes.summary: Masakazu Tanaka is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at Tohoku University (~1974-1980) and the London School of Economics and Political Science (~1981-1986). He held an academic post at Kyoto University from 1988 to 2019.

nodes.label: Ryuta Kikutani
nodes.summary: Ryuta Kikutani works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held posts as a specialist researcher at Tohoku University (attested 2015) and at Kyoto University's Hakubi Center and Graduate School of Letters (attested 2020).

nodes.label: Ryosho Hayashi
nodes.summary: Ryosho Hayashi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University (~1948–1952) and Tokyo Metropolitan University (~1953–1958). He later served as president of Taisho University (~1991–1995).

nodes.label: Frits Staal
nodes.summary: Frits Staal worked in Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. He studied at Amsterdam and Banaras Hindu University, later holding posts at the University of Amsterdam (1962–1967), MIT (~1967–1968), and UC Berkeley (~1968–1991).

nodes.label: Yoshitsugu Sawai
nodes.summary: Yoshitsugu Sawai (born 1951) works in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Tenri, Tohoku, and Harvard universities, supervised by John B. Carman. From ~1985, he served as professor and dean of human studies at Tenri University.

nodes.label: Christian Luczanits
variants: Christian LUCZANITS クリスチャン・ルクザニッツ

nodes.label: Arindam Chakrabarti
nodes.summary: Arindam Chakrabarti is a philosopher and Indologist who earned his DPhil at the University of Oxford. He served as professor of philosophy at the University of Delhi (attested 1999) and the University of Hawaii (attested 2009–2014).

nodes.label: Gösta Liebert
nodes.summary: Gösta Liebert (1916–1998) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Hjalmar Frisk, Nils M. Holmer, and Stig Wikander (~1945–1950) and held a post at the University of Gothenburg (~1951–1982).

nodes.label: Stig Wikander
nodes.jawiki: スティグ・ヴィカンデル
nodes.description: Swedish historian of religion and iranologist (1908–1983)
nodes.summary: Stig Wikander was an Indologist, linguist, and Iranian-Central Asian studies scholar who studied at Uppsala and Copenhagen under Henrik Samuel Nyberg, Arthur Christensen, and Geo Widengren. He held posts at Lund (1941–1953) and Uppsala (~1953–1974).

nodes.label: Hugh Richardson
nodes.summary: Hugh Richardson was a Tibetology and history/archaeology scholar. He studied at Keble College (~1924–1928) and worked for the Indian Civil Service (~1930–1947).

nodes.label: Keishin Okamura
nodes.summary: Keishin Okamura (1931–2019) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1950–1958). Okamura held posts at Koyasan University as an associate professor (~1967–1974) and at Kōchi University.

nodes.label: Maruo Ujiie
nodes.summary: Maruo Ujiie is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied as a research student at Tribhuvan University (attested 1970). He held an attested post as a lecturer at Koyasan University in 1970.

nodes.label: Naoji Okuyama
nodes.summary: Naoji Okuyama is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his doctoral studies (~1980–1985) and held teaching posts (~1985–1993) at Tohoku University, followed by a professorship at Koyasan University (~1993–2021).

nodes.label: Munenobu Sakurai
nodes.summary: Munenobu Sakurai (born 1961) is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at Tohoku University around 1984–1990. He served as assistant professor at Iwate University (~1993–2002) and became a professor at Tohoku University around 2002.

nodes.label: Koken Unno
nodes.summary: Koken Unno (born 1936), a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, earned his doctorate at Nagoya University (-2000). He held posts at Nagoya University, Aichi Prefectural University of Fine Arts and Music, and Meijo University (professor, attested 2002).

nodes.label: Tetsuhiko Shibata
nodes.summary: Tetsuhiko Shibata is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He studied at Taisho University under teachers Eijun Hattori, Yukan Ozawa, and Mitsuo Sato.

nodes.label: Takeshi Fujii
nodes.summary: Takeshi Fujii specialized in Indology and history, studying at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1974–1981). He held a post at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1993–2021) and taught Kei Kataoka.

nodes.label: Takashi Yamada

nodes.label: Hidenaka Tanaka

nodes.label: Jeffrey L. Broughton

nodes.label: Yuko Kamishima
nodes.summary: Yuko Kamishima is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied at the University of Tokyo, including as a research student under Ekai Kawaguchi, and held a post at Ritsumeikan University.

nodes.label: Hans-Werner Köhler
nodes.summary: Hans-Werner Köhler is an Indologist who completed his doctoral studies under the supervision of Ernst Waldschmidt (attested 1973) and also studied under Eduard Hermann.

nodes.label: Eduard Hermann
nodes.summary: Eduard Hermann was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Berthold Delbrück (~1891–1893). He held academic posts at the University of Kiel (~1913–1917), Goethe University Frankfurt (~1917–1924), and the University of Göttingen (~1924–1940).

nodes.label: George Peiris Malalasekera
nodes.summary: George Peiris Malalasekera worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at the University of London and SOAS under Caroline A. F. Rhys Davids and William Stede. He held posts at Ceylon University College and the University of Ceylon.

nodes.label: Oliver Hector de Alwis Wijesekera
nodes.summary: Oliver Hector de Alwis Wijesekera (1909–1990) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at Ceylon and SOAS under William Stede and Betty Heimann, he headed Sanskrit at Ceylon and held visiting roles at Pennsylvania, Harvard, and Smith College.

nodes.label: James Mallinson

nodes.summary: Isaline Blew Horner was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at Newnham College around 1914–1917 and served as Honorary Secretary of the Pali Text Society from circa 1942 to 1958.

nodes.label: Thanon Chitkament
nodes.summary: Thanon Chitkament is a researcher in the field of history and archaeology who studied under the guidance of V. D. Gogte and co-guide P. S. Joshi (attested 2021).

nodes.label: Brendan S. Gillon
nodes.summary: Brendan S. Gillon specializes in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (~1979–1984) and served as Associate Professor of Linguistics at McGill University (~1992).

nodes.label: Richard P. Hayes
nodes.summary: Richard P. Hayes studied Sanskrit and Indian studies at Toronto under Bimal Krishna Matilal, Shoryu Katsura, and T. Venkatacharya. He taught at Toronto, Leiden, McGill University (attested 1997–2009), and the University of New Mexico (attested 2011–2016).

nodes.label: Eugen Hultzsch
nodes.summary: Eugen Hultzsch (1857–1927) was an Indology and archaeology scholar who studied under Georg Bühler (~1880–1886). From circa 1886 to 1903, he served as an epigraphist for the Archaeological Survey of India, Government of Madras, and Government of India.

Deutsche Akademie der Wissenschaften in Berlin
ベルリン・アカデミー東洋学研究所

nodes.label: Georg von Simson
nodes.summary: Georg von Simson (1933–) is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He was an editor at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 1968 and served as professor at the University of Oslo from around 1977 to 2003.

nodes.label: Thích Minh Châu
nodes.summary: Thích Minh Châu (1918–2012) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a PhD from Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar Bihar University (circa 1961–1964) and served as a lecturer in Chinese at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (attested 1984).

nodes.label: Ashok Aklujkar
nodes.summary: Ashok Aklujkar is a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. Educated at Savitribai Phule Pune University and Harvard (Ph.D. under Daniel H. H. Ingalls), he served as a professor at the University of British Columbia (~1969–2006).

nodes.label: Tatiana Oranskaia
nodes.summary: Tatiana Oranskaia is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. She studied at Saint Petersburg State University (~1967–1972) and served as a professor at the University of Hamburg (~2001–2016).

nodes.label: Arthur W. Ryder
nodes.summary: Arthur W. Ryder was an Indologist who studied at Harvard University (~1894–1901) under Charles Rockwell Lanman and at Leipzig University (~1901–1902) under Karl Friedrich Geldner. He taught Sanskrit at Harvard (~1902–1906) and was a professor at UC Berkeley (~1906–1938).

nodes.label: Raniero Gnoli
nodes.summary: Raniero Gnoli (1930–2025) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Giuseppe Tucci. He held a post at Sapienza University of Rome from approximately 1964 to 2000.

nodes.label: K. V. Sarma
nodes.summary: K. V. Sarma worked in Indology, history, and archaeology after studying at the University of Kerala (~1937–1942). He held posts at the Oriental Research Institute and Manuscripts Library (~1943–1951), University of Madras (1951–1962), and Sri Sarada Education Society Research Centre (~1991–2005).

nodes.label: Mark Singleton
nodes.summary: Indology and religious studies scholar Mark Singleton earned his PhD at the University of Cambridge and studied under Lakshmi Tatacharya. He is attested as a Senior Research Fellow at SOAS University of London in 2020.

nodes.label: Suzanne Newcombe
nodes.summary: Suzanne Newcombe works in religious studies and Indology. After earning a doctorate at the University of Cambridge (attested 2008), she held posts at Cambridge, LSE, Inform (attested 2008, 2020), King's College London (attested 2020), and the Open University (attested 2020).

nodes.label: Gangs zhun
nodes.summary: Gangs zhun is a Tibetology scholar. They studied at Hainan College for Nationalities (until 1989) and completed a master's degree at Northwest Minzu University (1998–2001) under the supervision of Alak Dorje Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Hainan College for Nationalities
variants: Teachers Training College for Nationalities in Chab-cha

nodes.label: Mysore Hiriyanna
nodes.description: Indian philosopher, Sanskrit scholar and authority on Indian aesthetics
nodes.summary: Mysore Hiriyanna (1871–1950) was a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Maharaja's College, Mysore (~1912–1927) and at the University of Mysore (~1917–1927).

nodes.label: Lalchandra Bhagawandas Gandhi
nodes.summary: Lalchandra Bhagawandas Gandhi worked in Indology, serving as Jain Pandit at Baroda Central Library and holding an appointment at the Oriental Institute, Vadodara (attested 1939).

nodes.label: K. V. Rangaswami Aiyangar
variants: R. B. Prof. K. V. Rangaswami Iyengar
nodes.summary: K. V. Rangaswami Aiyangar was an Indologist and historian who served as Principal of Central Hindu College (~1935–1938) and as Principal at Banaras Hindu University (attested 1937–1939).

nodes.label: Sukhlal Sanghvi
nodes.description: Jain Scholar and Philosopher from India

nodes.label: Govindlal Hargovind Bhatt
nodes.summary: Govindlal Hargovind Bhatt was an Indologist. He served as a professor at Baroda College (attested 1933–1939) and later as Director of the Oriental Institute, Vadodara (attested 1953–1957).

nodes.label: Lothar von Falkenhausen
nodes.jawiki: ロータール・フォン・ファルケンハウゼン
nodes.description: German-American Archaeologist, Sinologist, and Art Historian
nodes.summary: Specializing in sinology and history/archaeology, Lothar von Falkenhausen held posts at the University of California, Los Angeles (~1993) and served as a visiting professor at the Research Institute for Humanity and Nature in 2003.

nodes.label: Jinbo Shi
nodes.summary: Jinbo Shi (born 1940) specializes in sinology, linguistics, and Tibetology. He studied at Minzu University of China (~1958–1962) and held posts at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences and its Institute of Ethnology and Anthropology (~1966/1977–2010).

nodes.label: Boston University
variants: Boston University Institute for Philosophy and Religion

nodes.label: École Polytechnique
variants: Centre de Récherche en Epistémologie Appliqué (CREA) at the Ecole Polytechnique in Paris
Centre de Recherche en Epistemologie Applique (CREA), at the Ecole Polytechnique, Paris

nodes.label: Dieter George
nodes.summary: An Indologist, Dieter George held a post at the Berlin State Library from around 1969 to 1985 and was attested in 1985 as the successor to Wolfgang Voigt.

nodes.label: Michael Schmidt
nodes.summary: Michael Schmidt specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities, serving as Redaktor des Wörterbuchs (attested 1981), in 1992, and as Mitarbeiter (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Vishwanath Narayan Mandlik
nodes.description: Indian lawyer, writer and social activist

nodes.label: Steven Heine
nodes.summary: Steven Heine works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. Educated at the University of Pennsylvania and Temple University, and having studied under Shudo Ishii, he held appointments at Villanova, Penn State, and Florida International University (~1997).

nodes.label: Charles S. Prebish
nodes.summary: Charles S. Prebish studied at Case Western Reserve University and under David M. Miller and Richard Hugh Robinson. A scholar of Buddhist and religious studies, he served as Professor at Pennsylvania State University (circa 1973–2007).

nodes.label: Raoul Birnbaum
nodes.summary: Raoul Birnbaum is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who served as a professor of Buddhist studies at the University of California, Santa Cruz (attested 2003, 2017).

nodes.label: Christopher S. Queen
nodes.summary: Christopher S. Queen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. At Harvard University, he served as Dean of Students for Continuing Education and lecturer on the Study of Religion (circa 1989) and Lecturer on Buddhism and World Religions (circa 1990).

nodes.label: Manfred Mayrhofer
nodes.jawiki: マンフレート・マイルホーファー
nodes.summary: Manfred Mayrhofer was a linguist, Indologist, and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar who studied at the University of Graz under Wilhelm Brandenstein. He held posts at Würzburg (~1958–1963), Saarland (~1963–1966), Vienna (~1966–1988), and the Austrian Academy of Sciences.

nodes.label: Ernest John Eitel
nodes.summary: Ernest John Eitel worked in sinology and Buddhist studies. After studying at the University of Tübingen (~1856–1860), he held posts with the London Missionary Society (~1865–1879) and at the University of Adelaide (~1897–1904).

nodes.label: Raffaele Torella
nodes.summary: Raffaele Torella is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Raniero Gnoli. He has served as a faculty member at Sapienza University of Rome and as a professor at the University of Naples "L'Orientale".

nodes.label: Anant Sadashiv Altekar
nodes.description: historian, archaeologist, and numismatist from Maharashtra, India
nodes.summary: Anant Sadashiv Altekar (1898–1959) was an Indologist and historian. He held posts at Banaras Hindu University (~1930–1949), Patna University (~1949–1959), and served as Director of the Kashi Prasad Jayaswal Research Institute (~1950–1959).

nodes.label: Cyril Henry Philips
nodes.summary: Cyril Henry Philips was a historian and Indologist who studied at the University of Liverpool (~1930–1934) and SOAS University of London (~1934–1936). He served as Director of SOAS (~1956–1976) and held a post at the University of London (1972–1976).

nodes.label: Ying-shih Yü
nodes.summary: Ying-shih Yü was a scholar of Sinology, history, and philosophy who studied at CUHK, Kansai University, and Harvard. He held professorships at the University of Michigan (~1962–1966), Yale University (~1977–1987), and Princeton University (~1987–2021).

nodes.label: Arunoday Natvarlal Jani
nodes.summary: Arunoday Natvarlal Jani was an Indologist who studied under M. V. Upadhyay and completed his Ph.D. at the University of Mumbai (~1948–1953) under Govindlal Hargovind Bhatt. He served as Senior Lecturer in Sanskrit at Baroda College (~1946–1957).

nodes.label: Parashuram Krishna Gode
nodes.image: Dr. Parshuram Krishna Gode, M.A., D. Litt.jpg
nodes.summary: Parashuram Krishna Gode was a scholar in Indology and history and archaeology. He served as Curator at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute from 1916 (or ~1919) to 1946 (or ~1961).

nodes.label: Kenneth Roy Norman
nodes.summary: Kenneth Roy Norman (1925–2020) was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies who studied at Downing College. He held positions at the Pali Text Society (President in 1988), the University of Cambridge, and SOAS.

nodes.label: Frank Raymond Allchin
nodes.summary: Frank Raymond Allchin was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at the University of London (~1946–1954), he held positions at SOAS, the University of Cambridge (~1954–1989), and the Ancient India and Iran Trust (~1978–2010).

nodes.label: David Roy Shackleton Bailey
nodes.summary: David Roy Shackleton Bailey was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. Educated at Gonville and Caius College, Cambridge, he held posts at Gonville and Caius, Jesus College, the University of Michigan (1968–1975), and Harvard University (1975–1982).

nodes.label: Paul Mus
nodes.summary: Paul Mus (1902–1969) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and archaeology who studied under Sylvain Lévi, Jean Przyluski, and Paul Pelliot. He held posts at EPHE, Collège de France, and Yale University.

nodes.label: Kun Chang
nodes.summary: Kun Chang (1917–2017) was a linguist, sinologist, and Tibetologist who studied at Tsinghua University and under Franklin Edgerton. He held academic posts at the University of Washington (~1957–1963) and the University of California, Berkeley (~1963–1988).

nodes.label: Samuel Beal
nodes.summary: Samuel Beal was a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. After graduating B.A. from Trinity College, Cambridge (~1843–1847), he served as Professor of Chinese at University College London and held a post at the University of London (~1877–1889).

nodes.label: Cornelis Petrus Tiele
nodes.jawiki: コルネーリス・ティーレ
nodes.summary: Cornelis Petrus Tiele (1830–1902) worked in religious studies and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Amsterdam (~1848–1853) and served as Professor of the History of Religions at Leiden University (~1877–1901).

nodes.label: Teruji Ishizu
nodes.summary: Teruji Ishizu was a religious studies and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1923–1926). He held academic posts at Tohoku University (~1942–1967), Keio University (~1967–1972), the University of Tokyo, Nihon University, and Aichi University.

nodes.label: Ichiro Hori
nodes.summary: Ichiro Hori (1910–1974) was a religious studies and archaeology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1932–1935). He held posts at Kokugakuin (~1952–1960), Tohoku (~1960–1967), University of Tokyo (~1967–1971), and Seijo University (~1971–1974).

nodes.label: Thomas Oberlies
nodes.summary: Thomas Oberlies works in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Albrecht Wezler and held a post at the University of Freiburg (attested 2001).

nodes.label: Max Deeg
nodes.summary: Max Deeg is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and sinology who earned his PhD and Habilitation at the University of Würzburg. He served as Head of the School of Religious and Theological Studies at Cardiff University (attested 2010–2021).

nodes.label: William J. Johnson
nodes.summary: William J. Johnson is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. He has held academic posts at Cardiff University and the University of Wales (attested 1998).

nodes.label: Hjalmar Edgren
nodes.summary: Hjalmar Edgren was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Nebraska–Lincoln and under William Dwight Whitney (~1871–1874). He held posts at Lund University (~1880–1885), the University of Gothenburg (~1891–1893), and the University of Nebraska–Lincoln (~1885–1901).

nodes.label: Per Kjeld Sørensen
nodes.summary: Per Kjeld Sørensen is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Erik Haarh at the University of Copenhagen (~1972–1980), holding posts at Copenhagen (~1981–1994), Bonn (1991–1992), and Leipzig University (1995).

nodes.label: Sangye Tenzin
nodes.summary: Sangye Tenzin was a scholar of Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Drepung Monastery and served as Abbot of Menri Monastery.

nodes.label: Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche is a Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies scholar. He studied at the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics (~1975–1986) and under Sangye Tenzin Rinpoche, Lopon Tenzin Namdak, and others, serving as the Institute's president (~1986–1991) and a Rockefeller Fellow at Rice University (1991).

nodes.label: Lungtok Tenpai Nyima
variants: H. H. Menri Khen Rinpoche Lungdog Denpa Nyima
nodes.summary: Lungtok Tenpai Nyima was a figure in Tibetology and religious studies. He founded Menri Monastery and served as its abbot and throne-holder from ~1969 to 2017.

nodes.label: Anne Carolyn Klein
nodes.summary: Anne Carolyn Klein specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. Educated at Binghamton, UW–Madison, and Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins and Tibetan lamas, she held posts at Harvard (~1987–1990), Rice (~1991), and Dawn Mountain, which she founded.

nodes.label: Geshe Tsondru Namgyal
nodes.summary: Geshe Tsondru Namgyal is a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies who earned Geshe degrees through his studies at Drepung Monastery and Yungdrung Ling Monastery.

Center for Cultural Studies at Rice University

variants: Dawn Mountain Community Center & Research Institute

nodes.label: Gergely Hidas
nodes.summary: Gergely Hidas is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed his DPhil at Balliol College, Oxford, supervised by Alexis Sanderson. He held posts at Eötvös Loránd University (2007–2014) and the British Museum (2014).

nodes.label: Hermann Hirt
nodes.summary: Hermann Hirt (1865–1936) was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at the University of Freiburg and Leipzig University. He held academic posts at Leipzig University (~1896–1912) and the University of Giessen (~1912–1935).

nodes.label: Wilhelm Streitberg
nodes.summary: Wilhelm Streitberg was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Leipzig University (~1885–1888). He later held posts at the University of Münster (~1899–1909), Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1909–1920), and Leipzig University (~1920–1925).

nodes.label: Donald R. Davis Jr.
nodes.summary: Donald R. Davis Jr. is an Indologist and scholar of religious studies who studied under Richard W. Lariviere, Ludo Rocher, and Patrick Olivelle.

nodes.label: Richard W. Lariviere
nodes.summary: Richard W. Lariviere studied Indology at Iowa and Pennsylvania. He served at the University of Texas at Austin (~1982–2006; Dean ~1999–2006), Kansas (~2006–2009), Oregon (~2009–2011), and as President of the Field Museum (~2012–2020).

nodes.label: Timothy Lubin
nodes.summary: Timothy Lubin is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Columbia University in 1994 and held a post at Washington and Lee University (attested 2020).

nodes.label: Louis Dumont
nodes.summary: Louis Dumont was an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at Collège d'Harcourt, EHESS, EPHE, and Institut d'ethnologie under Marcel Mauss (~1936–1939). He held positions at ATP (1937–1951), Oxford (1951–1955), EPHE (1955), and EHESS (attested 1985).

variants: Department of Archaeology, Museums and Archives in Madhya Pradesh

nodes.label: Anne Casile
nodes.summary: Anne Casile works in Indology, history, and archaeology. She served as an AHRC research assistant at the British Museum (~2008–2010) and held a post at the French National Research Institute for Sustainable Development (~2013).

nodes.label: Virendra Nath Misra
nodes.summary: Virendra Nath Misra specialized in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Savitribai Phule Pune University (~1958–1961) and served as Director of the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1993–2000).

nodes.label: Heidi Pauwels
nodes.summary: Heidi Pauwels is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. She studied at KU Leuven in 1983 and 1986, earned her PhD at the University of Washington in 1994, and held a post at the University of Washington around 1996.

nodes.label: Helga Uebach
nodes.summary: Helga Uebach was a Tibetologist who earned her Ph.D. at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1961–1967). In 1964, she served as a wissenschaftliche Mitarbeiterin at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

nodes.summary: Jampa Losang Panglung worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1969–1979) and served as a wissenschaftlicher Mitarbeiter at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities (~1978–2004, attested 2005).

nodes.label: Erich Haenisch
nodes.jawiki: エーリヒ・ヘーニシュ
nodes.summary: Erich Haenisch (1880–1966) was a scholar of Sinology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held professorships at Leipzig University (~1925–1932), Humboldt University of Berlin (~1932–1945), and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1946–1952), among other posts.

nodes.label: Saraju Rath
nodes.summary: Saraju Rath is an Indologist and linguist who held posts at the International Institute for Asian Studies, attested in 2012 and 2022.

nodes.label: Christopher Minkowski
nodes.summary: Christopher Minkowski is an Indologist and religious studies scholar educated at Harvard. He held positions at Brown University, the University of Iowa, Cornell University (circa 1989–2005), and served as Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford and Balliol College (circa 2005–2023).

nodes.label: Gérard Colas
nodes.summary: Gérard Colas (born 1952) is an Indologist. He has served as a directeur de recherche and Senior Fellow at CNRS (attested 2004, 2009) and at École des hautes études en sciences sociales (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Kim Plofker
nodes.summary: Kim Plofker (b. 1964) is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. She studied at Haverford College and Brown University under David Pingree, and later held posts at MIT, the American Oriental Society, and Union College (~2007).

nodes.label: Sreeramula Rajeswara Sarma
nodes.description: Sreeramula Rajeswara Sarma, Dept. of Sanskrit, Aligarh Muslim U., Aligarh-202002
nodes.summary: Sreeramula Rajeswara Sarma works in Indology, history, and archaeology. Educated at Visva-Bharati University, Andhra University, and the University of Marburg (PhD circa 1963–1966), he served as a professor at Aligarh Muslim University, attested 2006–2012.

nodes.label: S. N. Savadi
nodes.summary: S. N. Savadi was an Indology scholar who held a post at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute, attested in 1953 and 1969.

nodes.label: Sao Htun Hmat Win
nodes.summary: Sao Htun Hmat Win is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Harvard University and under Mingun Jetawun Sayadaw. He taught at the University of Yangon and headed research at the International Institute of Advanced Buddhistic Studies.

nodes.label: Kashinath Vasudev Abhyankar
nodes.summary: Kashinath Vasudev Abhyankar was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Gujarat College (~1914–1945) and Honorary Professor of Sanskrit at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (~1945–1976), and he taught Masaaki Hattori.

nodes.label: Subhash Kak
nodes.image: Subhash Kak at Single Photon Workshop, Geneva, July 2015.jpg
nodes.summary: Subhash Kak is an Indologist and historian who studied at NIT Srinagar and IIT Delhi. He has held academic posts at Imperial College London (~1975–1976), Louisiana State University (attested 2005–2008), and Jawaharlal Nehru University (~2019).

nodes.label: Albert Debrunner
nodes.summary: Albert Debrunner was a linguist and Indologist. He held posts at the University of Zurich (circa 1903–1907), Basel (circa 1918–1920), Greifswald (circa 1920–1927), Jena (circa 1927–1935), and Bern (circa 1935–1954).

nodes.label: Robert B. Ekvall
nodes.description: missionary, explorer, ethnographer, curator of Asian ethnology (1898-1983)
nodes.summary: Robert B. Ekvall was a Tibetologist. He served at the University of Chicago (~1953–1958), the University of Washington (1958), and as honorary curator of Asian ethnology at the Burke Museum of Natural History and Culture (~1973–1983).

nodes.label: Csaba Dezső
nodes.summary: Csaba Dezső specializes in Indology. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University (~1992–1999) and earned a PhD at the University of Oxford (1998–2004) under Alexis Sanderson. Around 2002, he became an Assistant Lecturer at Eötvös Loránd University.

nodes.label: Surendranath Dasgupta
nodes.description: Bengali scholar of Sanskrit and philosophy (1887-1952)
nodes.summary: Surendranath Dasgupta (1887–1952) worked in philosophy and Indology, earning PhDs from Calcutta and Cambridge. He held posts at Cambridge, Presidency University, Sanskrit College as Principal (~1931–1942), and Calcutta University as Chair of Philosophy (~1942–1945).

nodes.label: Christopher D. Wallis
nodes.summary: Christopher D. Wallis works in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Rochester, the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson, and UC Berkeley under Robert P. Goldman and Alexander von Rospatt. He lectured at Naropa University in 2020.

nodes.label: Robert P. Goldman
nodes.summary: Robert P. Goldman is an Indologist who studied at Columbia University (~1960–1964) and the University of Pennsylvania (~1964–1971), also learning from Shivaram Dattatray Joshi, T. S. Srinivasa Sastri, and T. Shrinivas Shastri. He held a post at UC Berkeley (~1971).

nodes.label: M. Seshagiri Sastri
nodes.summary: M. Seshagiri Sastri worked in Indology and linguistics. In 1899, he was attested as Curator at the Government Oriental Manuscripts Library and Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology at Presidency University, Kolkata.

nodes.label: K. Kunjunni Raja
nodes.summary: Indologist and linguist K. Kunjunni Raja earned PhDs at the University of Madras under C. Kunhan Raja and the University of London under John Brough. He was Reader In-Charge at Madras (~1954–1980) and Research Committee Chairman at Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute (~1980–2005).

nodes.label: Harald Hauptmann
nodes.description: German praehistorian and near eastern archaeologist
nodes.summary: Harald Hauptmann specialized in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studying at Heidelberg University, he held posts at Heidelberg University (~1980–2001), DAI Istanbul (~1994–2001), and the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities (~1989–2018).

nodes.label: Shivaram Dattatray Joshi
nodes.summary: Shivaram Dattatray Joshi (1926–2013) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Daniel H. H. Ingalls, Shankashastri Marulkar, and Maheshwarshastri Joshi. He served as professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University and headed Deccan College's Sanskrit Dictionary Department.

nodes.label: Luca Maria Olivieri
nodes.summary: Specializing in history/archaeology and Indology, Luca Maria Olivieri earned his doctorate at the Free University of Berlin (~2005–2010). He served as director at IsMEO (~2011) and became Associate Professor at Ca' Foscari University of Venice (~2021).

nodes.label: Florinda De Simini
nodes.summary: Florinda De Simini is an Indologist. She held an attested post at the University of Naples Federico II in 2016 and a post at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" circa 2017.

nodes.label: Andrea Acri
nodes.summary: Andrea Acri is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He studied under Raffaele Torella and completed his PhD at Leiden University under Arlo Griffiths and Willem van der Molen, joining the École Pratique des Hautes Études in 2016.

nodes.label: Nirajan Kafle
nodes.summary: Nirajan Kafle is an Indologist who studied under Diwakar Acharya, Bhim Kandel, and Kashinath Nyupane, and completed his doctorate under Peter Bisschop at Leiden University in 2015. He held posts at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (2019) and Leiden University (2021).

nodes.label: A. N. Krishna Aiyangar
nodes.summary: A. N. Krishna Aiyangar was an Indologist who served as Joint Editor of Brahmavidyā: The Adyar Library Bulletin at the Adyar Library and Research Centre (attested 1940–1942).

nodes.label: John Myrdhin Reynolds
nodes.summary: John Myrdhin Reynolds is a scholar in the fields of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teachers Dudjom Rinpoche and Namkhai Norbu.

nodes.label: Namkhai Norbu
nodes.summary: Namkhai Norbu (1938–2018) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at institutions including Derge Gonchen Monastery. He taught at Southwest Minzu University (~1958–1960) and was Professor of Oriental Studies at the University of Naples Federico II (~1964–1992).

Khri brtan nor bu rtse Monastery

nodes.label: Megumu Honda
nodes.summary: Megumu Honda is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied under Paul Tedesco and Rulon Wells. He served as a professor at Doho University (attested 1996).

nodes.label: Rulon Wells
nodes.summary: Rulon Wells worked in linguistics, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at the University of Utah (circa 1935–1939) and Harvard University (circa 1939–1942), and served on the faculty at Yale University from circa 1945 to 1989.

nodes.label: Johannes Rahder
nodes.summary: Johannes Rahder studied at Utrecht (~1915–1926). Specializing in Indology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies, he succeeded Willem Caland in 1929, held posts at Utrecht, Leiden (1931–1946), Hawaii (1946–1947), and served as professor at Yale (1961–1962).

nodes.label: Eng Jin Ooi
nodes.summary: Eng Jin Ooi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at Mahidol University by 2021, supervised by Giuliano Giustarini, Peter Skilling, and Kengo Harimoto, alongside several other teachers.

nodes.label: Walter Clawiter

nodes.label: Zhihua Yao
nodes.summary: Zhihua Yao specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD at Boston University (~1998–2002) under Malcolm David Eckel and held posts at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (~2003) and the University of Hong Kong (2005).

nodes.label: Dipesh Chakrabarty
nodes.jawiki: ディペシュ・チャクラバルティ
nodes.summary: Historian Dipesh Chakrabarty studied at Calcutta, IIM Calcutta, and the Australian National University (~1977-1980). He taught at the University of Melbourne (~1983-1995) and held a post at the University of Chicago starting in 1995.

nodes.label: Christopher Pinney
nodes.image: The President, Shri Pranab Mukherjee presenting the Padma Shri Award to Prof. Christopher Pinney, at an Investiture Ceremony-II, at Rashtrapati Bhavan, in New Delhi on April 20, 2013.jpg
nodes.summary: Christopher Pinney is a scholar in Indology and history and archaeology. He held posts at the Australian National University from circa 1996 to 1999 and at University College London beginning circa 1999.

nodes.label: Siniruddha Dash
nodes.summary: Siniruddha Dash (b. 1955) specializes in Indology and linguistics. He served as head of the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Madras (2000–2014; attested 2022) and was Director of the Oriental Research Institute, Mysore (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Godabarish Mishra
nodes.summary: Godabarish Mishra (1886–1956) was a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Ravenshaw College (~1906–1910) and the University of Calcutta (~1910–1912), and later served as Director at the University of Madras.

nodes.label: C. Kunhan Raja
nodes.summary: C. Kunhan Raja was an Indologist who served as Head of the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Madras in 1927 and 1946. His students included K. Kunjunni Raja, Madhav Krishna Sharma, and H. G. Narahari.

nodes.label: N. Veezhinathan
nodes.summary: N. Veezhinathan is an Indology and philosophy scholar who earned a PhD from Savitribai Phule Pune University (-1964) under A. Sankaran. After research at Deccan College (1960–1963), he became Lecturer in Sanskrit at University of Madras in 1964, succeeding K. Kunjunni Raja.

nodes.label: Elisa Freschi
nodes.summary: Elisa Freschi works in Indology and philosophy, having studied under Raffaele Torella (~2003–2007). She has held posts at Sapienza University of Rome, the Austrian Academy of Sciences, the University of Vienna, and the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.

nodes.label: Nirmal Chandra Sinha
nodes.summary: Nirmal Chandra Sinha was a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. He studied at Presidency University (~1929-1933) and the University of Calcutta (~1931-1935), later serving at Krishnath College (~1938-1942), the National Archives of India (~1942-1958), and Calcutta University (~1970-1975).

nodes.label: John Taber
nodes.summary: Working in Indology and philosophy, Taber completed his D.Phil. at the University of Hamburg (1973–1979) under Lambert Schmithausen and Reiner Wiehl. He held posts at Case Western Reserve University (~1984–1991) and the University of New Mexico (~1991).

nodes.label: K. Srinivasan
nodes.summary: K. Srinivasan is an Indologist who taught Hugo David, Steven Edward Lindquist, and Mattia Salvini. He held posts as a professor at Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda College (attested 2008) and at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute (attested 2020).

nodes.label: Khammai Dhammasami

nodes.summary: Khammai Dhammasami (b. 1965) is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his DPhil at the University of Oxford (~2000–2004). Around 2005, he became a Fellow and Trustee at the Oxford Centre for Buddhist Studies and a professor at the International Theravāda Buddhist Missionary University.

nodes.label: Oxford Centre for Buddhist Studies

nodes.label: Volker Grabowsky
nodes.summary: Volker Grabowsky specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at the University of Kiel, he held positions at the University of Passau, University of Hamburg, National University of Laos, and University of Münster.

nodes.label: Elizabeth Guthrie
nodes.summary: Elizabeth Guthrie is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD at the University of Canterbury by 1994. She served as a tutor in Religious Studies at the University of Otago (attested 2007).

nodes.label: Peter Gyallay-Pap
nodes.summary: Peter Gyallay-Pap works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the London School of Economics and Political Science by 1990 and was an adjunct at Adams State University (attested 2007).

nodes.label: Ian Charles Harris
nodes.summary: Ian Charles Harris (1952–2014) worked in Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at Cambridge and Lancaster, he was Professor Emeritus at the University of Cumbria (~1986–2014) and held posts at Oxford, Lancaster, and National University of Singapore.

nodes.summary: Peter Koret is a scholar of Buddhist studies and linguistics who completed a doctoral thesis at SOAS University of London. He held posts at Arizona State University and the University of California, Berkeley.

nodes.label: John Marston
nodes.summary: John Marston is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD from the University of Washington in 1997. He later held an academic appointment at El Colegio de México.

nodes.label: Juliane Schober
nodes.summary: Juliane Schober specializes in religious studies and Buddhist studies, earning her PhD from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign in 1989. She was attested as an Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Arizona State University in 2007.

nodes.summary: Hugo David specializes in Indology and philosophy. After earning a PhD at École Pratique des Hautes Études (–2012) and studying with several traditional teachers, he held a fellowship at Cambridge (2013–2014) and joined EFEO as a permanent member in 2015.

nodes.label: Bret W. Davis
nodes.summary: Bret W. Davis works in philosophy, Japanology, and religious studies. He studied at Vanderbilt and Kyoto University, held research posts at Otani and Kyoto, taught at Shiga and Kwansei Gakuin, and served as a philosophy professor at Loyola University Maryland.

nodes.label: Jake H. Davis
nodes.summary: Jake H. Davis works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. Educated at Marlboro College, University of Hawaii, and CUNY Graduate Center, he held posts at City College of New York, NYU, Barre Center for Buddhist Studies, and Brown University (attested 2013–2018).

nodes.summary: William Edelglass works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He has taught philosophy at Colby College (attested 2007), served as a professor at Marlboro College (attested 2013), and was a visiting professor at the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics.

nodes.label: Alan Fox
nodes.summary: Alan Fox specializes in philosophy, Sinology, and religious studies. He completed a PhD at Temple University (attested 1988) and has served as a faculty member in philosophy at the University of Delaware since 1992.
