nodes.label: Christine Chojnacki
nodes.summary: Christine Chojnacki is an Indologist who completed her doctoral thesis at Sorbonne Nouvelle University in 1991 and has served as a professor at Jean Moulin University Lyon 3 (attested 2018).

nodes.label: Ingo Strauch
nodes.summary: Ingo Strauch is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. Strauch earned a PhD at the Free University of Berlin by 2000, taught Kathrin Holz, and served as Professeur at the University of Lausanne, attested in 2018.

nodes.label: Emi Matsushita
nodes.summary: Emi Matsushita (b. 1970) studied at Nanzan University, the University of East Anglia, and earned an MA from Ohio State University under John C. Huntington. She held positions with the Shizuoka Prefectural Board of Education (1994–1996) and Ohio State University (1999–2001).

nodes.label: Bahadur Chand Chhabra
nodes.summary: Bahadur Chand Chhabra worked in Indology and archaeology. He was Government Epigraphist for India (~1945–1953), served in leadership roles at the Archaeological Survey of India (~1953–1965), and became Professor of Ancient Indian Culture and Archaeology at Panjab University (~1965).

nodes.label: Nalinaksha Dutt
nodes.summary: Nalinaksha Dutt (1894–1973) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Chittagong College, the University of Calcutta (PhD), and the University of London (DLitt ~1921–1924), later serving as Head of the Pali Department at Calcutta and teaching Kshanika Saha.

nodes.label: Durgamohan Bhattacharyya
nodes.summary: Durgamohan Bhattacharyya (1899–1965) was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Scottish Church College, Vidyasagar College, and the University of Calcutta, where he also held an academic post.

nodes.label: Gajanan Balkrishna Palsule
nodes.summary: Gajanan Balkrishna Palsule (b. 1921) is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He served as a sub-editor at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1954–1960) and held a post at Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 1987).

nodes.label: Natasja Bosma
nodes.summary: Natasja Bosma is an Indologist who completed her PhD at the University of Groningen between circa 2008 and 2018, supervised by Hans T. Bakker.

nodes.label: Dale S. Wright
nodes.summary: Dale S. Wright is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied under Alan Anderson, Wang Pachow, and Robert Scharlemann, and served as a professor of religious and Asian studies at Occidental College (~1980–2019).

nodes.label: Michel Mohr
nodes.summary: Michel Mohr is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Geneva, where he was an assistant (1987–1992), and held posts at Hanazono University (attested 2000–2006) and the University of Hawaii (attested 2008–2012).

nodes.label: Mario Poceski
nodes.summary: Mario Poceski works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. After completing his PhD at UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr., he held positions at the University of Iowa and the University of Florida (attested 2004–2019).

nodes.label: David E. Riggs
nodes.summary: David E. Riggs is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who earned his Ph.D. from UCLA. He taught at UCSB, UIUC, and the University of Hawaii, and held research posts at Nichibunken (attested 2006) and Oberlin College (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Albert Welter
nodes.summary: Albert Welter is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He completed his PhD at McMaster University under Koichi Shinohara and Yun-hua Jan, later serving at the University of Winnipeg and University of Arizona.

nodes.label: Anthony Tribe
nodes.summary: Anthony Tribe is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at the University of Bristol and Oxford under Paul Williams, Steven Collins, and Alexis Sanderson, later holding posts at the University of Montana and University of Arizona.

nodes.label: University of Arizona
variants: Center for Buddhist Studies at the University of Arizona

nodes.label: Nina Mirnig
nodes.summary: Nina Mirnig is an Indology and religious studies scholar. She completed her DPhil at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson in 2010, founded the University of Oxford in 2008, and held a post at the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (attested 2020).

nodes.label: John Nemec
nodes.summary: John Nemec is an Indology, religious studies, and philosophy scholar who studied at Rochester, UCSB, Oxford, and Penn (PhD 2005) under Alexis Sanderson. He was appointed Associate Professor at the University of Virginia (attested 2020).

nodes.label: Stephen C. Berkwitz
nodes.summary: Stephen C. Berkwitz specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Kelaniya and has held posts at Missouri State University, Ruhr University Bochum, and the University of Colombo.

nodes.label: Pattaratorn Chirapravati
nodes.summary: Pattaratorn Chirapravati specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Cornell (~1988–1994), held posts at Sonoma State and the Asian Art Museum of San Francisco (1997–2002), and became an associate professor at California State University, Sacramento (2002–2016).

nodes.label: Natasha Heller
nodes.summary: Natasha Heller is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD from Harvard University in 2005. She was a postdoctoral fellow at UC Berkeley in 2008, taught Yu-Chen Tsui, and served at UCLA in 2016.

nodes.label: Justin McDaniel
nodes.summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies and religious studies, Justin McDaniel served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at the University of California, Riverside, and Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Pennsylvania (attested 2011–2018).

nodes.label: Zenno Ikuno
nodes.summary: Zenno Ikuno specialized in Indology and Buddhist studies. He completed an MA at the University of Tokyo and held a post at Asia University (attested 1982).

nodes.label: Bindeshwari Prasad Sinha
nodes.description: Indian archeologist and historian from Bihar
nodes.summary: Bindeshwari Prasad Sinha (1919–2002) was a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology who earned his Ph.D. from the University of London. He was a long-serving professor at Patna University (~1948–1982) and joint director at Kashi Prasad Jayaswal Research Institute.

nodes.label: Elke Rogersdotter
nodes.summary: Elke Rogersdotter is an archaeologist and Indologist. Attested in 2006, she completed her PhD at Umeå University under Thomas B. Larsson, Bozena Werbart, Karin Viklund, and P. Ajithprasad.

nodes.label: Asko Parpola
nodes.summary: Asko Parpola is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Pentti Aalto, R. Panneerselvam, and P. R. Subramanian. He held positions at the Nordic Institute of Asian Studies, the Academy of Finland, and the University of Helsinki (~1982–2004).

nodes.label: Asutosh Mookerjee
nodes.description: Bengali educator, jurist, barrister and mathematician (1864-1924)
nodes.summary: Asutosh Mookerjee worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta, where he later held posts (1906–1914) and served as President (1921–1923). He was also at Calcutta High Court (1904).

nodes.label: Bhikkhu Bodhi
nodes.description: American Theravada Buddhist monk and scholar (born 1944)
nodes.summary: Bhikkhu Bodhi is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Brooklyn College and Claremont Graduate University, and under Balangoda Ananda Maitreya and Nyanaponika Thera. He served as editor at the Buddhist Publication Society and held a post at Chuang Yen Monastery.

nodes.label: Nyanaponika Thera
nodes.summary: Nyanaponika Thera was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Ceylon. He served as an editor at the Buddhist Publication Society from circa 1958 to 1984.

nodes.label: W. S. Karunaratne
nodes.summary: W. S. Karunaratne was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Dharmaraja College, Ananda College, University of Ceylon, and SOAS University of London. He was Dean of the Faculty of Oriental Studies at Ceylon (1952–1973).

nodes.label: David Friedman
nodes.summary: David Friedman was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He served as Reader in Indian Philosophy at SOAS University of London (~1950–1970) and as Professor at the University of London (~1965–1970).

nodes.label: Guang Xing
nodes.summary: Guang Xing is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD from the University of London and SOAS under Tadeusz Skorupski and Timothy H. Barrett. He served at the University of Hong Kong and as a visiting professor at the University of British Columbia.

nodes.label: Jing Yin
nodes.summary: Jing Yin specializes in Buddhist studies. Having studied under K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 1995), Yin served as Director at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2006–2010).

nodes.label: Maurizio Taddei
nodes.summary: Maurizio Taddei (1936–2000) was a scholar in archaeology, history, and Indology. He was a professor at the Istituto Italiano per il Medio ed Estremo Oriente (~1964–1995) and director of the editorial committee at the Istituto Italiano per l'Africa e l'Oriente (~1995–2000).

nodes.label: Edeltraud Harzer
nodes.summary: Working in Indology and philosophy, Edeltraud Harzer studied at Charles University and the University of Washington (PhD), and under traditional teachers Shree Narayan Mishra and Ram Shankar Bhattacharya. She held posts at Puget Sound, Washington, Stanford, Indiana, and UT Austin (1998).

nodes.label: Kamlesh Dutt Tripathi
nodes.summary: Kamlesh Dutt Tripathi is an Indology and religious studies scholar who taught Hisayoshi Miyamoto and Shujun Motegi. He held posts at Banaras Hindu University and served as an advisor at the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (attested 2009).

nodes.label: Steven Edward Lindquist
nodes.summary: Steven Edward Lindquist is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Texas at Austin under Patrick Olivelle, also studying under traditional teachers, and held a post at Concordia University.

nodes.label: Matthew R. Sayers
nodes.summary: Matthew R. Sayers is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Texas at Austin under Joel Peter Brereton and Patrick Olivelle, and held an attested post at Lebanon Valley College in 2013.

nodes.label: International Academy of Indian Culture
variants: International Academy of Indian Culture, New Delhi

nodes.label: Ram Shankar Tripathi
nodes.summary: Ram Shankar Tripathi (1929–2019) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He held professorial posts at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (~1977–1994) and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1989–1998).

nodes.label: Stanley Wolpert
nodes.summary: Stanley Wolpert was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. Educated at City College of New York and the University of Pennsylvania, he served as a distinguished professor emeritus of history at UCLA from circa 1959 to 2002.

nodes.label: Wannaporn Rienjang
nodes.summary: Wannaporn Rienjang is an archaeologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD from the University of Cambridge. She held posts at the British Museum, the University of Oxford (attested 2019–2022), and Thammasat University (attested 2022–2023).

nodes.label: Peter Stewart
nodes.summary: Peter Stewart (b. 1971) is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. In 2011, he held posts at the Classical Art Research Centre and as Associate Professor of Classical Art and Archaeology at the University of Oxford.

nodes.label: Horace Geoffrey Quaritch Wales
nodes.summary: Horace Geoffrey Quaritch Wales (1900–1981) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Charterhouse School and Queens' College, Cambridge (~1919–1922), he served as Field Director for the Greater India Research Committee (~1934–1941).

nodes.label: John Allan
nodes.summary: John Allan was an Indologist and historian. He studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1901–1906) and Leipzig University (~1906–1907), later serving as Keeper of the Department of Coins and Medals at the British Museum (~1931–1949).

nodes.label: Jean Philippe Vogel
nodes.summary: Jean Philippe Vogel was an Indology and archaeology scholar who studied at the University of Amsterdam (~1890–1897). He worked for the Archaeological Survey of India (1910–1911) and served as director at Leiden University (attested 1910, 1914–1939).

nodes.label: Niranjan Prasad Chakravarti
nodes.summary: Niranjan Prasad Chakravarti was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied at Paris, Berlin, and Cambridge (PhD ~1924-1926). He lectured at Calcutta University (1917) before serving in the Archaeological Survey of India (1929-1950), becoming Director General of Archaeology in India (1948-1950).

nodes.label: Ryutaro Tsuchida
nodes.summary: Ryutaro Tsuchida (born 1947) is an Indologist. He studied at the University of Tokyo and at the University of Marburg (~1973–1979) under Wilhelm Rau and others, later serving as professor at the University of Tokyo (~1986–2012).

nodes.label: Tej Ram Sharma
nodes.summary: Tej Ram Sharma is an Indologist and historian who completed his doctoral thesis at Banaras Hindu University in 1968 and held a post at Himachal Pradesh University (~1976).

nodes.label: Vishwa Nath Pathak
nodes.summary: Vishwa Nath Pathak was an Indology and history scholar who held posts, including Professor, at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University (attested 1978 and 1987).

nodes.label: Travis L. Smith
nodes.summary: Travis L. Smith is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at UC Berkeley under Vasudha Dalmia and Robert and Sally Goldman, and earned his PhD at Columbia under John Stratton Hawley in 2007. He held posts at Barnard and Florida.

nodes.label: C. S. Srinivasachariar
nodes.summary: C. S. Srinivasachariar worked in Indology and history and archaeology. He served as a professor at Pachaiyappa's College and as a professor at Annamalai University (attested 1932–1933).

nodes.summary: Haridas Bhattacharyya was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Scottish Church College and the University of Calcutta. He held academic posts at the University of Calcutta (~1917–1921), University of Dhaka (~1921–1947), and Banaras Hindu University (~1948–1952).

nodes.label: Alfred Cooper Woolner
nodes.description: British academic (1878–1936); Vice-Chancellor of the University of the Punjab
nodes.summary: Alfred Cooper Woolner (1878–1936) was an Indologist and linguist educated at Ipswich School and Trinity College, Oxford. He served as Principal of Oriental College, Lahore (c. 1903–1936), Honorary Librarian at Panjab University, and Vice-Chancellor of the University of the Punjab.

nodes.label: Kshetresh Chandra Chattopadhyaya
nodes.summary: Kshetresh Chandra Chattopadhyaya (1896–1974) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Presidency University, University of Calcutta, and University of Allahabad. He taught at Calcutta (~1919–1924) and Allahabad (~1924–1956), and served as Ex-Director at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1956–1968).

nodes.label: Sheldon Pollock
nodes.summary: Sheldon Pollock is an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at Harvard University (~1971–1975). He held posts at the University of Iowa (~1977–1989), University of Chicago (~1989–2005), Columbia University (~2005), and Clay Sanskrit Library (~2005–2008).

nodes.label: Isabelle Onians
nodes.summary: Isabelle Onians works in Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed a PhD at the University of Oxford by 2002 and served as an editor at the Clay Sanskrit Library.

nodes.label: David N. Lorenzen
nodes.summary: David N. Lorenzen is an Indologist and historian. He studied at SOAS and the Australian National University (doctoral supervisor A. L. Basham), and he held a long-term post as professor and research scholar at El Colegio de México (~1970).

nodes.label: Sonam Kachru
nodes.summary: Sonam Kachru specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology, earning a PhD at the University of Chicago under Dan Arnold. He held posts at the University of Chicago, Max Planck Institute for the History of Science, and Forum Transregionale Studien.

nodes.label: Jitendranath Mohanty
nodes.summary: Jitendranath Mohanty (1928–2023) worked in philosophy and Indology, studying at the University of Calcutta (~1947–1949) and the University of Göttingen (~1952–1954). He held posts at Calcutta (~1954–1967), Oklahoma (~1972–1986), and Temple University (~1986–2008).

nodes.label: Edward C. Dimock
nodes.summary: Edward C. Dimock specialized in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Yale University (~1950–1953) and held a post at the University of Chicago from ~1957 to 1992.

nodes.label: Kashinath Trimbak Telang
nodes.description: Indian judge, Indologist, writer and translator (1850–1893)
nodes.summary: Kashinath Trimbak Telang was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at the University of Mumbai and Elphinstone College from circa 1864 to 1869, later serving as a Senior Dakshina Fellow at Elphinstone College from around 1869 to 1872.

nodes.label: Mahesh A. Deokar
nodes.summary: Mahesh A. Deokar is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He has held positions at Savitribai Phule Pune University, where he is attested as Professor in 2011 and as Head in 2020–2021.

nodes.id: I:Deshana Institute of Buddhist and Allied Studies
nodes.label: Deshana Institute of Buddhist and Allied Studies
variants: Deshana Institute of Buddhist and Allied Studies

nodes.label: Johannes Schneider
nodes.summary: Johannes Schneider works in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He has been affiliated with the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2013) and served as an editorial board member at the Deshana Institute (attested 2021).

nodes.label: David Drewes
nodes.summary: David Drewes is an indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at Lawrence University, UW-Madison, and the University of Virginia (MA 1999, PhD 2006 under Karen C. Lang), he taught at Virginia, Indiana University (2006), and the University of Manitoba (attested 2009–2010).

nodes.label: Saroja Bhate
nodes.summary: Saroja Bhate (b. 1942) is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. She served as a professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University, attested in 2000 and 2011.

nodes.label: Rasiklal Chhotalal Parikh
nodes.summary: Rasiklal Chhotalal Parikh (1897–1982) was an Indologist and historian who studied at Fergusson College and under Sukhlal Sanghvi. He served as Professor at Gujarat Vidyapith (~1920–1940) and as Secretary of Gujarat Puratattva Mandir.

nodes.label: Ramchandra B. Athavale
nodes.summary: Ramchandra B. Athavale was an Indologist who served as Professor of Sanskrit at Gujarat Vidyapith and at L. D. Arts College (attested 1938).

nodes.label: James McHugh
nodes.summary: James McHugh works in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Cambridge, Oxford, and Harvard (PhD), taught by scholars including Alexis Sanderson, Lawrence McCrea, Anne E. Monius, and Parimal G. Patil. He held posts at USC and Cornell.

nodes.label: Lawrence McCrea
nodes.summary: Lawrence McCrea is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. He studied at Cornell University (ca. 1985–1989) and the University of Chicago (ca. 1990–1998) under Sheldon Pollock, later joining the faculty at Cornell University in ca. 2009.

nodes.label: Anne E. Monius
nodes.summary: Anne E. Monius was a scholar of religious studies and Indology. She studied at Harvard University (~1989–1997) under Diana L. Eck and Kausalya Hart, later holding posts at the University of Virginia (~1997–2001) and Harvard University (2002).

nodes.label: Parimal G. Patil
nodes.summary: Parimal G. Patil specializes in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Harvard University (~1989–1993) and the University of Chicago (~1993–2002), and took up a post at Harvard University circa 2003.

nodes.label: Bhatsakorn Piyobhaso
nodes.native: ภัทรกร ปิโยภาโส

nodes.label: Pondicherry University
variants: Subramania Bharathi School of Tamil Language and Literature, Pondicherry University

nodes.label: K. A. Subramania Iyer
nodes.summary: K. A. Subramania Iyer was an Indologist, linguist, and philosopher who taught Dwijendra Nath Shukla. He served as Vice-Chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and was a professor at the University of Lucknow (attested 1972 and 1987).

nodes.id: I:Oriental Research Institute and Manuscripts Library
nodes.label: Oriental Research Institute and Manuscripts Library
variants: Department for the Publication of Oriental Manuscripts, Trivandrum

nodes.label: Victor Turner
nodes.jawiki: ヴィクター・ターナー
nodes.summary: Victor Turner worked in religious studies and related fields. He studied at University College London (~1938–1949) and the University of Manchester (~1950–1955), and served as chair of the Committee on Social Thought at the University of Chicago (~1968–1977).

nodes.label: Lawrence E. Sullivan
nodes.summary: Lawrence E. Sullivan is a religious studies scholar. He served as Director at Harvard University (attested 2000–2004) and as Professor in the Department of Theology at the University of Notre Dame (attested 2005).

nodes.label: Joseph Mitsuo Kitagawa
nodes.summary: Joseph Mitsuo Kitagawa (1915–1992) studied at Rikkyo University and earned his PhD at the University of Chicago, where he held posts from c. 1951 to 1985 and served as Dean of the Divinity School.

nodes.label: Shimane Prefectural Junior College
variants: 島根県立国際短期大学

nodes.label: Alexandra van der Geer
nodes.summary: Alexandra van der Geer is a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology. She studied under teachers Leendert A. van Daalen, Henk Bodewitz, and Paul Yves Sondaar.

nodes.label: Hirotomo Teranishi
variants: Teranishi Hirotomo 寺西 宏友
nodes.summary: Hirotomo Teranishi succeeded Hiroshi Kanno in 2009 and served as director at Soka University (attested 2010–2011).

nodes.label: Herbert Härtel
nodes.summary: Herbert Härtel (1921–2005) worked in Indology, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, studying under Ernst Waldschmidt (~1948–1953). He served as Director of the Museum für Asiatische Kunst (~1963–1986) and held a professorship at Humboldt University of Berlin (attested 1993–1994).

nodes.label: Oliver Philipp Frey
nodes.summary: Oliver Philipp Frey works in Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Vienna and later held an academic post there.

nodes.label: Alessandro Graheli
nodes.summary: Alessandro Graheli works in Indology and philosophy. By 2022, he was a university assistant at the University of Vienna and a principal investigator at the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.

nodes.label: Yasutaka Muroya
nodes.summary: Yasutaka Muroya works in Indology and philosophy. He has held research associate positions at the University of Vienna (attested 2007), Leipzig University (attested 2015), and the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (attested 2022).

nodes.label: Philipp A. Maas
nodes.summary: Philipp A. Maas is an Indology and philosophy scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Bonn under Claus Vogel and Albrecht Wezler. He held posts at Bonn, the Austrian Academy of Sciences, University of Vienna, and Leipzig University.

nodes.label: Elena Mucciarelli
nodes.summary: Elena Mucciarelli is an Indologist who studied at the University of Tübingen and later held posts there (2016–2017, attested 2022). In 2020, she was Assistant Professor for Hinduism in the Sanskrit Tradition and Gonda Lecturer at the University of Groningen.

nodes.label: Annette L. Heitmann
nodes.summary: Annette L. Heitmann specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and the University of Vienna (doctoral degree, 2002), studying under David Seyfort Ruegg and Christian Lindtner.

nodes.label: Eshin Nishimura
nodes.summary: Eshin Nishimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religion, and philosophy who earned his PhD from Kyoto University (~1957–1965). He held a post at Carleton College (~1966–1967) and served as professor and director at Hanazono University between ~1968 and ~2009.

nodes.label: Paul Pelliot
nodes.summary: Paul Pelliot (1878–1945) was a sinologist, Tibetologist, and Central Asian studies scholar who studied under Édouard Chavannes and Émile Senart. He held positions at EFEO, Collège de France (1909, 1911–1945), and the Institut de France.

nodes.id: I:Institut Belge des Hautes Études Chinoises

variants: ベルギー中國學高等研究所

nodes.label: Gaston Renondeau
variants: ガストン・ルノンドー
nodes.image: Major Gaston Renondeau - Allied missions at Vladivostock LCCN2014708663 (cropped).jpg

nodes.label: Henri Maspero
nodes.image: 201230 camp de Buchenwald dessins de prisonniers par Léon Mazeaud Henri Maspéro Bloc 61 1944 JB (2) (cropped).jpg
nodes.summary: Henri Maspero specialized in Sinology, religious studies, and linguistics, studying at Lycée Louis-le-Grand and ENLOV. He held posts at the École française d'Extrême-Orient, as professor at the Collège de France (1920–1945), and at the Maison Franco-Japonaise (1928–1930).

nodes.label: Marcel Granet
nodes.summary: Marcel Granet was a Sinologist and religious studies scholar who studied at École Normale Supérieure and under Édouard Chavannes. He held posts at École Pratique des Hautes Études, Institut des Hautes Études Chinoises, INALCO, and Collège de France.

nodes.label: Institut des Hautes Études Chinoises
variants: パリ大學中國學高等研究所

nodes.label: Étienne Balázs
variants: エティエンヌ・バラ―シュ
nodes.summary: Étienne Balázs was a sinologist and historian/archaeologist who studied under Otto Franke in 1923. He held posts as a senior researcher at the CNRS in 1949 and as a professor of Chinese economic history at the University of Paris (~1949–1963).

nodes.label: Otto Franke
nodes.summary: Otto Franke was a scholar of Sinology and Indology. He studied at the University of Freiburg (~1883–1884) and the University of Göttingen (~1884–1888), later holding posts at the University of Hamburg (~1910–1923) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1923–1931).

nodes.label: Jacques Gernet
nodes.summary: Jacques Gernet studied at the University of Algiers 1 and École nationale des langues orientales vivantes. A scholar of Sinology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, he held posts at CNRS, EHESS, Sorbonne, Paris Diderot, and Collège de France (1975–1992).

nodes.label: André Bareau
nodes.summary: André Bareau (1921–1993) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Paris, École Pratique des Hautes Études, and Collège de France, later serving as Directeur d'Études at the EPHE (1956) and Directeur at the Collège de France (1971–1991).

nodes.label: Bernard Frank
variants: ベルナール・フランク
nodes.summary: Bernard Frank worked in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, having studied under Rolf Alfred Stein. He served as head of the Maison Franco-Japonaise (~1979–1982) and held the chair of Civilisation japonaise at the Collège de France (1979–1996).

nodes.id: I:Scuola Italiana di Studi sull'Asia Orientale
nodes.label: Scuola Italiana di Studi sull'Asia Orientale

nodes.id: I:Hiroshima Prefectural Chiyoda Senior High School
nodes.label: Hiroshima Prefectural Chiyoda Senior High School
Annette Schmiedchen
nodes.summary: Annette Schmiedchen is an Indology, history, and archaeology scholar. She studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (circa 1985–1994) and the University of Halle-Wittenberg (circa 2000–2007), holding posts at Halle-Wittenberg (circa 1995–2006) and Humboldt University (circa 2011).

nodes.label: Edwin Felix Thomas Atkinson
nodes.summary: Edwin Felix Thomas Atkinson was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at Trinity College Dublin (~1857–1861). He served as President of the Asiatic Society (~1886–1888) and Accountant General for the Government of Bengal (~1888–1890).

nodes.label: Atsushi Kiyozawa
nodes.summary: Atsushi Kiyozawa worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He completed doctoral studies at the University of Delhi and held a lecturer position at Kindai University (attested 1989).

nodes.label: Joseph E. Schwartzberg
nodes.summary: Joseph E. Schwartzberg (1928–2018) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Brooklyn College (c. 1945–1949) and served as a professor of geography at the University of Minnesota from circa 1964 to 2000.

nodes.label: Yaroslav Vassilkov
nodes.summary: Yaroslav Vassilkov (born 1943) is an Indologist who studied at St. Petersburg University (~1960–1966). He held posts at the Russian Academy of Sciences (~1967) and the Faculty of Philosophy at Saint Petersburg State University.

nodes.label: Adam Bowles
nodes.summary: Adam Bowles is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who completed his doctoral studies under Greg Bailey (attested 2004). He served as a senior lecturer in Asian Religions at the University of Queensland (attested 2016–2018).

nodes.label: Greg Bailey
nodes.summary: Greg Bailey is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He completed doctoral studies under J. Durham and was taught by Madeleine Biardeau, later serving as a professor at La Trobe University (attested 1994, 2004).

nodes.label: Julia Leslie
nodes.summary: Julia Leslie worked in Indology and religious studies. She founded SOAS University of London and later held an academic post there from approximately 1993 to 2004.

nodes.label: Palmira Brummett
nodes.summary: Palmira Brummett is a historian and archaeologist. She studied at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (~1968–1974) and the University of Chicago (~1984–1988), and she held a post at the University of Tennessee from circa 1989 to 2011.

nodes.label: Debi Prasanna Pattanayak
nodes.image: Debi Prasanna Pattanayak introducing himself for Voice intro project.jpg
nodes.summary: Debi Prasanna Pattanayak is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Cornell University (~1959–1961) and served as director of the Central Institute of Indian Languages in 1988.

nodes.label: Robin Coningham
nodes.summary: Robin Coningham is a scholar of archaeology and Indology who studied at King's College (1985–1994) and the University of Cambridge (~1989–1994). He held posts at the University of Bradford (~1994–2005) and Durham University (2005).

nodes.label: Ryūō Asahi
nodes.summary: Ryūō Asahi worked in Buddhist studies. He held teaching posts at Koyasan University and at Toji.

nodes.label: Friedrich Hirth
nodes.summary: Friedrich Hirth specialized in Sinology and history and archaeology. He studied at Leipzig (~1865–1866), Berlin (~1866–1867), and Greifswald (~1867–1869), and later held a post at Columbia University (~1902–1917).

nodes.label: William Woodville Rockhill
nodes.jawiki: ウィリアム・ウッドヴィル・ロックヒル
nodes.summary: William Woodville Rockhill (1854–1914) was a scholar in Tibetology and Sinology. He completed his studies at Lycée Condorcet (~1868–1871) and École Spéciale Militaire de Saint-Cyr (~1871–1873).

nodes.label: Phra Brahmapundit
nodes.native: พระพรหมบัณฑิต
nodes.summary: Phra Brahmapundit is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He served as Rector of Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (~1997-2018) and held leadership roles with the International Council for the Day of Vesak and International Association of Buddhist Universities.

nodes.label: Govind Sakharam Kathavate
nodes.summary: Govind Sakharam Kathavate was an Indologist. He held the Sanskrit chair at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute, where he succeeded Ramkrishna Gopal Bhandarkar.

nodes.label: Andrew J. Nicholson
nodes.summary: Andrew J. Nicholson specializes in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied under traditional teacher Shree Narayan Mishra and held a post at Stony Brook University.

nodes.label: John Marshall
nodes.summary: John Marshall was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at Dulwich College, King's College, and the University of Cambridge. He served as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India from 1902 to 1931.

nodes.label: Kashinath Narayan Dikshit
nodes.summary: Kashinath Narayan Dikshit was a scholar in Indology and history and archaeology. He succeeded Rakhaldas Bandyopadhyay and served as Director General of Archaeology at the Archaeological Survey of India in 1937.

nodes.label: Devadatta Ramkrishna Bhandarkar
nodes.summary: Devadatta Ramkrishna Bhandarkar was an Indologist, historian, and archaeologist. He served as Superintendent of the Western Circle at the Archaeological Survey of India (1911-1917) and Carmichael Professor of Ancient Indian History and Culture at the University of Calcutta.

nodes.label: George Abraham Grierson
nodes.jawiki: ジョージ・エイブラハム・グリアソン
nodes.description: Irish linguistic scholar and civil servant (1851–1941)
nodes.summary: George Abraham Grierson (1851–1941) was a linguist and Indologist. He was educated at St. Bees School and Trinity College Dublin, and served in the Indian Civil Service from around 1873 to 1902.

nodes.label: M. H. Krishna
nodes.image: Portrait photograph of M. H. Krishna.jpg
nodes.summary: M. H. Krishna was an Indologist and historian/archaeologist. He studied at Maharaja's College, Mysore (~1907–1911) and served as Professor of History at the University of Mysore (attested 1910).

nodes.label: Charles Duroiselle
nodes.summary: Charles Duroiselle (1871–1951) was a scholar in archaeology, buddhist studies, and indology. He held posts at the École française d'Extrême-Orient (~1905–1916), the University of Yangon (~1908–1919), the Archaeological Survey of India (1919, 1936), and the Department of Archaeology (1936).

nodes.id: I:Department of Archaeology, National Museum and National Library
nodes.label: Department of Archaeology, National Museum and National Library
Madeleine Biardeau
nodes.summary: Madeleine Biardeau (1922–2010) was an Indologist and scholar of philosophy and religious studies. After studying at the École normale supérieure de jeunes filles (~1941–1945), she served as an enseignante at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1956–1989).

nodes.label: Geoffrey Samuel
nodes.summary: Geoffrey Samuel is a scholar of religious studies, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Cambridge under Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah, Peter J. Wilson, and Edmund Leach, later holding professorships at Newcastle, Lancaster, and Cardiff University.

nodes.label: University of Newcastle
variants: University of Newcastle, New South Wales

nodes.label: Sandra Bell
nodes.summary: Sandra Bell works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She completed her doctoral thesis at Durham University by 1991 and later held an academic post there.

nodes.label: Jules Oppert
nodes.jawiki: ジュール・オッペール
nodes.summary: Jules Oppert was a scholar of history, archaeology, linguistics, and Indology. He studied at the Gelehrtenschule des Johanneums and the universities of Heidelberg, Bonn, Berlin, and Kiel. From 1874 to 1905, he served as a professor at the Collège de France.

nodes.label: Klaus Röhrborn
nodes.summary: Klaus Röhrborn (born 1938) is a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. Röhrborn held professorships at the University of Giessen (~1974–1993) and the University of Göttingen (~1993–2004).

nodes.label: R. Venkatraman
nodes.summary: R. Venkatraman completed a PhD at Madurai Kamaraj University (1975–1980) under doctoral supervisors N. Subrahmanian and N. Jagadeesan. Specializing in history, archaeology, and religious studies, he was attested as a Reader at Madurai Kamaraj University in 1990.

nodes.label: Madurai Kamaraj University
variants: Department of Art History, M.K. University, Madurai

nodes.label: Kamil Zvelebil
nodes.summary: Kamil Zvelebil (1927–2009) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Charles University circa 1946–1952 and held positions at the Oriental Institute, ASCR (circa 1952–1968), and Utrecht University (1980–1990).

nodes.label: Herbert Niel Randle
nodes.summary: Herbert Niel Randle (1880–1973) was an Indologist and philosopher. He served as Librarian at the India Office (~1933–1949), a post he is also attested as holding at the India Office Library in 1973.

nodes.label: Sadahiko Kariya
nodes.summary: Sadahiko Kariya worked in Buddhist studies. He held posts as an assistant professor at Shuchiin University (attested 1977) and as a professor in the Faculty of Buddhist Studies at Chizan Senmon Gakko (attested 2001).

nodes.label: Minobusan University
variants: 身延山大学東洋文化研究所
身延山短期大学宗教科

nodes.label: Gensho Imanari
nodes.summary: Gensho Imanari (1925–2020) was a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Waseda University (~1948–1957), held a post at Kokushikan University (~1963–1975), and was an emeritus professor at Rissho University (attested 2001).

nodes.label: Gyoshu Chujo
nodes.summary: Gyoshu Chujo is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor at Minobusan University (attested 1996 and 2001).

nodes.label: Masumi Mochizuki
nodes.summary: Masumi Mochizuki is a Buddhist studies scholar who has served at Minobusan University, where he was attested as a Faculty of Buddhism lecturer in 2001 and as a professor in 2015.

nodes.label: Nobunaga Takasa
nodes.summary: Nobunaga Takasa is a scholar of Buddhist studies who held an assistant professor post at the National Institute of Technology, Sendai College (attested 1991) and a researcher post at Rissho University (attested 2001).

nodes.label: Surama Dasgupta
nodes.summary: Surama Dasgupta (1907–1998) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. She completed an MA and PhD at the University of Calcutta and earned a second PhD at the University of Cambridge.

nodes.label: Elizabeth Ann Cecil
nodes.summary: Elizabeth Ann Cecil, a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and history/archaeology, earned degrees from Hastings College, University of Tennessee, and Brown University under James L. Fitzgerald. She held posts at Groningen, Baroda College, Leiden University, and Florida State University (~2019).

nodes.label: Sam van Schaik
nodes.summary: Sam van Schaik is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Manchester (~1997–2001). He held positions at the British Library, including project manager for the International Dunhuang Project (~2002–2019).

nodes.label: Lewis Doney
nodes.summary: Lewis Doney is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at SOAS University of London and has held posts at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (attested 2018) and the University of Bonn (attested 2021).

nodes.label: Anna Filigenzi
nodes.summary: Anna Filigenzi works in archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. A member of IsMEO in 1984, she later served as director of the Italian Archaeological Mission in Afghanistan (2003) and taught at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" and Federico II.

nodes.label: Metropolitan Museum of Art
variants: Department of Asian Art, The Metropolitan Museum of Art
Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York

nodes.label: Jason Neelis
nodes.summary: Jason Neelis works in Indology and Buddhist studies. Educated at UT Austin and the University of Washington under Richard Salomon, he held posts at Washington, Ruhr University Bochum, and Wilfrid Laurier University.

nodes.label: Richard K. Payne
nodes.summary: Richard K. Payne is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology who studied under Chisei Aratano and Taisen Miyata. He served as Dean at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (~1990–2020) and taught at the Graduate Theological Union (~1996).

nodes.id: I:Centre d'Études de l'Inde et de l'Asie du Sud
nodes.label: Centre d'Études de l'Inde et de l'Asie du Sud
Lhagpa Phuntshogs
nodes.summary: Lhagpa Phuntshogs is a Tibetologist who served as president of the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences (1983–1991) and secretary-general of the Research Association for the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau (1991–2000). In 2000, he became Director General of the China Tibetology Research Center.

nodes.label: Prods Oktor Skjærvø
nodes.summary: Prods Oktor Skjærvø is a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He earned degrees from the University of Oslo and Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz, later holding posts at Mainz, Columbia University, and Harvard University (~1993–2014).

nodes.label: Maheshachandra Nyayaratna Bhattacharyya
nodes.summary: Maheshachandra Nyayaratna Bhattacharyya (1836–1906) worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied under Edward Byles Cowell and served as Principal of the Sanskrit College and University, an affiliation attested in 1882 and 1914.

nodes.label: Vitus Angermeier
nodes.summary: Vitus Angermeier is an Indology scholar. He studied under Roque Mesquita, Chlodwig H. Werba, and Karin Preisendanz (MA supervisor).

nodes.label: Thomas Edward Colebrooke
nodes.summary: Thomas Edward Colebrooke (1813–1890) was an Indologist and historian educated at Eton College and East India Company College. He served as President (1864–1882) and Vice-President (until 1890) of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland.

nodes.label: Pascale Hugon
nodes.summary: Pascale Hugon works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. She held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences and the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia, and taught Flavio A. Geisshuesler.

nodes.label: Friedhelm Hardy
nodes.summary: Friedhelm Hardy (1943–2004) was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He served on the faculty at King's College London (~1974–2004) and as Wilde Lecturer in Comparative Religion at the University of Oxford (1985–1987).

nodes.label: A. N. Narasimhia
nodes.summary: A. N. Narasimhia was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who completed his doctoral studies under Ralph Lilley Turner (attested 1941) and held a post at the University of Mysore.

nodes.label: Ralph Lilley Turner
nodes.description: Indic languages philologist and university administrator (1888–1983)
nodes.summary: Ralph Lilley Turner (1888–1983) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. After studying at Christ's College, Cambridge (~1907–1913), he held posts at Banaras Hindu University (~1920–1922) and served as Director of SOAS University of London (~1937–1957).

nodes.label: Sanne Dokter-Mersch
nodes.summary: Sanne Dokter-Mersch is an Indology scholar who earned her PhD at Leiden University (~2016–2021) under doctoral supervisors Peter Bisschop and Yuko Yokochi.

nodes.label: Heinrich Hettrich
nodes.summary: Heinrich Hettrich (1947–2020) was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at the University of Giessen and Saarland University, and held posts at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1982–1988), Saarland University (~1988–1989), and the University of Würzburg (~1989–2012).

nodes.label: J. G. de Casparis
nodes.summary: J. G. de Casparis was an Indology and history and archaeology scholar. He held a professorship at Leiden University (attested 1987) and a post at SOAS University of London (attested 1991).

nodes.label: Nalini Balbir
nodes.summary: Nalini Balbir (born 1955) is an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied under Colette Caillat (~1976–1980). She has served as a professor at Sorbonne Nouvelle University (~1988–2020) and as Directeur d'études at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~2000).

nodes.label: Sylvain Brocquet
nodes.summary: Sylvain Brocquet is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure in 1980 and held a post at Aix-Marseille University.

nodes.label: Whitney Cox
nodes.summary: Whitney Cox is an Indologist who studied at the University of Virginia (~1993–1997) and at the University of Chicago under Sheldon Pollock (~2000–2006). Cox also held a post at the University of Chicago (attested 2003).

nodes.label: Bard College
variants: Institute of Advanced Theology, Bard College

nodes.label: François Gros
nodes.summary: François Gros (1933–2021) was an Indologist who studied at the University of Lyon (~1951–1956). He later served on the faculty at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1977–2002).

nodes.label: Albert Lutz
nodes.description: Swiss art historian, director Museum Rietberg

nodes.label: Christoph Cüppers
nodes.summary: Christoph Cüppers is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Hamburg (~1974–1983), completing his doctorate under Lambert Schmithausen, and served as Director of the Lumbini International Research Institute (~1993–2013).

nodes.label: Christopher Key Chapple
nodes.summary: Christopher Key Chapple works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He held positions at the Institute for Advanced Studies of World Religions, Stony Brook University, and Loyola Marymount University, where he was named Doshi Professor of Indic and Comparative Theology.

nodes.label: Bloomfield College
variants: Bloomfield College of Montclair State University

nodes.label: Ramesh Shankar Gupte
nodes.summary: Ramesh Shankar Gupte was an Indologist and historian. In 1967, he was Head of History & Ancient Indian Culture at Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Marathwada University and a visiting lecturer at Wake Forest University, Salem College, and Winston-Salem State University.

nodes.label: Dineschandra Sircar
nodes.summary: Indologist and historian Dineschandra Sircar was Government Epigraphist for India at the Archaeological Survey of India (until 1961, attested 1963) and held posts at the University of Calcutta, including Carmichael Professor of Ancient Indian History and Culture from 1962.

nodes.label: Kalikinkar Datta
nodes.summary: Kalikinkar Datta was a historian and Indologist who taught Vishwanath Prasad Varma. He held a long post at Patna University (~1930–1965), where he also served as Vice-Chancellor (attested 1973).

nodes.label: Ram Sharan Sharma
nodes.summary: Ram Sharan Sharma (1919–2011) was a historian and Indologist. He studied at Patna College, Patna University, and SOAS, later holding posts at Patna College (~1946–1970), SOAS, the University of Toronto (~1965–1966), and the University of Delhi (~1973–1985).

nodes.label: Madhav M. Deshpande
nodes.summary: Madhav M. Deshpande (born 1946) is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He served as a Professor at the University of Michigan, with posts attested in 1976 and from 2006 to 2009.

nodes.label: Pandurang Vaman Kane
nodes.image: Pandurang Vaman Kane 2022 stamp of India.jpg
nodes.summary: Pandurang Vaman Kane was an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Mumbai (~1898–1908). He held posts at Elphinstone High School, Elphinstone College, Wilson College, the University of Mumbai, and was National Professor of Indology (~1959–1972).

nodes.label: Amalananda Ghosh
nodes.summary: Amalananda Ghosh (1910–1981) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at University College London and served as Director-General of the Archaeological Survey of India from around 1953 to 1968.

nodes.label: Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan
nodes.image: Photograph of Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan presented to First Lady Jacqueline Kennedy in 1962.jpg
nodes.jawiki: サルヴパッリー・ラーダークリシュナン
nodes.description: 2nd President and 1st Vice President of India, Indian philosopher and politician (1888–1975)
nodes.summary: Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan (1888–1975) was a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and religious studies educated at MCC and Madras. He held professorships at Mysore, Calcutta, and Oxford, and served as vice chancellor of BHU and chancellor of Delhi University.

nodes.label: Edwin Whitfield Fay
nodes.summary: Edwin Whitfield Fay was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Rhodes College and Johns Hopkins under Bloomfield, Gildersleeve, Wright, Smyth, Warren, and Bright. He held posts at the University of Michigan (~1890–1891) and Washington and Lee University (~1893–1899).

nodes.label: Rhodes College
variants: South-Western Presbyterian University of Clarksville, Tennessee

nodes.label: Basil Lanneau Gildersleeve
nodes.summary: Basil Lanneau Gildersleeve was a linguist who studied at Princeton (~1847-1849), the University of Bonn (~1851-1852), and under Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl (~1851-1853). He served as a professor at Johns Hopkins University (~1876-1915).

nodes.label: John Henry Wright
nodes.image: John Henry Wright young age photo.jpg
nodes.summary: John Henry Wright was a scholar of linguistics and history/archaeology who studied at Dartmouth College (~1869–1873). He held appointments at Johns Hopkins University (~1886–1887) and as a professor at Harvard University (~1887–1908).

nodes.label: Herbert Weir Smyth
nodes.summary: Herbert Weir Smyth (1857–1937) was a linguist who studied at Swarthmore, Harvard, Leipzig, and Göttingen. He held posts at Williams College (~1881–1882), Johns Hopkins (~1883–1885), Bryn Mawr (~1888–1901), and Harvard University (~1901–1925).

nodes.label: Minton Warren
nodes.summary: Minton Warren was a linguist who studied at Yale University (~1866–1870). He served on the faculty at Johns Hopkins University (~1879–1899) and Harvard University (~1899–1907).

nodes.label: James Wilson Bright
nodes.summary: Linguist James Wilson Bright studied at Lafayette College (~1873–1877) and Johns Hopkins University (~1879–1882). He taught Edwin Whitfield Fay and Franklin Edgerton, holding posts at Cornell University (~1885–1886) and Johns Hopkins University (~1885–1925).

nodes.label: Yukio Yamanaka
nodes.summary: Yukio Yamanaka works in Indology and linguistics. Yamanaka was a graduate student at Kyoto University (attested 1996) and served as a DFG Research Fellow at the University of Göttingen (attested 2015).

nodes.summary: Eisaku Okada works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. After studying at Kyoto University (attested 2014), he held positions at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (2014), Koyasan University (2014), and Kyoto University (2015).

nodes.label: Huanhuan He
nodes.summary: Huanhuan He works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He has held positions at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, the University of Tokyo (attested 2015), and Zhejiang University as a professor (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Hisataka Ishida
nodes.summary: Hisataka Ishida works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his doctorate at the University of Vienna under Helmut Krasser, having also studied under Akira Saito, Hiroshi Marui, Yoichi Fukuda, and Masahiro Inami, and lectured at Aichi Gakuin University (attested 2015).

nodes.summary: Siegfried Lienhard (1924–2011) specialized in Indology. He studied at the University of Vienna (~1943–1949), held a post at the University of Kiel (~1962–1967), and served as a professor at Stockholm University (attested 1991).

nodes.label: Paul Fredericq
nodes.description: historian, teacher, professor and rector from Belgium (1850-1920)
nodes.summary: Paul Fredericq (1850–1920) was a historian who studied at Ghent University and the University of Liège. He held academic posts at the University of Liège (circa 1879–1883) and Ghent University (circa 1883–1920).

nodes.label: Henri Pirenne
nodes.summary: Henri Pirenne was a historian who studied at the University of Liège, Ghent University, Berlin, Leipzig, and Paris. He held academic posts at the University of Liège (~1885–1886) and Ghent University (1886–1930).

nodes.label: Edward James Rapson
nodes.summary: Edward James Rapson worked in Indology, linguistics, and history and archaeology. Educated at St John's College, Cambridge (~1879–1883), he worked at the British Museum (~1887–1906) and UCL (~1903–1906) before serving as professor of Sanskrit at Cambridge (~1906–1936).

nodes.label: Kisari Mohan Ganguli
nodes.summary: Kisari Mohan Ganguli (1848–1908) was an Indologist. Ganguli studied at Presidency University, Kolkata, and the University of Calcutta.

nodes.label: Michael Hutt
nodes.description: Professor of Nepali and Himalayan Studies
nodes.summary: Michael Hutt is an Indology and linguistics scholar. He completed his undergraduate and doctoral studies at SOAS and the University of London between 1977 and 1984, becoming Lecturer in Nepali at SOAS around 1987.

nodes.label: Francis Tiso
nodes.summary: Francis Tiso is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He completed studies at Cornell University (~1968–1972), Harvard Divinity School (~1972–1975), and Columbia University (~1982–1989).

nodes.label: Lobsang Shastri
nodes.summary: Lobsang Shastri specializes in Tibetology. He served as Head Librarian of the Tibetan Section at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives (attested 2003–2006) and as Senior Librarian at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center (attested 2018).

nodes.label: Albrecht Hanisch
nodes.summary: Albrecht Hanisch is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his doctorate at the University of Marburg under Michael Hahn. He held posts at the Nepal Research Centre and the Nepalese-German Manuscript Cataloguing Project.

nodes.label: S. S. Suryanarayana Sastri
nodes.summary: S. S. Suryanarayana Sastri was a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He served at the University of Madras, where he was attested as Reader in Indian Philosophy in 1929 and as Reader and Head of the Department of Philosophy in 1942.

nodes.label: R. Balasubramanian
nodes.summary: R. Balasubramanian (1929–2017) was an Indian philosopher and Indologist who studied under the traditional teacher Varahur Kalyanasundara Sastri. He served as Director at the University of Madras from circa 1976 to 1990.

nodes.label: Harold G. Coward
nodes.summary: Harold G. Coward (born 1936) is an Indology, religious studies, and philosophy scholar. He was a Professor at the University of Calgary (~1974–1992) and later held a post at the University of Victoria (~1992–2004).

nodes.label: Tse-fu Kuan
nodes.summary: Tse-fu Kuan is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a doctorate at the University of Oxford in 2004 under Richard Gombrich. He later held a postdoctoral research post at National Cheng Kung University and a position at Yuan Ze University.

nodes.label: Alexander Yiannopoulos
nodes.summary: Alexander Yiannopoulos specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling and worked under supervisor Karin Myers (attested 2012–2017) along with several other teachers.

nodes.label: John J. Makransky
nodes.summary: John J. Makransky is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1990. He held faculty posts at Boston College, the Rangjung Yeshe Institute, and CIHTS.

nodes.label: Jay L. Garfield
nodes.summary: Jay L. Garfield is a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar. He has held faculty posts at Hampshire College, Smith College, the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, the University of Massachusetts Amherst, the University of Melbourne, and NUS.

nodes.label: T. S. Srinivasa Sastri
variants: シュリーニヴァーサ・シャーストリー
nodes.summary: T. S. Srinivasa Sastri worked in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He held positions at the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute, attested in 1972 and later as professor from 1984 to 1992.

nodes.label: Yao Wang
nodes.summary: Yao Wang (1928–2015) was a scholar of Tibetology and Sinology who studied under traditional teacher Gongkar Tulku and served as a guest professor at the University of Vienna.

nodes.label: Susan J. Rosenfield
nodes.summary: Susan J. Rosenfield is an Indologist who completed her PhD at Harvard University in 2004, studying under faculty including Stephanie W. Jamison and George L. Hart.

nodes.label: Bhagavan Das
nodes.summary: Bhagavan Das (1869–1958) was a scholar in philosophy and Indology who earned an M.A. from the University of Calcutta. He served as Honorary Secretary at Central Hindu College (~1898–1914).

nodes.label: John W. Spellman

nodes.label: Wolfgang Morgenroth
nodes.summary: Wolfgang Morgenroth (1930–2021) was an Indologist and linguist. He completed his PhD at the University of Jena under Richard Hauschild and held posts at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1976–1995) and the University of Potsdam (2020).

nodes.label: Ram Karan Sharma
nodes.summary: Ram Karan Sharma (1927–2018) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Patna University and earned his PhD at UC Berkeley under Murray Barnson Emeneau, later holding posts at Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar Bihar University and the Central Sanskrit Board.

nodes.label: Arvind Sharma
nodes.summary: Arvind Sharma is a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned degrees from Allahabad, Syracuse, Harvard Divinity School, and Harvard University. He held positions at Queensland, Harvard (Infinity Foundation Visiting Professor), and McGill (Birks Chair, circa 1987).

nodes.label: Gyatsho Tshering
nodes.summary: Gyatsho Tshering (1936–2009) was a Tibetology scholar who studied at the University of Calcutta. He founded the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives and served as its director from around 1972 to 1998.

nodes.label: Ellen M. Raven
nodes.summary: Ellen M. Raven is an Indologist and archaeologist who held posts at Leiden University, attested in 2003 and on the Editorial Board in 2018.

nodes.label: Corrado Pensa
nodes.summary: Corrado Pensa worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, having studied under Raniero Gnoli and Giuseppe Tucci. He served as Professor of Religions and Philosophy of India and the Far East at Sapienza University of Rome (attested 1971).

nodes.label: K. V. Ramesh

nodes.label: Gudrun Melzer

nodes.label: Annemarie Schimmel
nodes.summary: Annemarie Schimmel (1922–2003) studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (circa 1939–1941). A scholar of religious studies, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology, she held posts at Marburg, Ankara, Bonn, and Harvard University (circa 1970–1992).

nodes.summary: Arinde L. Jonker is an Indologist who completed a Research MA at Leiden University (attested 2018). Her studies were supervised by Peter Bisschop alongside instruction from Jonathan A. Silk.

nodes.label: Hermann Goetz
nodes.summary: Hermann Goetz (1898–1976) worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. After studying at the Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1920–1923), he served as curator at Baroda Museum and Picture Gallery (~1939–1953) and held a post at Heidelberg University (~1961–1972).

nodes.label: Haraprasad Shastri
nodes.summary: Haraprasad Shastri was an Indologist and historian who studied at Sanskrit College and University and Presidency University, Kolkata. He held posts at Hare School, Presidency University, Sanskrit College and University (~1895–1908), and the University of Dhaka (~1921–1924).

nodes.label: Ibrahim Shah
nodes.summary: Ibrahim Shah is an archaeology scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Peshawar under Muhammad Farooq Swati in 2007. He serves as Associate Professor and Department Chairman at Hazara University.

nodes.label: Pratapaditya Pal
nodes.summary: Pratapaditya Pal works in Indology, Tibetology, and history and archaeology. He held posts at the Los Angeles County Museum of Art (~1970–1995, attested 2007) and the Art Institute of Chicago (1995).

nodes.label: Gustaaf Houtman

nodes.label: Prahlad Pradhan
nodes.summary: Prahlad Pradhan was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied at Visva-Bharati University and Patna University. His career included posts at Ravenshaw College, Utkal University (~1960–1975), Gangadhar Meher University, and Shri Jagannath Sanskrit University.

nodes.label: N. Aiyaswami Sastri
nodes.summary: N. Aiyaswami Sastri was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held professorships at Sri Venkateswara Oriental College (attested 1940) and Visva-Bharati University (attested 1971).

nodes.summary: Thubten Zopa Rinpoche (1946–2023) was an active figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Thubten Yeshe (circa 1959–1984), Trijang Rinpoche (circa 1959–1981), and Denma Lochö Rinpoche, and co-founded Kopan Monastery by 1971.

nodes.label: Kurt Andrew Johnson
nodes.summary: Kurt Andrew Johnson is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He completed his PhD at the University of York in 2010 under the supervision of Jane Moody.

nodes.label: Martin Baumann
nodes.description: German university teacher in religious studies at university of Lucerne (Switzerland)
nodes.summary: Martin Baumann is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies. He joined the University of Lucerne in 2001, where he served as Professor of Religious Studies.

nodes.label: J. Gordon Melton
nodes.summary: Religious studies scholar J. Gordon Melton studied at Birmingham–Southern College, Garrett-Evangelical Theological Seminary, and Northwestern University. His posts include directing the Institute for the Study of American Religion (~1969) and positions at UC Santa Barbara (~1985–2011) and Baylor University (~2011).

nodes.label: George D. Bond
nodes.summary: George D. Bond (1942–) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at the University of Sri Lanka and Northwestern University, where he completed his PhD and served as Professor of Religion from around 1974 to 2011.

nodes.label: Richard Kieckhefer
nodes.summary: Richard Kieckhefer is a scholar of religious studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Saint Louis University (~1964–1968) and the University of Texas at Austin (~1968–1972), joining Northwestern University in 1975.

nodes.label: Gavin Flood
nodes.summary: Gavin Flood (born 1954), an Indology and religious studies scholar, studied at Lancaster University (~1980–1989) under Andrew Rawlinson and David Smith. He held positions at Lampeter, the University of Stirling, Oxford Centre for Hindu Studies, and the University of Oxford.

nodes.label: Carola Roloff
nodes.summary: Carola Roloff is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She completed her PhD at the University of Hamburg (~2004–2009) under David P. Jackson, worked at Tibetisches Zentrum Hamburg (~1985–2000), and was a researcher at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (2006–2007).

nodes.label: C. W. Huntington
nodes.summary: C. W. Huntington worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan (~1980–1986) under Luis Oscar Gómez and Madhav M. Deshpande, and served as a professor at Hartwick College (~1992–2020).

nodes.label: Monika Zin
nodes.summary: Monika Zin is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. After studying at Jagiellonian University and LMU Munich, she held professorships at LMU Munich and the Free University of Berlin, and became a team leader at the Saxon Academy in 2016.

nodes.id: I:Saxon Academy of Sciences and Humanities in Leipzig
nodes.label: Saxon Academy of Sciences and Humanities in Leipzig
variants: Saxon Academy of Sciences in Leipzig

nodes.label: Dalsukh D. Malvania
nodes.summary: Dalsukh D. Malvania was an Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies scholar. He held an attested post at Banaras Hindu University in 1951 and served as Director of the L.D. Institute of Indology, attested from 1965 to 1971.

nodes.label: L.D. Institute of Indology
variants: L. D. Bharatiya Sanskriti Vidya Mandir

nodes.label: Douglas Osto
nodes.summary: Douglas Osto is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his Master's at the University of Washington and his PhD at SOAS under Ulrich Pagel. Around 2005, he became a Senior Lecturer at Massey University.

nodes.label: Dan Lusthaus
nodes.summary: Dan Lusthaus is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed his Ph.D. at Temple University. He has taught at Grinnell College, Bates College, Macalester College, Florida State University, the University of Georgia, and Harvard University.

nodes.label: Gunapala Dharmasiri
nodes.summary: Gunapala Dharmasiri is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who held an academic post at the University of Ceylon, attested in 1991 and 2008.

nodes.label: Ulrich Pagel
nodes.summary: Ulrich Pagel works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied under Tadeusz Skorupski, Philip Denwood, and Renate Söhnen-Thieme, and held an academic post at SOAS University of London (attested 2013–2020).

nodes.label: Carola S. Carstens
nodes.summary: Carola S. Carstens works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She held a post at Rice University (1998–1999) and earned her PhD from the University of Hamburg by 2005.

nodes.label: Michael Balk
nodes.summary: Michael Balk is a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He was a doctoral student at the University of Bonn until 1988 and held a post at the Berlin State Library, attested in 1991.

nodes.label: Richard Carnac Temple
nodes.summary: Richard Carnac Temple (1850–1931) studied at Harrow School and Trinity Hall. A scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology, he served in the Bengal and Indian Staff Corps and was editor and proprietor of The Indian Antiquary.

nodes.label: Friedrich Alexander Bischoff
nodes.summary: Friedrich Alexander Bischoff (1928–2009) worked in Sinology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Paris (~1954–1959) and served as Professor of Sinology at the University of Hamburg (~1976–1982).

nodes.label: William C. Kirby
nodes.summary: William C. Kirby (born 1950) is a Sinologist and historian. He studied at Dartmouth College (~1968–1972) and Harvard University (~1973–1981), later holding a post at Harvard (~1992).

nodes.label: Philip A. Kuhn
nodes.summary: Philip A. Kuhn was a sinologist and historian who studied at Harvard, SOAS, and Georgetown. He served at the University of Chicago (1963-1978), Harvard University from 1978, and directed the Fairbank Center for Chinese Studies (1980-1986).

nodes.label: Nicola Di Cosmo
nodes.summary: Nicola Di Cosmo works in Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at Indiana State University and Indiana University (~1985-1991). He held posts at Cambridge (~1989-1992), Harvard (~1993-1999), Canterbury (~1999-2003), and the Institute for Advanced Study (~2003).

nodes.label: Amdo Geshe Thubten Gyatso
variants: A mdo dge bshes Thub bstan rgya mtsho

nodes.label: Arthur Waley
nodes.jawiki: アーサー・ウェイリー
nodes.summary: Arthur Waley worked in Sinology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Rugby School and King's College, and having studied under Gustav Haloun, he held posts at the British Museum (1913) and SOAS University of London (~1934–1939).

nodes.label: William Theodore de Bary
nodes.jawiki: ウィリアム・セオドア・ド・バリー
nodes.description: American sinologist and scholar of East Asian philosophy (1919–2017)
nodes.summary: William Theodore de Bary (1919–2017) was a scholar of Sinology, Japanology, and philosophy. He studied at Columbia and Harvard universities, later serving as Carpentier Professor of Oriental Studies at Columbia from around 1953 to 1990.

nodes.label: Charles A. Moore
nodes.summary: Charles A. Moore (1901–1967) was a philosopher who studied at Yale University (~1926–1932). He served as a professor at the University of Hawaii (~1936–1967) and edited Philosophy East and West (~1951–1967).

nodes.label: William James
nodes.image: William James by Alice M. Boughton, c. 1907, platinum print, from the National Portrait Gallery - NPG-NPG 87 37James-000001 (cropped).jpg
nodes.jawiki: ウィリアム・ジェームズ
nodes.summary: William James (1842–1910) was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. Educated at Plymouth College and Harvard University (~1861–1869), he held a post at Harvard University from ~1872 to 1907.

nodes.label: Maurice O'Connell Walshe
nodes.summary: Maurice O'Connell Walshe (1911–1998) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and linguistics who studied under Walpola Rahula. He held a post at the Institute of Germanic and Romance Studies from circa 1955 to 1979.

nodes.id: I:Institute of Germanic and Romance Studies
nodes.label: Institute of Germanic and Romance Studies
variants: Institute of Germanic Studies, University of London
Institute of Germanic Studies in London University

nodes.label: Ann Heirman
nodes.summary: Ann Heirman is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. She held posts at the National Fund for Scientific Research (1995–2009) and Ghent University (2003–2012), where around 2002 she was professor of Chinese language and culture and head of the Centre for Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Lisa N. Owen
nodes.summary: Lisa N. Owen is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. She earned her Ph.D. at the University of Texas at Austin under doctoral supervisor Janice Leoshko, and studied under Walter M. Spink in 1995.

nodes.id: I:Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts
nodes.label: Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts
variants: Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts
Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA)

nodes.label: Mattia Salvini
nodes.summary: Mattia Salvini is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at SOAS University of London under Tadeusz Skorupski and held posts at the International Buddhist College and Mahidol University.

nodes.label: Daud Ali
nodes.summary: Daud Ali (born 1964) is a scholar of Indology and history. He studied at William & Mary (~1982–1986) and the University of Chicago (~1988–1996), and held posts at the University of Pennsylvania (~2009) and SOAS University of London (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Harold Hargreaves
nodes.description: British archaeologist; active in British India
nodes.summary: Harold Hargreaves (1876–1951) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Officiating Director General of Archæology in India at the Archaeological Survey of India in 1914 and from 1928 to 1931.

nodes.label: Biraja Sankar Guha
nodes.summary: Biraja Sankar Guha (1894–1961) was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied at Scottish Church College, Calcutta, and Harvard. He held posts at Calcutta, the Zoological Survey of India (~1927–1945), and the Ethnographic Survey of India.

nodes.label: Frederick M. Asher
nodes.summary: Frederick M. Asher (1941–2021) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He spent his career at the University of Minnesota, serving as Professor from ~1970 to 2021.

nodes.label: Shailendra Bhandare
nodes.summary: Shailendra Bhandare specializes in history, archaeology, and Indology. He held positions at the British Museum and Fitzwilliam Museum, and served at the Ashmolean Museum (attested 2006–2022) and as a Fellow at St Cross College, Oxford (attested 2022).

nodes.label: Dilip K. Chakrabarti
nodes.summary: Archaeologist and Indologist Dilip K. Chakrabarti studied at the University of Calcutta (~1959-1965). He held posts at Calcutta (~1965-1977), the University of Delhi (~1977-1990), and Cambridge (~1990-2007) as Professor of South Asian Archaeology.

variants: Library of Congress Field Office in India
Library of Congress Middle Eastern Office
United States Library of Congress Field Office

variants: 長谷川仏教文化研究所

nodes.label: Saileswar Sen
nodes.summary: Saileswar Sen was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at the University of Calcutta until 1920 and completed doctoral studies under Barend Faddegon.

nodes.label: Barend Faddegon
nodes.summary: Barend Faddegon was a scholar of indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Amsterdam (~1894-1904) and later held a post there from 1907 to 1944.

nodes.label: Krishna Kanta Handiqui
nodes.image: Krishna Kanta Handique 1983 stamp of India.jpg
nodes.summary: Krishna Kanta Handiqui was an Indologist who earned M.A. degrees from the University of Calcutta and the University of Oxford. He served as Principal at Jagannath Barooah College (~1930–1948) and Vice-Chancellor of Gauhati University (~1948–1957).

nodes.label: Suryya Kumar Bhuyan
nodes.summary: Suryya Kumar Bhuyan (1894–1964) was an Indology and history scholar. He studied at Cotton University, Presidency University, Kolkata, and the University of Calcutta (~1913–1916), later serving as a professor at Cotton University (attested 1956).

nodes.label: Banikanta Kakati
nodes.summary: Banikanta Kakati worked in linguistics and indology. He studied at the University of Calcutta (~1916-1918) and served as a professor at Cotton University (~1918-1947).

nodes.label: Cathy Cantwell
nodes.summary: Cathy Cantwell specializes in tibetology and buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Kent (~1984–1989) and held a post at the University of Oxford in 2002.

nodes.label: Robert Mayer
nodes.summary: Robert Mayer specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed a dissertation at the University of Bristol (-1985), earned a Ph.D. at Leiden University supervised by Tilmann Vetter, Alexis Sanderson, and Pieter Cornelis Verhagen, and joined Oxford's Oriental Studies Faculty in 2002.

nodes.label: Esho Kawasaki
nodes.summary: Esho Kawasaki is a Buddhist studies scholar. Kawasaki served as director of the Buddhist Cultural Institute (attested 1999) and president of Kyushu Ryukoku Gakkai (attested 2002).

nodes.label: Fang-kuei Li
nodes.summary: Fang-kuei Li specialized in linguistics, sinology, and Tibetology. After studying at Tsinghua University (~1921–1924) and the University of Michigan (~1924–1926), he held posts at Chicago (~1928–1929), Yale (~1937–1939), the University of Washington (~1949–1969), and Hawaii (~1969–1974).

nodes.label: Hellmut Wilhelm
nodes.summary: Hellmut Wilhelm worked in Sinology, studying at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1928–1932). He later served as Professor of Chinese Studies and Associate Director of the Far Eastern Institute at the University of Washington (~1948–1973).

nodes.label: Joseph Rock
nodes.jawiki: ジョセフ・フランシス・チャールズ・ロック

nodes.label: Peter M. Scharf
nodes.summary: Peter M. Scharf (b. 1957) is an Indologist and linguist. He completed his dissertation at the University of Pennsylvania under George Cardona, and also studied under Shree Narayan Mishra, Ludo Rocher, and Narendranath Pandey.

nodes.label: Qian Lin
nodes.summary: Qian Lin specializes in Buddhist studies. She studied at Fudan University, the University of Bristol, and the University of Washington, where she was supervised by Collett Cox and taught by Rupert Gethin, among others.

nodes.label: Fudan University
variants: National Institute for Advanced Humanistic Studies at Fudan University

nodes.label: Amy Snyder Ohta
nodes.summary: Amy Snyder Ohta works in linguistics and Japanology. She studied at the University of California, Los Angeles (1990, 1993), taught Qian Lin, and held a post at the University of Washington (~1995).

nodes.label: Izumi Matsuda-Kiami
nodes.summary: Izumi Matsuda-Kiami works in the fields of linguistics and Japanology. Educated at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, she later held an academic post at the University of Washington.

nodes.label: Chi-chiang Huang
nodes.summary: Chi-chiang Huang specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history and archaeology. He earned his PhD at the University of Arizona in 1986 under doctoral supervisor Jing-shen Tao, also studying under Robert M. Gimello.

nodes.label: John Jorgensen
nodes.summary: John Jorgensen is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and Japanology who completed his MA under Kenneth H. J. Gardiner at Australian National University in 1979. He has held appointments at ANU, Griffith University, and La Trobe University.

nodes.label: Miriam Levering
nodes.summary: Miriam Levering was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. She earned her PhD from Harvard University in 1978 and served as Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Tennessee (attested 2007–2010).

nodes.label: Whalen Lai
nodes.summary: Whalen Lai studied at International Christian University and Harvard University (~1968–1975). In Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies, he held posts at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (attested 1993) and the University of California, Davis (attested 2009).

nodes.label: Taigen Dan Leighton
nodes.summary: Taigen Dan Leighton is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the Graduate Theological Union and studied under multiple traditional teachers. He held posts at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (adjunct professor, attested 2006–2010) and Loyola University Chicago (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Shohaku Okumura
nodes.summary: Shohaku Okumura (born 1948) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University (~1968–1972) and under Kosho Uchiyama (1972–1975). He held posts at Minnesota Zen Meditation Center and the Soto Zen Buddhism International Center.

nodes.label: Ruth Fuller Sasaki
nodes.summary: Ruth Fuller Sasaki was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at the University of Chicago (~1910–1913). She served as director of the First Zen Institute of America (~1945–1967) and abbess of Ryōsen-an (~1958–1967).

nodes.label: Nandamālābhivaṃsa
nodes.native: နန္ဒမာလာဘိဝံသ
