variants: Department of Oriental Studies, Art and Sciences University, Mandalay

nodes.label: Masanori Nakagawa
nodes.summary: Masanori Nakagawa is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a lecturer (attested 1991) and assistant professor of literature (attested 2002) at Chikushi Jogakuen University.

nodes.label: M. Shinoda
nodes.image: Linkin Park - From Zero Lead Press Photo - James Minchin III (Mike Shinoda).jpg
nodes.description: American musician, rapper, singer and songwriter
nodes.summary: M. Shinoda (born 1977) is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. Shinoda studied at Agoura High School and the Art Center College of Design, and was taught by Seiren Matsunami.

nodes.label: Mun-keat Choong
nodes.summary: Mun-keat Choong is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Paramadhamma Buddhist Institute (1982) and Komazawa University (BA ~1986–1990). He completed an MA (~1991–1994) supervised by Roderick S. Bucknell and a PhD (~1994–1998) at the University of Queensland.

nodes.label: Roderick S. Bucknell
nodes.summary: Roderick S. Bucknell is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. He held academic posts at the University of Queensland from around 1976 to 1998 and as Associate Professor from around 1999 to 2002.

nodes.label: Asim Kumar Chatterjee
nodes.description: indologist; writer; taught at Dept. of Ancient Hist. and Culture, Calcutta U., India
nodes.summary: Asim Kumar Chatterjee is a historian and Indologist. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Calcutta under D. Mukherjee (~1963–1967), where he later was a Senior Research Fellow (~1968–1972). He also lectured in English at Jangipur College.

nodes.label: Lobsang Dargyay
nodes.summary: Lobsang Dargyay (1935–1994) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Rahor Monastery, Drepung Monastery (~1952–1959), and earned a Dr.phil. at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1970–1974), later teaching Donald Hamilton.

nodes.label: Jeffrey Moussaieff Masson
nodes.image: Jeffrey Masson appearing on "After Dark", 23 September 1989.jpg
nodes.summary: Jeffrey Moussaieff Masson is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at Harvard University (~1964–1970). He held posts at the University of Toronto (~1969–1980), UC Berkeley (~1977–1980 as Professor of Sanskrit), and the University of Michigan.

nodes.label: Anukul Chandra Banerjee
nodes.summary: Anukul Chandra Banerjee was an Indian scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied under Vidhusekhara Bhattacharya and earned a PhD at the University of Calcutta, where he taught Pali, later directing the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology.

nodes.label: Mario Kozah
nodes.summary: Mario Kozah specializes in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Cambridge under James Montgomery and held a post at the American University of Beirut.

nodes.label: James Montgomery
nodes.summary: James Montgomery (b. 1962) studied at the University of Glasgow (~1980–1989). In 1997, he took up a post at the Faculty of Asian and Middle Eastern Studies at Cambridge.

nodes.label: Tarif Khalidi
nodes.summary: Tarif Khalidi is a historian and religious studies scholar. Educated at University College, Oxford (~1957–1960) and the University of Chicago (~1963–1970), he held academic posts at the American University of Beirut (~1970–1996) and the University of Cambridge (~1996–2002).

nodes.label: Richard D. Mann
nodes.summary: Richard D. Mann is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He completed a PhD at McMaster University (attested 2003) under the supervision of Phyllis Granoff.

nodes.label: Elizabeth Errington
nodes.description: specialist on the archaeology of Gandhara and the collections of Charles Masson, and a numismatist specialising in Asian coins
nodes.summary: Elizabeth Errington is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied at SOAS University of London under Adrian David Hugh Bivar (~1980–1987). She served as a curator at the British Museum (~1992–2017).

nodes.label: Gombojab Tsybikov
nodes.summary: Gombojab Tsybikov (1873–1930) was a scholar of Tibetology and Central Asian studies. He studied at Tomsk State University and Saint Petersburg State University, and later served as Lecturer of the Mongolian Language at Far Eastern Federal University (~1902–1917).

nodes.label: Iwao Nakajima
nodes.summary: Iwao Nakajima earned a master's degree from Hitotsubashi University and studied under Nichiki Kimura. Nakajima held posts at the NHK Broadcasting Culture Research Institute until 1975 and as chief editor (主幹) at Sandhaan, attested in 1999.

nodes.label: Robert M. Gimello
nodes.summary: Robert M. Gimello was a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar who earned his PhD at Columbia University (~1968–1976). He headed Oriental Studies and was professor emeritus at the University of Arizona, and served as professor at Harvard University (attested 2004–2007).

nodes.label: Bruce Matthews
nodes.summary: Bruce Matthews, a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies, pursued graduate studies at McMaster University (~1971–1974). He held posts at the University of Ceylon and Acadia University (~1976–2006), where he was C. B. Lumsden Professor of Comparative Religion.

nodes.label: Mathieu Boisvert
nodes.summary: Mathieu Boisvert works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied under Anthony Kennedy Warder and Ravindra Panth, founded the Groupe de recherches interdisciplinaire sur le Montréal ethno-religieux, and became a professor at Université du Québec à Montréal in 1992.

nodes.label: Victor Chan
nodes.image: The Dalai Lama @ The Vancouver Peace Summit.jpg
nodes.summary: Victor Chan (born 1945) is a scholar of Tibetology who studied at the University of Chicago. He served as Executive Director of the Contemporary Tibetan Studies Program at the University of British Columbia (~2005).

nodes.label: Larry DeVries
nodes.summary: Larry DeVries earned a PhD from the University of Minnesota and worked in Indology and religious studies. He taught at Minnesota, Hawaii, and Washington, held a research post at Chicago, and was affiliated with Langara College (attested 2005).

nodes.label: Mavis L. Fenn
nodes.summary: Mavis L. Fenn studied English at the University of Winnipeg, religious studies at the University of Calgary, and completed a PhD under Graeme MacQueen at McMaster University. She held positions at United College (attested 2005–2006) and the University of Waterloo (attested 2016).

nodes.label: James G. Mullens
nodes.summary: James G. Mullens is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at McMaster University and held a post at the University of Saskatchewan in 1989.

nodes.label: Robert Florida
nodes.summary: Robert Florida is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. He served as Dean of Arts and Professor of Religion at Brandon University and later as an Emeritus Fellow at the University of Victoria (attested 2000–2005).

nodes.label: University of Victoria
variants: Centre for the Study of Religion and Society at the University of Victoria

nodes.label: Baihui Wu
nodes.summary: Baihui Wu was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Visva-Bharati University (~1946–1951), Peking University as Professor of Sanskrit (~1952), the Institute of Philosophy (~1956), and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1978).

nodes.label: Jan C. Heesterman
nodes.summary: Jan C. Heesterman was an Indologist who held posts at Leiden University from 1964 to 1990 and as Professor (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Robert Gardner
nodes.summary: Robert Gardner worked in Indology and other fields. He studied at Harvard University (~1944–1958), where he later served as professor from ~1957 to 1997, and held a post at the University of Puget Sound.

nodes.label: R. Gordon Wasson
nodes.jawiki: ロバート・ゴードン・ワッソン
nodes.summary: R. Gordon Wasson (1898–1986) worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Columbia University and the London School of Economics, and held posts in journalism, the American Expeditionary Forces, Guaranty Trust Company, and J.P. Morgan & Co.

nodes.label: Ernest Bender
nodes.summary: Ernest Bender was an Indologist and linguist. After studying at Temple University (~1937–1941) and the University of Pennsylvania (~1941–1947), he served at the University of Pennsylvania as Professor of Indo-Aryan Languages and Literatures (~1950–1989).

nodes.label: Paul Thieme
nodes.summary: Paul Thieme worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Göttingen (~1923–1928) and held posts at Breslau (~1936–1939), Halle-Wittenberg (~1939–1945), Frankfurt (~1953–1960), and Tübingen (1960–1973).

nodes.label: David Webster
nodes.summary: David Webster is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed his PhD at the University of Bristol under the supervision of Peter Harvey.

nodes.label: University of Gloucestershire
variants: Cheltenham and Gloucester College of Higher Education

nodes.label: Ananya Jahanara Kabir
nodes.summary: Ananya Jahanara Kabir is a scholar in Indology and other fields. She studied at the University of Cambridge and took up a post at King's College London in ~2013.

nodes.label: Kanai Lal Hazra
nodes.summary: Kanai Lal Hazra (b. 1932) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He earned his PhD at the University of Ceylon (circa 1965–1968) under Sirima Kiribamune, also studied under Sukumar Sengupta, and was a Pali lecturer at Calcutta.

nodes.label: Dilip Kumar Roy
nodes.summary: Dilip Kumar Roy worked in archaeology and Indology, serving in the Department of Museology at the University of Calcutta, where he was attested as Reader in 1982 and attested again in 1994.

nodes.label: Paul Fuller
nodes.summary: Paul Fuller is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his PhD at the University of Bristol under doctoral supervisor Rupert Gethin, and also studied under Paul Dundas.

nodes.label: Jürgen Neuß
nodes.summary: Jürgen Neuß works in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied under Harry Falk and completed his PhD at the Free University of Berlin in 2007.

nodes.label: Anne Feldhaus
nodes.description: American academic researching Marathi Philology and Ethanography
nodes.summary: Anne Feldhaus is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. She studied at Manhattanville University (~1967–1971) and the University of Pennsylvania (~1971–1976), and held an academic post at Arizona State University (~1981).

nodes.label: John Dowson
nodes.summary: John Dowson was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He held posts at University College London and as Professor of Hindustani at the Staff College, Camberley (~1855–1877).

nodes.label: Krishna Mohan Banerjee
nodes.summary: Krishna Mohan Banerjee was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and philosophy who studied at Hare School and Presidency University, Kolkata. He held posts at Hare School (~1829–1832) and Bishop's College, Kolkata (attested 1869–1870).

nodes.label: Edward Backhouse Eastwick
nodes.summary: Edward Backhouse Eastwick worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at Charterhouse School and Merton College, he served as Professor of Hindústání at East India Company College (~1845–1857) and in the Foreign Office (~1860–1863).

nodes.label: Kuladasa Karunadasa Jayatilleke
nodes.summary: Kuladasa Karunadasa Jayatilleke (1920–1970) worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under Oliver Hector de Alwis Wijesekera and Ludwig Wittgenstein at the University of Cambridge, and later served as Senior Lecturer in Philosophy at the University of Ceylon.

nodes.label: Ludwig Wittgenstein
nodes.jawiki: ルートヴィヒ・ウィトゲンシュタイン
nodes.summary: Ludwig Wittgenstein worked in philosophy. After studies including the University of Manchester and Trinity College, Cambridge (~1911–1913), he held posts at Trinity College, Cambridge (1929–1947) and the University of Cambridge (1939–1947).

nodes.label: Patrick Jory
nodes.summary: Patrick Jory is a historian who studied at the University of Western Australia (~1985–1989) and completed his PhD at the Australian National University (~1991–1996) under Craig J. Reynolds. He held a post at the University of Queensland (~2011).

nodes.label: Craig J. Reynolds
nodes.description: Scholar of Thai literature and culture
nodes.summary: Craig J. Reynolds is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Amherst College (~1959–1963) and Cornell University (~1964–1973), and held posts at the Australian National University around 1989.

nodes.label: Simo Parpola
nodes.summary: Simo Parpola (b. 1943) is a scholar in linguistics and history/archaeology. He served as Professor of Assyriology at the University of Helsinki from ~1979 to 2009.

nodes.label: Pentti Aalto
nodes.summary: Pentti Aalto was an Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at the University of Helsinki (~1934–1949), where he later held an academic post (~1949–1980).

nodes.label: Kimmo Koskenniemi
nodes.summary: Kimmo Koskenniemi (b. 1945) is a linguist who attended Helsingin Suomalainen Yhteiskoulu. He served at the University of Helsinki as Professor of Computer Linguistics (~1989–2012) and as director of the BAULT research community (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Frank Ernest Keay
nodes.birth_place: London Borough of Richmond upon Thames

nodes.label: Thomas Zehnder
nodes.summary: Thomas Zehnder is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He earned his PhD at the University of Zurich under the supervision of Alexander Lubotsky.

nodes.label: Alexander Lubotsky
nodes.summary: Alexander Lubotsky (born 1956) is an Indologist, linguist, and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at Moscow State University (c. 1974–1979) and Leiden University (c. 1979–1987), where he later held a post in 1999.

nodes.label: Jan Gonda
nodes.summary: Jan Gonda worked in Indology, linguistics, and religious studies. He studied at Utrecht University (PhD 1923–1929) and Leiden University (1929–1931), later holding posts at Utrecht University (1932–1950) and the University of Chicago.

nodes.label: M. S. Nagaraja Rao
nodes.summary: M. S. Nagaraja Rao (1932–2011) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Mysore (circa 1951–1955) and served as Director of the Department of Archaeology, Museums and Heritage from circa 1972 to 1983.

nodes.id: I:Department of Archaeology, Museums and Heritage
nodes.label: Department of Archaeology, Museums and Heritage
Govind Swamirao Gai
nodes.summary: Govind Swamirao Gai (1917–1995) was an Indology, history and archaeology, and linguistics scholar. He served the Government of India as Chief Epigraphist (attested 1958–1966) and the Archaeological Survey of India as Chief Epigraphist for India (1966–1976), succeeding Dineschandra Sircar.

nodes.label: Wei-jen Teng
nodes.summary: Wei-jen Teng works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Chicago and Harvard University (PhD attested 2011) under Robert M. Gimello and Parimal G. Patil, later teaching at Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts.

nodes.label: Dylan Esler
nodes.summary: Dylan Esler is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA at SOAS University of London and completed his PhD at KU Leuven by 2018, where he also served as a research scholar.

nodes.label: Chen-kuo Lin
nodes.summary: Chen-kuo Lin studied Buddhist philosophy at Temple University. A scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy, he served as Professor and Distinguished Professor at National Chengchi University and held visiting posts at IIAS and Leiden University.

nodes.label: Andrea Schlosser
nodes.summary: Andrea Schlosser is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. She completed both her Master's degree (-2008) and her PhD (-2014) at the Free University of Berlin.

nodes.label: Yao-ming Tsai
nodes.summary: Yao-ming Tsai is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD from the University of California in 1997 and served as Professor of Philosophy at National Taiwan University.

nodes.label: Cristina Pecchia
nodes.summary: Cristina Pecchia is an Indologist and Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. She studied at Sapienza University of Rome (PhD ~1999–2003) and the University of Vienna (2000), and worked as a project researcher at the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (~2009).

nodes.label: K. Meenakshi
nodes.summary: K. Meenakshi works in Indology and linguistics. She earned a PhD at Savitribai Phule Pune University in 1964 under Madhukar Anant Mehendale and held a post at Jawaharlal Nehru University (attested 1983).

nodes.label: Madhukar Anant Mehendale
nodes.summary: Madhukar Anant Mehendale (1918–2020) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He served as Joint Secretary of the Linguistic Society of India in 1955 and was a Professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 1970, 1983).

nodes.label: Adyar Library and Research Centre
variants: The Adyar Library and Research Centre

nodes.label: James Haughton Woods
nodes.summary: James Haughton Woods (1864–1935) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at Harvard, Strasbourg, and under Paul Deussen, Arthur Venis, Mukunda Shastri Adkar, and Charles Rockwell Lanman. He held a post at Harvard in 1914.

nodes.label: Charles Henry Tawney
nodes.summary: Charles Henry Tawney studied at Trinity College, Cambridge. An Indologist, he was Principal of Presidency University, Kolkata (1876–1892) and Librarian at the India Office and India Office Library (1892/1893–1903).

nodes.label: Institute of Oriental Manuscripts
variants: Institute of Oriental Studies, Russian Academy of Sciences
Institute of Oriental Studies, Russian Academy of Science

nodes.label: Robert Ford Campany
nodes.summary: Robert Ford Campany is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. He was a professor at Indiana University (~1989–2004) and was affiliated with Vanderbilt University around 2010.

nodes.label: Dwijendra Nath Shukla
nodes.summary: Dwijendra Nath Shukla was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who completed a D.Litt. under K. A. Subramania Iyer at the University of Lucknow and held a post at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University (attested 1958).

nodes.label: Jitendra Nath Banerjea
nodes.summary: Jitendra Nath Banerjea (1895–1966) was an Indologist and historian who studied under Hemchandra Raychaudhuri (~1916–1918). He served as Carmichael Professor of Ancient Indian History and Culture at the University of Calcutta (~1952–1959).

nodes.label: Tiziana Pontillo
nodes.summary: Tiziana Pontillo works in the fields of Indology and linguistics. She studied at the University of Cagliari in 2016 and held a post there in 2022.

nodes.label: David Burton
nodes.summary: David Burton specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his doctoral thesis at the University of Bristol (1994–1997) and served as Senior Lecturer in Theology and Religious Studies at Canterbury Christ Church University (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Kodo Akino
nodes.summary: Kodo Akino (1858–1934) worked in Buddhist studies. He studied at Komazawa University and later served as its president (学長).

nodes.label: Nyoten Jimbo
nodes.summary: Nyoten Jimbo (1880–1946) worked in Buddhist studies. He studied under Baisen Azegami and held a professorship at Komazawa University.

nodes.label: Kodo Yamada
nodes.summary: Kodo Yamada (1867–1939) was a Buddhist studies scholar. During his career, he taught at both Komazawa University and Keio University.

nodes.label: Totsudo Kato
nodes.summary: Totsudo Kato (1870–1949) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied under Enryo Inoue (~1890–1893) and Seiran Ouchi, and later held a post at Nihon University.

nodes.label: Tokugen Sakai
nodes.summary: Tokugen Sakai was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Kyoto University. He later served as a professor at Komazawa University.

nodes.label: George Watt
nodes.jawiki: ジョージ・ワット (植物学者)
nodes.summary: George Watt studied at the University of Aberdeen (~1868–1871) and the University of Glasgow (~1871–1873). He later held an academic post at the University of Calcutta from ~1873 to 1884.

nodes.label: Moodeen Sheriff
nodes.description: Indian surgeon and practitioner of native medicine

nodes.label: G. V. Devasthali
nodes.summary: G. V. Devasthali (1906–1994) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Hari Damodar Velankar (attested 1944) and held posts at H.P.T. Arts and R.Y.K. Science College (attested 1944) and Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 1967–1968).

nodes.label: Ram Niwas Pandey
nodes.summary: Ram Niwas Pandey is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed doctoral studies under Hit Narayan Jha and studied at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University and Pt. Deendayal Upadhyaya Institute of Archaeology.

nodes.id: I:Pt. Deendayal Upadhyaya Institute of Archaeology
nodes.label: Pt. Deendayal Upadhyaya Institute of Archaeology
variants: School of Archaeology at New Delhi

nodes.label: Francis X. Clooney
nodes.summary: Francis X. Clooney specializes in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. Educated at Fordham and the University of Chicago (doctorate ~1984), he held posts at Boston College, University of Oxford, Harvard University, and the Oxford Centre for Hindu Studies.

nodes.label: Jacqueline Suthren Hirst
nodes.summary: Jacqueline Suthren Hirst specializes in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy, completing her doctoral studies under Julius Lipner. She held an academic post at the University of Manchester, attested in 2005.

nodes.label: Julius Lipner
nodes.summary: Julius Lipner is an Indologist, philosopher, and religious studies scholar. He studied at King's College London, Clare Hall, Cambridge, and the University of Birmingham. He held posts at the University of Birmingham (~1974–1975) and the University of Cambridge (~1975).

nodes.label: T. V. Ramachandra Dikshitar
nodes.summary: T. V. Ramachandra Dikshitar was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He served as principal of The Madras Sanskrit College (attested 1938) and as professor of Advaita Vedānta at Banaras Hindu University (attested 1946).

nodes.label: Tibet Cultural Relics Bureau
variants: Administrative Commission of Museum and Archaeological Data, Tibet

nodes.label: Elliot M. Stern
nodes.summary: Elliot M. Stern is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He pursued his doctoral studies at the University of Pennsylvania, where he was a Ph.D. candidate until 1988 and earned his Ph.D. by 1998.

nodes.label: Peter Gaeffke
nodes.summary: Peter Gaeffke (1927–2005) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He held posts at Utrecht University (~1964–1975) and served as Professor at the University of Pennsylvania (~1975–1998).

nodes.label: James Morison
nodes.summary: James Morison was an Indology scholar who studied under Georg Bühler. He served as Librarian at the University of Oxford (attested 1917–1920).

nodes.label: Vindhyeshwari Prasad Dube
nodes.summary: Vindhyeshwari Prasad Dube was an Indology scholar who held posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1920 and 1939).

nodes.id: I:United Free Church of Scotland Mission
nodes.label: United Free Church of Scotland Mission
Erik Zürcher
nodes.summary: Erik Zürcher was a scholar in sinology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Leiden University (~1946–1959) and studied under Paul Demiéville, Prabodh Chandra Bagchi, Édouard Chavannes, and Jan Julius Lodewijk Duyvendak, later serving as Leiden's Professor of East Asian History (1961–1993).

nodes.label: John Powers
nodes.summary: John Powers is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his Ph.D. under Jeffrey Hopkins at the University of Virginia. He held professorships at the Australian National University (~1995–2016), Deakin University (2016–2022), and Melbourne (2022).

nodes.label: Vasudev Vishnu Mirashi
nodes.summary: Vasudev Vishnu Mirashi (1893–1985) was an Indologist and historian. He served as Principal and Professor of Sanskrit at Morris College (~1919–1947) and Government Vidarbha Institute (~1947–1950), and later taught at Rashtrasant Tukadoji Maharaj Nagpur University (~1957–1966).

nodes.label: Youru Wang
nodes.summary: Youru Wang works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Temple University under Charles Wei-hsun Fu and Thomas J. Dean, later holding posts at The Chinese University of Hong Kong and Rowan University.

nodes.label: Charles Wei-hsun Fu
nodes.summary: Charles Wei-hsun Fu was a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at National Taiwan University and the University of Illinois System, and held a post at Ohio University circa 1969–1972.

nodes.label: Marc Aurel Stein
nodes.summary: Marc Aurel Stein was a scholar of archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology, educated in Vienna, Leipzig, and Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth. His posts included Principal of Oriental College, Lahore, and Superintendent in the Archaeological Survey of India.

nodes.label: Jinhua Chen
nodes.summary: Jinhua Chen works in Buddhist studies and sinology. He completed graduate studies at McMaster University and postdoctoral research at Kyoto University. Chen held posts at the University of Virginia (attested 2001) and the University of British Columbia (attested 2008–2018).

nodes.label: P. K. Mukhopadhyay
nodes.summary: P. K. Mukhopadhyay works in philosophy and Indology. He was a Professor of Philosophy at Jadavpur University and served as a National Fellow at the Indian Council of Philosophical Research (attested 2009).

nodes.label: Ana Agud
nodes.summary: Ana Agud is an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Salamanca and the University of Tübingen. She served as a professor in the Department of Classical and Indo-European Philology at the University of Salamanca (~1976–2018).

nodes.label: Andrew Glass
nodes.summary: Andrew Glass works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at Bukkyo University (2003) and earned his MA (2000) and PhD (2006) from the University of Washington under Richard Salomon and Collett Cox.

nodes.label: Embar Krishnamacharya
nodes.summary: Embar Krishnamacharya was an Indologist. He held posts as Pandit at the Oriental Research Institute and Manuscripts Library, at the Sanskrit Pathashala in Vadtal (attested 1937), and at Baroda College (attested 1939).

nodes.label: Noémie Verdon
nodes.summary: Noémie Verdon is a scholar of Indology and archaeology. She earned her PhD at the University of Lausanne under Johannes Bronkhorst and Charles Genequand, and held a post at Kyoto University attested in 2019.

nodes.label: John Faithfull Fleet
nodes.summary: John Faithfull Fleet was an Indology and history scholar. Educated at University College London, he served in the Bombay Civil Service and Indian Civil Service (~1867–1897), and as Epigraphist for the Government of India (1883–1886).

nodes.label: C. S. Sundaram
nodes.summary: C. S. Sundaram was an Indologist who held a post at The Madras Sanskrit College and served as Reader in Sanskrit at the University of Madras in 1951. He taught Tomy Augustine.

nodes.label: Masato Kobayashi
nodes.summary: Masato Kobayashi is a linguist and Indologist who studied at Kyoto University and earned his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under George Cardona. He served as a research fellow at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies from circa 2000 to 2002.

nodes.label: University of Pennsylvania Libraries
variants: Van Pelt Library, University of Pennsylvania

nodes.label: Junglan Bang
nodes.summary: Junglan Bang is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Dongguk University, trained under Seung-suk Jung and Sungdoo Ahn, and earned a PhD at the University of Hamburg (2012) under Harunaga Isaacson, later visiting Kyoto University as a researcher.

nodes.label: Karma Lekshe Tsomo
nodes.description: Buddhist nun, scholar and social activist
nodes.summary: Karma Lekshe Tsomo completed a doctorate in comparative philosophy at the University of Hawaii. She held posts at Chaminade University, East-West Center, Jamyang Foundation, University of San Diego, and the University of California, San Diego (attested 2013).

nodes.id: I:Sakyadhita International Association of Buddhist Women
nodes.label: Sakyadhita International Association of Buddhist Women
variants: Sakyadhita: International Association of Buddhist Women
Sakyadhita International Association of Buddhist Women

nodes.label: Michael Alram
nodes.summary: Michael Alram is a historian, archaeologist, and specialist in Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological studies. After studying at the University of Vienna (~1977–1982), he held posts there (~1986) and at the Kunsthistorisches Museum (~1982–2020).

nodes.label: Deborah Klimburg-Salter
nodes.description: Austrian art historian and professor for non-European art history
nodes.summary: Deborah Klimburg-Salter specializes in history/archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She studied at the University of Vienna (~1965–1968) and Harvard University (~1968–1976) under Oleg Grabar, later serving on the faculty at the University of Vienna (~1989–2015).

nodes.label: Durga Prasad Dikshit
nodes.summary: Durga Prasad Dikshit is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who completed doctoral studies under Baij Nath Puri and also studied under R. K. Dikshit and Vasudev Vishnu Mirashi.

nodes.label: Baij Nath Puri
nodes.summary: Baij Nath Puri was an Indian scholar in indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Oxford (~1948-1950) and served as Professor and Head of Ancient Indian History and Archaeology at the University of Lucknow (~1971-1976).

nodes.label: Satya Swarup Misra
nodes.summary: Satya Swarup Misra works in linguistics and Indology. He served as Professor and Head of the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Lucknow (attested 1958) and as Professor of Indology and Linguistics at Banaras Hindu University.

nodes.label: Reiner Wiehl
nodes.summary: Reiner Wiehl (1929–2010) was a philosopher who taught John Taber. He held posts at the University of Hamburg from circa 1970 to 1977 and Heidelberg University from circa 1977 to 1997.

nodes.label: Klaus-Dieter Mathes
nodes.summary: Klaus-Dieter Mathes is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned degrees from Marburg and Hamburg, studying under Michael Hahn and Klaus Sagaster. Mathes held posts with the NGMCP, University of Hamburg, and University of Vienna (attested 2012–2013).

nodes.label: Markus Viehbeck
nodes.summary: Markus Viehbeck works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Vienna under Helmut Tauscher and Franz-Karl Ehrhard, and has held positions at the University of Vienna and Heidelberg University.

nodes.label: University of Lille
variants: Charles de Gaulle University – Lille III

nodes.label: R. N. Gadre
nodes.summary: R. N. Gadre was an Indologist. In 1959, he was attested as Professor of Sanskrit at both Sir Parashurambhau College and Savitribai Phule Pune University.

nodes.label: R. P. Paranjpye
nodes.summary: R. P. Paranjpye (1876–1966) was a student of Vaman Shivram Apte. He served as Vice-Chancellor of Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 1959).

nodes.label: Volker Caumanns
nodes.summary: Volker Caumanns is a Tibetologist who earned an MA under David P. Jackson at the University of Hamburg and a PhD under Franz-Karl Ehrhard at LMU Munich. He held posts at Munich, Lumbini International Research Institute, and Bern.

nodes.label: Wilhelm Wackernagel
nodes.summary: Wilhelm Wackernagel worked in linguistics, studying at Humboldt University of Berlin from ~1824 to 1827. He held a post at the University of Basel from ~1833 to 1869.

nodes.label: Haruka Yanagisawa
nodes.summary: Haruka Yanagisawa (1944–2015) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1992–2007) and Chiba University (attested 2005).

nodes.label: Hiroshi Yamashita
nodes.summary: Hiroshi Yamashita is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Madras. He served as an associate professor at Tohoku University (attested 1996–1999).

nodes.label: Nobuhiro Ota
nodes.summary: Nobuhiro Ota works in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1988-1998), where he served as a Research Fellow (~1998-2001), and held a post at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~2004).

nodes.label: Akio Tanabe
nodes.summary: Akio Tanabe works in Indology and other fields. He studied at the University of Tokyo from ~1984 to 1993, served as an associate professor at Kyoto University (~1998–2016), and took a post at the University of Tokyo in ~2016.

nodes.label: Nicolas Tournadre
nodes.jawiki: ニコラ・トゥルナドル
nodes.summary: Nicolas Tournadre specializes in linguistics and Tibetology. He studied at Sorbonne Nouvelle University (-1992) and Paris 8 University (-2002). He held posts at Paris 8, LACITO, INALCO (~1992-2004), University of Virginia (~2000-2004), University of Provence (~2004-2011), and Aix-Marseille University (~2012).

nodes.label: Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje
nodes.summary: Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje (1932–1999) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Katok Monastery under Penor Rinpoche, Dzongsar Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Dudjom Rinpoche, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, later teaching numerous prominent students.

nodes.label: Khenpo Appey
nodes.summary: Khenpo Appey (1927–2010) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Dzongsar Monastery (1950) and under Khenpo Dragyab Lodrö. He held posts at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and served as head (1972–1985) and director (attested 1991) of Sakya College.

nodes.label: Chokyi Nyima Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Chokyi Nyima Rinpoche (1951–) works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He studied under teachers including Rangjung Rigpe Dorje and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, founded the Rangjung Yeshe Institute in 1981, and taught numerous scholars.

nodes.label: Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche was a Tibetan Buddhist master who studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Dzongsar Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje. He taught numerous students, including Chokyi Nyima Rinpoche and Tsoknyi Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Mahinda Deegalle
nodes.image: Mahinda Deegalle in the video 'Imagine a Buddhist AI...'.png
nodes.summary: Mahinda Deegalle (born 1961) is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Harvard Divinity School and the University of Chicago, holding posts at Harvard, Bath Spa University (~2001), and Colgate University (~2012–2013).

nodes.label: John Clifford Holt
nodes.summary: John Clifford Holt works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Gustavus Adolphus College, Graduate Theological Union, and the University of Chicago under Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah. He held posts at Bowdoin College (~1978–2017) and the University of Calgary (2006).

nodes.label: P. D. Premasiri
nodes.summary: P. D. Premasiri is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Sri Jayawardenepura Maha Vidyalaya, the University of Ceylon, the University of Canterbury, and the University of Hawaii under Eliot Deutsch, later serving as professor at the University of Ceylon.

nodes.label: Asanga Tilakaratne
nodes.summary: Asanga Tilakaratne is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. At the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, he served as Head of Buddhist thought (attested 1993), Professor (~1996–2009), and Head of Buddhist Philosophy (~2003–2009).

nodes.label: Alvappillai Veluppillai
nodes.summary: Alvappillai Veluppillai (1936–2015) studied at the University of Oxford (~1962–1964) and worked in Indology, religious studies, and linguistics. He held posts at the universities of Kerala, Edinburgh, Virginia, Uppsala (~1990–2005), and Arizona State University (~1990–2000).

nodes.label: Abdur Rehman
nodes.summary: Abdur Rehman, a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology, earned his PhD at the Australian National University under Arthur Llewellyn Basham (attested 1988). He served as an assistant professor of archaeology at the University of Peshawar (attested 1988).

nodes.label: Luise Hercus
nodes.summary: Luise Hercus was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. She studied at St Anne's College (~1944–1948) and the Australian National University, where she later served as a Reader in the Department of South Asian and Buddhist Studies (~1969–1991).

nodes.label: Johanna Engelberta van Lohuizen-de Leeuw
nodes.summary: Johanna Engelberta van Lohuizen-de Leeuw worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. After studying at Utrecht University (~1939–1949), she held posts at Groningen (~1950–1951) and directed the Institute of South Asian Archaeology at Amsterdam (1959–1983).

nodes.label: Sakda Hemthep
nodes.summary: Sakda Hemthep studied Buddhist studies and religious studies at Cardiff University, earning a Master of Philosophy under supervisor Max Deeg in 2014.

nodes.label: Radhika Herzberger
nodes.summary: Radhika Herzberger is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Toronto (circa 1975–1982) under Bimal Krishna Matilal, and served as Director of Studies at Rishi Valley School (~1982–2012).

nodes.label: Jean Dantinne
nodes.summary: Jean Dantinne is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied under Étienne Lamotte. He held a post as a librarian at the University of Liège.

nodes.id: I:Royal Academy of Science, Letters and Fine Arts of Belgium
nodes.label: Royal Academy of Science, Letters and Fine Arts of Belgium
Michael Carrithers
nodes.summary: Michael Carrithers is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He held a post at Wolfson College, Oxford in 1977 and served as Lecturer in Social Anthropology at Durham University (~1984–1992).

nodes.label: Caroline Humphrey
nodes.summary: Caroline Humphrey studied at Girton College, Cambridge (~1962–1966) and under Edmund Leach (~1968–1973). She held posts at Scott Polar Research Institute (~1975–1978), King's College (~1978), University of Cambridge (~1978–2010), and University of Michigan (~2002–2003).

nodes.label: Mary Jaksch
nodes.summary: Mary Jaksch works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She studied at the University of Sunderland under Peter Harvey, attested in 2007.

nodes.label: Pedro Manuel Castro Sánchez
nodes.summary: Pedro Manuel Castro Sánchez is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned an MA at the University of Sunderland, studying under Peter Harvey.

nodes.label: Patricia Berger
nodes.summary: Patricia Berger works in Tibetology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her Ph.D. at UC Berkeley, studied under Mark C. Elliott and Steven D. Goodman, curated at the Asian Art Museum of San Francisco, and joined UC Berkeley's faculty in 1996.

nodes.label: Sanjay Subrahmanyam
nodes.summary: Historian Sanjay Subrahmanyam studied at the University of Delhi and Delhi School of Economics. He has held academic posts at EHESS (~1995–2002), Oxford (~2002–2004), UCLA (~2004), and Collège de France (~2013–2021).

nodes.label: Calambur Sivaramamurti
nodes.summary: Calambur Sivaramamurti worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Presidency University, Kolkata (~1928–1932) under S. Kuppuswami Sastri, and held posts at the Government Museum, Chennai (1935–1946), Indian Museum (1946), and National Museum, New Delhi (attested 1952).

nodes.label: Mortimer Wheeler
nodes.summary: Mortimer Wheeler was an archaeologist and Indologist educated at Bradford Grammar School and University College London. He held posts at Museum Wales, the London Museum, the UCL Institute of Archaeology, and as Director-General of the Archaeological Survey of India.

nodes.label: Hermann Beythan
nodes.summary: Hermann Beythan (1875–1945) worked in Indology and linguistics. He pursued his studies under the traditional teachers Ramasami Aiyar and Radscha Pillai.

nodes.label: Kodo Kawamura
nodes.summary: Kodo Kawamura (1933–2011) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University. He later taught there as a professor (attested 1978; until 2003).

nodes.label: Sibani Dasgupta
nodes.summary: Sibani Dasgupta is an Indologist who studied at the University of Dhaka and under Rajendra Chandra Hazra. She completed a doctorate at the University of Calcutta by 1954 under the supervision of Sushil Kumar De.

nodes.label: John Collinson Nesfield
nodes.summary: John Collinson Nesfield was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Highgate School and Merton College (~1855–1860).

nodes.label: Lodrö Sangpo
nodes.summary: Lodrö Sangpo (born 1953) is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under Ernst Steinkellner. He founded the Nitartha Institute in 1996 and served as a senior teacher at Gampo Abbey (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Thupten Jinpa
nodes.image: HH the Dalai Lama enlightened translator, Dr. Thupten Jinpa.jpg
nodes.summary: Thupten Jinpa is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Ganden Shartse Monastery and the University of Cambridge, later holding posts at Girton College, Cambridge (circa 1996–1999) and the Institute of Tibetan Classics (circa 1999).

nodes.label: Tashi Tsering
nodes.summary: Tashi Tsering is a Tibetologist, historian, and linguist. He founded and directed the Amnye Machen Institute (~1992) and held positions at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives (attested 1985–1995) and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 2014–2019).

nodes.label: Elizabeth Napper
nodes.summary: Elizabeth Napper is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Virginia, studying under Jeffrey Hopkins, Paul Groner, and Geshe Wangyal, and served as co-director at the Tibetan Nuns Project (attested 2001–2006).

nodes.label: Rory Mackenzie
nodes.summary: Rory Mackenzie is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies who completed his doctoral studies under Peter Harvey. He held a teaching post at International Christian College.

nodes.label: Timothy Lenz
nodes.summary: Timothy Lenz works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Washington under Richard Salomon and Collett Cox, and later held posts there, including as a professor (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Norvin Hein

nodes.label: Mark Allon

nodes.label: Harold Walter Bailey
nodes.jawiki: ハロルド・ウォルター・ベイリー
nodes.summary: Harold Walter Bailey (1899–1996) was a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, Indological, and linguistic studies. He studied at the University of Western Australia (~1921–1927) and served as Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Cambridge (1938–1967).

nodes.label: Franz Bernhard
nodes.summary: Franz Bernhard (1931–1971) worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Ernst Waldschmidt (~1951–1957) and completed his habilitation at Goethe University Frankfurt (~1963–1965). In 1966, he was appointed Professor and Director at the University of Hamburg.

nodes.label: Ivo Fišer
nodes.summary: Ivo Fišer was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He was attested as a lecturer at Charles University in 1960 and at the University of Copenhagen's Institute for Indian Philology in 1970.

nodes.label: Herbert V. Guenther
nodes.summary: Herbert V. Guenther (1917–2006) specialized in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. Educated at the University of Saskatchewan and by traditional teachers including Geshe Ngawang Nyima and Damcho Rinchen, he served as a professor at the University of Saskatchewan (~1964–1984).

nodes.label: Ananda W. P. Guruge
nodes.summary: Ananda W. P. Guruge (1928–2014) studied at the University of Ceylon and the University of London. An Indology and Buddhist studies scholar, he taught at NIEPA (attested 1970) and was Dean Emeritus of Academic Affairs at University of the West (~2000–2014).

Carmen Meinert
nodes.summary: Carmen Meinert is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and sinology who earned her PhD from the University of Bonn by 2001. She has held posts as a research fellow at the University of Hamburg (attested 2008) and as a fellow at Ruhr University Bochum.

nodes.label: Christoph Anderl
nodes.summary: Christoph Anderl specializes in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He earned his MA at the University of Vienna (-1995) and completed his PhD at the University of Oslo (~1997–2003) under Christoph Harbsmeier.

nodes.label: N. Venkataramanayya
nodes.summary: N. Venkataramanayya (1891–1976) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology who studied under Ferrand Edward Corley. He served as Reader of Indian History and Archæology at the University of Madras and Deputy Director for Epigraphy in Andhra Pradesh.

nodes.label: Evan Thompson
nodes.summary: Evan Thompson is a philosopher who studied under Robert A. F. Thurman at Amherst and Francisco Varela at Toronto. He held posts at Concordia, York, the University of Toronto (2005), and the University of British Columbia (2013).

nodes.label: Dan Zahavi
nodes.summary: Dan Zahavi is a philosopher who completed a PhD at KU Leuven (~1989–1994) and a Habilitation at the University of Copenhagen (~1995–1999). Around 2002, he became Professor and Director of the Center for Subjectivity Research at Copenhagen.

nodes.label: Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad
nodes.summary: Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad specializes in philosophy, religious studies, and indology. After earning a doctorate at the University of Oxford, he held posts at Clare Hall, Cambridge, Trinity College, Oxford, the National University of Singapore, and Lancaster University, where he was Professor (attested 2007–2012).

nodes.label: Francisco Varela
nodes.jawiki: フランシスコ・バレーラ
nodes.summary: Francisco Varela worked in philosophy and Buddhist studies. Educated at the Pontifical Catholic University of Chile, University of Chile, and Harvard, he co-founded the Mind & Life Institute and held posts at the University of Chile, Naropa University, and CNRS.

nodes.label: Eleanor Rosch
nodes.summary: Eleanor Rosch is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied at Reed College (~1956–1960) and Harvard University (~1964–1969). She joined the University of California, Berkeley around 1971.

nodes.label: Karen O'Brien-Kop
nodes.summary: Karen O'Brien-Kop works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She completed her PhD and served as a senior teaching fellow at SOAS, later becoming a lecturer in Asian Religions and Ethics at the University of Roehampton (attested 2020).

nodes.label: Daniela Bevilacqua

nodes.label: Mikel Burley
nodes.summary: Mikel Burley works in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Essex and the University of Bristol (PhD 2005) under supervisors including John Peacock, and became an Associate Professor of Religion and Philosophy at the University of Leeds.

nodes.label: Philip Deslippe

nodes.label: Ramaprasad Chanda

nodes.label: Brandon Dotson
nodes.summary: Brandon Dotson (born 1978) works in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He completed his DPhil at Oxford under Charles Ramble (~2002–2006) and a habilitation at LMU Munich, later holding posts at SOAS (~2006–2010) and LMU Munich (~2010–2018).

nodes.label: Alex McKay
nodes.summary: Alex McKay works in Tibetology, history/archaeology, and Indology. He earned his PhD from SOAS University of London in 1995 and held a research fellowship at University College London.

nodes.label: Kapila Vatsyayan

nodes.label: Karl Debreczeny

nodes.label: Fabienne Jagou
nodes.summary: Fabienne Jagou is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. She earned her PhD from the École des hautes études en sciences sociales (~1992–1999) and became a Maître de conférences at the École française d'Extrême-Orient around 2001.

nodes.label: Rob Linrothe
nodes.summary: Rob Linrothe specializes in art history, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from the University of Chicago (~1982–1992) and held academic posts at Skidmore College (1992–2009) and Northwestern University (2010–2022).

nodes.label: Paul Nietupski
nodes.summary: Paul Nietupski is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD from Columbia University and held a post at John Carroll University, attested in 2008.

nodes.label: Rita Langer
nodes.summary: Rita Langer is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at SOAS, the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, and the University of Hamburg (PhD 2004 under Lambert Schmithausen), later holding a post at the University of Bristol.

nodes.label: Shrikant S. Bahulkar
nodes.summary: Shrikant S. Bahulkar is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Vasudev Vishwanath Gokhale. He served as Chief Editor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and held a post at Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth (attested 2000).

nodes.label: Catherine Ludvik
nodes.summary: Catherine Ludvik specializes in religious studies, japanology, and indology. She earned her PhD from the University of Toronto (completed 2001) under David Waterhouse, Antonino Forte, Yuko Matsuda, and Werner Knobl. She held posts at the Italian School of East Asian Studies and Hanazono University.

nodes.label: Akio Donohashi
nodes.summary: Akio Donohashi is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1968–1976) and served as a professor at Kobe University (~1989–2012).

nodes.label: Hitoshi Obara
nodes.summary: Hitoshi Obara is a scholar of history, Japanology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Hokkaido University (~1964–1968). He served as a professor at the University of the Sacred Heart (~1996–2015).

nodes.label: Makoto Nagamura
nodes.summary: Makoto Nagamura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history and archaeology who studied at Azabu Junior and Senior High School. He served as a professor at Japan Women's University from around 1989 to 2017.

nodes.label: Makoto Funaoka
nodes.summary: Makoto Funaoka is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He studied at Meiji University from around 1965 to 1974 and served as a professor at Hokkai-Gakuen University from circa 1988 to 2014.

nodes.label: Hokkai-Gakuen University
variants: 北海道学園大学人文学部

nodes.label: Robert E. Morrell
nodes.summary: Robert E. Morrell works in Japanology and Buddhist studies. He studied under doctoral supervisor Robert H. Brower and teacher William H. McCullough, and held a post at Washington University in St. Louis (attested 1985 and 2006).

nodes.label: Washington University in St. Louis
variants: Washington University in St. Louis Missouri

nodes.label: James W. Heisig
nodes.jawiki: ジェームズ・ハイジック
nodes.summary: James W. Heisig works in philosophy, religious studies, and Japanology. After studying at the University of Cambridge (~1974–1978), he held posts at Nanzan University (~1978), the Nanzan Institute for Religion and Culture (1978; director 1991–2001), and Pompeu Fabra University.

nodes.label: Barbra R. Clayton
nodes.summary: Barbra R. Clayton works in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at McGill University (attested 2001) under Richard P. Hayes and Katherine K. Young, also studying with G. Raj, and held a post at Mount Allison University (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Katherine K. Young
nodes.summary: Katherine K. Young is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Chicago (~1968–1970) and McGill University (~1970–1977). She served as Professor at McGill University from around 1978 to 2017 and taught Barbra R. Clayton.

nodes.label: Damien Keown
nodes.summary: Damien Keown is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy who earned degrees at Lancaster University and the University of Oxford. He held a post at Goldsmiths, University of London (~1990–2013), and founded the Journal of Buddhist Ethics.

nodes.label: Sarah J. Horton
nodes.summary: Sarah J. Horton works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She studied under Stanley Weinstein at Yale University and served as an assistant professor at Macalester College (attested 2006).

nodes.label: Gopinath Kaviraj
nodes.summary: Gopinath Kaviraj (1887–1976) was an Indian scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Allahabad (~1910–1914) and served as Professor of Tantra-Śāstra at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1964–1969).

nodes.label: Melvyn C. Goldstein
nodes.summary: Melvyn C. Goldstein is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Michigan and the University of Washington (PhD 1960–1968), and became a professor at Case Western Reserve University around 1968.

nodes.label: Asatoshi Kamiya
nodes.summary: Asatoshi Kamiya is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned an M.A. from Komazawa University and worked as a teacher at Mejiro Kenshin Junior and Senior High School (attested 1978).

nodes.id: I:Mejiro Kenshin Junior and Senior High School
nodes.label: Mejiro Kenshin Junior and Senior High School
The New School
variants: The New School for Social Research, New York

nodes.label: Osmund Bopearachchi
nodes.summary: Osmund Bopearachchi (born 1949) specializes in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied under Paul Bernard (~1983–1987) and took up a post at the Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique around 1989.

nodes.label: Deborah Carlson
nodes.summary: Deborah Carlson is a scholar in the field of history and archaeology. She held posts at Texas A&M University and the Institute of Nautical Archaeology (both attested 2015).

nodes.label: Paul Bernard
nodes.summary: Paul Bernard specialized in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Paris 1 Pantheon-Sorbonne (through 1983) and held a post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1980–1997).

nodes.label: Axel Michaels
nodes.summary: Axel Michaels is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied under Laxmi Nath Srestha. He held academic posts at the University of Bern (~1989–1996) and Heidelberg University (~1996–2018).

nodes.label: Hans Hartog
nodes.summary: Hans Hartog studied Indology and linguistics across Tübingen, Bethel, and Munich before earning his PhD at the University of Marburg (1937–1939) under Friedrich Heiler. His teachers included Walther Wüst, Hanns Oertel, and Ferdinand Sommer.

nodes.label: Walther Wüst
nodes.description: Rector of the University of Munich and SS member (1901-1993)
nodes.summary: Walther Wüst was a scholar in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1920–1923), where he later served as rector from 1941 to 1946.

nodes.label: Jakob Wilhelm Hauer
nodes.image: Bundesarchiv Bild 183-2004-0413-501, Prof. Jakob Wilhelm Hauer.jpg
nodes.summary: Jakob Wilhelm Hauer (1881–1962) worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the Basel Mission, Oxford, and Tübingen under Richard von Garbe, later holding posts at the University of Marburg (~1925–1927) and University of Tübingen (1927–1945).

nodes.label: Kurt Huber
nodes.description: German folk song researcher, professor at the Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität (LMU) in Munich, member of the White Rose (1893-1943)
nodes.summary: Kurt Huber (1893–1943) was a philosopher who studied at Eberhard-Ludwigs-Gymnasium and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1913–1917). He later held an academic post at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich from around 1920 until 1943.

nodes.label: Erich Rudolf Jaensch
nodes.summary: Erich Rudolf Jaensch (1883–1940) was a scholar in philosophy and other fields. He held academic posts at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1910–1913) and the University of Marburg (~1913–1940).

nodes.label: Fritz-Joachim von Rintelen
nodes.summary: Fritz-Joachim von Rintelen was a philosopher. He studied at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (1919–1923), later holding posts there (~1934–1941) and at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (~1947–1969).

nodes.label: Wolfgang Schultz
nodes.description: German philosopher, historian and art historian (1881-1936)

nodes.label: Ferdinand Sommer
nodes.summary: Ferdinand Sommer was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Freiburg (~1894–1896). He held posts at Leipzig, Basel, Rostock, Jena, Bonn, and the Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1926–1942).

nodes.label: Giovanni Vacca
nodes.summary: Giovanni Vacca (1872–1953) was an Italian sinologist and historian. He studied at the University of Genoa and held academic posts at the University of Florence (~1911–1921) and Sapienza University of Rome (~1923–1947), teaching scholars including Giuseppe Tucci.

nodes.id: I:Kaivalyadhama Health and Yoga Research Center
nodes.label: Kaivalyadhama Health and Yoga Research Center
S. Krishnaswami Aiyangar
nodes.summary: S. Krishnaswami Aiyangar was an Indology and history and archaeology scholar who studied at the University of Madras (~1890–1897). He later held the Chair of Indian History and Archæology at the University of Madras (~1914–1929).

nodes.label: John Kieschnick
nodes.summary: John Kieschnick is a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies. He held an academic post at the University of Bristol (~2005–2011) before joining Stanford University as Professor of Buddhist Studies in circa 2011.

nodes.label: F. B. J. Kuiper
nodes.summary: F. B. J. Kuiper worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Leiden University (~1925–1934), where he succeeded Jean Philippe Vogel in 1939 and held a post until 1972.

nodes.label: Oscar Botto
nodes.summary: Oscar Botto (1922–2008) was an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Turin from around 1941 to 1945. He also founded the journal Indologica Taurinensia.

nodes.label: Daniel Dubuisson
nodes.summary: Daniel Dubuisson (born 1950) is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He served as a director of research at the Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique and the University of Lille, and held a post at University Lille-III (~1981–2015).

nodes.label: Jonathan Z. Smith
nodes.summary: Jonathan Z. Smith (1938–2017) was a religious studies scholar who studied at Haverford College, Yale Divinity School, and Yale University. He held posts at UC Santa Barbara (c. 1966–1968) and the University of Chicago (c. 1968–2017).

nodes.label: Ajit Ranjan Bhattacharyya
nodes.summary: Ajit Ranjan Bhattacharyya, an Indologist and scholar of Buddhist studies, studied under Vidhusekhara Bhattacharya. He held a post at the University of Calcutta as an Ex-Puranchand Nahar Fellow.

nodes.label: Gregory Max Seton
nodes.summary: Gregory Max Seton works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Naropa University, UC Santa Barbara, and the University of Oxford (D.Phil 2015), where he was supervised by Vesna A. Wallace and Alexis Sanderson.

nodes.label: Martin Joachim Kümmel
nodes.summary: Martin Joachim Kümmel works in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Freiburg (~1990–1998) under Eva Tichy, Helmut Rix, and others. He held a post at the University of Jena around 2013.

nodes.label: Helmut Rix
nodes.summary: Helmut Rix specialized in linguistics and Indology, studying at the University of Würzburg (~1946–1950). He held posts at the University of Regensburg (~1968–1978) and the University of Freiburg (~1978–1993).

nodes.label: Chih-mien Adrian Tseng
nodes.summary: Chih-mien Adrian Tseng specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He earned a PhD from McMaster University under James A. Benn, Nobuyoshi Yamabe, and Canshan Cheng, and became Assistant Professor at Fo Guang University (attested 2016).

nodes.label: Fo Guang University
variants: 佛光人文社會學院宗教學系

nodes.label: Peter Moran
nodes.summary: Peter Moran specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at Tufts University and completed his PhD at the University of Washington under Charles F. Keyes, also studying under traditional teachers Chokyi Nyima Rinpoche, Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, and Khenpo Choga Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Thomas Watters
nodes.description: British diplomat in China and Korea, sinologist
nodes.summary: Thomas Watters (1840–1901) was a scholar in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Queen's University Belfast in 1857 and completed a B.A. at Queen's University of Ireland circa 1857–1861.

nodes.label: Willem van der Molen
nodes.summary: Willem van der Molen (born 1952) specializes in linguistics, history/archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Leiden University (~1970–1983) and held posts at Leiden (~1978–2017) and the University of Indonesia.

nodes.label: Muhammad Ashraf Khan
nodes.summary: Muhammad Ashraf Khan is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He has served as Director at the Department of Archaeology and Museums (Government of Andhra Pradesh), Deputy Director at Taxila Museum, and Director at Quaid-i-Azam University (attested 2019).

nodes.label: Zarawar Khan
nodes.summary: Zarawar Khan specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA and PhD in archaeology at the University of Peshawar and served as Assistant Professor of Archaeology at the University of Swat (attested 2019–2022).

nodes.label: Jessie Pons
nodes.summary: Jessie Pons is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and religious studies. She completed a doctoral thesis at Paris-Sorbonne University (-2011) and was Junior Professor in South Asian History of Religion at Ruhr University Bochum (attested 2019).

nodes.label: Max Walleser
nodes.summary: Max Walleser (1874–1954) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He held a post at Heidelberg University (~1902–1938) and founded both the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities and the Institut für Buddhismus-Kunde.

nodes.label: Michael Comans
nodes.summary: Michael Comans works in Indology and philosophy. He studied under Swami Dayananda Saraswati, R. Krishnamurthi Sastri, and completed his doctorate under Jan Willem de Jong at Australian National University (~1984–1987), later holding posts at Sydney and Sri Venkateswara Temple.

nodes.label: Swami Dayananda Saraswati
nodes.description: Hindu monk and founder of Arsha Vidya Gurukulam (1930-2015)

nodes.label: Rahul Peter Das
nodes.description: German professor of South Asian studies (born 1954)
nodes.summary: Rahul Peter Das is a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied at Calcutta, Cologne, and Hamburg. He held research and teaching posts at Hamburg, Bonn, Groningen, and Marburg, and took a chair at Halle-Wittenberg in 1994.

nodes.label: Nagin J. Shah
nodes.summary: Nagin J. Shah (born 1931) is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He served as Acting Director at the L.D. Institute of Indology (attested 1968), where he succeeded Dalsukh D. Malvania, and he taught Maria Heim.

nodes.label: Ernest Mackay
nodes.summary: Ernest Mackay was a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology. He was educated at Bristol Grammar School and the University of Bristol, and served at the Department of Antiquities in Mandatory Palestine (~1919–1922).

nodes.label: Rakhaldas Bandyopadhyay
nodes.summary: Rakhaldas Bandyopadhyay (1885–1930) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta, and later held posts at Calcutta (~1908–1911), Presidency University, and Banaras Hindu University (~1928–1930).

nodes.label: Alexander Rogers
nodes.summary: Alexander Rogers (1825–1910) was active in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at East India Company College (c. 1843–1845) and served in the Indian Civil Service from around 1845 to 1879.

nodes.label: Henry Beveridge
nodes.description: British linguist and Indian Civil Service officer

nodes.label: Klaus Ludwig Janert
nodes.description: born:1922|died:1994|; Janert, Klaus Ludwig, 1922-1994; Janert, Klaus L.

nodes.label: Christophe Vielle
nodes.summary: Christophe Vielle is an Indologist who taught Sandra Smets. He served as professeur de sanskrit at KU Leuven (attested 2009) and as a professor at Université catholique de Louvain (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Robert Deliège
nodes.summary: Robert Deliège is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at the University of Oxford from ~1982 to 1985. He held posts at the University of Kerala and the Université catholique de Louvain, where he was professor around 1989.

nodes.label: Jacques Scheuer
nodes.summary: Jacques Scheuer (born 1942) works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at Université catholique de Louvain and Sorbonne Nouvelle University under Madeleine Biardeau, later holding posts at Facultés Loyola Paris and Université catholique de Louvain (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Utz Podzeit
nodes.image: Venia Legendi 1997- Dr. Utz Podzeit mit Mechthild.jpg

nodes.label: Roderick Chisholm
nodes.summary: Roderick Chisholm (1916–1999) was a philosopher who studied at Harvard University (~1938–1942). He held long-term posts at Brown University (~1947–1987) and the University of Massachusetts Amherst (~1987–1996).

nodes.label: Philip L. Quinn
nodes.summary: Philip L. Quinn was a philosopher and religious studies scholar who studied at Georgetown, Delaware, and Pittsburgh. He held academic posts at Brown University (~1969-1985) and the University of Notre Dame (~1985-2004).

nodes.label: Ernest Sosa
nodes.summary: Ernest Sosa is a philosopher who studied at the University of Miami and the University of Pittsburgh (~1961–1964). He served as a professor at Brown University (~1964–2007) and took up a post at Rutgers University around 2007.

nodes.label: August Wilhelm Heyde
nodes.description: German missionary to Tibetans in Northern India; b. Wilhelm Heide, Feb. 16, 1825; later changed surname to Heyde; d. Aug. 27, 1907

nodes.label: Karunesh Shukla
nodes.summary: Karunesh Shukla is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. In 1991, he is attested as Professor and Head of the Department of Sanskrit and Prakrit Languages at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University.

nodes.label: Eduard Müller
nodes.summary: Eduard Müller was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He completed his Inauguraldissertation at Leipzig University (~1872–1874) and served as a professor at the University of Bern from ~1886 to 1908.

nodes.label: David Ludden
nodes.summary: David Ludden is a historian and Indologist. He held academic posts at the University of Virginia (~1979–1981), the University of Pennsylvania (~1981–2007), and New York University (~2007).

nodes.label: Yigal Bronner
nodes.summary: Yigal Bronner is an Indologist who studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1988–1994) and the University of Chicago under Sheldon Pollock (~1994–1999). He joined the faculty at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem around 2008.

nodes.label: James B. Apple
nodes.summary: James B. Apple specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He completed his graduate and doctoral studies at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, where his teachers included Geshe Lhundub Sopa and doctoral supervisor John D. Dunne.

nodes.label: Glenn H. Mullin
nodes.image: Visit of Telo Tulku to Roerich House, U.B. (3861963599).jpg

His Holiness the Fourteenth Dalai Lama
nodes.description: 14th Dalai Lama, the spiritual and temporal leader of Tibetans
nodes.summary: Tenzin Gyatso, the 14th Dalai Lama, works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at Sera and Drepung Monasteries, the Universities of Melbourne and British Columbia, and under teachers including Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, Dilgo Khyentse, Trijang, and Trulshik.

nodes.label: Luciano Petech
nodes.summary: Luciano Petech was a scholar in Tibetology and history/archaeology who studied under Giuseppe Tucci. He held posts at the University of Allahabad (1938–1946), Sapienza University of Rome (from 1955), and served as president of the International Association for Tibetan Studies (~1989–1995).

nodes.label: Edward Espe Brown
nodes.summary: Edward Espe Brown is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Shunryu Suzuki (~1966–1971), Reb Anderson, and Jack Kornfield.

nodes.label: Elena De Rossi Filibeck
nodes.summary: Elena De Rossi Filibeck is a scholar in Tibetology. She has held posts at the University of Bonn and Sapienza University of Rome (attested 1997).

nodes.label: Stefan Maul
nodes.summary: Stefan Maul is a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics. He held academic posts at the Free University of Berlin from 1987 to 1995 and at Heidelberg University beginning in 1995.

nodes.label: Søren Sørensen
nodes.summary: Søren Sørensen was an Indology scholar who held posts at Herlufsholm School from 1876 to 1878 and at the University of Copenhagen from circa 1887 to 1902.

nodes.label: Vilhelm Thomsen
nodes.jawiki: ヴィルヘルム・トムセン
nodes.summary: Vilhelm Thomsen was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studying at Randers State School and the University of Copenhagen (~1859–1869), he served as a professor at the University of Copenhagen (~1887–1913).

nodes.label: Karl Verner
nodes.summary: Karl Verner was a linguist who studied at Aarhus Katedralskole. He held a post at the University of Copenhagen from around 1883 to 1896.

nodes.label: Rosina Pastore
nodes.summary: Rosina Pastore specializes in Indology and religious studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Lausanne under supervisors Maya Burger and Stefania Cavaliere, also serving there as an assistant and PhD candidate.

nodes.label: Marianne Winder
nodes.summary: Marianne Winder specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of London and SOAS, and served as Keeper of the Oriental Manuscripts at the Wellcome Trust (~1964–1983) after a post at the University of Nottingham.

nodes.label: Wellcome Trust
variants: Wellcome Institute for the History of Medicine

nodes.label: Nigel Allan
nodes.summary: Nigel Allan specializes in history and archaeology. Attested in 1993, he succeeded Marianne Winder and held the post of Curator of Oriental Books and Manuscripts at the Wellcome Trust.

nodes.label: Charles Edmund Godakumbura
nodes.summary: Charles Edmund Godakumbura was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at Kingswood College and served as Senior Lecturer at the University of London circa 1953–1960.

nodes.label: Union Theological Seminary
variants: Union Theological Seminary in New York City

nodes.label: Hartford International University for Religion and Peace
Anne MacDonald
nodes.summary: Anne MacDonald works in Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at the University of British Columbia under Shotaro Iida, Ashok Aklujkar, Geshe Tashi Namgyal, Lambert Schmithausen, and Karin Preisendanz, and held posts at the University of Vienna and Austrian Academy of Sciences.

nodes.label: Vaibhav Singh
nodes.summary: Vaibhav Singh is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Reading in 2017 and held a post there attested in 2018.

nodes.label: Himanshu Prabha Ray
nodes.summary: Himanshu Prabha Ray works in history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied at Panjab University (~1966–1968), Cambridge (~1974–1975), and Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1980–1984), where she was Associate Professor (~1986–2006). She also held posts at LMU Munich, OCHS (2005), and the Humboldt Foundation (2014–2019).

nodes.label: Kuvempu University
variants: Centre for the Study of Local Cultures, Kuvempu University

nodes.label: Geoff Childs
nodes.summary: Geoff Childs is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. He completed his PhD at Indiana University, studying under Tsetan Chonjore, and held posts at the Australian National University and Washington University in St. Louis.

nodes.label: Tibetan Tripitaka Research Center
variants: 財団法人西蔵大蔵経研究会

nodes.label: Anthony François Paulus Hulsewé
nodes.summary: Anthony François Paulus Hulsewé (1910–1993) was a scholar of Sinology and history and archaeology. He studied at Leiden University under Jan Julius Lodewijk Duyvendak (circa 1928–1952) and held appointments at Leiden University from 1947 through 1975.

nodes.label: David N. Keightley
nodes.summary: David N. Keightley was a sinologist and historian who served as a professor at the University of California, Berkeley (attested 1985 and 1999).

nodes.label: Robert H. Brower
nodes.description: Professor of far east language and literature (1923–1988)
nodes.summary: Robert H. Brower was a scholar of Japanology who studied at Harvard University (~1940–1944) and the University of Michigan (~1947–1952). He served as Chairman of the Department of Far Eastern Languages and Literatures at the University of Michigan (~1966–1986).

nodes.label: Arthur F. Wright
nodes.summary: Arthur F. Wright was a scholar of Sinology, history, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Stanford (~1931–1935), Oxford (~1935–1937), and Harvard (~1935–1947), and served as Charles Seymour Professor of History at Yale University (~1959–1976).

nodes.label: University of Missouri
variants: University of the State of Missouri

nodes.label: Steven Lukes
nodes.jawiki: スティーヴン・ルークス
nodes.summary: Steven Lukes works in philosophy and other fields. After studying at Balliol College and Nuffield College, he held posts at Balliol College (~1966–1987), the European University Institute (~1987–1995), the University of Siena, LSE, and NYU (~2001).

nodes.id: I:Department of Archaeology and Museums, Government of Andhra Pradesh
nodes.label: Department of Archaeology and Museums, Government of Andhra Pradesh
variants: Andhra Pradesh Department of Archaeology and Museums

nodes.label: Unnikrishnan Payyappallimana
nodes.summary: Unnikrishnan Payyappallimana studied at Ayurveda College, Coimbatore (until 1992) and the University of Amsterdam (until 2000). Working in Indology, he held posts at FRLHT (1995), Amala Institute of Medical Sciences, and the University of Toyama (1998, 2003–2004).

variants: Amala Cancer Hospital and Research Center

nodes.label: Foundation for the Revitalization of Local Health Traditions
variants: Foundation for the Revitalization of Local Health Traditions

nodes.label: Robert E. Svoboda
nodes.summary: Robert E. Svoboda works in Indology and other fields. He studied at the University of Oklahoma (~1970–1972) and under Vimalananda (~1975–1983), and held adjunct posts at the Ayurvedic Institute, Bastyr University, and the Institute for Religion and Health in 2008.

nodes.label: Soonil Hwang
nodes.summary: Soonil Hwang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned an MA at Dongguk University and a DPhil at Mansfield College, Oxford, under Richard Gombrich, later holding a post at Dongguk University.

nodes.label: Kirby Flower Smith
nodes.description: American classical philologist and religious studies scholar

nodes.label: Bhikkhu Anālayo
nodes.description: German Buddhist monk, scholar, and meditation teacher (born 1962)
nodes.summary: Bhikkhu Anālayo is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at the University of Ceylon, University of Marburg, and under Bhikkhu Bodhi, and held posts at Dharma Drum Buddhist College, University of Hamburg, and Sri Lanka International Buddhist Academy.

nodes.label: Wataru S. Ryose
nodes.summary: Wataru S. Ryose is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison by 1987 under Minoru Kiyota, having also studied under Genjun Sasaki and Frances A. Wilson.

nodes.label: Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thayé
variants: Kong sprul Blo gros mtha’ yas
nodes.jawiki: ジャムグン・コントゥル・ロドゥ・タイェ
nodes.summary: Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thayé was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied under Thekchok Dorje (~1833–1868) and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo (~1840–1892), and he taught Karma Tashi Chophel and Khakyab Dorje.

nodes.label: Sukumar Sen
nodes.image: Sukumar Sen linguist 2020 cover of India cr.jpg
nodes.summary: Sukumar Sen was an Indian scholar in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Calcutta (~1919–1923), where he later held a post (~1930–1964), and served as Secretary of the Linguistic Society of India (~1954–1964).

nodes.label: David Kopf
nodes.summary: David Kopf was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Chicago (~1960–1964) and held a post at the University of Minnesota from around 1967 to 1997.

nodes.label: Willard Van Orman Quine
nodes.image: Willard Van Orman Quine on Bluenose II in Halifax NS harbor 1980.jpg
nodes.jawiki: ウィラード・ヴァン・オーマン・クワイン
nodes.summary: Willard Van Orman Quine (1908–2000) was a philosopher and linguist. He studied at Oberlin College and Harvard, served in the U.S. Navy (1942–1945), and held posts at Harvard (1933–1978) and Wesleyan University (1964–1965).

nodes.label: P. S. Subrahmanya Sastri
nodes.summary: P. S. Subrahmanya Sastri worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under traditional teachers Nilakantha and Vaidyanatha, graduated from the University of Madras (~1910–1914), and served as Professor of Sanskrit at Annamalai University from circa 1932 to 1947.

nodes.label: National Museum of Denmark
variants: National Museum of Denmark's Greenland Research Centre
National Museum of Denmark's Department of Research

nodes.label: Alexander W. Macdonald
nodes.summary: Alexander W. Macdonald (1923–2018) worked in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He held a post at the Musée de l'Homme (attested 1972) and served as Professor at Paris Nanterre University from around 1974 to 1993.

nodes.label: Rasmus Rask
nodes.summary: Rasmus Rask (1787–1832) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Copenhagen (~1807–1812). He later served there as Professor of Literary History and Librarian (~1825–1832).

nodes.label: Stella Kramrisch
nodes.summary: Stella Kramrisch was an Indologist and art historian/archaeologist. After studying at the University of Vienna (~1914–1919), she held academic posts at the University of Calcutta (~1923–1950) and the University of Pennsylvania (~1950–1972).

nodes.label: Sarasi Kumar Saraswati
nodes.summary: Sarasi Kumar Saraswati (1914–1980) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied under Jitendra Nath Banerjea. During his career, he served as librarian at the Asiatic Society and held a post at the University of Calcutta.

nodes.label: H. G. Narahari
nodes.summary: H. G. Narahari is an Indologist who studied at the University of Mysore and the University of Madras, where he completed an MA under C. Kunhan Raja. He held posts at Madras and the Adyar Library and Research Centre (attested 1944).

nodes.label: Charles Philip Brown
nodes.summary: Charles Philip Brown studied at Haileybury and Imperial Service College (circa 1814–1817). A scholar of Indology and linguistics, he served in the Indian Civil Service (circa 1817–1854) and as Professor of Telugu at the University of London (circa 1855–1869).

nodes.label: Daniel Clarke Waugh
