nodes.summary: Daniel Clarke Waugh is a historian specializing in Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Yale University (1963) and Harvard University (1965, 1972) before holding a faculty post at the University of Washington from circa 1972 to 2017.

nodes.label: Katia Buffetrille
nodes.summary: Katia Buffetrille is a Tibetology and religious studies scholar. She completed her studies, including a PhD, at Paris Nanterre University under Alexander W. Macdonald between roughly 1985 and 1996, and took up a post at École Pratique des Hautes Études around 1997.

nodes.label: Shunryu Suzuki
nodes.image: Shunryu Suzuki at Zen Mountain Center (cropped).png
nodes.summary: Shunryu Suzuki (1904–1971) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Gyokujun So-on, Ian Kishizawa, and at Komazawa University (~1926–1930). He founded the San Francisco Zen Center and Tassajara Zen Mountain Center.

nodes.label: Richard Baker
nodes.summary: Richard Baker (born 1936) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Harvard University (~1954–1958) and under Shunryu Suzuki in 1971, whom he succeeded. He taught Philip Whalen and Taigen Dan Leighton.

nodes.label: Huston Smith
nodes.summary: Huston Smith was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Central Methodist University and the University of Chicago, held a professorship at MIT (~1958–1973), and was Thomas J. Watson Professor Emeritus at Syracuse University.

nodes.label: Medawachchiye Dhammajothi
nodes.summary: Medawachchiye Dhammajothi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Sri Jayewardenepura, PGIPBS, and Nanjing University, later holding posts at the University of Colombo (~2004), Buddhist and Pali University (2008), and PGIPBS (2008).

nodes.id: I:Buddhist and Pali University of Sri Lanka
nodes.label: Buddhist and Pali University of Sri Lanka
variants: Buddhist and Pāli University in Sri Lanka
Buddhist and Pali University of Sri Lanka

nodes.label: Srisa Chandra Vasu
nodes.description: Indian judge, writer, and scholar in Sanskrit

nodes.label: Johanna Narten
nodes.description: Professor of Indo-European and Indo-Iranian Linguistics (1930-2019)
nodes.summary: Johanna Narten specialized in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. She studied at Saarland University (~1951–1956) and held a post at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg from circa 1971 to 1993.

nodes.label: Jadunath Sarkar
nodes.summary: Jadunath Sarkar (1870–1958) was a historian and archaeologist. He studied at the University of Calcutta and Presidency University, Kolkata (~1887–1892), and later held a post at the University of Calcutta (~1926–1928).

nodes.label: Ananda Coomaraswamy
nodes.summary: Ananda Coomaraswamy (1877–1947) worked in Indology, history, archaeology, and philosophy. Educated at University College London (~1897–1904), he later held posts at the Smithsonian Institution and the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston (~1917–1947).

nodes.label: Peter Masefield
nodes.summary: Peter Masefield specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under supervisors L. P. N. Perera and Ninian Smart (attested 1986).

nodes.label: Karel Werner
nodes.summary: Karel Werner (1925–2019) worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. In 1968, he taught Sanskrit and Indian philosophy and religion at Cambridge and Durham, later serving as Honorary Professorial Research Associate at SOAS (circa 1993–2019).

nodes.label: Ninian Smart
nodes.summary: Ninian Smart specialized in religious studies and philosophy. Educated at The Glasgow Academy, The Queen's College, Oxford (~1948-1954), and Yale (~1950-1952), he held posts at Nottingham, Birmingham, Lancaster (1967), and the University of California, Santa Barbara (attested 1993-2001).

nodes.label: Herbert Franke
nodes.summary: Herbert Franke (1914–2011) studied sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history. He studied at Cologne, Bonn, and Humboldt University under Erich Haenisch. He served as President of the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities (~1980–1985) and professor at Munich.

nodes.label: S. N. Balagangadhara
nodes.summary: S. N. Balagangadhara studied at Ghent University (~1978–1987) in the fields of philosophy and religious studies. He served as Professor in Comparative Science of Cultures and director of its research centre at Ghent University (~1991–2018).

nodes.label: Kazu Uehara
nodes.summary: Kazu Uehara (1924–2017) specialized in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyushu University (~1948–1953) and was professor emeritus at Seijo University (~1995–2017).

nodes.label: Masahiro Asada
nodes.summary: Masahiro Asada is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (~1964-1974). He later served as an assistant professor at Ryukoku University (~1984-1991).

nodes.id: I:The Society for the History of Buddhism
nodes.label: The Society for the History of Buddhism
Jacqueline I. Stone
nodes.summary: Jacqueline I. Stone works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, having studied at SFSU and UCLA. She was president of the Society for the Study of Japanese Religions (~1996–1999) and a professor at Princeton University (~1990–2019).

nodes.label: Kuroda Institute
variants: Kuroda Institute for the Study of Buddhism and Human Values

nodes.label: Qingzhi Zhu
nodes.summary: Qingzhi Zhu specializes in linguistics, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He held posts as a professor at Peking University (attested 2004) and The Education University of Hong Kong (attested 2010).

nodes.id: I:The Education University of Hong Kong
nodes.label: The Education University of Hong Kong
Jinchuan Wan
nodes.summary: Jinchuan Wan works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. In 2010, Wan was attested as holding professorships at both National Central University and Fo Guang University.

nodes.label: Christoph Harbsmeier
nodes.description: German professor of Chinese linguistics and syntax
nodes.summary: Christoph Harbsmeier is a Sinologist and linguist who earned his PhD from the University of Copenhagen. He was a professor at the University of Oslo (~1985–2016) and served as advisory professor at Peking, Fudan, and Shanghai Normal Universities (attested 2001).

nodes.label: Shu-fen Chen
nodes.summary: Shu-fen Chen is a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at National Tsing Hua University under Chin-Fa Lien and completed doctoral work under Hans Henrich Hock. She served as a professor at National Tsing Hua University (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Ryan Richard Overbey
nodes.summary: Ryan Richard Overbey works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. He earned degrees from Brown University (AB, 2001) and Harvard University (PhD, 2010). His appointments include UC Berkeley (2013–2015), Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities, Holy Cross, and Wesleyan University (attested 2016).

nodes.label: Todd Thornton Lewis
nodes.summary: Todd Thornton Lewis works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Columbia University under numerous mentors and held posts at the College of the Holy Cross, where he was attested as professor from 1996 to 2017.

nodes.label: Lothar Ledderose
nodes.summary: Lothar Ledderose is a scholar of sinology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at Princeton University (~1969–1970) and Harvard University (~1970–1972), later holding posts at Heidelberg University as Professor (~1976–2009) and the University of Cambridge (~1992–1993).

nodes.label: Graduate Theological Union
variants: Graduate Theological Union in Berkeley, California

nodes.label: Wai-lun Tam
nodes.summary: Wai-lun Tam works in religious studies, sinology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD at McMaster University under Koichi Shinohara and served as professor and Department Chairperson at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (attested 2016).

nodes.label: David Faure
nodes.summary: David Faure is a historian and sinologist. He completed his studies at the University of Hong Kong (~1966–1969) and Princeton University (~1970–1976).

nodes.label: Michel Strickmann
nodes.summary: Michel Strickmann (1942–1994) worked in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied under teachers including Hulsewé, Zürcher, Vos, Kaltenmark, Stein, Schipper, and Vandermeersch, completing his PhD at Paris Diderot University. He held positions at UC Berkeley, Bordeaux, and Wissenschaftskolleg zu Berlin.

nodes.id: I:Government Vidarbha Institute of Science and Humanities
nodes.label: Government Vidarbha Institute of Science and Humanities
Qinni Liu
nodes.summary: Qinni Liu works in Buddhist studies. She earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University (attested 2009), studying under supervisor Kirill Jurievitch Solonin and committee members D.-D. Huang and Cheng-I Weng.

nodes.label: Jules Bloch
nodes.summary: Jules Bloch (1880–1953) was an Indologist and linguist educated at EPHE, ENLOV, and the University of Paris. He held positions at EPHE, ENLOV, the University of Lyon, and served as Chair of Sanskrit at the Collège de France (1936–1951).

nodes.label: Olivier Lacombe
nodes.summary: Olivier Lacombe (1904–2001) worked in philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure (~1925–1928) and the Faculty of Arts of Paris (~1934–1939), later holding posts at Paris (~1947–1970) and Paris-Sorbonne University (~1970–1974).

nodes.label: Institut Français Frankfurt
variants: French Insitute at Frankfurt am Main

nodes.label: Tu Weiming
nodes.summary: Tu Weiming is a philosopher and Sinologist who earned his Ph.D. at Harvard. He taught at Princeton, UC Berkeley, Harvard—serving as Harvard-Yenching Institute Director (~1996–2008)—and Peking University (~2010).

nodes.label: Urs App
nodes.description: Swiss historian of Ideas, Religion, and Philosophy
nodes.summary: Urs App (born 1949) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology who studied at the University of Fribourg and Temple University. Mentored by Yoshitaka Iriya, Richard DeMartino, and Seizan Yanagida, he worked at Hanazono University and EFEO.

nodes.label: Richard DeMartino
nodes.description: American psychoanalyst and religious studies scholar (1922-2013)

nodes.label: András Róna-Tas
nodes.image: András Róna-Tas is rector at the Univrsity of Szeged, 14.02.1991..JPG
nodes.summary: András Róna-Tas specializes in linguistics, Tibetology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University (1950–1955), was a guest lecturer at the University of Vienna (1983–1984), and served as president of the International Association for Tibetan Studies (~1985–1989).

nodes.label: Sara Marie Conrad
nodes.summary: Sara Marie Conrad specializes in Tibetology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She completed an MA at Indiana University, where Elliot Sperling served on her committee.

nodes.label: Anam Thubten Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Anam Thubten Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied under traditional teacher Tsurlo Rinpoche and has served as a teacher at the Vajrayana Foundation.

nodes.label: Vajrayana Foundation
variants: Vajrayana Foundation College of Buddhist Studies

nodes.label: City University of Hong Kong
variants: Chinese Civilisation Centre, City University of Hong Kong
City University of Hong Kong Center for East Asian and Comparative Philosophy

nodes.label: Barend ter Haar
nodes.summary: Barend ter Haar is a scholar of sinology, history, archaeology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Leiden University (-1990) and held posts at the Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences (attested 1994), Heidelberg University, and Leiden (attested 2002-2013).

nodes.label: Carl Olson
nodes.summary: Carl Olson works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. Mentored by John Y. Fenton, he served as Teacher-Scholar Chair in the Humanities at Allegheny College (attested 2005–2015).

nodes.label: Tai-shing Wut
nodes.summary: Tai-shing Wut is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under the doctoral supervision of Ming-Wood Liu.

nodes.label: Sangharakshita
nodes.description: Founder of the Friends of the Western Buddhist Order (1925–2018)
nodes.summary: Sangharakshita was a religious studies and Buddhist studies figure who studied under traditional teacher C. M. Chen (~1957–1964) and founded the Triratna Buddhist Community in 1968.

nodes.label: Triratna Buddhist Community
variants: Friends of the Western Buddhist Order

nodes.label: Wilt L. Idema
nodes.summary: Wilt L. Idema is a sinologist who studied under Anthony François Paulus Hulsewé at Leiden University (~1963–1974). He held a professorship at Leiden (1975–1999) and posts at Harvard University (~1999–2013) and the Radcliffe Institute (2001–2002).

nodes.label: David Schaberg
nodes.summary: David Schaberg is a scholar in sinology. He studied at Stanford University (~1982–1986) and Harvard University (~1989–1996), and took up a post at the University of California, Los Angeles around 1996.

nodes.label: Nicolas Revire
nodes.summary: Nicolas Revire works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Silpakorn University (2012-2013) and under Claudine Bautze-Picron, Peter Skilling, Michel Jacq-Hergoualc'h, Peter Masefield, Kannika Wimonkasem, and U-tain Wongsathit. He held a post at Thammasat University (attested 2016).

nodes.label: U-tain Wongsathit
nodes.native: อุเทน วงศ์สถิตย์

nodes.label: Thich Thien Nghiem
nodes.summary: Thich Thien Nghiem is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Delhi, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Shalini Singhal (attested 2012).

nodes.label: K. T. S. Sarao
nodes.summary: K. T. S. Sarao is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned degrees at the University of Delhi and the University of Cambridge. He taught history at Kirori Mal College (1981) and became a professor at Delhi in 1995.

nodes.label: David Ownby
nodes.summary: David Ownby is a scholar in sinology, religious studies, and history. After earning his Ph.D. at Harvard University (~1982–1989), he held posts at Harvard (1991), Southern Methodist University (attested 1994), and Université de Montréal (from ~1993).

nodes.label: Vincent Goossaert
nodes.summary: Vincent Goossaert works in Sinology, religious studies, and history. He studied under Kristofer Schipper (~1992–1997) and held posts at CNRS (~1998–2012), The Chinese University of Hong Kong, and EPHE as Professor of Daoist History (~2012).

nodes.label: Zhe Ji
nodes.summary: Zhe Ji works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He earned a PhD in sociology from the École des hautes études en sciences sociales (-2007) and served as an Associate Professor at INALCO (attested 2011–2017).

nodes.label: Benjamin A. Elman
nodes.image: Benjamin A. Elman (born 1946) at the lecture 'The Role of Shanghai in Building Modern Science in China in the 19th Century'.png
nodes.jawiki: ベンジャミン・エルマン
nodes.summary: Benjamin A. Elman is a scholar of Sinology and history/archaeology who studied at Hamilton College, American University, and the University of Pennsylvania. He taught at UCLA (attested 2004) and directed the East Asian Studies Program at Princeton University (~2005–2012).

nodes.label: William M. Bodiford
nodes.jawiki: ウィリアム・ボディフォード
nodes.summary: William M. Bodiford is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology. Educated at the University of Kansas, Yale, Komazawa, and Tsukuba, he held posts at Meiji Gakuin and Iowa before becoming Professor at UCLA around 1992.

nodes.label: Mark Juergensmeyer
nodes.summary: Mark Juergensmeyer works in religious studies and indology. He studied at the University of Illinois System, Columbia University's SIPA, and Union Theological Seminary, and was appointed professor of sociology and religious studies at UC Santa Barbara around 1993.

nodes.label: Nanyang Technological University
variants: Institute of Defence and Strategic Studies, Singapore
Institute of Defence and Strategic Studies (IDSS), Nanyang Technological University, Singapore
Institute of Defence and Strategic Studies, Nanyang Technological University, Singapore

nodes.label: Friederike Assandri
nodes.summary: Friederike Assandri works in Sinology and religious studies. She studied under Gunther-Dietz Sontheimer as a Ph.D. student at Heidelberg University, where she also held a post (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Tufts University
variants: Tufts University School of Veterinary Medicine

nodes.label: Karen Nelson Villanueva
nodes.summary: Karen Nelson Villanueva works in philosophy and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the California Institute of Integral Studies (attested 2013) and studied under traditional teachers Geshe Ngawang Dakpa and Lobsang Chökyi.

nodes.label: Stefan Larsson
nodes.summary: Stefan Larsson specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Stockholm University in 2009 under Per-Arne Berglie and held a postdoctoral fellowship at the University of California, Berkeley, attested in 2012.

nodes.label: Shayne Clarke
nodes.summary: Shayne Clarke specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Bukkyo University, the University of Canterbury (MA under Paul Harrison), and UCLA (PhD 2006 under Gregory Schopen), later becoming an Associate Professor at McMaster University (attested 2015–2016).

nodes.label: Sonya S. Lee
nodes.summary: Sonya S. Lee is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. She earned her PhD from the University of Chicago and taught at Swarthmore College before holding posts at the University of Southern California and Stanford University.

nodes.label: Wu Hung
nodes.summary: Wu Hung studied at Harvard University (~1980–1987) and works in history, archaeology, and sinology. Around 1994, he held posts at the Smart Museum of Art and as a professor at the University of Chicago.

nodes.label: Jerome Silbergeld
nodes.summary: Jerome Silbergeld is a scholar in Sinology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Oregon (~1962–1966) and Stanford University (~1969–1974), and held a post at Princeton University (~2001–2016).

nodes.label: William L. Ames
nodes.summary: William L. Ames is a Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology scholar. He earned an M.S. from Caltech and a Ph.D. from the University of Washington under Collett Cox and David Seyfort Ruegg, later holding posts at Washington, CIIS, and JFK University.

nodes.id: I:University of North Carolina at Charlotte
nodes.label: University of North Carolina at Charlotte
variants: University of North Carolina at Charlotte

nodes.label: Richard A. Hutch
nodes.summary: Richard A. Hutch (born 1945) is a religious studies scholar educated at Gettysburg College, Yale Divinity School, and the University of Chicago. He taught Peter Fenner and held posts at Southern Illinois University (~1975–1978) and the University of Queensland (~1978–2010).

nodes.label: Southern Illinois University Carbondale
variants: Morris Library, Southern Illinois University at Carbondale

nodes.label: William R. LaFleur
nodes.jawiki: ウィリアム・R・ラフルーア
nodes.summary: William R. LaFleur (1936–2010) was a scholar in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. After studying at the University of Chicago, he held posts at Princeton, UCLA, and the University of Pennsylvania.

nodes.label: Sibraj Chetry
nodes.summary: Sibraj Chetry specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied under doctoral supervisor Sibnath Sarma as well as teachers D. K. Chakravarty, N. Sharma, Girish Sarma, and M. Boruah, and was Lecturer of Philosophy at North Lakhimpur College (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Huiwen Zhuang
nodes.summary: Huiwen Zhuang is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under supervisor Kirill Jurievitch Solonin, while also studying under traditional teacher Hsing Yun.

nodes.label: Aaron P. Proffitt
nodes.summary: Aaron P. Proffitt is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who completed an MA at the University of Colorado Boulder and a PhD at the University of Michigan (~2009–2015). He was appointed assistant professor at University at Albany, SUNY (~2016).

nodes.label: Valdo H. Viglielmo
nodes.jawiki: ヴァルド・ヴィリエルモ
nodes.summary: Valdo H. Viglielmo (1926–2016) was a scholar of Japanology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Pennsylvania and Harvard University (~1948–1956), later holding posts at Meiji Gakuin University, Princeton University (~1960–1965), and the University of Hawaii (~1965–1995).

nodes.label: Dan Smyer Yü
nodes.summary: Dan Smyer Yü is a scholar in religious studies and Tibetology who completed his PhD at the University of California, Davis. He served as a Research Group Leader at the Max Planck Institute for the Study of Religious and Ethnic Diversity.

nodes.label: David L. McMahan
nodes.summary: David L. McMahan is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He taught at the University of California, Santa Barbara and the University of Vermont, and held posts as Assistant Professor (attested 2002) and Professor (attested 2013) at Franklin & Marshall College.

nodes.label: Hugh Gray
nodes.summary: Hugh Gray was active in Indology and other fields. He studied at Battersea Grammar School and held an attested post at the University of Cambridge in 1983.

nodes.label: Drolma
nodes.summary: Drolma is a Tibetology scholar who completed an M.Phil. in Tibetan Studies at the University of Oslo under the supervision of Hanna Havnevik (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Lori Meeks
nodes.summary: Lori Meeks (born 1976) specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She completed doctoral studies under Jacqueline I. Stone and Ryuichi Abe, held a postdoctoral fellowship at Stanford (~2003–2004), and became Assistant Professor at USC in ~2004.

nodes.label: Masayuki Taira
nodes.summary: Masayuki Taira is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and history and archaeology. After studying at Kyoto University, he held posts at Kansai University (circa 1983–1989), Osaka University (circa 1989–2017), and Kyoto Tachibana University (circa 2017–2022).

nodes.label: Shunsho Manabe
nodes.summary: Shunsho Manabe (born 1939) specializes in Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Tohoku University (~1959–1968) and held posts at Hosen Gakuen College and Shikoku University, where he was a professor (~2004).

nodes.label: Shenpen Hookham
nodes.summary: Shenpen Hookham is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied under multiple traditional Tibetan teachers and earned a D.Phil from the University of Oxford (~1980–1986) under doctoral supervisor Michael M. Broido.

nodes.label: Hildegard Diemberger
nodes.summary: Hildegard Diemberger specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. She conducted work supervised by Luciano Petech and Ernst Steinkellner.

nodes.label: Wilfred Cantwell Smith
nodes.summary: Wilfred Cantwell Smith was a religious studies scholar who studied at Upper Canada College, the University of Toronto (~1934–1938), and Princeton University (~1944–1948). He held a post at Harvard University as 所長 (~1964–1973).

nodes.label: Lama Kunga Rinpoche
nodes.description: Buddhist Lama of the Sakya school

nodes.label: Kemu Jin
nodes.summary: Kemu Jin (1912–2000) was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Sinology. He held a post at Visva-Bharati University (1941–1945) and served as Professor of Sanskrit at Peking University (~1948–2000).

nodes.label: Fabio Rambelli
nodes.jawiki: ファビオ・ランベッリ
nodes.summary: Fabio Rambelli works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied under mentors Allan G. Grapard and William F. Powell, and held posts at Sapporo University as Associate Professor (2001–2002) and Professor of Religion and Semiotics (~2000–2010).

nodes.label: Eric Reinders
nodes.summary: Eric Reinders works in religious studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under mentors Allan G. Grapard and William F. Powell.

nodes.label: Allan G. Grapard
nodes.summary: Allan G. Grapard (1944–2025) worked in Japanology and religious studies. He taught in the Department of Religious Studies at the University of California, Santa Barbara (~1985–2008) and served as ISF Professor of Shinto Studies at the University of California (~1999–2008).

nodes.label: Gregory P. A. Levine
nodes.summary: Gregory P. A. Levine (born 1963) specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and art history. Educated at Oberlin College and Princeton University, he became an Associate Professor of Japanese art and Buddhist visual cultures at UC Berkeley (~2000).

nodes.label: Lin Heng
nodes.summary: Lin Heng is an Indology scholar who completed an MA at Silpakorn University under the supervision of Chainarong Klinnoi (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Chainarong Klinnoi
nodes.native: ชัยณรงค์ กลิ่นน้อย

nodes.label: Roger T. Ames
nodes.summary: Roger T. Ames is a philosopher and sinologist who studied at the University of British Columbia and National Taiwan University. He was a professor at the University of Hawaii (~1978–2016) and later held a post at Peking University (~2016).

nodes.label: Steve Odin
nodes.summary: Steve Odin is a scholar of philosophy and Japanology. He completed graduate study at Stony Brook University (~1975–1980) under David A. Dilworth and Edward S. Casey, later becoming Professor of Philosophy at the University of Hawaii (1982).

nodes.label: Jason M. Wirth
nodes.image: Jason Martin Wirth (born 1963) in the video 'Everybody's Climate 2025 – Jason Wirth on Humanity in the Anthropocene'.png

nodes.label: Graham Priest
nodes.jawiki: グレアム・プリースト
nodes.summary: Graham Priest (born 1948) works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at Cambridge and the LSE, later holding posts at Melbourne, St Andrews (attested 2011–2018), and CUNY as Distinguished Professor (~2009).

nodes.label: Jan Westerhoff
nodes.summary: Jan Westerhoff is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. Educated at Cambridge and the University of London (including SOAS), he held positions at Durham University, Lady Margaret Hall, and the University of Oxford.

nodes.label: Lili Zheng
nodes.summary: Lili Zheng is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Yongdong Shi (attested 2011).

nodes.label: Uma Chakravarti
nodes.summary: Uma Chakravarti is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. She studied at Miranda House (~1958–1962) and the University of Delhi (~1962–1981), where she completed doctoral research under D. Devahuti.

nodes.label: D. Devahuti
nodes.description: D. Devahuti, 1929-1988; taught at universities of Malaya, Queensland, and Delhi

nodes.label: Ron Garry
nodes.summary: Ron Garry is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teacher Lama Tharchin Rinpoche and teacher Tulku Thubten Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Stuart Ray Sarbacker
nodes.summary: Stuart Ray Sarbacker is a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 2001 under the supervision of David M. Knipe.

nodes.label: B. Alan Wallace
nodes.description: American author, translator, teacher, researcher, interpreter, and Buddhist practitioner
nodes.summary: B. Alan Wallace, a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology, studied at Stanford under Carl Bielefeldt and with several traditional teachers. He held a post at UC Santa Barbara (~1997–2001) and headed the Santa Barbara Institute for Consciousness Studies (~2003).

nodes.label: Berthe Jansen
nodes.description: Assistant Professor of Tibetan Studies at Leiden University
nodes.summary: Berthe Jansen specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Leiden University (BA, PhD under Jonathan A. Silk) and Oxford (MPhil), later serving as a fellow at Heidelberg (~2015–2016) and visiting professor at Leiden (2015–2016).

nodes.label: Vincent Breugem
nodes.summary: Vincent Breugem specializes in Japanology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Taisho, Hanazono, and Kyoto universities, and at Leiden University under Lucia Dolce. He was a research fellow at Leiden University (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Tulku Thondup
nodes.summary: Tulku Thondup was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Dodrupchen Monastery under Kyala Khenpo and Khenpo Chemchok. He later served as a visiting scholar at Harvard University.

nodes.label: David E. Cooper
nodes.summary: David E. Cooper is a philosopher who studied at Highgate School (~1955–1960). He served as Professor of Philosophy at Durham University from 1986 to 2009.

nodes.label: Purushottama Bilimoria
nodes.summary: Purushottama Bilimoria works in philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. He studied under Shivesh Thakur and earned a PhD from La Trobe University, later holding posts at Deakin, Melbourne, Columbia, Stony Brook, and UC Berkeley.

nodes.label: Simon P. James
nodes.summary: Simon P. James is a scholar in philosophy and religious studies. He held posts at Durham University, serving as a tutor in philosophy (attested 2001) and lecturer in philosophy (attested 2013–2014).

nodes.label: University of Wisconsin-Stevens Point
variants: University of Wisconsin at Stevens Point

nodes.label: Latika Lahiri
nodes.summary: Latika Lahiri was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Peking University under Xianlin Ji in 1958 and held a post at the University of Delhi from ca. 1969 to 1988.

nodes.label: Tan Chung
nodes.summary: Tan Chung (1929–2024) was a scholar of Sinology, history and archaeology, and Indology. He served as Professor of Chinese at the University of Delhi (~1964–1978) and Head of Chinese and Japanese Studies at Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1978–1994).

nodes.label: Michael Kowalewski
nodes.summary: Michael Kowalewski is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Cambridge from 1969 to 1972 and at SOAS University of London from 1987 to 1990.

nodes.label: Sonam Chhoki
nodes.summary: Sonam Chhoki is a Tibetology and history scholar who earned an M.A. from Jawaharlal Nehru University and a Ph.D. from SOAS University of London. She has served as a history teacher at Samtse College of Education.

nodes.label: Thierry Mathou
nodes.summary: Thierry Mathou (born 1963) works in history, archaeology, and Tibetology. He studied at EDHEC Business School and the Paris Institute of Political Studies, and served as an Associated Political Scientist at the Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique.

nodes.label: Françoise Pommaret
nodes.summary: Françoise Pommaret is a Tibetologist and historian who studied at INALCO (~1975–1979) and the University of Paris (~1985–1997). She served as a lecturer at INALCO and became Directeur de recherche at the CNRS in 2002.

nodes.label: Karma Ura
nodes.summary: Karma Ura studied at Magdalen College, Oxford (~1983–1986) and the University of Edinburgh (~1988–1989). Working in Tibetology and other fields, he became Director of the Centre for Bhutan Studies around 1999.

nodes.label: Ronald E. Purser
nodes.summary: Ronald E. Purser works in religious studies, philosophy, and management, and studied under Koshin Ogui (1985). He held posts at Loyola University Chicago (~1989–1995) and San Francisco State University (~1995).

nodes.label: David R. Loy
nodes.summary: David R. Loy is a scholar in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Carleton College, University of Hawaii, and National University of Singapore (PhD 1984), where he also taught (~1978–1984), later serving as professor at Xavier University (~2006–2008).

nodes.label: Pamela D. Winfield
nodes.summary: Pamela D. Winfield specializes in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. She held a post at Temple University (attested 2001) and served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Elon University (attested 2015–2017).

nodes.label: Paula Kane Robinson Arai
nodes.summary: Paula Kane Robinson Arai is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. She studied at Kalamazoo College and Harvard University under Masatoshi Nagatomi and Wilfred Cantwell Smith, later holding posts at Vanderbilt (~1994–2002) and LSU (~2007).

nodes.label: Patricia Fister
nodes.jawiki: パトリシア・フィスター
nodes.summary: Patricia Fister specializes in Japanology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her Ph.D. from the University of Kansas, where she was assistant professor of art history (~1985–1991), before becoming a professor at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (~2001–2019).

nodes.label: Michaela Mross
nodes.summary: Michaela Mross is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who completed her PhD at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (-2014). She held posts at the University of Göttingen, UC Berkeley, and Stanford University (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Diane E. Riggs
nodes.summary: Diane E. Riggs specializes in Japanology and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at UCLA in 2010 under William M. Bodiford, and later held posts at Pepperdine University, Kenyon College, and Western Michigan University.

nodes.label: Daniel Aitken
nodes.summary: Daniel Aitken is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Tasmania under the supervision of Jay L. Garfield, and also studied under Parimal G. Patil and Leonard van der Kuijp.

nodes.label: Chanju Mun
nodes.summary: Chanju Mun is a buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (2001–2002) and earned a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 2002). His supervisors and teachers included Charles Hallisey, Masahiro Shimoda, Morten Schlütter, Gudrun Bühnemann, and John D. Dunne.

nodes.label: Yifa
nodes.description: Taiwanese Buddhist nun, scholar and writer
nodes.summary: Yifa is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. She studied under Hsing Yun, earned degrees from National Taiwan University, the University of Hawaii, and a PhD at Yale under Stanley Weinstein, later holding posts at University of the West and Harvard.

nodes.label: Reginald A. Ray
nodes.summary: Reginald A. Ray (b. 1942) is a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar. Trained under Mircea Eliade, Chögyam Trungpa, and others, he held posts at Naropa University (attested 2001–2006) and the University of Colorado Boulder (attested 2001–2002).

nodes.label: Dainin Katagiri
nodes.summary: Dainin Katagiri was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under traditional teacher Eko Hashimoto (~1946–1953) and at Komazawa University (~1948–1951). He later founded the Minnesota Zen Meditation Center.

nodes.label: Thich Nhat Hanh
nodes.jawiki: ティク・ナット・ハン
nodes.summary: Thich Nhat Hanh (1926–2022) was a Buddhist and religious studies figure who studied at Columbia and Princeton (1961–1963) and taught at both in 1961. He founded the An Quang Pagoda and the School of Youth for Social Service.

nodes.label: John Daido Loori
nodes.image: Daido Roshi in the Buddha Hall.jpeg
nodes.summary: John Daido Loori was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Taizan Maezumi, whom he succeeded. He served as Abbot at Zen Mountain Monastery from circa 1980 to 2009.

nodes.label: Dagfinn Føllesdal
nodes.jawiki: ダグフィン・フェレスダール
nodes.summary: Dagfinn Føllesdal was a philosopher who studied at the University of Oslo (~1950–1957) and Harvard University (~1957–1961) under Willard Van Orman Quine. He held major academic posts at the University of Oslo (~1967–1999) and Stanford University (~1968–2026).

nodes.label: Jiang Wu
nodes.summary: Jiang Wu works in Buddhist studies and sinology. He pursued graduate studies at Nankai University and earned his doctorate at Harvard under Tu Weiming and Robert M. Gimello. He was attested as a professor at the University of Arizona (2011–2018).

nodes.label: Yonsei University
variants: Institute of East and West Studies at Yonsei University

nodes.label: Thierry Meynard
nodes.summary: Thierry Meynard (born 1963) is a sinologist and philosopher who earned his PhD from Peking University under Yulie Lou. He became Professor of Philosophy at Sun Yat-sen University around 2006 and director of The Beijing Center for Chinese Studies in 2012.

nodes.id: I:The Beijing Center for Chinese Studies
nodes.label: The Beijing Center for Chinese Studies
variants: The Beijing Center for Chinese Studies

nodes.label: Scott Pacey
nodes.summary: Scott Pacey is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He completed his doctorate at the Australian National University in 2011, held a postdoctoral fellowship at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, and lectured at the University of Manchester.

nodes.label: Kalu Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Kalu Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who studied at Palpung Monastery under teachers including Lama Norbu Dondrup, Khakyab Dorje, and Tai Situ Pema Wangchok Gyalpo. He directed three-year retreats at Palpung Monastery (~1940–1955) and taught numerous students.

nodes.label: Tomy Augustine
nodes.summary: Tomy Augustine works in philosophy and Indology. He earned a master's at the University of Madras studying under C. S. Sundaram, completed a PhD at Banaras Hindu University under Munni K. Agrawal, and held a post at Salesian College (attested 2008).

nodes.label: T. S. Devadoss
nodes.summary: T. S. Devadoss specializes in philosophy and Indology. His career includes posts at the University of Madras, where he was attested in 1994 and served as professor as attested in 2008.

nodes.label: Michela Clemente
nodes.summary: Michela Clemente is a scholar of Tibetology. She studied under Elena De Rossi Filibeck and Hildegard Diemberger (2013–2015), and held a post as a Marie Sklodowska Curie Fellow at the University of Cambridge.

nodes.label: Agnieszka Helman-Ważny
nodes.description: Polish bibliologist, paper historian, conservator of monuments.
nodes.summary: Agnieszka Helman-Ważny is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. She studied at the Academy of Fine Arts, Warsaw, and earned her PhD at Nicolaus Copernicus University in Toruń. She held posts at Cornell University (~2008–2010) and the University of Warsaw (2015).

nodes.label: Thomas Cleary
nodes.summary: Thomas Cleary (1949–2021) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He was educated at Harvard University, where he studied under E. Bruce Brooks.

nodes.label: J. C. Cleary
nodes.summary: J. C. Cleary was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at Harvard University (~1973–1980) under doctoral supervisor Masatoshi Nagatomi. He served as an instructor at Wesleyan University.

nodes.label: Mary Clabaugh Wright
nodes.summary: Mary Clabaugh Wright specialized in Sinology and history/archaeology. She studied at Vassar College (~1934–1938) and Radcliffe College/Harvard University (~1938–1951), and held a faculty post at Yale University (~1959–1970).

nodes.label: Torkel Brekke
nodes.summary: Torkel Brekke specializes in Indology and religious studies. He earned an MPhil at the University of Oslo and a doctorate at the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich, later holding posts at Oxford (~1995–1999) and Oslo (~2001–2021).

nodes.label: Kenryu Tsuji
nodes.summary: Kenryu Tsuji (1919–2004) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University in 1938 and at the University of Toronto.

nodes.id: I:National Museum Institute of the History of Art, Conservation and Museology
nodes.label: National Museum Institute of the History of Art, Conservation and Museology
Rebecca Redwood French
nodes.summary: Rebecca Redwood French is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Washington and Yale University under mentors including Stanley Weinstein and Robert Thurman, she held law faculty posts at Colorado Boulder and University at Buffalo.

nodes.label: Rafal Stepien
nodes.summary: Rafal Stepien, a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy, completed his PhD at Columbia University under Chun-fang Yu and Bernard Faure. He was an Academic Visitor at Wadham College (2012–2013) and an Exchange Scholar at Harvard University (2015).

nodes.label: Chun-fang Yu
nodes.summary: Chun-fang Yu is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. She studied at Columbia University (~1968–1973) and under Nanting and Sheng Yen. She held posts at Rutgers University (~1972–2001) and as Professor at Columbia University (attested 2007–2015).

nodes.label: Michael Chase
nodes.summary: Michael Chase is a philosopher who studied at the University of Victoria and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1993–1997). In ~2002, he became a researcher in ancient philosophy at the Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique.

nodes.label: Philippe Turenne
nodes.summary: Philippe Turenne is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at McGill University under G. Victor Sōgen Hori, also studying under Richard P. Hayes, Khenpo Palden Sherab, and other traditional Tibetan scholars.

nodes.label: Peter Schwieger
nodes.summary: Peter Schwieger (b. 1952) is a scholar of Tibetology. He studied under Dieter Schuh (~1972–1978), succeeded Klaus Sagaster in 2001, and served as Professor at the University of Bonn (~2002–2018).

nodes.label: Dieter Schuh
nodes.summary: Tibetologist Dieter Schuh studied under Shri Krishna Sharma at the University of Cologne (~1967-1972). He served as a special professor in Tibetology at the University of Bonn (~1978-2007) and founded the International Institute for Tibetan and Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Christian Wittern
nodes.summary: Christian Wittern is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies who has held academic posts at Kyoto University (attested 1993 as Professor, and 2008) and Hanazono University (attested 2011).

nodes.label: Eliot Deutsch
nodes.summary: Eliot Deutsch was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at Columbia University (~1956–1960). He was a professor at the University of Hawaii (~1967–2015), editor of Philosophy East and West (~1967–1988), and held posts at Harvard, Chicago, and Cambridge.

nodes.label: Kamala Tiyavanich
nodes.summary: Kamala Tiyavanich specializes in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. She studied at Cornell University under David K. Wyatt, A. Thomas Kirsch, and Richard Polenberg, and held a Mellon Postdoctoral Fellowship there from 1993 to 1994.

nodes.label: David K. Wyatt
nodes.jawiki: デビッド・K・ワイアット
nodes.summary: David K. Wyatt was a historian who studied at Harvard (~1955–1959), Boston University (~1959–1960), and Cornell (~1960–1966). He held posts at SOAS (~1962–1968), the University of Michigan (~1968–1969), and Cornell University (~1969–2002).

nodes.label: Richard Polenberg
nodes.summary: Richard Polenberg was a historian who studied at Columbia University (~1959–1964) and held a faculty post at Cornell University from ~1966 to 2011.

nodes.label: Trung Huynh
nodes.summary: Trung Huynh is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed a PhD at the University of the West under doctoral supervisor Darui Long, attested in 2016.

nodes.label: Susan Whitfield
nodes.summary: Susan Whitfield (born 1960) specializes in history, archaeology, and Sinology. After studying at SOAS University of London (~1986–1995), she directed the International Dunhuang Project at the British Library (1993–2017) and joined the University of East Anglia (~2018).

nodes.label: Imre Galambos
nodes.description: Scholar of medieval Chinese and Tangut manuscripts
nodes.summary: Imre Galambos (born 1967) specializes in Sinology and Tibetology. Educated at ELTE, Nankai, and UC Berkeley (PhD ~2002), he worked at the British Library (~2002–2012) before becoming a lecturer at the University of Cambridge in 2012.

nodes.label: Joseph Margolis
nodes.jawiki: ジョセフ・マーゴリス
nodes.summary: Joseph Margolis (1924–2021) was a philosopher who studied at Columbia University from circa 1947 to 1953. He taught Youru Wang and held a post at Temple University from circa 1968 to 2021.

nodes.label: Sandra A. Wawrytko
nodes.summary: Sandra A. Wawrytko is a scholar of philosophy, sinology, and Buddhist studies who has held faculty posts at San Diego State University, including Professor (attested 1999) and Associate Professor of Philosophy (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Megan Bryson
nodes.summary: Megan Bryson is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. She studied at Stanford University and held a post at the University of Tennessee (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Rachelle M. Scott
nodes.summary: Rachelle M. Scott is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She completed her dissertation at Northwestern University under George D. Bond and Robert Launay, and held a post at the University of Tennessee (attested 2009–2017).

nodes.id: I:Ferenc Hopp Museum of Asiatic Arts
nodes.label: Ferenc Hopp Museum of Asiatic Arts
variants: Ferenc Hopp Museum of Eastern Asiatic Art

nodes.label: Hungarian Academy of Sciences
variants: Oriental Library of the Hungarian Academy of Sciences
Oriental Collection, Hungarian Academy of Sciences

nodes.label: Géza Bethlenfalvy
nodes.summary: Géza Bethlenfalvy (1936–2021) specialized in Tibetology, Indology, and Central Asian studies. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University under Louis Ligeti, later holding posts there, at the Hungarian Academy of Sciences, the University of Delhi, and the University of Vienna.

nodes.label: Zsóka Gelle
nodes.description: Hungarian Tibetologist, translator, writer, filmmaker and guide
nodes.summary: Zsóka Gelle is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who pursued a PhD at the University of Vienna. Gelle held posts at Tibet House Foundation, the East-West Research Institute, Eötvös Loránd University (2014–2016), and the Budapest Centre for Buddhist Studies (2014–2016).

nodes.label: Tsutomu Horio
nodes.summary: Tsutomu Horio is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied under Keiji Nishitani. He served as a professor at Otani University, attested in 1990.

nodes.label: Benjamin Bogin
nodes.summary: Benjamin Bogin works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan, studying under doctoral supervisor Donald S. Lopez Jr. and teachers Janet Gyatso and Gareth Sparham.

nodes.label: Tomoko Masuzawa
nodes.summary: Tomoko Masuzawa works in religious studies and history/archaeology. She studied at International Christian University, Yale University, and UC Santa Barbara (~1979–1985), and held faculty posts at UNC Chapel Hill (~1987–2000) and the University of Michigan (1999, ~2000).

nodes.label: James Robson
nodes.image: James Robson (academic) on Filled with Meaning.png
nodes.summary: James Robson (b. 1965) specializes in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He held posts as Assistant Professor at the University of Michigan (attested 2006–2014) and Associate Professor at Harvard University (~2008).

nodes.label: John J. Holder
nodes.summary: John J. Holder is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied under Harry Krebs. He held a visiting research post at the University of Oxford and taught at St. Norbert College (attested 2006, 2018).

nodes.label: Eric Huntington
nodes.summary: Eric Huntington is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and history and archaeology. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under the supervision of Gary A. Tubb.

nodes.label: Dina Bangdel
nodes.summary: Dina Bangdel was a scholar of religious studies and archaeology. She held a post at Virginia Commonwealth University from around 2002 to 2017, and an affiliation with Ohio State University is attested in 2006.

nodes.label: Virginia Commonwealth University
variants: Virginia Commonwealth University School of Medicine

nodes.label: Peter Alan Roberts
nodes.summary: Peter Alan Roberts is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teacher Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche in 1979 and completed his doctorate under supervisor Michael Aris.

nodes.label: Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche
nodes.image: Thrangu Rinpoche on 24 May 2016 face detail, from- 17th Karmapa performs Long Life Offering to Kenchen Thrangu Rinpoche (cropped).jpg
nodes.summary: Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche (1933–2023) worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied under Rangjung Rigpe Dorje (~1959–1981), founded Thrangu Monastery, served as abbot of Rumtek Monastery (~1960–2023), and directed the Karma Shri Nalanda Institute (~1981–2023).

nodes.label: Somphong Santacitto
nodes.summary: Somphong Santacitto works in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned a master's degree in Buddhist studies at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (attested 2006) under supervisor Phra Suthithammanuwat and committee member Watchara Ngamchitcharoen.

nodes.label: Phra Suthithammanuwat
nodes.native: พระสุทธิธรรมนิเทศ

nodes.label: Watchara Ngamchitcharoen
nodes.native: วัชระ งามจิตรเจริญ

nodes.label: Prayudh Payutto
nodes.native: ประยุทธ์ ปยุตฺโต
nodes.image: ป.อ. ปยุตฺโต.jpg
nodes.description: Thai Buddhist monk, abbot of Wat Nyanavesakavan

nodes.id: I:Centre de Recherches sur les Civilisations de l'Asie Orientale
nodes.label: Centre de Recherches sur les Civilisations de l'Asie Orientale
Brian D. Ruppert
nodes.summary: Brian D. Ruppert (born 1962) specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. Mentored by Willis Stoesz, he held posts at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (~1999–2018) and Bates College (~2018) as Kazushige Hirasawa Professor of Japanese Studies.

nodes.label: Patricia Schiaffini-Vedani
nodes.summary: Patricia Schiaffini-Vedani works in Sinology and Tibetology. She completed graduate study at Peking University (1990–1994) under Zumo Zhou, Zhuhong Zhang, and Shufen Mu, and earned a PhD from the University of Pennsylvania under Perry Link.

nodes.label: Perry Link
nodes.summary: Perry Link is a Sinology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Harvard University (~1962–1976) and held faculty posts at Princeton University (~1989–2008) and the University of California, Riverside (~2008).

nodes.label: James Ishmael Ford
nodes.summary: James Ishmael Ford (b. 1948) is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He studied under Houn Jiyu-Kennett and John Tarrant, attended the Pacific School of Religion (~1988–1991), and founded Boundless Way Zen.

nodes.label: Houn Jiyu-Kennett
nodes.summary: Houn Jiyu-Kennett (1924–1996) was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at Durham University and under traditional teachers Sek Kim Seng (~1962) and Keidō Chisan Kohō (~1962–1963).

nodes.label: Jonathan C. Gold
nodes.summary: A scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, Gold held teaching posts at the University of Vermont, Drew University (attested 2006), and Princeton University (attested 2015–2016).

nodes.label: Gudo Wafu Nishijima
nodes.summary: Gudo Wafu Nishijima (1919–2014) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at the University of Tokyo and under Kodo Sawaki. He held positions at the Ministry of the Treasury and Japan Securities Finance.

nodes.label: Anna Balikci Denjongpa
nodes.summary: Anna Balikci Denjongpa specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. Supervised by Lionel Caplan, she earned a PhD from SOAS University of London, and also studied under Lopen Dugyal and Gorlok Tulku. In 2002, she became Research Coordinator at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology.

nodes.label: Nathaniel DeWitt Garson
nodes.summary: Nathaniel DeWitt Garson is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins and also studied under Khenpo Namdrol.

nodes.label: Southern Methodist University
variants: Perkins School of Theology, Southern Methodist University

nodes.label: Elizabeth Morrison
nodes.summary: Elizabeth Morrison works in Buddhist studies and sinology. She studied under Bernard Faure, Carl Bielefeldt, Ellen Neskar, Janet Gyatso, and Susan Niditch, and held posts at Amherst College (1998–1999) and Middlebury College (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Chögyam Trungpa
nodes.image: Trungpa from Khenpo gangshar2 cropped image.jpg
nodes.jawiki: チョギャム・トゥルンパ
nodes.summary: Chögyam Trungpa (1939–1987) was a figure in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. He studied at St Antony's College, University of Oxford (~1963–1967), and with multiple teachers including Khenpo Gangshar and Shechen Kongtrul Pema Drime. He founded Naropa University in 1973.

nodes.label: Aruna Haldar
nodes.summary: Aruna Haldar is an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Girindrasekhar Bose and Kedar Nath Ojha. She worked as a teacher at Patna University.

nodes.label: Girindrasekhar Bose
nodes.summary: Girindrasekhar Bose (1887–1953) studied at Presidency University, Medical College Kolkata, and the University of Calcutta. He worked at Medical College Kolkata (1911–1915) and was Professor of Experimental Psychology at the University of Calcutta (1917–1949).

nodes.label: Joachim Gentz
nodes.summary: Joachim Gentz works in sinology, religious studies, and philosophy. He served as Junior Professor in Religious Studies at the University of Göttingen and as Reader in Chinese Studies at the University of Edinburgh (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Perry Schmidt-Leukel
nodes.summary: Perry Schmidt-Leukel is a religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies scholar. He held academic posts at Munich (~1988–1998), Innsbruck (~1996–1998), Salzburg (~1998–2000), Glasgow (~2000–2009), and Münster (~2009–2020).

nodes.label: Philip Clart
nodes.description: German Sinologist, Professor of Chinese Studies at Leipzig University, Germany

nodes.label: Michael Stanley-Baker
nodes.summary: Michael Stanley-Baker is a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and history/archaeology who earned an MA at Indiana University under Stephen R. Bokenkamp. He has held posts at the Max Planck Institute, Leipzig University, University of Pittsburgh, and Nanyang Technological University.

nodes.label: Harold Stewart
nodes.summary: Harold Stewart (1916–1995) was a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed his education at the Sydney Conservatorium of Music and the University of Sydney.

nodes.label: David Tracy
nodes.summary: David Tracy worked in religious studies and philosophy. After studying at Saint Joseph's Seminary (~1956–1960) and the Pontifical Gregorian University (~1960–1969), he held posts at the Catholic University of America (~1967–1969), the University of Chicago (~1985–2006), and the Committee on Social Thought (~1985–2006).

nodes.label: Peter Schwabland
nodes.summary: Peter Schwabland works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA at the University of Washington under supervisor Leonard van der Kuijp.

nodes.label: Michael L. Walter
nodes.summary: Michael L. Walter specializes in Tibetology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Larry Moses and held posts as a Research Fellow at the Lumbini International Research Institute (attested 2000) and Special Languages Cataloger at Indiana University (attested 2020).

nodes.label: Akimichi Eda
nodes.summary: Akimichi Eda is an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Dr. phil. from the University of Marburg (attested 2005). Eda studied under Katsumi Mimaki, Khangkar Tsultrim Kelsang, and doctoral supervisor Michael Hahn.

nodes.label: Lita Peipina
nodes.summary: Lita Peipina is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She earned an MA at the University of Oslo (attested 2008) under MA supervisor Jens Braarvig in 2003, and also studied under Jens-Uwe Hartmann.

nodes.label: Stephen Prothero
nodes.summary: Stephen Prothero is a scholar of religious studies. He completed his education at Yale University, Jonathan Edwards College, and Harvard University (~1986–1990), later joining the faculty at Boston University (~1996).

nodes.label: Duncan Ryūken Williams
nodes.summary: Duncan Ryūken Williams specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. After studying at Reed College and Harvard University, he served as Assistant Professor at UC Irvine (~2002–2006) and held a post at UC Berkeley (~2006–2011).

nodes.label: Kenneth K. Tanaka
nodes.summary: Kenneth K. Tanaka is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and UC Berkeley under Padmanabh S. Jaini. He held posts at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (~1984–1998) and Musashino University (~1998–2018).

nodes.label: Kosho Uchiyama
nodes.summary: Kosho Uchiyama was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Waseda University (~1932–1937) and under Kodo Sawaki (~1941–1965), whom he succeeded. He taught Shohaku Okumura.

nodes.label: Kodo Sawaki
nodes.summary: Kodo Sawaki (1880–1965) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and under traditional teacher Sotan Oka. He served as a professor at Komazawa University (~1935–1963) and taught Kosho Uchiyama, Sodo Yokoyama, and Gudo Wafu Nishijima.

nodes.label: Ian Kishizawa
nodes.summary: Ian Kishizawa (1865–1955) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Saitama University and under Sotan Oka. He taught Shunryu Suzuki.

nodes.label: See Mui Yian
nodes.summary: See Mui Yian is a scholar in Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under the supervision of K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Warren Lee Todd
nodes.summary: Warren Lee Todd is a scholar in philosophy and Indology who completed his PhD at Lancaster University (attested 2012) under doctoral supervisor Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad. He also studied under Irina Kuznetsova, Chogye Trichen Rinpoche, and Peter Harvey.

nodes.label: Alison Denton Jones
nodes.summary: Alison Denton Jones works in sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She studied under doctoral supervisor Martin King Whyte, committee member Christopher Winship, and teachers Allan H. Barr, Mingfei Gao, and Margaret Dornish.

nodes.label: Martin King Whyte
nodes.summary: Martin King Whyte is a scholar of Sinology and other fields. He studied at Cornell University (~1960–1964) and Harvard University (~1966–1971). His career includes positions at the University of Michigan (~1970–1994) and Harvard University (~2000).

nodes.label: Allan H. Barr
nodes.summary: Allan H. Barr is a sinologist who completed his doctorate at the University of Oxford by 1983. He held a post as Professor of Asian Languages and Literatures at Pomona College, attested in 2001.

nodes.label: Margaret Dornish
nodes.summary: Margaret Dornish is a scholar of religious studies and Sinology. She studied at Yale University, Claremont Graduate University, and the University of Southern California, and served as Associate Professor of Religion at Pomona College (attested 1989).

nodes.label: Daniela Berti
nodes.summary: Daniela Berti specializes in Indology and ethno-anthropology, having earned her PhD from the University of Siena. In 2004, she was attested as a fellow at Milieux, Cultures et Sociétés en Himalaya.

nodes.id: I:Milieux, Cultures et Sociétés en Himalaya
nodes.label: Milieux, Cultures et Sociétés en Himalaya
variants: Milieux, Cultures et Sociétés en Himalaya, Paris

nodes.label: Gilles Tarabout
nodes.summary: Gilles Tarabout is an Indology and religious studies scholar. In 2004, he was attested as a senior fellow at CNRS, a member at EHESS, and an exchange program director at Fondation Maison des Sciences de l'Homme.

nodes.id: I:Fondation Maison des Sciences de l'Homme
nodes.label: Fondation Maison des Sciences de l'Homme
variants: Maison des Sciences de l'Homme, Paris

nodes.label: Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen
nodes.summary: Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen (1895–1977) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Rumtek Monastery and under teachers including Khenpo Shenga (~1914–1927) and Dzongsar Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, later teaching at Men-Tsee-Khang.

nodes.label: Myōsei Tatsuguchi
nodes.summary: Myōsei Tatsuguchi is a Buddhist studies scholar who taught Diane E. Riggs and Jeff Wilson. Tatsuguchi served at Ryukoku University as a professor (attested 1987) and later as professor emeritus (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Robert Charles Zaehner
nodes.image: Internationaal Theologisch Congres toekomst van de religie, religie van de toeko, Bestanddeelnr 925-4729.jpg
nodes.description: British spy and academic on Eastern religions (1913–1974)
nodes.summary: Robert Charles Zaehner was a scholar of religious studies, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and Indology. After studying at Christ Church (~1933–1937) and serving in the Secret Intelligence Service (~1943–1952), he was Spalding Professor at Oxford (~1952–1974).

nodes.label: James A. Benn
nodes.summary: James A. Benn works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He studied at Cambridge, SOAS under Timothy H. Barrett, and UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr., holding posts at Lewis & Clark College, Arizona State, and McMaster University.

nodes.label: Kyoko Tokuno
nodes.summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies and Sinology, Kyoko Tokuno held posts at the University of Oregon and the University of Washington, where she was attested as a professor in 2017.

nodes.label: Dudjom Rinpoche
nodes.image: Dudjom Rinpoche with Prince Paljor Namgyal and Maharani Kunzang Dechen Tshomo Namgyal.jpg

nodes.label: Leonard C. D. C. Priestley
nodes.summary: Leonard C. D. C. Priestley specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and sinology. He studied under F. E. L. Priestley and earned his doctorate under Anthony Kennedy Warder, holding an attested post at the University of Toronto in 1991.

nodes.label: Julia Ching
nodes.summary: Julia Ching was a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and philosophy. She studied at the College of New Rochelle, Catholic University of America, and Australian National University. She later held a post at the University of Toronto (~1978–2001).

nodes.label: Willard Gurdon Oxtoby
nodes.summary: Willard Gurdon Oxtoby (1933–2003) was a religious studies scholar. He studied at Tamalpais High School, Stanford, Harvard (~1955–1958), and Princeton (~1958–1962), and held a position at the University of Toronto (~1971–1999).

nodes.label: Jacob Holubeck
nodes.summary: Jacob Holubeck is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Jurievitch Solonin, attested in 2013.

nodes.label: Eric Stephen Goodell
nodes.summary: Eric Stephen Goodell is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned an MA at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and studied at the University of Virginia (attested 2012) under doctoral supervisor Paul Groner.

nodes.label: Kristin Johnston Largen
nodes.summary: Kristin Johnston Largen is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. In 2018, she was attested as Professor of Systematic Theology at United Lutheran Seminary and Associate Dean of Religious and Spiritual Life at Gettysburg College.

nodes.label: Marcus Bingenheimer
nodes.summary: Marcus Bingenheimer specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at the University of Würzburg under Norbert Klaes, at Nagoya University, and under Huinan Yang. His posts include Dharma Drum Buddhist College, Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts, and Temple University.

nodes.label: Jongmyung Kim
nodes.summary: Jongmyung Kim works in Buddhist studies, history, and religious studies. He studied at Yonsei University, Seoul National University, and UCLA (MA by 1994, under Robert E. Buswell Jr.), later serving as an associate professor at the Academy of Korean Studies.

nodes.label: Roderick Whitfield
nodes.summary: Roderick Whitfield is a scholar of archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the British Museum (attested 1986) and SOAS University of London, where he was an emeritus professor (attested 2011).

nodes.label: Central Academy of Fine Arts
variants: Central Academy of Fine Arts in Beijing

nodes.label: Eugene Y. Wang
nodes.summary: Eugene Y. Wang is a scholar of archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied under Wu Hung and John M. Rosenfield (~1990–1997), taught at the University of Chicago (~1996–1997), and became Abby Aldrich Rockefeller Professor at Harvard University (~1997).

nodes.label: Kristofer Schipper
nodes.summary: Kristofer Schipper (1934–2021) was a scholar of sinology and religious studies who studied at the Faculty of Arts of Paris, ENLOV, and EPHE (~1958–1962). He held posts at the École française d'Extrême-Orient (~1962–1970) and Leiden University (~1993–1999).

nodes.label: Erik Haarh
nodes.summary: Erik Haarh (1929–1993) was a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics. He earned a doctor's degree at the University of Copenhagen (attested 1969) and held a post at the Royal Danish Library from around 1957 to 1974.

nodes.label: Helen J. Baroni
nodes.summary: Helen J. Baroni specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She studied at Grinnell College, Princeton Theological Seminary, and Columbia University under Paul B. Watt, and she took up a post at the University of Hawaii around 1993.

nodes.label: Shou-chien Shih
nodes.summary: Shou-chien Shih (b. 1951) works in history, archaeology, and sinology. He served as director of the National Palace Museum (~2000–2004) and as a professor at National Taiwan University (attested 2002), teaching Pei-jung Wu.

nodes.label: Institut für Buddhismus-Kunde
variants: an active society for the study of Mahāyāna

nodes.label: Brian J. Nichols
nodes.summary: Brian J. Nichols specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. He studied at the Inter-University Program for Chinese Language Studies and completed a PhD at Rice University (attested 2011) under doctoral supervisor Anne Carolyn Klein.

nodes.id: I:Inter-University Program for Chinese Language Studies
nodes.label: Inter-University Program for Chinese Language Studies
variants: Inter-University Program for Chinese language studies at Tsinghua University

nodes.label: Tansen Sen
nodes.summary: Tansen Sen works in history and archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied at Peking University under Yinzeng Geng and earned his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under Victor H. Mair, later holding a post at Baruch College (attested 2003).

nodes.label: Takeshi Umehara
nodes.summary: Takeshi Umehara studied philosophy and Japanology at Kyoto University (~1945–1948) and Nagoya University. He held posts at Ryukoku University, Ritsumeikan University (professor ~1967–1972), the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (director general ~1987–1995), and the Institute of Technologists.

nodes.label: Kennard Lipman
nodes.summary: Kennard Lipman works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He completed his doctoral studies under Herbert V. Guenther and held a post as a sessional instructor at the University of Calgary.

nodes.label: Derge Gonchen Monastery
variants: sDe dge dbon stod slob grwa at sDe dge dgon chen Monastery

nodes.label: Kuse Serjong Shedra
variants: sDe dge Ku se gSer ljongs bshad grwa

nodes.label: Khenpo Dragyab Lodrö
variants: mKhan Rinpoche Brag gyab Blos gros

nodes.label: Sarah Aoife Richardson
nodes.summary: Sarah Aoife Richardson is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She earned her PhD from the University of Toronto by 2016 under the supervision of Jenny Purtle.

nodes.label: Julia F. Andrews
nodes.summary: Julia F. Andrews specializes in Sinology and history and archaeology. She completed her studies at Brown University, UC Berkeley, and Harvard University. She took up a post at Ohio State University around 1987.

nodes.label: Frank J. Hoffman
nodes.summary: Frank J. Hoffman is a scholar in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Hawaii under teachers including Eliot Deutsch and David J. Kalupahana, and completed his doctorate under Stewart Sutherland.

nodes.label: Trent Walker
nodes.summary: Trent Walker is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of California, Berkeley, where his doctoral supervisor was Alexander von Rospatt.

nodes.label: Tina Rasmussen
nodes.summary: Tina Rasmussen specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied under traditional teacher Pa-Auk Sayadaw and under MA supervisor Christian K. Wedemeyer.

nodes.label: Pa-Auk Sayadaw
nodes.native: ဖားအောက်ဆရာတော်

nodes.label: Jan Chozen Bays
nodes.summary: Jan Chozen Bays is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Shodo Harada (~1995) and Taizan Maezumi (attested 2011). Around 2002, she became abbess at Great Vow Zen Monastery.

nodes.label: UMass Chan Medical School
variants: Center for Mindfulness in Medicine, Health Care, and Society
マサチューセッツ大学医学部

nodes.label: Neal Arvid Donner
nodes.summary: Neal Arvid Donner is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at the University of British Columbia, where he was a student of Leon Hurvitz.

nodes.label: Wenjie Qin
nodes.summary: Wenjie Qin specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. Qin earned a PhD at Harvard University, studying under doctoral supervisor Tu Weiming as well as Diana L. Eck, Masatoshi Nagatomi, Charles Hallisey, and Robert M. Gimello.

nodes.label: Bing Chen
nodes.summary: Bing Chen is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He served as a professor at Sichuan University from around 1987 and held a post at the Chengdu Academy of Social Sciences attested in 1993.

nodes.label: Yun-hua Jan
nodes.summary: Yun-hua Jan was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies who studied under Yun-shan Tan. He was a Research Fellow at Visva-Bharati University (1953) and a Professor at McMaster University (attested 1984–1990).

nodes.label: Stephanie Roemer
nodes.summary: Stephanie Roemer is a scholar in the field of Tibetology. She completed her doctoral studies under supervisors Eberhard Sandschneider and Toni Huber.

nodes.label: Eberhard Sandschneider
nodes.summary: Eberhard Sandschneider studied at Saarland University (~1976–1986). A specialist in Sinology and other fields, he held posts at Mainz (1995–1998), the Free University of Berlin (1998), and the German Council on Foreign Relations (2003–2016).

nodes.label: Naoki Nabeshima
nodes.summary: Naoki Nabeshima is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He founded Ryukoku University and served there as Professor of Shin Buddhist Studies (attested 2004).

nodes.label: David Matsumoto
nodes.summary: David Matsumoto is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as Director of the Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2004) and held a post there attested in 2013.

nodes.label: Jing-shen Tao
nodes.summary: Jing-shen Tao (born 1933) is a historian and sinologist. He studied at National Taiwan University (~1952–1959) and Indiana University (~1964–1967), later serving as Professor of East Asian Studies at the University of Arizona (~1976–2000).

nodes.label: Christian Coseru
nodes.description: American philosopher and scholar of Buddhist philosophy
nodes.summary: Christian Coseru is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his PhD at the Australian National University under John Powers (~1999–2003) and has served as a fellow at the Asiatic Society and Associate Professor at the College of Charleston (~2006).

nodes.label: Kevin Buckelew
nodes.summary: Kevin Buckelew is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at Sarah Lawrence College. His doctoral supervisors included Chun-fang Yu, Bernard Faure, and Zhaohua Yang.

nodes.label: Shu-fen Liu
nodes.summary: Shu-fen Liu works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history and archaeology. She held posts at Academia Sinica (attested 2012), including as professor at the Institute of History and Philology (attested 2018).

nodes.id: I:Institute of History and Philology, Academia Sinica
nodes.label: Institute of History and Philology, Academia Sinica
variants: Institute of History and Philology at Academia Sinica
Institute of History and Philology at the Academia Sinica, Taipei, Taiwan
Institute of History and Philology, Academia Sinica

nodes.label: Valeria Gazizova
nodes.summary: Valeria Gazizova works in Tibetology, religious studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She wrote her master's thesis at the University of Oslo under the supervision of Per Kvaerne (attested 2009).

nodes.label: Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso
variants: mKhan po Tshul khrims rgya mtsho

nodes.label: Loden Sherab Dagyab
nodes.summary: Loden Sherab Dagyab (born 1940) is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Tenzin Gyatso, the 14th Dalai Lama (~1959), and held an academic post at the University of Bonn (~1966–2004).

nodes.label: Martin Brauen
nodes.summary: Martin Brauen is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who studied at the universities of Delhi and Zurich, as well as with traditional teachers. He worked as a Konservator at the University of Zurich from around 1975 to 2008.

nodes.label: Günter Grönbold
nodes.summary: Günter Grönbold (born 1943) is a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the Bavarian State Library from around 1974 to 2008, including serving as Head of the South Asia Department (~1976–2008).

nodes.label: Michael J. Sweet
nodes.summary: Michael J. Sweet (d. 2021) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He earned his PhD at Wisconsin–Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, studying also with several traditional teachers, and later held clinical psychiatry appointments there.

nodes.label: John Ross Carter
nodes.summary: A scholar of Buddhist and religious studies, Carter studied at King's College London, SOAS, and Harvard (doctoral work ~1968–1972 under Wilfred Cantwell Smith). He was a professor at Chapel House at Colgate University (~1972–2006).

nodes.label: Amita Chatterjee
nodes.summary: Amita Chatterjee is a scholar in philosophy and Indology. She held a post as professor of philosophy at Jadavpur University, attested in 1999 and 2009.

nodes.label: Catholic University of America
variants: The Catholic University of America (Washington, DC)

nodes.label: Knut A. Jacobsen
nodes.summary: Knut A. Jacobsen (born 1956) is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. After studying at the University of California, Santa Barbara (~1989–1994), he held professorships at the University of Bergen (~1996) and the University of Oslo (attested 1999).

nodes.label: Thomas P. Kasulis
nodes.summary: Thomas P. Kasulis is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Japanology. He held posts at Ashland University (circa 1980–1991) and Ohio State University, where he served as a professor from circa 1991 to 2018.

nodes.label: John M. Koller
nodes.summary: John M. Koller is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Indology who studied at the East-West Center under Shri Krishna Saksena and Charles A. Moore. He served as a philosophy professor at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute.

nodes.id: I:Institute of Philosophy, Russian Academy of Sciences
nodes.label: Institute of Philosophy, Russian Academy of Sciences
variants: Institute of Philosophy, Academy of Sciences USSR

nodes.label: Michiko Yusa
nodes.summary: Michiko Yusa (born 1951) is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Japanology. She completed her PhD at the University of California, Santa Barbara under Raimon Panikkar (~1978–1983) and became a professor of foreign languages at Western Washington University (~1983).

nodes.label: Diego Loukota
nodes.summary: Diego Loukota works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned an MA at Peking University and a PhD in 2019 at the University of California, Los Angeles.

nodes.label: Ruixuan Chen
nodes.summary: Ruixuan Chen is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Chen completed a PhD at Leiden University (attested 2018) supervised by Paul Harrison and held a post at Heidelberg University.

nodes.label: Susan Andrews
nodes.summary: Susan Andrews is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned her PhD at Columbia University under the doctoral supervision of Chun-fang Yu.

nodes.label: Michael Como
nodes.summary: Michael Como specializes in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Kuo-liang Wang and advisers Carl Bielefeldt and Bernard Faure, and held an attested post at Columbia University in 2009.

nodes.label: Bokar Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Bokar Rinpoche (1940–2004) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Kalu Rinpoche (~1960–1989). He held a post at Bokar Ngedon Choekhor Ling Monastery (~1984–2004) and taught Shenpen Hookham and Lama Palden Drolma.

nodes.label: Michael M. Broido
nodes.summary: Michael M. Broido specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Cambridge, taught Shenpen Hookham, and held a post at the University of Oxford.

nodes.label: Geshe Tashi Tsering
nodes.summary: Geshe Tashi Tsering (born 1958) is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Sera and Gyuto monasteries, taught at Kopan Monastery and Gandhi Foundation College, and became resident teacher at Jamyang Buddhist Centre in 1994.

nodes.label: Qiwen Xiao
nodes.summary: Qiwen Xiao is a scholar in Buddhist studies. Xiao earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University, where the degree was supervised by Yongdong Shi (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Nandini Bhattacharyya-Panda
nodes.summary: Nandini Bhattacharyya-Panda is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. She has held posts as a Project Fellow at the Maulana Abul Kalam Azad Institute of Asian Studies (attested 2011) and as a Senior Fellow at the Indian Council of Historical Research.

nodes.id: I:Maulana Abul Kalam Azad Institute of Asian Studies
nodes.label: Maulana Abul Kalam Azad Institute of Asian Studies
variants: Maulana Abul Kalam Azad Institute for Asian Studies

nodes.label: Shri Krishna Saksena
nodes.summary: Shri Krishna Saksena is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who taught John M. Koller. He held professorships at the University of Lucknow and the University of Hawaii (both attested 2016).

nodes.label: Ashok Kumar Malhotra
nodes.summary: Ashok Kumar Malhotra is a scholar in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at the East-West Center (~1964–1968) and founded the State University of New York at Oneonta.

nodes.label: Gregory Forgues
nodes.summary: Gregory Forgues is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a Magister der Philosophie at the University of Vienna (attested 2011) under MA supervisor Helmut Tauscher, and studied under Birgit Kellner and several traditional teachers.

nodes.label: Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Sakya College and SOAS University of London under teachers such as Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Dudjom Rinpoche, and Sakya Trizin.

nodes.label: Chanmyay Sayadaw U Janakābhivaṃsa
nodes.native: ချမ်းမြေ့ဆရာတော် ဦးဇနကာဘိဝံသ

nodes.label: Pema Bhum
nodes.summary: Pema Bhum is a Tibetology scholar. He served as a professor of Tibetan languages and letters at Lanzhou University and Indiana University, and was director of the Latse Contemporary Tibetan Cultural Library (attested 2003–2009).

nodes.label: Morton Klass
