nodes.summary: Morton Klass was a scholar of religious studies and Indology. After studying at Brooklyn College and Columbia University, he held posts at the US Merchant Marine, Bennington College, Barnard College, and Columbia University.

nodes.label: Margaret Mead
nodes.jawiki: マーガレット・ミード
nodes.summary: Margaret Mead was an anthropologist who studied at Barnard College and Columbia University. She spent her career primarily at the American Museum of Natural History (~1926–1978) and Columbia University (~1954–1978), also holding a post at the University of Rhode Island.

nodes.label: Xiaoting Wei
nodes.summary: Xiaoting Wei works in sinology and Buddhist studies. Attested in 2004, Wei earned an MA from the National University of Singapore under the supervision of Cheng-Mei Ku.

nodes.label: Jinshi Fan
nodes.summary: Jinshi Fan is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Peking University (~1958–1963). She served as Director of the Dunhuang Academy (~1998–2014) and held a post at Lanzhou University.

nodes.label: Sanjit Kumar Sadhukhan
nodes.summary: Sanjit Kumar Sadhukhan works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied under teacher and guide Mrinalkanti Gangopadhyaya (attested 1994) as well as traditional teacher A. P. Lama.

nodes.label: Bhajagovinda Ghosh
nodes.summary: Bhajagovinda Ghosh works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Attested in 1994, he held posts as Assistant Director at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and editorial board member for the Bulletin of Tibetology.

nodes.label: Martin Collcutt
nodes.jawiki: マーティン・コルカット
nodes.summary: Martin Collcutt, a historian of Japan, studied at Fitzwilliam College, Cambridge, and earned his PhD from Harvard (1969). He taught at Yokohama National University, the University of Tokyo, and served at Princeton University (1975-2015), directing its East Asian Studies Program.

nodes.label: Luang Por Teean Jittasubho
nodes.native: หลวงพ่อเทียน จิตฺตสุโภ

nodes.label: Andrew Quintman
nodes.summary: Andrew Quintman works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Jay L. Garfield and was an assistant professor in the Department of Religious Studies at Yale University, attested in 2015.

nodes.label: Masaharu Imai
nodes.summary: Masaharu Imai works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at Tokyo University of Education (~1962-1970) and held posts at Ibaraki University (~1974-1990) and the University of Tsukuba (~1990-2006).

nodes.label: Juhn Y. Ahn
nodes.summary: Juhn Y. Ahn is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He earned his PhD from the University of California, Berkeley in 2007 and was attested in 2019 as an Associate Professor at the University of Michigan.

nodes.label: Lobsang Yongdan
nodes.summary: Lobsang Yongdan works in Tibetology and history and archaeology. He studied at Kumbum Monastery and completed a PhD at the University of Cambridge under Hildegard Diemberger (ending 2014), later holding postdoctoral posts at Bonn and the Max Planck Institute.

variants: Max Planck Institute for the History of Science
Max Planck Institute for the History of Science, Berlin

nodes.label: Fernando Jose Benetti
nodes.summary: Fernando Jose Benetti is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Nalanda University under doctoral supervisor Aleksandra Wenta (attested 2018).

nodes.label: William H. Nienhauser, Jr.
nodes.summary: William H. Nienhauser, Jr. (born 1943) is a Sinologist who studied at Bonn and Indiana University under Irving Yucheng Lo and Friedrich Alexander Bischoff. He held appointments at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, including Halls-Bascom Professor (~2002).

nodes.label: Kristina Myrvold
nodes.summary: Kristina Myrvold is a religious studies and Indology scholar. She worked as an editor (attested 2005) and was a Ph.D. candidate (attested 2008) at Lund University, and later served as Assistant Professor at Linnaeus University (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Olle Qvarnström
nodes.summary: Olle Qvarnström (born 1953) is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at Harvard, Washington, and Copenhagen under scholars including Tord Olsson and Karl H. Potter, and served as ansvarig utgivare at Lund University (attested 2000–2005).

nodes.label: Gurinder Singh Mann
nodes.summary: Gurinder Singh Mann is a religious studies and Indology scholar who studied at the English and Foreign Languages University and Harvard. He held posts at Columbia University from around 1988 to 1999 and UC Santa Barbara from around 1999 to 2015.

nodes.label: Anne Hardgrove
nodes.summary: Anne Hardgrove studied at Carleton College (circa 1986–1990) and the University of Michigan (circa 1991–1999). Working in history, archaeology, and Indology, she held posts at the University of Texas at San Antonio in 2000 and circa 2001.

nodes.id: I:University of Texas at San Antonio
nodes.label: University of Texas at San Antonio
variants: University of Texas at San Antonio

nodes.label: Paul Copp
nodes.summary: Paul Copp is a Sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at UMass Amherst and Princeton (PhD attested 2005). He held posts at Heidelberg Academy of Sciences (2006), Western Michigan University, and the University of Chicago (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Donald E. Gjertson
nodes.summary: Donald E. Gjertson worked in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Akira Takeda and completed his PhD under John Ching-yu Wang at Stanford (~1969–1975). He held a post at UMass Amherst (~1975–2012).

nodes.label: Stephen Batchelor
nodes.summary: Stephen Batchelor is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under traditional teachers Ngawang Dhargyey, Geshe Rabten, and Kusan Sunim, and held a post at Songgwangsa (1981–1984).

nodes.label: Royall Tyler
nodes.summary: Royall Tyler is a scholar of Japanology and religious studies. He studied at Harvard University (circa 1953–1957) and Columbia University (circa 1964–1977), later holding posts at the University of Oslo (~1983–1989) and the Australian National University (~1990–2000).

nodes.label: Huai-Chin Nan
nodes.summary: Huai-Chin Nan (1918–2012) worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and sinology. He studied at the Republic of China Military Academy and under teacher Huanxian Yuan (~1942–1945), later serving as Professor of Philosophy at Chinese Culture University (attested 1986).

nodes.label: Chinese Culture University
variants: College of Chinese Culture Graduate School in Taipei
Institute of Chinese Culture in Taipei

nodes.label: Mae Chee Huynh Kim Lan
nodes.summary: Mae Chee Huynh Kim Lan is a scholar in Buddhist studies. She earned a Master of Arts in Buddhist Studies from Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University, where she was advised by Phra Suthithammanuwat and Veerachart Nimanong (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Gareth Fisher
nodes.summary: Gareth Fisher works in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned a Ph.D. in socio-cultural anthropology from the University of Virginia in 2006 and was an Assistant Professor of Religion and Anthropology at Syracuse University (attested 2011–2016).

nodes.label: Nirupam Chakma
nodes.summary: Nirupam Chakma is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College under supervisors Tilak Kariyawasam and Fa Qing (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Tilak Kariyawasam
nodes.summary: Tilak Kariyawasam works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He served as head of Pali and Buddhist Studies at the University of Kelaniya (attested 1993) and as Dean of the Graduate School at the International Buddhist College (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Fa Qing
nodes.summary: Fa Qing specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Calgary, where his doctoral supervisor was Leslie S. Kawamura, with interim supervision by A. W. Barber.

nodes.label: Ki-yong Rhi
nodes.summary: Ki-yong Rhi (1922–1996) worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He held academic posts at Dongguk University, where he is attested in 1983 and was attested as professor emeritus in 2007.

nodes.label: Martin Willson
nodes.summary: Martin Willson was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers including Thubten Yeshe, Thubten Zopa Rinpoche, Geshe Thubten Loden, Zasep Tulku Rinpoche, Geshe Rabten, Jampa Tegchok, and Geshe Lhundub Sopa.

nodes.label: Jampa Tegchok
nodes.summary: Jampa Tegchok studied at Sera Monastery and worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He taught at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (~1971–1978), Nalanda Monastery (~1982–1993), and Land of Medicine Buddha (~1998–2001).

nodes.label: Daniel L. Overmyer
nodes.description: Scholar of the history of Chinese popular religions
nodes.summary: Daniel L. Overmyer (1935–2021) was a sinologist and scholar of religion who studied at the University of Chicago (~1966–1973). He held posts at Oberlin College (~1970–1973) and the University of British Columbia, including Department Head (~1985–1993) and Professor (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Klaus Mylius
nodes.summary: Klaus Mylius (1930–2025) was an Indologist. Mylius held posts at Leipzig University (~1968–1992), the University of Bayreuth, and Goethe University Frankfurt (attested 2003).

nodes.label: Peter James Gilks
nodes.summary: Peter James Gilks works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned a PhD from Australian National University (attested 2010) under John Powers, and studied at Drepung Gomang Dratsang under traditional teachers including Geshe Ngawang Jangchup and Tsultrim Phuntsok.

nodes.label: Aleix Ruiz-Falqués
nodes.summary: Aleix Ruiz-Falqués is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He earned his PhD at the University of Cambridge under Eivind Kahrs and held posts at Shan State Buddhist University and Singapore University of Technology and Design.

nodes.label: Di Luo
nodes.summary: Di Luo specializes in Sinology, archaeology, history, and Buddhist studies. She earned her Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Southern California under doctoral supervisors Dominic Cheung, Sonya S. Lee, and Bettine Birge.

nodes.label: Bettine Birge
nodes.summary: Bettine Birge is a scholar of Sinology and history/archaeology. She completed her Ph.D. at Columbia University under William Theodore de Bary and was a visiting scholar at Academia Sinica in 1994.

nodes.label: Richard von Glahn
nodes.summary: Richard von Glahn is a scholar of sinology and history/archaeology. He was a visiting fellow at the University of Tokyo (1988–1989) and became a professor at the University of California, Los Angeles around 1987.

nodes.label: Miranda Shaw
nodes.summary: Miranda Shaw is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied with doctoral supervisor Masatoshi Nagatomi (attested 1994) and Robert A. F. Thurman, and completed postdoctoral work under B. N. Mukherjee.

nodes.label: Justin Shimeld
nodes.summary: Specializing in philosophy, Justin Shimeld earned a PhD from the University of Tasmania (attested 2012), where he studied under doctoral supervisors Jeff Malpas and Sonam Thakchoe.

nodes.label: Jeff Malpas
nodes.summary: Jeff Malpas is a philosopher who taught Sonam Thakchoe and Justin Shimeld. He held a professorship at the University of Tasmania (~1999) and a post at La Trobe University in 2019.

nodes.label: Sonam Thakchoe
nodes.summary: Sonam Thakchoe is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology who completed a PhD at the University of Tasmania (~1998–2002) under Jay L. Garfield and Jeff Malpas. He also held a post at the University of Tasmania (~2005).

nodes.label: Barry Kerzin
nodes.image: Barry Kerzin, American Professor of Medicine and Buddhist monk.gif
nodes.summary: Barry Kerzin is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at UC Berkeley (~1969-1972), Keck School of Medicine of USC (~1972-1976), and under traditional teacher Geshe Namgyal Wangchen.

nodes.label: Junyi Tang
nodes.image: Tang Chun-i - New Asia College and Yale-China Association Cooperation 1954 (cropped).jpg
nodes.summary: Specializing in philosophy and sinology, Junyi Tang studied at Peking University and under Thomé H. Fang and Shili Xiong. He held posts at National Central University (circa 1937–1949) and New Asia Institute of Advanced Chinese Studies (circa 1949–1978).

nodes.label: Shili Xiong
nodes.summary: Shili Xiong (1885–1968) was a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied at the China Inner Learning College in 1920. He held an academic post at Peking University from 1923 to 1955.

nodes.label: Zongsan Mou
nodes.summary: Zongsan Mou was a philosopher and sinologist who studied at Peking University (~1929–1933) under Shili Xiong. Mou held posts at Zhejiang University, National Taiwan University, National Taiwan Normal University, Tunghai University, and the New Asia Institute of Advanced Chinese Studies.

China Inner Learning College

nodes.label: Philip Whalen
nodes.summary: Philip Whalen was an author and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Reed College and under Richard Baker. He served as visiting poet at Naropa University, resident teacher at South Ridge Zendo, and abbot of Hartford Street Zen Center.

nodes.id: I:Institute of Fine Arts, New York University
nodes.label: Institute of Fine Arts, New York University
variants: Institute of Fine Arts of New York University

nodes.label: Oleg Grabar
nodes.summary: Oleg Grabar (1929–2011) was a historian and archaeologist. He studied at the University of Paris (~1946–1948), Harvard University (~1948–1950), and Princeton University (~1950–1955), later holding posts at the University of Michigan (~1954–1969) and Harvard University (~1969–1990).

nodes.label: Jörg Heimbel
nodes.summary: Specializing in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Jörg Heimbel studied at Tibet University and completed a PhD at the University of Hamburg (2014) under David P. Jackson, Dorji Wangchuk, and Franz-Karl Ehrhard. He was attested as a Hamburg lecturer in 2019.

nodes.label: Elizabeth English
nodes.summary: Elizabeth English is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She earned her PhD from the University of Oxford by 1999, studying under Alexis Sanderson and Harunaga Isaacson.

nodes.label: Sung Bae Park
nodes.summary: Sung Bae Park (born 1933) is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied under Lewis Lancaster (~1972–1979). He served as assistant professor at Dongguk University (~1968–1972) and held a post at Stony Brook University beginning in 1977.

nodes.label: David A. Dilworth
nodes.summary: David A. Dilworth is a scholar of philosophy and Japanology. He studied under Masao Abe and Valdo H. Viglielmo (1968), and held a post at Stony Brook University around 1970.

nodes.label: Antonio T. de Nicolás
nodes.summary: Antonio T. de Nicolás worked in philosophy and Indology. He completed his studies at Fordham University (~1965–1968) and held a post at Stony Brook University from circa 1968 to 1996.

nodes.label: Alfred Bloom
nodes.jawiki: アルフレッド・ブルーム
nodes.summary: Alfred Bloom (1926–2017) studied at Pennsylvania, Andover Newton, Harvard Divinity School, and Harvard University (PhD c. 1955–1963). In Buddhist and religious studies, he held posts at Harvard, Dean at IBS (c. 1986–1994), and Emeritus Professor at Hawaii.

University at Albany (State University of New York)
University at Albany, State University of New York

nodes.label: Ruben L. F. Habito
nodes.summary: Ruben L. F. Habito specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his doctorate at the University of Tokyo (~1972–1979) under Akira Hirakawa and Jikido Takasaki, and held posts at Sophia University (~1980–1989) and Southern Methodist University (~1989; Professor ~2002).

nodes.label: Yutai Ikeda
nodes.summary: Yutai Ikeda was a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts at Otani University and Doho University, where he was Emeritus Professor (attested 2006).

nodes.label: Kenshi Kusano
nodes.summary: Kenshi Kusano is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at Otani University from ~1971 to 1980 and served as a professor there from ~1999 to 2018.

nodes.label: Shunshō Terakawa
nodes.summary: Shunshō Terakawa (1928–2021) was a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1950–1955). He later served as an emeritus professor at Otani University (attested 1998–2006).

nodes.label: Michael K. Jerryson
nodes.summary: Michael K. Jerryson was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed undergraduate studies at Wisconsin–Madison under Harold Scheub. He held professorships in religious studies at Eckerd College (~2008–2012) and Youngstown State University (~2012–2021).

nodes.label: Daniel W. Kent
nodes.summary: Daniel W. Kent is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned his Ph.D. from the University of Virginia. In 2010, he held instructor posts at the University of Virginia and Mary Baldwin University.

nodes.label: Brian Daizen Victoria
nodes.jawiki: ブライアン・ヴィクトリア
nodes.summary: Brian Daizen Victoria (born 1939) is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and history. He studied at Nebraska Wesleyan, Komazawa, and Temple University (PhD 1991), later holding posts at Antioch University (~2005–2013) and the University of Adelaide (attested 2011).

nodes.label: Baruch College
variants: Baruch College, City University of New York

nodes.label: Franz-Karl Ehrhard
nodes.summary: Franz-Karl Ehrhard is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Lambert Schmithausen and habilitated at Hamburg. He directed the Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project (1988–1993) and held an endowed seat and professorship at Munich (2001, 2006–2012).

nodes.label: Navina Lamminger
nodes.summary: Navina Lamminger is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich under doctoral supervisor Franz-Karl Ehrhard.

nodes.label: Orna Almogi
nodes.summary: Orna Almogi specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Ngagyur Nyingma Institute, with Khenpo Wangchuk Sonam, and under David P. Jackson and Lambert Schmithausen, holding posts at the Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project and University of Hamburg.

nodes.label: Stacey Van Vleet
nodes.summary: Stacey Van Vleet specializes in Tibetology, sinology, history, and archaeology. She earned an MA from the University of Colorado Boulder and a PhD from Columbia University, where she held a post attested in 2013.

nodes.label: Geoffrey Barstow
nodes.summary: Geoffrey Barstow is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He held a post at the University of Virginia around 2006 to 2013 and became assistant professor of religious studies at Oregon State University around 2014.

nodes.label: Yutaka Yoshida
nodes.summary: Yutaka Yoshida is a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at Hitotsubashi University and the University of Tokyo (~1977–1981), and held posts at Hitotsubashi University and Kyoto University (~2006–2020).

nodes.label: James Burnell Robinson
nodes.summary: James Burnell Robinson (born 1944) works in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1967–1975) under Richard Hugh Robinson and Geshe Lhundub Sopa, later teaching at the University of Northern Iowa (attested 1996).

nodes.label: Cuong T. Mai
nodes.summary: Cuong T. Mai works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. He earned an MA at the University of Hawaii and a PhD at Indiana University under John R. McRae (attested 2009), later serving as Adjunct Lecturer at the University of Vermont.

nodes.label: Reiko Ohnuma
nodes.summary: Reiko Ohnuma (b. 1964) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. Educated at UC Berkeley and the University of Michigan under Luis Oscar Gómez, she held posts at UT Austin, University of Alabama, and Dartmouth College.

nodes.label: Gereon Kopf
nodes.summary: Gereon Kopf works in religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Temple University, was mentored by Yasuo Yuasa, and held posts at J. F. Oberlin University, Luther College, the Nanzan Institute for Religion and Culture, and the University of Hong Kong.

nodes.label: John C. Maraldo
nodes.summary: John C. Maraldo is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He held posts at the University of North Florida, where he is attested in 1988 and as distinguished professor emeritus of philosophy in 2015.

nodes.label: Seijun Ishii
nodes.summary: Seijun Ishii is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University from around 1977 to 1986. He held a post as professor at Komazawa University around 1996.

nodes.label: Tairyu Tsunoda
nodes.summary: Tairyu Tsunoda is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He held posts as a lecturer at Komazawa Junior College (attested 1995) and as a professor at Komazawa University (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Ruth W. Dunnell
nodes.summary: Ruth W. Dunnell is a scholar of Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history. She earned her PhD from Princeton University in 1983 and studied under Jinbo Shi (1987–1988). She became James P. Storer Associate Professor of Asian History at Kenyon College.

nodes.label: Mark C. Elliott
nodes.summary: Mark C. Elliott works in sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history. He has held posts as a professor of history at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and as Professor of Chinese and Inner Asian History at Harvard University.

nodes.label: Stephen G. Covell
nodes.description: professor of world religions and cultures
nodes.summary: Stephen G. Covell works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He earned his doctorate at Princeton University (~1995–2001) under Jacqueline I. Stone and took up a post at Western Michigan University (~2003).

nodes.label: Wendi L. Adamek
nodes.summary: Wendi L. Adamek specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies, completing a PhD at Stanford University in 1998. She held positions at Barnard College (attested 2008) and the University of Calgary (attested 2018).

nodes.label: Sadajiro Sugiura
nodes.summary: Sadajiro Sugiura was a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied at Rikkyo University (~1889–1893) and the University of Pennsylvania (~1895–1898). He later held a post at Rikkyo University.

nodes.label: Bo Jiang
nodes.summary: Bo Jiang is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Jiang earned a PhD at Columbia University (attested 2008) under the supervision of Robert A. F. Thurman.

nodes.label: Soochow University
variants: School of Foreign Languages, Soochow University

nodes.label: Zhiru Ng
nodes.summary: Zhiru Ng specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. She earned an MA at the University of Michigan under Luis Oscar Gómez and a PhD at the University of Arizona under Robert M. Gimello, later serving at Pomona College.

nodes.label: Masao Yamaguchi
nodes.summary: Masao Yamaguchi worked in Japanology and religious studies, studying at the University of Tokyo (~1949-1953) and Tokyo Metropolitan University (~1955-1960). He held posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1967-1997), University of Shizuoka (~1997-1999), Sapporo University (~1999-2003), and Chuo University.

nodes.label: Ryoshun Okubo
nodes.summary: Ryoshun Okubo (born 1954) specializes in Buddhist studies. After studying at Waseda University (~1973–1982), he became Professor of Sino-Japanese Buddhism there (~2006) and served as director of Taimon Kenkyūkai (attested 2007).

nodes.summary: Shashibhusan Dasgupta was an Indian scholar of religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Scottish Church College and the University of Calcutta, where he later served as a Lecturer from circa 1945 to 1964.

nodes.label: Dung Ngoc Duong
nodes.summary: Dung Ngoc Duong is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed a PhD at Boston University under the supervision of Malcolm David Eckel (attested 2001).

nodes.label: Diego Cosmelli
nodes.summary: Diego Cosmelli earned his PhD at the École Polytechnique under the doctoral supervision of Francisco Varela.

nodes.label: Antoine Lutz
nodes.summary: Antoine Lutz is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed his PhD at Pierre and Marie Curie University under the supervision of Francisco Varela.

nodes.label: Christine Mollier
nodes.summary: Christine Mollier works in Sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She studied under Kristofer Schipper and served at the CNRS as a researcher (1989–1995) and Director of Research (attested 2006–2014), as well as Visiting Professor at the University of Chicago.

nodes.label: Jacques Giès
nodes.summary: Jacques Giès (1950–2021) worked in sinology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. He studied at Paris-Sorbonne University and Beaux-Arts de Paris, and served as Chief Curator of Chinese Painting at the Musée Guimet from circa 1980 to 2008.

nodes.label: Koun Yamada
nodes.summary: Koun Yamada was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at the First Higher School (~1924–1927) and Tokyo Imperial University (~1927–1930). He succeeded Hakuun Yasutani, taught Ruben L. F. Habito, and worked at NOF Corporation (~1941–1969).

nodes.label: Yaroslav Komarovski
nodes.summary: Yaroslav Komarovski specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at multiple Tibetan institutions under various traditional teachers, completed graduate research at the University of Virginia, held a Mellon postdoctoral fellowship at Washington University, and worked at the University of Nebraska–Lincoln.

nodes.label: Dzongsar Shedra
variants: Dzongsar Institute for Advanced Studies of Buddhist Philosophy and Research in Bir, India

nodes.label: McDougal
nodes.summary: McDougal is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts (Research) at the University of Sydney under the supervision of Geoffrey Samuel and Mark Allon.

nodes.label: Dhivan Thomas Jones
nodes.summary: Dhivan Thomas Jones is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Richard Gombrich and Margaret Cone. He served as an associate lecturer at the Open University and held a post at the University of Chester in 2019.

nodes.label: Shan Shan Zhao
nodes.summary: Shan Shan Zhao is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts at McMaster University under the supervision of James A. Benn, also studying under Shayne Clarke and Mark Rowe.

nodes.label: Margaret Gouin
nodes.summary: Margaret Gouin is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She earned her PhD from the University of Bristol under the supervision of Paul Williams.

nodes.label: Thinh Canh Quang
nodes.summary: Thinh Canh Quang specializes in Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of the West (attested 2007) under doctoral supervisor Kottegoda S. Warnasuriya, having also studied under Lewis Lancaster and Ananda W. P. Guruge.

nodes.label: Noa Ronkin
nodes.summary: Noa Ronkin works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She studied under Shlomo Biderman and earned a D.Phil. from the University of Oxford (Wolfson College) under Richard Gombrich by 2003. She was also a Visiting Research Fellow at Stanford University.

nodes.label: Patricia Buckley Ebrey
nodes.summary: Patricia Buckley Ebrey is a historian and Sinologist. Educated at Chicago (1968) and Columbia (1970, 1975), she held posts at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (~1975–1997), the Institute for Advanced Study (1998), and the University of Washington (1997).

nodes.label: Kate Wharton
nodes.summary: Kate Wharton works in philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. She earned her Ph.D. from SOAS University of London in 2008 and held a post at Birkbeck, University of London, attested in 2010.

nodes.label: Peter Fenner
nodes.summary: Peter Fenner works in Buddhist studies and philosophy, holding a post at Deakin University. He studied under advisers Noble Ross Reat, Arvind Sharma, and Richard A. Hutch, as well as traditional teacher Thubten Zopa Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Lindsay G. McCune
nodes.summary: Lindsay G. McCune works in Tibetology and religious studies. She studied under Kathleen M. Erndl and John Corrigan, completing an MA under the supervision of Bryan J. Cuevas (attested 2007).

nodes.label: Nancy Grace Lin
nodes.summary: Nancy Grace Lin specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She completed graduate study at Columbia University and earned her PhD at the University of California, Berkeley, studying under teachers including Bryan J. Cuevas, Michael Hahn, and Somadeva Vasudeva.

nodes.label: Hermann Kulke
nodes.summary: Hermann Kulke is a historian, archaeologist, and Indologist who earned his PhD from the University of Freiburg (~1962–1967). He held the Chair of Asian History at the University of Kiel (1988) and an attested post at Heidelberg University (2004).

nodes.label: Yanling Chen
nodes.summary: Yanling Chen works in Buddhist studies. Attested in 2012, Chen earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under MA supervisor Yongdong Shi and studied under traditional teacher Hsing Yun.

nodes.label: Agehananda Bharati
nodes.summary: Agehananda Bharati was a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Vienna. He held posts at Banaras Hindu University, Delhi, Tokyo, Kyoto, the University of Washington, and Syracuse University (professor of anthropology, 1961–1991).

nodes.label: Ron Leifer
nodes.summary: Ron Leifer was a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under Agehananda Bharati (1964) and traditional teacher Khenpo Karthar Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Khenpo Karthar Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Khenpo Karthar Rinpoche (1924–2019) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Thrangu Monastery (~1936–1959). He served as a teacher at Rumtek Monastery from 1959 and became abbot of Karma Triyana Dharmachakra in 1978.

nodes.label: Tessa J. Bartholomeusz
nodes.summary: Tessa J. Bartholomeusz worked in religious and Buddhist studies. She studied at the Universities of Florida, Virginia, Ceylon, Cornell, Florida State, and Banaras Hindu University. She taught at the University of Virginia, Indiana University–Purdue University Indianapolis (~1991–2001), and Florida State (1993).

nodes.label: Krishnanath Chatterjee
nodes.summary: Krishnanath Chatterjee is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied under Surendra Nath Bhattacharya, Haripada Chakravarty, Ramaranjan Mukherji, Krishna Gopal Goswami, Satkari Mookerjee, Amareshwar Thakur, and Siddheshwar Bhattacharya.

nodes.label: Ramaranjan Mukherji
nodes.summary: Ramaranjan Mukherji (1928–2010) was an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Calcutta (~1944–1953) and later held an academic post there (~1956–1970).

nodes.label: James Matthew Baskind
nodes.summary: James Matthew Baskind specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Yale University under the supervision of Stanley Weinstein (attested 2006).

nodes.label: Katsuhiro Yoshizawa
nodes.summary: Katsuhiro Yoshizawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Doshisha University from circa 1964 to 1968 and served as a professor at Hanazono University.

nodes.label: Tsuneki Nishiwaki
nodes.summary: Tsuneki Nishiwaki is a scholar of philosophy, Sinology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Tokyo University of Education (~1962–1971). He held posts at Doshisha University (~1972–1990) and served as professor at Kyoto University (~1990–2007).

nodes.label: Anthony Cerulli
nodes.summary: Anthony Cerulli specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Chicago (circa 2001–2007) and served as Professor of South Asian Studies at the University of Wisconsin-Madison circa 2014.

nodes.label: Projit Bihari Mukharji
nodes.summary: Projit Bihari Mukharji works in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Presidency University, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and SOAS, later holding posts at Newcastle University, McMaster University, the University of Pennsylvania (~2011–2022), and Ashoka University (~2022).

nodes.label: Pierce Salguero
nodes.description: professor of Asian history and religious studies
nodes.summary: Pierce Salguero works in Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and religious studies. Educated at the University of Virginia and Johns Hopkins University (~2005–2010), he held posts at Pennsylvania State University (2010) and the University of Pennsylvania (2011–2012).

nodes.label: Christoph Kleine
nodes.description: German japanologist and religious studies scholar
nodes.summary: Christoph Kleine works in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD and completed his Habilitation at the University of Marburg, held a postdoctoral post at EFEO, and was a professor at LMU Munich before joining Leipzig University.

nodes.label: Mervin Viggo Hanson
nodes.summary: Mervin Viggo Hanson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of British Columbia (attested 1980) under doctoral supervisor Leon Hurvitz, having also studied under Kathryn A. A. Cissell.

nodes.label: Kendall Marchman
nodes.summary: Kendall Marchman specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Marchman studied under Mario Poceski (attested 2009) and completed a PhD at the University of Florida in 2015.

nodes.label: Si Ti La
nodes.summary: Si Ti La is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Acharya Nagarjuna University under doctoral supervisor J. Sitaramamma. He also studied under multiple traditional teachers, including U Kundala, U Sajjanasāra, and U Sāsana.

nodes.label: Osvald Sirén
nodes.summary: Osvald Sirén (1879–1966) worked in sinology and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Helsinki (~1897–1900) and held posts at Stockholm University (1908–1923) and the Nationalmuseum (1928–1945).

nodes.label: Erik-Jan Zürcher
nodes.summary: Erik-Jan Zürcher is a historian. He studied at Het Rijnlands Lyceum Oegstgeest (~1965–1971) and Leiden University (~1971–1984), where he later held an academic post around 1993.

variants: College of the City of New York
City College in New York City

nodes.label: A. H. Armstrong
nodes.summary: A. H. Armstrong studied at Jesus College (~1928–1932) and worked in philosophy. He held academic posts at Swansea University (~1936–1939), the University of Malta (~1939–1943), Cardiff University (~1947–1950), and the University of Liverpool (~1950–1972).

nodes.label: Joseph John Loizzo
nodes.summary: Joseph John Loizzo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology educated at Amherst College and Harvard University, studying under Robert A. F. Thurman. He founded the Nalanda Institute for Contemplative Science and was a visiting scholar at Columbia University.

nodes.label: Nalanda Institute for Contemplative Science
variants: Nalanda Institute for Meditation and Healing

nodes.label: Trijang Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Trijang Rinpoche (1901–1981) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Sherab Gyatso. He taught at Ganden Shartse Monastery; his students included the 14th Dalai Lama, Zong Rinpoche, and Thubten Yeshe.

nodes.label: Ji Hao
nodes.summary: Ji Hao is a Sinologist who earned a PhD at the University of Minnesota under doctoral supervisor Paul Rouzer. Hao held an academic post at the College of the Holy Cross (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Paul Rouzer
nodes.summary: Paul Rouzer is a scholar in the fields of sinology and Buddhist studies. He has held academic posts at Harvard University and the University of Minnesota (attested 2007).

nodes.label: Culadasa
nodes.summary: Culadasa was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar who studied under Joti Dhamma Bhikkhu. He served as director of the Dharma Treasure Buddhist Sangha (attested 2011).

nodes.label: Matthew Immergut
nodes.summary: Matthew Immergut is a religious studies scholar who studied under Culadasa. In 2011, he was attested as an Associate Professor of Sociology at the State University of New York at Purchase.

nodes.label: Sun-Ah Choi
nodes.summary: Sun-Ah Choi is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Chicago under doctoral supervisor Juhyung Rhi, also studying under Richard Neer, Robert S. Nelson, Jaś Elsner, and Aden Kumler.

nodes.label: Robert S. Nelson
nodes.summary: Robert S. Nelson is a historian and archaeologist who studied at Rice University (~1965–1969) and New York University (~1969–1978). He served as a professor at the University of Chicago (~1977–2005) and held a post at Yale University (~2005–2021).

nodes.label: Jaś Elsner
nodes.summary: Jaś Elsner works in the fields of religious studies and history and archaeology. He has held academic posts at the University of Michigan and the University of Chicago (~2013), and he taught Sun-Ah Choi.

nodes.label: Richard Wilhelm
nodes.summary: Richard Wilhelm was a Sinologist who studied at Eberhard-Ludwigs-Gymnasium. He held posts at Peking University (~1922–1924) and Goethe University Frankfurt (~1924–1930).

nodes.label: David L. Gosling
nodes.summary: David L. Gosling is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He held a Spalding Fellowship at Clare Hall, Cambridge in 1992 and held an attested post at the University of Cambridge in 2001.

nodes.label: Jean-Luc Achard

nodes.label: Ramin Etesami
nodes.summary: Ramin Etesami is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed an MA at the International Buddhist College (attested 2015) under the supervision of Lobsang Jamspal and Krishna Ghosh Della Santina.

nodes.label: Benjamin Brose
nodes.description: American cultural historian of religion in China
nodes.summary: Benjamin Brose is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his Ph.D. at Stanford University (~2003–2009) under Carl Bielefeldt and Bernard Faure, becoming an assistant professor of Chinese Buddhism at the University of Michigan around 2011.

nodes.label: Erik J. Hammerstrom
nodes.summary: Erik J. Hammerstrom specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned a PhD from Indiana University and served as assistant professor of religion at Pacific Lutheran University (attested 2016).

nodes.label: Michelle C. Wang
nodes.summary: Michelle C. Wang works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. She studied under Eugene Y. Wang (~2003–2008) and became an assistant professor in the Department of Art and Art History at Georgetown University circa 2012.

nodes.label: Tak Pui Sze
nodes.summary: Tak Pui Sze is a scholar of sinology and religious studies who earned a PhD at the University of British Columbia under the supervision of Jinhua Chen.

nodes.label: Mungunchimeg Batmunkh
nodes.summary: Mungunchimeg Batmunkh is a scholar of religious studies and Tibetology. Batmunkh earned a Dr.phil. at the University of Vienna (attested 2010), studying under doctoral supervisor Brigitte Marschall.

nodes.label: Brigitte Marschall
nodes.summary: Brigitte Marschall studied at the University of Vienna (~1976–1983). She later served as Professorin at the University of Vienna (~2000–2022).

nodes.label: Guo Jun
nodes.summary: Guo Jun is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Fuyan Buddhist Institute, Monash University, and the University of Sydney, training under Sheng Yen, Song Nian, and Qinyin. He served as abbot at Mahabodhi Monastery, attested in 2013.

nodes.label: George Lakoff
nodes.summary: George Lakoff is a scholar in linguistics and philosophy. He studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (~1958–1962) and Indiana University (~1962–1966), and later held a post at the University of California, Berkeley (~1972–2016).

nodes.label: Alexander Berzin
nodes.summary: Alexander Berzin is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Rutgers, Princeton, and Harvard University, and trained under traditional teachers including Tsenshab Serkong Rinpoche, Ling Rinpoche, and Dudjom Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Akira Takeda
nodes.summary: Akira Takeda was a Sinologist who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1949–1956). His career included posts at Tokyo Woman's Christian University (~1965–1979), the University of Tokyo as professor (~1979–1991), and Meikai University (~1991–2001).

nodes.label: Charlene Elizabeth Makley
nodes.summary: Charlene Elizabeth Makley specializes in tibetology and anthropology. She earned her PhD from the University of Michigan (completed 1999) under Norma Diamond and Roy Rappaport, and she became an associate professor of anthropology at Reed College.

nodes.label: Roy Rappaport
nodes.summary: Roy Rappaport was a scholar of religious studies who studied at Columbia University from circa 1959 to 1966. He held a faculty post at the University of Michigan from circa 1965 until 1997.

nodes.label: Marco Walther
nodes.summary: Marco Walther is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich under doctoral supervisor Franz-Karl Ehrhard (attested 2017). He also studied under Khenpo Dondrub Namgyal.

nodes.label: Jamie Hubbard
nodes.summary: Jamie Hubbard works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Komazawa University under Kazuo Okabe and earned a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Minoru Kiyota. He held a professorship at Smith College (attested 2016).

nodes.description: Indian epigraphist, archaeologist and art historian

nodes.label: John Woodroffe
nodes.summary: Woodroffe was an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at University College, Oxford (~1884–1888). He served as a judge at the Calcutta High Court (~1904–1922) and Reader in Indian Law at the University of Oxford (~1923–1930).

nodes.label: Eishoji
variants: Eishoji Zen training and practice facility

nodes.label: Bintao Ma
nodes.summary: Bintao Ma is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. Ma completed an MA at Peking University in 2008 and a PhD at The Chinese University of Hong Kong under Xueyu, attested in 2015.

nodes.label: Cécile Ducher
nodes.summary: Cécile Ducher specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Matthew T. Kapstein (-2017) and later served there as a research fellow.

nodes.label: Nicholas J. Allen
nodes.summary: Nicholas J. Allen was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at Rugby School and the University of Oxford (~1969-1976). He held posts at SOAS (1969-1971), Durham University (1972-1976), Wolfson College, Oxford (~1976-2006), and the University of Oxford (~1976-2001).

nodes.label: Michel Clasquin
nodes.description: Professor of Religious Studies at the University of South Africa
nodes.summary: Michel Clasquin (born 1960) works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at the University of South Africa, where he completed degrees in 1991, 1993, and a doctoral thesis in 1999, and held a post there in 1990.

nodes.label: Chi-wah Chan
nodes.summary: Chi-wah Chan specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned a PhD from UCLA in 1993, studying under Robert E. Buswell Jr. and Benjamin A. Elman, and worked as a teaching assistant at The Chinese University of Hong Kong.

nodes.label: Barend Jan Terwiel
nodes.summary: Barend Jan Terwiel works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He held posts at Leiden University, Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1990-1992), and the University of Hamburg (~1992-2007) as Professor Dr.

nodes.label: Patrice Ladwig
nodes.summary: Patrice Ladwig works in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Münster, University of Edinburgh, and EHESS, and held positions at the University of Bristol and the Max Planck Institute for Social Anthropology (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Ingmar Heise
nodes.summary: Ingmar Heise focuses on Sinology and Buddhist studies. Heise earned an MA in Chinese Studies from Leiden University by 2005 and was attested as a PhD candidate at the University of Bristol in 2012.

nodes.label: Peter D. Hershock
nodes.summary: Peter D. Hershock works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at Yale University and with traditional teachers Seungsahn and Ji Kwang Dae Poep Sa Nim, later serving as Director of the Asian Studies Development Program at the East-West Center (attested 2007–2013).

nodes.label: Stephen J. Laumakis
nodes.summary: Stephen J. Laumakis is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied under John Kronen, Ramdas Lamb, and George J. Tanabe, Jr., and serves as a professor of philosophy at the University of St. Thomas.

Christopher Ives
nodes.summary: Christopher Ives is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He was an assistant professor of religion at the University of Puget Sound from circa 1987 to 2001 and became professor and chair of religious studies at Stonehill College circa 2001.

nodes.label: Sharon J. Roe
nodes.summary: Sharon J. Roe is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who earned a PhD at the California Institute of Integral Studies under the supervision of Steven D. Goodman (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Shin'ichi Yoshinaga
nodes.summary: Shin'ichi Yoshinaga (1957–2022) specialized in religious and Buddhist studies, studying at Kyoto University from around 1976 to 1985. He held an academic post at the National Institute of Technology, Maizuru College, from around 1988 to 2018.

nodes.label: National Institute of Technology, Maizuru College
Yozo Taniyama
nodes.summary: Yozo Taniyama (born 1972) specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tohoku University (~1991–1996) and held positions at St. Thomas University, Japan (~2005–2008), Shitennoji University (~2008–2012), Tohoku University (~2012), and Sophia University (~2014).

nodes.label: Dickwela Piyananda
nodes.summary: Dickwela Piyananda is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at the Catholic University of America under the doctoral supervision of Siegfried A. Schulz.

nodes.label: Christian Bernert
nodes.summary: Christian Bernert specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the International Buddhist Academy and the University of Vienna, earning a Magister under supervisor Klaus-Dieter Mathes, alongside teachers Junjie Chu, Karin Preisendanz, and Gerald Hödl.

nodes.label: Hugh J. Silverman
nodes.summary: Hugh J. Silverman was a philosopher who studied at Stanford University (~1969–1973). He held academic posts at the University of Vienna, the University of Klagenfurt, and the University of Turin.

nodes.label: Lang Chen
nodes.summary: Lang Chen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned a PhD at Yale University (attested 2015), where she was supervised by Koichi Shinohara and Phyllis Granoff, and studied under Janet Gyatso.

nodes.label: Matthew B. Orsborn
nodes.summary: Matthew B. Orsborn is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under doctoral supervisors Guang Xing and Y. Karunadasa, alongside traditional teachers Hsing Yun and Huishang (all attested 2012).

nodes.label: Richard Barron
nodes.summary: Richard Barron is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Kalu Rinpoche, Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima, and the 3rd Jamgön Kongtrul.

nodes.label: Sogyal Rinpoche
nodes.description: Tibetan Dzogchen lama of the Nyingma tradition
nodes.summary: Sogyal Rinpoche was active in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Delhi and the University of Cambridge, as well as under traditional teachers Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje, and founded Rigpa (1975).

nodes.label: Pham Thi Tuyet Tam
nodes.summary: Pham Thi Tuyet Tam is a scholar of Buddhist studies. She completed her MA at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University under the supervision of Phra Maha Somboon Vuddhikaro and Sanu Mahatthanadull.

nodes.label: Lara Braitstein
nodes.summary: Lara Braitstein is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD at McGill University under Richard P. Hayes and later taught Alnis Dickson.

nodes.label: David Kinsley
nodes.summary: David Kinsley was a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied at Drew University (~1957–1961), Union Theological Seminary (~1961–1964), and the University of Chicago (~1964–1970), and held a post at McMaster University from 1969 to 2000.

nodes.label: Liang Cai
nodes.summary: Liang Cai works in sinology and history/archaeology. She studied under Daniel Boucher and held an appointment as a junior scholar at the University of Arkansas (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Kenneth Doo Young Lee
nodes.summary: Kenneth Doo Young Lee specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Columbia University under doctoral supervisor Ryuichi Abe and held an attested post at Stetson University in 2007.

nodes.label: David Phillip Stanley
nodes.summary: David Phillip Stanley is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins and David Germano, and has held posts at Naropa University and the Nitartha Institute (attested 2019).

nodes.label: Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Karma Shri Nalanda Institute, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and Columbia University. He founded and directed the Nitartha Institute (~1996) and directed the Kamalashila Institute (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Lorne Ladner
nodes.summary: Working in Buddhist studies and other fields, Lorne Ladner studied under traditional teacher Thubten Zopa Rinpoche (attested 2004). He served as an adjunct faculty member in the counseling program at Argosy University (attested 2004).

nodes.label: W. F. Jayasuriya
nodes.summary: W. F. Jayasuriya was a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under Rerukane Ariyaratne (attested 1963), H. D. Dharmasiriwardhana, and M. U. Sri Kaveeswara.

nodes.label: Victoria Sujata
nodes.summary: Victoria Sujata is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at Harvard University, where she studied under Michael Aris.

nodes.label: Beata Grant
nodes.summary: Beata Grant is a scholar of sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. After earning her Ph.D. at Stanford (~1980-1987) and a fellowship at UC Berkeley (~1987-1988), she was Associate Professor of Chinese Language and Literature at Washington University in St. Louis (~1989-2021).

nodes.label: Weiru Guan
nodes.summary: Weiru Guan is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Yongdong Shi (attested 2011).

nodes.label: Edo Shonin
nodes.summary: Edo Shonin works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. Attested in 2015, he held posts as a research psychologist at Nottingham Trent University and Research Director at the Awake to Wisdom Centre for Meditation and Mindfulness Research.

nodes.label: William Van Gordon
nodes.summary: William Van Gordon is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. Attested in 2015, he was a research psychologist at Nottingham Trent University and founded the Awake to Wisdom Centre for Meditation and Mindfulness Research.

nodes.label: Mark D. Griffiths
nodes.summary: Mark D. Griffiths studied at the University of Exeter from 1987 to 1990. He held posts at the University of Plymouth (1990-1995) and Nottingham Trent University, where he became Professor of Gambling Studies around 1995.

nodes.label: Charles Gabriel Seligman
nodes.summary: Charles Gabriel Seligman studied at St Thomas' Hospital (circa 1892–1896) and worked in Indology and other fields. He taught Bronislaw Malinowski and held a post at the University of London circa 1910–1934.

nodes.label: James C. Dobbins
nodes.summary: James C. Dobbins works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD from Yale University by 1984 and held the position of Fairchild Professor of Religion and East Asian Studies at Oberlin College (attested 2015–2019).

nodes.label: Francis H. Cook
nodes.summary: Francis H. Cook is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison. He served as professor (~1970–1989) and emeritus professor (~1989) at UC Riverside, and chaired the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research in 1999.

nodes.label: Taitetsu Unno
nodes.summary: Taitetsu Unno worked in Buddhist and religious studies after studying at UC Berkeley (~1947-1951) and the University of Tokyo (~1951-1968). He subsequently served as professor at Smith College (~1971-2007).

nodes.label: Joshua W. C. Cutler
nodes.summary: Joshua W. C. Cutler specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under the traditional teacher Geshe Wangyal and held a post at the Tibetan Buddhist Learning Center, attested in 2004.

nodes.label: Anna Sawerthal
nodes.summary: Anna Sawerthal specializes in Tibetology. She completed an MA at the University of Vienna under Klaus-Dieter Mathes and Johanna Buß, and a PhD at Heidelberg University under Birgit Kellner and Roland Wenzlhuemer. She also studied with Dawa Tsering and Norbu Tashi.

nodes.label: Lauran Hartley
nodes.summary: Lauran Hartley is a Tibetologist who served as a visiting assistant professor at Indiana University, an adjunct lecturer at Columbia University, a teacher at Rutgers University (attested 2003), and a consultant and editor at Latse Contemporary Tibetan Cultural Library (attested 2003).

nodes.label: Ann Appleby Hazlewood
nodes.summary: Ann Appleby Hazlewood is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed a Master of Arts at the Australian National University (attested 1983), where she studied under supervisors Tissa Rajapatirana and Luise Hercus.

nodes.label: Nika Jovic
nodes.summary: Nika Jovic works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Géza Bethlenfalvy (2007-2008) and earned her Magistra der Philosophie at the University of Vienna under MA supervisor Klaus-Dieter Mathes (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Conor Roddy
nodes.summary: Conor Roddy is a philosophy scholar who completed a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Texas at Austin (attested 2011) and studied under Arindam Chakrabarti and Roger T. Ames.

nodes.label: John W. Pettit
nodes.summary: Working in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Pettit completed undergraduate studies at Haverford College and pursued doctoral studies under Robert A. F. Thurman. He also studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche (1985–1990) and Ashok Gangadean.

nodes.label: Lal Mani Joshi
nodes.summary: Lal Mani Joshi (1935–1984) studied at Allahabad, BHU, and Gorakhpur under Govind Chandra Pande. A scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and religion, he taught at Haverford College (~1983–1984) and mentored John W. Pettit and Nawang Tsering Shakspo.

nodes.label: Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa
nodes.summary: Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa (1926–2008) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Dudjom Rinpoche, Trijang Rinpoche, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and taught John W. Pettit.

nodes.label: New College of Florida
variants: New College of the University of South Florida

nodes.label: Rongdao Lai
nodes.summary: Rongdao Lai specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD at McGill University (attested 2013) under supervisors G. Victor Sōgen Hori and Robin D. S. Yates, and was a visiting fellow at the Center for Chinese Studies.

nodes.label: Zhenhua
nodes.summary: Zhenhua was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Tianning Buddhist College (1947) and under Yin Shun (1952). He later served as manager at Fuyan Buddhist Institute (attested 1992).

nodes.label: Robert Aitken
nodes.summary: Robert Aitken was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar. He studied under Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki, at the University of Hawaii, UC Berkeley, and Ryutaku-ji, and later held a post at the University of Hawaii.

nodes.label: Bruno Dagens
nodes.summary: Bruno Dagens was an Indology and archaeology scholar who studied under Colette Caillat. He served as a professor at KU Leuven (~1977–1986).

nodes.label: Constance Powell Chin
nodes.summary: Constance Powell Chin specializes in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. She completed a Master's degree at San Jose State University in 2012 under John W. Bernhardt, and also studied under Christian Luczanits.

nodes.label: Michael G. Morony
nodes.summary: Michael G. Morony is a scholar of history, archaeology, and religious studies. He studied at UC Berkeley (~1957–1961) and UCLA (~1961–1972), where he later served as professor from ~1974 to 2015.

nodes.label: Benjamin Wood
nodes.summary: Benjamin Wood specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. He completed his Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Toronto under Frances Garrett, having also studied under Shayne Clarke, Thupten Champa, and Khenpo Kunga Sherab.

nodes.label: Peipei Qiu
nodes.summary: Peipei Qiu is a scholar in Japanology and Sinology. She studied at Peking University and Columbia University, where she was taught by Paul Rouzer, and held an academic post at Vassar College (attested 2005).

nodes.label: Kathleen M. Erndl
nodes.summary: Kathleen M. Erndl was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. She held posts at DePauw University, University of Wisconsin-Madison, Lewis & Clark College (~1988–1993), and Florida State University as Associate Professor of Religion (~1993–2017), where she taught Cameron Bailey and Lindsay G. McCune.

nodes.label: D. Dennis Hudson
nodes.summary: D. Dennis Hudson was a scholar in Indology and religious studies. He taught in the Department of Religion and served as Professor in the Department of Religion and Biblical Studies at Smith College (~1970–2004).

nodes.label: Dominique-Sila Khan
nodes.summary: Dominique-Sila Khan was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at Paris-Sorbonne University. She served as a research fellow at the Institute of Rajasthan Studies, attested in 2000.

nodes.label: June McDaniel
nodes.summary: June McDaniel is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who earned an MTS at Emory University and a PhD at the University of Chicago. She served as Professor of the History of Religions at the College of Charleston (attested 2000, 2015).

nodes.label: Yu-Chen Tsui
nodes.summary: Yu-Chen Tsui works in Buddhist studies. Tsui completed master's study at Columbia University under Chun-fang Yu, undertook doctoral work under Natasha Heller and Robert E. Buswell Jr., and also studied under Sheng Yen.

nodes.label: Dermott Joseph Walsh
nodes.summary: Dermott Joseph Walsh specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned his BA at Trinity College Dublin in 2003, an MA at Leiden University in 2009, and a PhD in 2018 from UCLA under doctoral supervisor William M. Bodiford.

nodes.label: C. D. Sebastian
nodes.summary: C. D. Sebastian specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his PhD at Banaras Hindu University, studied under Abhimanyu Singh, Ashok Kumar Chatterjee, Paul Williams, and Gavin D'Costa, and was Professor of Indian Philosophy at IIT Bombay (attested 2016).

nodes.label: Gavin D'Costa
nodes.summary: Gavin D'Costa (born 1958) is a religious studies scholar. He attended Bedford Modern School and studied at the University of Birmingham (~1977–1984). In ~2003, he served as Professor in Catholic Theology at the University of Bristol.

nodes.label: Dennis A. Johnson
nodes.summary: Dennis A. Johnson is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Vienna, earning his Magister der Philosophie under supervisor Klaus-Dieter Mathes (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Hiroko Kawanami
nodes.summary: Hiroko Kawanami works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She studied under John Okell and Anna Allott, and served as a senior lecturer at Lancaster University (attested 2013–2016).

nodes.label: Alfred Gell
nodes.summary: Alfred Gell (1945–1997) studied at the London School of Economics and Political Science from around 1968 to 1971. He later held a post there from circa 1979 until 1997.

nodes.label: John Okell
nodes.summary: John Okell was a linguist who studied at The Queen's College from circa 1953 to 1957. He subsequently held an academic post at SOAS University of London from circa 1965 to 1999.

nodes.label: Sunhee Kim
nodes.summary: Sunhee Kim completed a Doctor of Philosophy in Performance Practice at the University of Exeter under the supervision of Phillip B. Zarrilli.

nodes.label: Phillip B. Zarrilli
nodes.summary: Phillip B. Zarrilli was a scholar of Indology and related fields. He held academic posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from approximately 1979 to 1998 and at the University of Exeter from approximately 1998 to 2020.

nodes.label: Nancy McCagney
nodes.summary: Nancy McCagney is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She studied under teachers including Chögyam Trungpa, Ninian Smart, and Gerald James Larson, and held an academic post at the University of Delaware (attested 1997).

nodes.label: Jeong-Eun Kim
nodes.summary: Jeong-Eun Kim is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Kim earned a PhD from SOAS University of London (to 2011), studying under doctoral supervisor Youngsook Pak and teacher Rosemary Smith.

nodes.label: Giovanni Verardi
nodes.summary: Giovanni Verardi (born 1947) is an Italian scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Allahabad, Banaras Hindu University, and Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University, and held a post at Kyoto University.

nodes.label: Vajragupta
nodes.summary: Vajragupta (born 1968) works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He served as director at the Birmingham Buddhist Centre (1997) and held a directorship within the Triratna Buddhist Community (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Hiroshi Aoyagi
nodes.summary: Hiroshi Aoyagi works in Japanology and related fields. He studied at International Christian University (~1977–1982) and held a post at Nanzan University (~2003).

nodes.label: Antonio Terrone
nodes.summary: Antonio Terrone is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Leiden University under Tilmann Vetter and Barend ter Haar in 2010, and served as scholar in residence at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center.

nodes.label: Bhuvan Chandel

nodes.label: Tulku Sherdor
nodes.summary: Tulku Sherdor is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Vassar College, Naropa University, and the University of Virginia, under teachers including Ted Norton, Jeffrey Hopkins, and Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Sharon Salzberg
nodes.summary: Sharon Salzberg is a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar. She studied at the University at Buffalo from circa 1969 to 1971 and under traditional teacher Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche circa 1971.

nodes.label: Yuko Matsuda

nodes.label: Natalie Gummer
nodes.summary: Natalie Gummer is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She held a post at Harvard University attested in 2001 and became professor of religious studies at Beloit College in 2001.

nodes.label: Wolfram Eberhard
nodes.summary: Wolfram Eberhard studied at the Humboldt University of Berlin (~1927–1933) and worked in sinology, history, and archaeology. He held posts at Ankara University (~1937–1948) and served as a professor at the University of California, Berkeley (~1948–1976).

nodes.label: Barbara Gerke
nodes.summary: Barbara Gerke is a tibetologist who earned her D.Phil. at Oxford under Charles Ramble and Geoffrey Samuel. She held posts at Humboldt University of Berlin (2011-2015), Oxford (attested 2017), and the Centre for the Study of Developing Societies.

nodes.label: Yi-hsun Huang
nodes.summary: Yi-hsun Huang specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She completed her PhD at the University of Virginia under the supervision of Paul Groner and has taught Huidi Zeng.

nodes.label: Prayoon Mererk

nodes.summary: Prayoon Mererk works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his doctoral thesis at the University of Delhi by 1985, studying under doctoral supervisors Margaret Chatterjee and Mahesh Tiwary.

nodes.label: David Azzopardi
nodes.summary: David Azzopardi is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at SOAS University of London under the supervision of Kate Crosby (attested 2010).

nodes.label: János Szerb

nodes.label: Kurt Tropper
nodes.summary: Kurt Tropper specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his doctorate at the University of Vienna under Ernst Steinkellner, Michael Torsten Much, and Tashi Geisler, later holding posts at the University of Vienna and the Austrian Academy of Sciences.

nodes.label: Ñāṇavīra Thera
nodes.summary: Ñāṇavīra Thera was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. Educated at Wellington College, St Edmund's School, and Magdalene College, he served in the Royal Artillery (1939–1941) and Intelligence Corps (1941–1945), later studying under Pelene Siri Vajirañāṇa (~1949–1955).
