nodes.label: Louis Komjathy
nodes.summary: Louis Komjathy specializes in religious studies and sinology. He earned his PhD at Boston University (~2000–2005) under Paul Rouzer and served as Assistant Professor of Chinese Religions and Comparative Religious Studies at the University of San Diego (~2008).

nodes.label: Heng Sure
nodes.summary: Heng Sure is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Oakland University, UC Berkeley, and the Graduate Theological Union, where he earned a PhD under supervisors Ronald Y. Nakasone and Edmond Yee, and also studied under Hsuan Hua.

nodes.label: Edmond Yee
nodes.summary: Edmond Yee is a scholar of religious studies and Sinology. He served on the faculty at both Pacific Lutheran Theological Seminary and the Graduate Theological Union (~1990–2008).

nodes.label: Hsuan Hua
nodes.summary: Hsuan Hua (1918–1995) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Hsu Yun in 1948. He founded Dharma Realm Buddhist University, the Buddhist Text Translation Society, and the Institute for World Religions, and was Abbot of the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas (~1976–1995).

nodes.label: Phramaha Niras Ruangsan
nodes.native: นิราศ เรืองแสน
nodes.summary: Phramaha Niras Ruangsan is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Sydney, supervised by Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle, Peter Oldmeadow, Mark Allon, and Prayong Seanburan.

nodes.label: Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle
nodes.summary: Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He completed his doctoral studies under Roderick S. Bucknell (attested 1994) and held a post at the University of Sydney.

nodes.label: Chien-hsing Ho
nodes.summary: Chien-hsing Ho works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He held a post as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Nanhua University (attested 2014) and later held a post at Academia Sinica (attested 2018).

nodes.label: Charles B. Jones
nodes.summary: Charles B. Jones works in buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Virginia under Paul Groner in 1996, later becoming an associate professor and associate dean at the Catholic University of America (attested 2016–2019).

nodes.label: Hürelbaatar Ujeed
nodes.summary: Hürelbaatar Ujeed works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned a Ph.D. from the University of Cambridge, was affiliated there in 2010, and serves as Professor at Inner Mongolia University for Nationalities.

nodes.id: I:Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology
nodes.label: Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology
variants: Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology, Chinese Academy of Sciences

nodes.label: Ralph Abraham
nodes.summary: Ralph Abraham (1936–2024) worked in philosophy and other fields, studying at the University of Michigan and under Debabrata SenSharma. He held posts at UC Berkeley (~1960–1962), Columbia University (~1962–1964), and UC Santa Cruz (attested 2009).

nodes.label: Sisir Roy
nodes.summary: Sisir Roy specializes in philosophy. He studied under Debabrata SenSharma and held a professorship at the Indian Statistical Institute (attested 2009) as well as a post at the National Institute of Advanced Studies (attested 2009).

nodes.label: Ajahn Brahm
nodes.summary: Ajahn Brahm is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Cambridge, including Emmanuel College (~1969–1972), and trained under Boonman Poonyathiro (~1970–1974).

nodes.label: Terese Tse Bartholomew
nodes.summary: Terese Tse Bartholomew specializes in history, archaeology, Tibetology, and sinology. She earned an M.A. from the University of California, Los Angeles, and served as Curator of Himalayan Art and Chinese Decorative Art at the Asian Art Museum of San Francisco (attested 2001–2003).

nodes.id: I:International Association of Shin Buddhist Studies
nodes.label: International Association of Shin Buddhist Studies
variants: International Association of Shin Buddhist Studies

nodes.label: Ryan Anningson
nodes.summary: Ryan Anningson specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at Acadia University and earned his PhD at Wilfrid Laurier University under the doctoral supervision of Jason Neelis (attested 2017).

nodes.id: I:Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences
nodes.label: Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences
variants: Royal Dutch Academy of Arts and Sciences

nodes.label: Amy Heller
nodes.summary: Amy Heller is a Tibetologist and historian-archaeologist. She studied at Barnard College, INALCO, and the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Ariane Macdonald. She was a visiting instructor at Yale (1982) and is attested at the CNRS in 2005.

nodes.label: Mireille Helffer
nodes.summary: Mireille Helffer was a tibetologist who held posts at the Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique as Chargé de Recherche (~1961–1993) and at Paris Nanterre University (~1967–1989).

nodes.label: Nawang Tsering Shakspo
nodes.summary: Nawang Tsering Shakspo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under doctoral supervisor Lal Mani Joshi. In 1985, he is attested as a lecturer at the Central Institute of Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Chien Y. Hsu
nodes.summary: Chien Y. Hsu specializes in Buddhist studies. Hsu studied under doctoral supervisors Leslie S. Kawamura (through 2011) and James B. Apple (attested 2013), as well as traditional teacher Zhenhua (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Joseph D. Markowski
nodes.summary: Joseph D. Markowski is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned a Master of Arts at McGill University under G. Victor Sōgen Hori, attested in 2004.

nodes.label: E. W. Adikaram
nodes.summary: E. W. Adikaram worked in Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of London (attested 1946), where he studied under William Stede.

nodes.label: Arthur McKeown
nodes.summary: Arthur McKeown is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He pursued doctoral studies in Sanskrit and Indian Studies at Harvard University (attested 2005) under Diana L. Eck, Parimal G. Patil, and Palri Sangye.

nodes.label: Nathan W. Hill
nodes.summary: Nathan W. Hill is a Tibetologist and linguist who studied at Harvard under Leonard van der Kuijp and Jay Jasanoff. He served as reader at SOAS University of London and joined Trinity College Dublin in 2021.

nodes.label: Cameron David Warner
nodes.summary: Cameron David Warner is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. He studied under Yudru Tsomu, earned a PhD from Harvard University, and held academic posts at Middlebury College and Dickinson College.

nodes.label: Polly Young-Eisendrath
nodes.summary: Polly Young-Eisendrath is a scholar in Buddhist studies. She was educated at Ohio University (~1967–1969), Goddard College (~1969–1971), and Washington University in St. Louis (~1974–1980).

nodes.label: Akira Onda
nodes.summary: Akira Onda worked in Buddhist studies and other fields after studying at the University of Tokyo (~1948–1952). He served as a professor at Toyo University (~1962–1986) and held posts at Kawamura Gakuen Women's University (~1988–1995) and Tokyo.

nodes.label: Yasuo Deguchi
nodes.summary: Yasuo Deguchi (born 1962) specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University (~1981–1991) and held appointments at Nagoya Institute of Technology (~1996–2006) and Kyoto University, where he was Associate Professor of Philosophy (~2006–2016).

nodes.label: Constance E. Kassor
nodes.summary: Constance E. Kassor works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied at Smith College (BA) and Emory University (PhD, attested 2014) under John D. Dunne and Sara L. McClintock, later serving on the faculty at Smith College (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Karin Meyers
nodes.summary: Karin Meyers specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She studied under Jay L. Garfield and served as assistant professor and director of the Buddhist studies MA program at Kathmandu University's Centre for Buddhist Studies at Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

nodes.label: Eyal Aviv
nodes.summary: Eyal Aviv is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. He completed his PhD at Harvard University (attested 2008) under Robert M. Gimello and Parimal G. Patil, and held a post at George Washington University in 2014.

nodes.label: Annette Baier
nodes.summary: Annette Baier (1929–2012) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Otago from circa 1947 to 1953. Her career included an attested post at the University of Pittsburgh in 2008.

nodes.label: Wilfrid Sellars
nodes.jawiki: ウィルフリド・セラーズ
nodes.summary: Wilfrid Sellars was a philosopher who studied at Göttingen, Michigan, Buffalo, and Oriel College. He held posts at Iowa (1938–1946), Minnesota (1947–1958), Yale (1958–1963), Pittsburgh (1963–1989), and Humboldt University of Berlin.

nodes.label: Ines Konczak
nodes.summary: Ines Konczak specializes in Iranian and Central Asian studies, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She held posts as a postdoctoral research fellow at Staatliche Museen zu Berlin and as a visiting research fellow at Ryukoku University in 2012.

nodes.label: Dorji Wangchuk
nodes.summary: Dorji Wangchuk is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his MA and PhD at the University of Hamburg under David P. Jackson and Lambert Schmithausen, becoming a professor there around 2009.

nodes.label: Angela Falco Howard
nodes.summary: Angela Falco Howard works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. She completed her doctorate at New York University's Institute of Fine Arts under Alexander Coburn Soper and served as a professor at Rutgers University, attested in 2005.

nodes.label: Giuseppe Vignato
nodes.summary: Giuseppe Vignato is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He pursued doctoral studies at Peking University under Angela Falco Howard, Chongfeng Li, Su Bai, and Shichang Ma, and held a post there (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Su Bai
nodes.summary: Su Bai was a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. After studying at Peking University (~1940–1944), he served there as Professor and Professor Emeritus in the Archaeology Department (~1988–2018).

nodes.label: Shichang Ma
nodes.summary: Shichang Ma was a scholar of archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He worked as a Buddhist archaeology researcher at Dunhuang Academy (1963–1978) and held a post in the Archaeology Department at Peking University beginning in 1982.

nodes.label: Max Oidtmann
nodes.summary: Max Oidtmann is a historian of Tibet and China. He studied at Carleton College, Indiana University, and Harvard University under Mark C. Elliott (~2007–2014), later holding a post at Georgetown University (~2013).

nodes.label: Gustav Haloun
nodes.summary: Gustav Haloun (1898–1951) was a Sinologist who studied under August Conrady. He held positions at Charles University (around 1927–1931), directed at the University of Göttingen (around 1931–1938), and served as Professor of Chinese at the University of Cambridge (around 1938–1951).

nodes.label: Jotika Khur-Yearn
nodes.summary: Jotika Khur-Yearn is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He earned his PhD at SOAS University of London, studying under doctoral supervisor Kate Crosby (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Rangama Chandawimala
nodes.summary: Rangama Chandawimala is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under Jing Yin and Kakkapalliye Anuruddha, having also studied under traditional teacher Attaragama Gnanawimala.

nodes.label: Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee
variants: Government Civil Engineering College at Rúrkí

nodes.label: Michael S. Drummond
nodes.summary: Michael S. Drummond is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts in Buddhist Studies from the University of Bristol and pursued PhD candidacy at Utrecht University (attested 2006).

nodes.label: Guy Claxton
nodes.summary: Guy Claxton is a scholar in Buddhist studies and education who served as Professor of the Learning Sciences at the University of Bristol from around 1996 to 2008 and founded Sharpham College for Contemporary Buddhist Inquiry.

nodes.id: I:Sharpham College for Contemporary Buddhist Inquiry
nodes.label: Sharpham College for Contemporary Buddhist Inquiry
variants: Sharpham College for Contemporary Buddhist Inquiry

nodes.label: Andrew Olendzki
nodes.summary: Andrew Olendzki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Lancaster University. He served as executive director of the Insight Meditation Society, executive director and resident scholar at Barre Center for Buddhist Studies (attested 2003–2014), and senior scholar at Mind & Life Institute (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Insight Meditation Society
variants: Insight Meditation Society in Barre, Massachusetts

nodes.label: Fazun
nodes.summary: Fazun specialized in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studying at Wuchang Buddhist Institute, Tibetan School, and Drepung Monastery, and under Taixu. He founded the Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Institute and served at the Buddhist Academy of China as president (1956) and director (1980).

nodes.label: Tzungkuen Wen
nodes.summary: Tzungkuen Wen is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Queensland (-2009) under Primož Pecenko, Tamara Ditrich, and Chris Kang. He served as a lecturer at Fuyan Buddhist Institute in 2005.

nodes.label: Clara Sue Kidwell
nodes.description: Native American academic scholar, historian, feminist

nodes.label: Karen McCarthy Brown
nodes.summary: Karen McCarthy Brown (1942–2015) was a religious studies scholar who taught Johan Elverskog. She completed her studies at Smith College (circa 1960–1964), Union Theological Seminary (circa 1964–1966), and Temple University (circa 1970–1976).

nodes.label: Suwanda H. J. Sugunasiri
nodes.summary: Suwanda H. J. Sugunasiri is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Nalanda College. He held posts at the University of Toronto (~1986–2006) and Nalanda College of Buddhist Studies (attested 2001).

nodes.label: Christopher Hatchell
nodes.summary: Christopher Hatchell is a Tibetologist and religious studies scholar. He completed his PhD at the University of Virginia under the mentorship of David Germano and committee members Paul Groner, Karen C. Lang, Kurtis R. Schaeffer, and Robert A. Hueckstedt.

nodes.label: Jason Matthew McCombs
nodes.summary: Jason Matthew McCombs specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a BS from the University of Michigan and a PhD from UCLA under Gregory Schopen, subsequently serving as a lecturer at UCLA around 2014.

nodes.label: Lobsang Tenpa
nodes.summary: Lobsang Tenpa works in Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history and archaeology. He earned a Master of Philosophy at Jawaharlal Nehru University, where he studied under supervisor Sharad Kumar Soni.

nodes.label: Jigmeth Junu
nodes.summary: Jigmeth Junu is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at Fo Guang University (attested 2013) under supervisor Yongdong Shi, having also studied under traditional teacher Hui Xian.

nodes.label: Miri Albahari
nodes.summary: Miri Albahari works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. She earned an MA at the University of Otago and a PhD from the University of Calgary under John A. Baker (-2005), and held posts at the University of New South Wales and University of Western Australia (attested 2006).

nodes.label: University of New South Wales
variants: The University of New South Wales

nodes.label: Christian Haskett
nodes.summary: Christian Haskett is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned an MA advised by Robert A. F. Thurman and a PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 2010), later holding a post at Washington and Lee University (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Graeme MacQueen
nodes.summary: Graeme MacQueen (1948–2023) worked in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He completed his doctorate under Masatoshi Nagatomi at Harvard University (~1971–1979) and served as a lecturer at McMaster University (~1977–2013).

nodes.label: Linda Jean LaMacchia
nodes.summary: Linda Jean LaMacchia is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison under the supervision of David M. Knipe (attested 2001).

nodes.label: Michael Sheehy
nodes.summary: Michael Sheehy is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who earned his PhD from the California Institute of Integral Studies under Steven D. Goodman. He held posts at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center and the University of Virginia (attested 2019).

nodes.label: Qingying Chen
nodes.summary: Qingying Chen worked in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Qinghai Normal University, Qinghai University for Nationalities, and Minzu University of China, later holding posts at Southwest Minzu University, Minzu University, and China Tibetology Research Center (~1988–2012).

nodes.label: Anagarika Govinda
nodes.image: Lama Govinda in an internment camp during World War II.jpg
nodes.summary: Anagarika Govinda (1898–1985) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He held a doctorate from the University of Freiburg, studied under Tomo Geshe Rinpoche, lectured at Patna University, and served as Ācārya at Arya Maitreya Mandala (~1933–1985).

nodes.label: Adeu Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Adeu Rinpoche was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under traditional teachers including Khamtrul Rinpoche Dongyud Nyima, Samten Gyatso, and Chögon Rinpoche, and taught Tsoknyi Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Zen Mountain Monastery
variants: Zen Mountain Monastery at Mt. Tremper

nodes.label: Hegoda Khemananda
nodes.summary: Hegoda Khemananda is a Buddhist studies scholar. In 1993, he was attested as Vice Principal at Vidyodaya Pirivena and as Director at Dharma Paryeshanalaya.

nodes.label: Dewei Zhang
nodes.summary: Dewei Zhang specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of British Columbia under doctoral supervisor Jinhua Chen and committee member Leo K. Shin.

nodes.label: Paul Crowe
nodes.summary: Paul Crowe is a scholar of sinology and religious studies. He completed his graduate studies under Leslie S. Kawamura at the University of Calgary, and he is attested as a professor at Simon Fraser University in 2010.

nodes.label: King Pong Chiu
nodes.summary: King Pong Chiu specializes in Indology and religious studies. Chiu earned a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Manchester under the doctoral supervision of Jacqueline Suthren Hirst (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Thomé H. Fang
nodes.summary: Thomé H. Fang (1899–1977) specialized in philosophy, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He held academic posts at National Central University from circa 1929 to 1948 and at National Taiwan University from circa 1948 to 1973.

nodes.label: Ilkka Pyysiäinen
nodes.description: Finnish cognitive science of religion scholar
nodes.summary: Ilkka Pyysiäinen (born 1959) is a religious studies scholar. He earned his PhD at the University of Helsinki (~1983–1993) under René Gothóni, later working as an Academy Research Fellow there (1984) and visiting researcher at Oxford (~1996–1997).

nodes.label: Hiram W. Woodward
nodes.summary: Hiram W. Woodward works in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at Harvard College (~1958–1962) and Yale University (~1966–1975). He held positions at the University of Michigan (~1975–1982), the University of Vermont (~1982–1986), and the Walters Art Museum (~1986–2003).

nodes.label: Scott Dalby
nodes.summary: Scott Dalby works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam and served as a lecturer at Amsterdam University College (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Andrew B. Irvine
nodes.summary: Andrew B. Irvine works in philosophy and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Boston University and was an assistant professor of philosophy at Maryville College, attested in 2009.

nodes.label: Brooke Schedneck
nodes.summary: Brooke Schedneck is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Arizona State University under the supervision of Juliane Schober.

nodes.label: Jacques P. Leider
nodes.summary: Jacques P. Leider (born 1962) specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales (~1987–1998) and served as director at the École française d'Extrême-Orient in 2001.

nodes.label: Adrian Zenz
nodes.summary: Adrian Zenz is a scholar of Tibetology and Sinology. He studied at the University of Auckland and completed his PhD at the University of Cambridge under Hildegard Diemberger. He held posts at Columbia International University Korntal and the Victims of Communism Memorial Foundation.

nodes.label: Xiuzhi Zeng
nodes.summary: Xiuzhi Zeng works in Buddhist and religious studies. Attested in 2006, Zeng completed an MA at Nanhua University under the supervision of Meihua Chen.

nodes.label: Renda Zheng
nodes.summary: Renda Zheng (born 1944) works in Buddhist studies. Zheng studied under traditional teachers Kaizhi, Shengfa, and Kaitong.

nodes.label: Ramón Prats
nodes.summary: Ramón Prats is a Tibetologist who held positions at Himalayan and Inner Asian Resources (attested 1999) and Pompeu Fabra University (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Pompeu Fabra University
variants: Department of Humanities of the University Pompeu Fabra

nodes.label: Isabelle Henrion-Dourcy
nodes.summary: Isabelle Henrion-Dourcy specializes in Tibetology. She studied at Free University of Brussels, Harvard University, École Pratique des Hautes Études, and Tibet University, and taught anthropology at Laval University around 2004 and 2007.

nodes.label: Tibetan Arts Research Bureau
variants: Tibetan Arts Research Bureau (Bod ljongs sgyu rtsal zhib 'jug khang)

nodes.label: James Whitehill
nodes.summary: James Whitehill is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy who founded the Columbia Zen Center. He served as Professor of Religion at Stephens College (attested 2000).

nodes.label: David Bubna-Litic
nodes.summary: David Bubna-Litic works in Buddhist studies and other fields. He earned his PhD from Western Sydney University (attested 2000) and was a Lecturer in Strategic Management and Responsible Business at the University of Technology Sydney (attested 2000).

nodes.label: University of Technology Sydney
variants: School of Management in the University of Technology, Sydney

nodes.label: Susan Naquin
nodes.summary: Susan Naquin (born 1944) is a scholar of Sinology, history, and archaeology. She served as a professor at the University of Pennsylvania (~1976–1993) and held a post at Princeton University (~1993–2013).

nodes.label: Jiyu Ren
nodes.summary: Jiyu Ren (1916–2009) worked in religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Peking University (~1934–1938), he served as director of the Institute of World Religions at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, attested in 2000.

nodes.label: Xiaoling Wu
nodes.summary: Xiaoling Wu worked in sinology and Indology. He held positions at Visva-Bharati University (~1942–1946), Peking University, Academia Sinica (~1950–1977), and served as a professor at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1977–1995).

nodes.label: Marion L. Matics
nodes.summary: Marion L. Matics is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed doctoral studies under the supervision of Horace L. Friess and Royal W. Weiler, having also studied under Robert A. Fowkes.

nodes.label: Horace L. Friess
nodes.summary: Horace L. Friess (1900–1975) was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who studied at Columbia University (~1915–1926) and Heidelberg University. He held posts at Johns Hopkins University and Columbia University, where he was attested as professor in 1970.

nodes.label: Soto Zen Buddhism International Center
variants: Soto Zen Education Center of North America

nodes.label: Jeffrey Wayne Bass
nodes.summary: Jeffrey Wayne Bass works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at UNC Wilmington (BA), UT (MA), and UCLA (PhD) under Gregory Schopen, James L. Fitzgerald, and William M. Bodiford. He held teaching posts at UCLA and UC San Diego.

nodes.label: William Chu
nodes.summary: William Chu is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed an MA at the University of California, Los Angeles (-2006), where he studied under Robert E. Buswell Jr. and William M. Bodiford.

nodes.id: I:International Institute for Tibetan and Buddhist Studies
nodes.label: International Institute for Tibetan and Buddhist Studies
variants: International Institute for Tibetan and Buddhist Studies

nodes.label: Dhirendra Sharma
nodes.summary: Dhirendra Sharma was a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He studied under David Friedman and traditional teacher Surendra Sharma.

nodes.label: John R. B. Campbell
nodes.summary: John R. B. Campbell works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his PhD at Columbia University under doctoral supervisors Robert A. F. Thurman and Gary A. Tubb, having also studied under the 14th Dalai Lama and others.

nodes.label: H. V. Nagaraja Rao
nodes.summary: H. V. Nagaraja Rao is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He held posts at the Oriental Research Institute, Mysore, and as a professor at the University of Mysore (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Geshe Karma Sonam
nodes.summary: Geshe Karma Sonam is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He held posts at Gyume Tantric College (attested 1987) and Sera Monastery (attested 1992).

nodes.label: Lang Eun Ra
nodes.summary: Lang Eun Ra is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who pursued doctoral studies at Temple University under Charles Wei-hsun Fu, also studying with Bibhuti S. Yadav, Norbert M. Samuelson, and Leonard Swidler.

nodes.label: Norbert M. Samuelson
nodes.description: Scholar and professor of Jewish philosophy
nodes.summary: Norbert M. Samuelson was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Northwestern, Hebrew Union College, and Indiana University, and held a post at Arizona State University from circa 1998 to 2020.

nodes.label: Alan Gerard Wagner
nodes.summary: Alan Gerard Wagner specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He earned a PhD from Harvard University (attested 2008), where he was supervised by Parimal G. Patil and studied with Robert M. Gimello, Charles Hallisey, Carl Bielefeldt, and Masatoshi Nagatomi.

nodes.label: Iselin Frydenlund
nodes.summary: Iselin Frydenlund works in religious and Buddhist studies. In 2016, she was attested as a Research Fellow at the University of Oslo and as a senior researcher at the Peace Research Institute Oslo.

nodes.label: Martin Lehnert
nodes.summary: Martin Lehnert specializes in Sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Freiburg and was attested in 2016 as Professor of East Asian Religion and Philosophy at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich.

nodes.label: James Mark Shields
nodes.summary: James Mark Shields (b. 1971) works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. In 2016, he was attested as Associate Professor at Bucknell University and Overseas Collaborative Researcher at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies.

nodes.label: Foundation for Buddhist Studies Hamburg
variants: Foundation for Buddhist Studies in Hamburg

nodes.label: Kim Gutschow
nodes.summary: Kim Gutschow is a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies who completed a PhD at Harvard University. She served as a teacher at Wesleyan University.

nodes.label: Geshe Ngawang Nyima
nodes.summary: Geshe Ngawang Nyima (1907–1990) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He held a post at Leiden University in 1960 and served at Drepung Monastery, where he was Abbot of Drepung Gomang Monastery.

nodes.label: Kamaleswar Bhattacharya
nodes.summary: Kamaleswar Bhattacharya (1928–2014) was a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He held academic posts at Brown University, the University of Toronto, and the University of Bonn.

nodes.label: Jenkuan Shih
nodes.summary: Jenkuan Shih is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 2006). Shih studied under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Charles Hallisey, Mark Csikszentmihalyi, and Gudrun Bühnemann.

nodes.label: Mark Csikszentmihalyi
nodes.summary: Mark Csikszentmihalyi is a scholar of sinology, philosophy, and religious studies. He served as an associate professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from around 1994 to 2006 and became Professor of East Asian Languages and Cultures at UC Berkeley around 2006.

nodes.label: Giuliana Martini
nodes.summary: Giuliana Martini is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. In 2010, she held posts at both the Italian School of East Asian Studies and Kyoto University.

nodes.label: Keith Dowman
nodes.description: Dzogchen teacher, translator of Tibetan Buddhist texts
nodes.summary: Keith Dowman (born 1945) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers including Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje (~1969–1987), Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche (~1971–1991), Chatral Sangye Dorje Rinpoche, and Taklung Tsetrul Rinpoche.

nodes.label: David Ralph Quinter
nodes.summary: David Ralph Quinter is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Colorado Boulder, Tokyo, and Stanford (PhD under Carl Bielefeldt and Bernard Faure), later becoming an associate professor of East Asian religions at the University of Alberta (attested 2019).

nodes.label: Inter-University Center for Japanese Language Studies

Inter-University Center for Advanced Language Study

nodes.label: Kenji Matsuo
nodes.summary: Kenji Matsuo (born 1954) is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1974–1984) and held an academic post at Yamagata University (~1987–2020).

nodes.label: Sonja Arntzen
nodes.summary: Sonja Arntzen is a Japanology scholar who studied at the University of British Columbia (~1967–1979) under doctoral supervisor Leon Hurvitz. She also studied under Seizan Yanagida and Sojo Hirano.

nodes.label: Shūichi Katō
nodes.summary: Shūichi Katō (1919–2008), active in Japanology and philosophy, studied at the University of Tokyo (~1940–1943) and held posts there (~1943–1951), UBC (~1960–1969), Free University of Berlin (~1969–1973), Sophia University (~1973–1984), Yale (~1980–1981), and Ritsumeikan University (~1993–2008).

nodes.label: Qichao Liang
nodes.summary: Qichao Liang worked in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. He studied under Kang Youwei (~1890–1898) and at National Tsing Hua University, later holding a post at Tsinghua University (~1925–1929).

nodes.label: Cameron Bailey
nodes.summary: Cameron Bailey specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Indiana University, Florida State University, and the University of Oxford (Wolfson College), guided by advisors including Richard F. Nance, Bryan J. Cuevas, and doctoral supervisor Ulrike Roesler.

nodes.label: Lucia Galli
nodes.summary: Lucia Galli is a scholar in Tibetology who completed her doctorate at the University of Oxford and held a post there.

nodes.label: Rory Brendan Lindsay
nodes.summary: Rory Brendan Lindsay specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Toronto and completed his PhD at Harvard University under Leonard van der Kuijp alongside numerous other teachers.

nodes.label: Donald K. Swearer
nodes.summary: Donald K. Swearer is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He served at Swarthmore College (~1970–2004) and held posts at Harvard University as Distinguished Visiting Professor (2004–2010) and Distinguished Visiting Fellow (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Amanda K. Goodman
nodes.summary: Amanda K. Goodman is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology who earned her PhD from the University of California, Berkeley. Supervised by Robert H. Sharf, Luis Oscar Gómez, and Donald S. Lopez Jr., she holds a teaching position at the University of Toronto.

Hong Kong University of Science & Technology

nodes.label: Mamoru Tonami
nodes.summary: Mamoru Tonami was a scholar of Sinology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Kyoto University (~1955–1964). He held a post at Otani University from around 2000 to 2008 and taught Benjamin Brose.

nodes.label: Jeffery D. Long
nodes.summary: Jeffery D. Long is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who earned his Ph.D. from the University of Chicago (~1993–2000). He became an Associate Professor of Religion and Asian Studies at Elizabethtown College (~2000).

nodes.label: Angela Sumegi
nodes.summary: Angela Sumegi specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She earned her PhD from the University of Ottawa and served as an assistant professor in the College of the Humanities at Carleton University, attested in 2008.

nodes.label: Lucia Dolce
nodes.summary: Lucia Dolce works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She has held posts at SOAS University of London, including Lecturer in Japanese Religions (attested 2003–2007) and Associate Professor (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Grace S. Fong
nodes.summary: Grace S. Fong (born 1948) is a sinologist who studied at McGill University and the University of British Columbia (~1978–1984). She taught at Smith College (attested 1986) and McGill University (~1989), where she chaired the Department of East Asian Studies.

nodes.label: Ching-mei Shyu
nodes.summary: Ching-mei Shyu specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She earned an MA at the University of Hawaii under Jan Nattier and a PhD from Cornell University in 2008 under Daniel Boucher, Jane-Marie Law, and Hubert Durt.

nodes.label: Ellison Banks Findly
nodes.summary: Ellison Banks Findly is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. She studied under Fred Pfeil (attested 2000) and held posts at Mount Holyoke College and Trinity College (attested 1989).

nodes.label: Kazuo Okabe
nodes.summary: Kazuo Okabe (born 1935) specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Komazawa University (~1954–1963), where he later served as a professor (~1976–2005) and taught Jamie Hubbard.

nodes.label: Yudru Tsomu
nodes.summary: Yudru Tsomu specializes in Tibetology and history/archaeology. She completed a PhD at Harvard University under Leonard van der Kuijp, Mark C. Elliott, Janet Gyatso, and Philip A. Kuhn, and taught Cameron David Warner and Hoong Teik Toh.

nodes.label: Somdet Phra Nyanasamvara
nodes.native: สมเด็จพระญาณสังวร
nodes.jawiki: ワシラガーナサンバラ

nodes.label: Hanung Kim
nodes.summary: Hanung Kim specializes in Tibetology and history and archaeology. Kim earned a master's degree from Columbia University and a PhD from Harvard University under the doctoral supervision of Leonard van der Kuijp.

nodes.label: Ruth Gamble
nodes.summary: Ruth Gamble specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at the Australian National University (ending 2014) supervised by John Powers, Roger R. Jackson, and David Templeman. She held posts at ANU and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (attested 2016).

nodes.label: Petra Maurer
nodes.summary: Petra Maurer is a scholar of Tibetology and Indology who studied under Dieter Schuh and Dunchu Sonam Dorje. She held posts at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities, University of Erlangen-Nuremberg, and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich.

nodes.label: Cuilan Liu
nodes.summary: Cuilan Liu specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Sinology. She held an appointment as Assistant Professor of Buddhist Studies at the University of Toronto (attested 2017) and held a post at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (attested 2018).

nodes.label: Emanuela Garatti
nodes.summary: Emanuela Garatti is a Tibetologist who held positions at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (attested 2018).

nodes.label: Satya Narayan Goenka
nodes.image: The Kalyanmitra Satyanarayan Goenka who brought Vipassana Meditation technique to India after 2500 years is seen with his wife while speaking at a talk on "Values in Education - Good Governance through Vipassana Meditation" in.jpg
nodes.jawiki: サティア・ナラヤン・ゴエンカ

nodes.label: Phramonchai Saitanaporn
nodes.summary: Phramonchai Saitanaporn works in Buddhist studies. He pursued a PhD at the University of Sydney (attested 2009) supervised by Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle, with committee member Jeff Wilson, and also studied under traditional teacher Phrathepyanmahamuni.

nodes.label: Jeff Wilson
nodes.summary: Jeff Wilson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who earned his PhD from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill. He studied under mentor Taitetsu Unno and postdoctoral mentor Myōsei Tatsuguchi, and taught Phramonchai Saitanaporn.

nodes.label: Phrathepyanmahamuni
nodes.native: พระราชภาวนาวิสุทธิ์

nodes.label: Shuman Chen
nodes.summary: Shuman Chen works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Chen studied under traditional teacher Wei Chueh and completed a PhD at Northwestern University in 2014 under the supervision of Brook Ziporyn.

nodes.label: Brook Ziporyn
nodes.summary: Brook Ziporyn, a scholar of philosophy, Sinology, and Buddhist studies, earned his PhD at Michigan under Donald J. Munro and studied at Chicago. He held posts at Northwestern (~2003–2013), National University of Singapore (~2012–2013), and Chicago (~2013).

nodes.label: Sarah E. Fraser
nodes.summary: Sarah E. Fraser is a scholar of history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Michigan and Kobe University. She held appointments as an associate professor at Northwestern University (1996) and directrice d'études at EPHE (2000).

nodes.label: Anne Ruth Hansen
nodes.summary: Anne Ruth Hansen works in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied under Charles Hallisey and held a post at the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee, attested in 2007.

nodes.label: Thomas Nathan Patton
nodes.summary: Thomas Nathan Patton is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Cornell University, where he studied under Anne M. Blackburn, and held a post at the City University of Hong Kong (attested 2018).

nodes.label: Anne M. Blackburn
nodes.summary: Anne M. Blackburn is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and history and archaeology. She studied at the University of Chicago (circa 1990–1996) and became Assistant Professor of Religion at Cornell University circa 2001.

nodes.label: Hoseok Leigh
nodes.summary: Hoseok Leigh works in philosophy and religious studies. He studied under teacher Ha-u Kim and earned a Doctor of Philosophy from the California Institute of Integral Studies, attested in 2010.

nodes.label: Carol S. Anderson
nodes.summary: Carol S. Anderson specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Chicago, studying under W. S. Karunatillake and John A. Brinkman, and served as Associate Professor of Religion at Kalamazoo College.

nodes.label: John A. Brinkman
nodes.summary: John A. Brinkman is a historian and archaeologist who held posts at the University of Chicago and served as professor at the Institute for the Study of Ancient Cultures from circa 1963 to 2005.

nodes.id: I:Institute for the Study of Ancient Cultures
nodes.label: Institute for the Study of Ancient Cultures
variants: Oriental Institute of the University of Chicago

nodes.label: Catherine Bell
nodes.summary: Catherine Bell (1954–2008) worked in religious studies and sinology. She studied at the University of Chicago under Joseph Mitsuo Kitagawa (~1976–1983) and served as the Bernard J. Hanley Professor of Religious Studies at Santa Clara University (1985–2008).

nodes.label: Hsiang-Kuang Chou
nodes.summary: Hsiang-Kuang Chou was a sinology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Swami Sivananda. He held posts at Delhi, Allahabad (attested 1960), the Lal Bahadur Shastri National Academy (attested 1960), and was Chancellor of Yoga-Vedanta Forest Academy (attested 1960).

nodes.id: I:Lal Bahadur Shastri National Academy of Administration
nodes.label: Lal Bahadur Shastri National Academy of Administration
Kin Cheung
nodes.summary: Kin Cheung is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at Temple University under the doctoral supervision of Shigenori Nagatomo (attested 2017).

nodes.label: James Blumenthal
nodes.summary: James Blumenthal (1967–2014) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa and held faculty posts at Oregon State University and Maitripa College.

nodes.label: Beatrice Erskine Lane Suzuki
nodes.jawiki: ベアトリス・レイン・スズキ
nodes.summary: A scholar of Buddhist and religious studies, Beatrice Erskine Lane Suzuki studied at Radcliffe College (~1895–1898) under William James, Josiah Royce, and George Santayana. She also studied at Columbia University (~1901–1903).

nodes.label: Josiah Royce
nodes.summary: Josiah Royce (1855–1916) was a philosopher who studied at UC Berkeley (~1871–1875) and Johns Hopkins University (~1876–1878). He held academic posts at UC Berkeley (~1878–1882) and Harvard University (~1882–1916).

nodes.label: George Santayana
nodes.jawiki: ジョージ・サンタヤーナ
nodes.summary: George Santayana was a philosopher who studied at Harvard College, the Humboldt University of Berlin, and Harvard University, completing his doctorate under William James (~1886–1889). He held an academic post at Harvard University from ~1889 to 1912.

nodes.label: Geshe Losang Chödar
nodes.summary: Geshe Losang Chödar is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. In 2010, he held an attested position at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and served as a Tibetan editor at the Institute of Tibetan Classics.

nodes.label: Thinley Norbu Rinpoche
nodes.image: Thinley Norbu Rinpoche wearing a white shirt, red zen, pink curtain in background.jpg

nodes.label: Chagdud Tulku Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Chagdud Tulku Rinpoche (1930–2002) was a figure in buddhist studies and tibetology. He studied under Delog Dawa Drolma, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and Dudjom Rinpoche, and he taught Albion Moonlight Butters.

nodes.label: Daniel R. Tuzzeo
nodes.summary: Daniel R. Tuzzeo is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his thesis at Florida State University, where he studied under advisors Jimmy Yu, Bryan J. Cuevas, and Joseph Hellweg.

nodes.label: George A. Keyworth
nodes.summary: George A. Keyworth (1970–) specializes in Buddhist studies, sinology, and Japanology. He studied at UCSB and UCLA (PhD under Robert E. Buswell Jr.) and held posts at the University of Colorado Boulder and the University of Saskatchewan.

nodes.label: Ronald Egan
nodes.summary: Ronald Egan is a Sinologist who earned his Ph.D. at Harvard (~1971–1977). He held posts at Harvard (~1977–1986), Wellesley College (~1986–1993), UC Santa Barbara (~1993–2012), and Stanford University (~2012).

nodes.label: Pieter Cornelis Verhagen
nodes.summary: Pieter Cornelis Verhagen specializes in Tibetology, Indology, and linguistics. He completed his PhD in 1991 at Leiden University, where he later held a post as a research fellow (attested 1996).

nodes.label: Stephen H. West
nodes.summary: Stephen H. West is a sinologist who studied at National Taiwan Normal University and the University of Michigan (~1967–1972). He held professorships at the University of California, Berkeley (~1986–2004) and Arizona State University (~2004–2019).

nodes.label: Ulrike Roesler
nodes.summary: Ulrike Roesler earned her PhD at the University of Münster. A specialist in Tibetology and Indology, she taught at the universities of Marburg and Freiburg before serving as Professor of Tibetan and Himalayan Studies at Oxford.

nodes.label: Nalini Devdas
nodes.summary: Nalini Devdas works in religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. She earned her PhD at Concordia University under Leslie Orr, also studying under teachers including Paul David Devanandan and Steven Collins, and held a post at Carleton University (attested 2004).

nodes.label: Tsultrim Gyatso
nodes.summary: Tsultrim Gyatso is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He served as a senior instructor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and as Abbot of Drepung Gomang Dratsang (attested 1987).

nodes.label: Hozen Seki
nodes.summary: Hozen Seki (1903–1991) was a Buddhist studies figure who founded the American Buddhist Academy and served as resident minister at the New York Buddhist Church (attested 1998).

nodes.label: Andrei Ivanovich Vostrikov
nodes.summary: Andrei Ivanovich Vostrikov (1904–1937) was a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology who studied under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy (Theodore Stcherbatsky).

nodes.label: Boris Vladimirovich Semichov
nodes.summary: Boris Vladimirovich Semichov (1900–1981) worked in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied under Theodore Stcherbatsky (~1923–1928) and held a post at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts (~1928–1937).

nodes.label: Jørn Borup
nodes.summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies, Jørn Borup earned his PhD at Aarhus University (~1998–2002) under Armin W. Geertz and Ian Reader. He later served as an associate professor at Aarhus University (~2007–2023).

nodes.label: Ian Reader
nodes.summary: Ian Reader (born 1949) specializes in Japanology and religious studies. After earning his doctorate at the University of Leeds (~1979–1983), he held posts at Kobe University of Commerce, Stirling (~1989–1995), Hawaii (~1999–2000), and Lancaster (~2003–2008).

nodes.label: Michaela Haas
nodes.summary: Michaela Haas works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Bonn under the supervision of Peter Schwieger, and studied under Rechungpa and traditional teacher Jigme Namgyal.

nodes.label: Jigme Namgyal
variants: ‘Jigs med rNam rgyal ‘Dzi sgar Kong sprul

nodes.label: Andreas Doctor
nodes.summary: Andreas Doctor is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Calgary under Leslie S. Kawamura and studied under several traditional teachers, including Chokyi Nyima Rinpoche and Tsikey Chokling Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Phakchok Rinpoche
nodes.description: Vajra Master of Ka-Nying Shedrup Ling monastery

nodes.image: Ngodup Tsering, Geshe Lhakdor and Geshe Lobsang Monlam.jpg

nodes.label: Susan Niditch
nodes.summary: Susan Niditch (born 1950) is a religious studies scholar who spent her career at Amherst College, serving in the religion department from approximately 1978 to 2020.

nodes.label: Will Sweetman
nodes.description: professor of religion in New Zealand
nodes.summary: Will Sweetman is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Lancaster University and the University of Cambridge (~1988–1992) and held a post at the University of Otago (~2003).

nodes.label: Barry Sautman
nodes.summary: Barry Sautman works in sinology and tibetology. He studied at UCLA School of Law (~1971-1974), NYU School of Law (~1980-1981), and Columbia University (~1985-1990), later holding a post at Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (~1993-2020).

nodes.label: Craig Preston
nodes.summary: Craig Preston is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed studies at the University of Virginia under Joe Bransford Wilson and Jeffrey Hopkins (1980–1981).

nodes.label: Katherine Anne Paul
nodes.summary: Katherine Anne Paul works in Tibetology, history and archaeology, and Indology. She was supervised for her doctorate by Gudrun Bühnemann and was taught by Tsetan Chonjore, Pasang Dhondup, Nawang Dorji, Gautam V. Vajracharya, Rama Joshi, and Geeta Manandhar.

nodes.label: David Jones
nodes.summary: David Jones is a scholar in philosophy and religious studies who earned his Ph.D. from the University of Hawaii. Attested in 2007, he served as a professor of philosophy in the University System of Georgia and director of the Center for the Development of Asian Studies.

nodes.id: I:Center for the Development of Asian Studies
nodes.label: Center for the Development of Asian Studies
variants: Center for the Development of Asian Studies

nodes.label: Maxime Kaltenmark
nodes.summary: Maxime Kaltenmark (1910–2002) was a scholar in sinology and religious studies. He held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1956–1979) and the University of Paris (~1957–1979).

nodes.label: Léon Vandermeersch
nodes.summary: Léon Vandermeersch was a Sinologist and philosopher who studied at Paris Law Faculty, INALCO, EPHE, and Paris Diderot University. He held academic posts at the University of Provence (~1970–1973), Paris Diderot (~1973–1979), and EPHE (~1979–1993).

nodes.label: Wen-ling Jane
nodes.summary: Wen-ling Jane is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She completed a PhD at Columbia University under doctoral supervisor Robert A. F. Thurman and also studied under Lobsang Jamspal.

nodes.label: Roy Tzohar
nodes.summary: Roy Tzohar works in philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tel Aviv University and Columbia University (PhD, circa 2003–2011) under Gary A. Tubb, later joining the faculty at Tel Aviv University around 2011.

nodes.label: Kammie Takahashi
nodes.description: academic, college faculty, Associate Professor of Religion Studies
nodes.summary: Kammie Takahashi works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Mount Holyoke College and earned her PhD from the University of Virginia (circa 2001–2009) under David Germano and Paul Groner, later holding a post at Muhlenberg College in 2011.

nodes.label: Sabine Löhr
nodes.summary: Sabine Löhr, an Indology scholar, studied at the University of Freiburg and the University of Hamburg, completing doctoral work under Lambert Schmithausen. She also served as a Wissenschaftliche Hilfskraft at the University of Hamburg.

nodes.label: Graham Lock
nodes.summary: Graham Lock is a scholar in Buddhist studies and linguistics who studied under Hsuan Hua and Saddhaloka Bhikkhu.

nodes.label: Robert Barnett
nodes.summary: Robert Barnett is a scholar of Tibetology. He studied at the University of Cambridge from ~1972 to 1976 and served as a professor at Columbia University from ~1999 to 2018.

nodes.label: Halle O'Neal
nodes.summary: Halle O'Neal works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. She earned her PhD at the University of Kansas (~2005–2011) under the supervision of Sherry Fowler.

nodes.label: David W. Tien
nodes.summary: David W. Tien is a scholar of sinology and philosophy. He studied at McGill University, the University of Toronto, and the University of Michigan (attested 2009) under James Robson and Robert H. Sharf.

nodes.label: Jim Rheingans
nodes.summary: Jim Rheingans specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed an MA at the University of Hamburg and a PhD through the University of the West of England and Bath Spa University, supervised by David P. Jackson, Mahinda Deegalle, and Fiona Montgomery.

nodes.id: I:University of the West of England
nodes.label: University of the West of England
variants: University of the West of England, Bristol
University of the West of England

nodes.label: Stephen Suen
nodes.summary: Stephen Suen is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Hong Kong under the doctoral supervision of K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 2009).

nodes.label: Mark T. Unno
nodes.summary: Mark T. Unno, a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies, studied at Oberlin College (~1977-1981) and Stanford University (~1987-1994). He held posts at Brown University (~1994-1998) and the University of Oregon (~1998).

nodes.label: Ganzorig Davaa-Ochir
nodes.summary: Ganzorig Davaa-Ochir is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He pursued an M.Phil in Tibetan Studies at the University of Oslo under MA supervisor Hanna Havnevik and traditional teacher Lama Byambaa (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Agata Bareja-Starzyńska
nodes.summary: Agata Bareja-Starzyńska works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She conducted research at the University of Oslo (1993) and the University of Bonn (1995), and held a post at the University of Warsaw (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Moscow State University
variants: Moscow State University's Institute of Asian and African Studies
Institute of Asian and African Studies

nodes.label: Cameron Kyle Bender Foltz
nodes.summary: Cameron Kyle Bender Foltz is a scholar in religious studies and Tibetology. He completed an MA at Florida State University (attested 2018) under the supervision of Bryan J. Cuevas, with Joseph Hellweg serving on his committee.

nodes.label: Yu Yan Pang
nodes.summary: Yu Yan Pang specializes in Buddhist studies. Pang earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong, where doctoral supervisors were Jing Yin and Cecilia Chan, and studied under Eric Kvan.

nodes.label: Elisabeth Schüssler Fiorenza
nodes.summary: Elisabeth Schüssler Fiorenza is a religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Würzburg (~1958–1963) and University of Münster (~1967–1970). She held posts at the University of Notre Dame (~1970–1985) and Harvard University (~1988).

nodes.label: Ngawang Jorden
nodes.summary: Ngawang Jorden is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who taught Constance E. Kassor. He held posts at Sakya College and served as director of the International Buddhist Academy.

nodes.label: B. N. Mukherjee
nodes.description: Indian historian, numismatist, epigraphist and iconographist
nodes.summary: B. N. Mukherjee was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Calcutta (~1951–1956) and later held an academic post there from around 1975 to 1997.

nodes.label: Sulak Sivaraksa
nodes.summary: Sulak Sivaraksa is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who studied at the University of Wales, Lampeter (~1954–1957). He served as editor for the Social Science Association of Thailand and held council and editorial roles at the Siam Society.

nodes.label: Subhadradis Diskul
nodes.native: สุภัทรดิศ ดิศกุล
nodes.image: สุภัทรดิศ ดิศกุล.jpg
nodes.jawiki: スパトラディット・ディッサクン
nodes.summary: Subhadradis Diskul worked in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the École du Louvre (~1949–1953) and later served as President of the Siam Society (~1982–1986) and Chairman of The Jim Thompson Foundation (~1987–2003).

nodes.label: David Kerman Tomlinson
nodes.summary: David Kerman Tomlinson works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under Dan Arnold (attested 2019) and held a post at Smith College.

nodes.label: Sven Wittemann
nodes.summary: Sven Wittemann is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts degree at the International Buddhist College under the supervision of Kapila Abhayawansa (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Juichiro Tanabe
nodes.summary: Juichiro Tanabe works in religious studies. He studied at the University of Bradford from 2000 to 2001 and as a PhD candidate attested in 2010, and also studied under traditional teacher Richard Hunn.

nodes.label: Bong Seok Joo
nodes.summary: Bong Seok Joo works in Buddhist studies and sinology. Joo completed undergraduate studies at UC Berkeley, where teachers included Lewis Lancaster, and earned a PhD from Princeton University under doctoral supervisor Stephen F. Teiser and teacher Jacqueline I. Stone.

nodes.label: Jeffrey Stout
nodes.summary: Jeffrey Stout is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Brown University (~1968–1972), Princeton University (~1972–1977), and California Culinary Academy (~1993–1994). He served on the Princeton University faculty from ~1975, becoming Professor (~1988–2018).

nodes.label: Ding-hwa Evelyn Hsieh
nodes.summary: Ding-hwa Evelyn Hsieh, a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies, completed a PhD at the University of California, Los Angeles. In 1998, she was appointed professor of Philosophy and Religion at Truman State University.

nodes.label: Jann Ronis
nodes.summary: Jann Ronis works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Virginia under David Germano, Nicolas Sihlé, Kurtis R. Schaeffer, and Jeffrey Hopkins, and held a post there attested in 2007.

nodes.label: Sik Fanin
nodes.summary: Sik Fanin works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She completed a PhD at Lancaster University in 2008 and served as a teaching consultant at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Wenbiao Mai
nodes.summary: Wenbiao Mai is an Indologist and linguist who studied at Peking University (PhD), the University of Hamburg, and Kyoto University. He held an appointment as a visiting assistant professor at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Zhonghui Cui
nodes.summary: Zhonghui Cui specializes in Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and sinology. Cui earned an MA from SOAS University of London and a PhD from the University of Hong Kong, where Cui held an attested post as teaching consultant in 2013.

nodes.label: Christopher D. Emms
nodes.summary: Christopher D. Emms is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his studies at McMaster University under the doctoral supervision of Shayne Clarke.

nodes.label: Jampa Samten
nodes.summary: Jampa Samten is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, serving as Director (attested 1991) and Professor (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Gin Ling Liu
nodes.summary: Gin Ling Liu is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Hong Kong under doctoral supervisor Jing Yin and also studied under Hsing Yun, attested in 2008.

nodes.label: Kim Knott
nodes.summary: Kim Knott (b. 1955) works in religious studies and Indology. She held a post at the University of Leeds (~1984–2012) and took up a position at Lancaster University around 2012.

nodes.label: John H. Berthrong
nodes.summary: John H. Berthrong was a scholar of sinology, philosophy, and religious studies who completed his graduate research under Alfonso Verdu. He held an academic post at Boston University from circa 1989 to 2019.

nodes.label: Jang-Kil Chun
nodes.summary: Jang-Kil Chun is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies. His studies were conducted under doctoral supervisor Minoru Kiyota, as well as teachers Paul J. Griffiths, Geshe Lhundub Sopa, and Frances A. Wilson.

nodes.label: Alexander Rödel
nodes.summary: Alexander Rödel is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He completed a Master of Science by Research at the University of Edinburgh, where he studied under the supervision of Steven Sutcliffe and Jeanne Openshaw (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Christian Matthias Boehm
nodes.summary: Christian Matthias Boehm is a scholar of Japanology, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at SOAS University of London under the supervision of John T. Carpenter (attested 2005).

nodes.label: Yongtong Tang
nodes.summary: Yongtong Tang was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Sinology. He studied at Tsinghua University (~1912–1916) and Harvard University (~1918–1922), and served in the Philosophy Department at Peking University in 1949.

nodes.label: Hsueh-li Cheng
nodes.summary: Hsueh-li Cheng (1939–2020) was a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. Cheng held academic posts at Ohio University and at the University of Hawaii at Hilo (~1977–2017).

nodes.label: Troy Organ
nodes.summary: Troy Organ (1912–1992) was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at the University of Iowa (~1939–1941). He held positions at Parsons College (~1944–1945), Chatham University (~1945–1946), the University of Akron (~1946–1954), and Ohio University (1954).

nodes.label: Aristotle C. Dy
nodes.summary: Aristotle C. Dy specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his PhD at SOAS University of London under the supervision of Antonello Palumbo (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Kristin Scheible
nodes.summary: Kristin Scheible is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied at Colby College and Harvard University. She taught at Harvard, Brown University, and Bard College (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Matthew Steven Mitchell
nodes.summary: Matthew Steven Mitchell works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He earned an MA from the University of Hawaii under Helen J. Baroni and Michel Mohr, and completed his PhD at Duke University under Richard M. Jaffe.

nodes.label: Richard M. Jaffe
nodes.summary: Richard M. Jaffe works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He held posts at North Carolina State University (~1995–2000) and Duke University (~2000).

nodes.label: Chong Go
nodes.summary: Chong Go is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Dongguk University and trained under traditional teacher Daehaeng Kun Sunim (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Bongkil Chung
nodes.summary: Bongkil Chung works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. Chung earned a PhD at Michigan State University under George C. Kerner and held posts at Florida International University, serving in 1991–1992 and as professor of philosophy (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Woosung Huh
nodes.summary: Woosung Huh works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, earning a PhD from the University of Hawaii. Attested in 2012, he served as a professor in the Department of Philosophy at Kyung Hee University.

nodes.label: Patrick R. Uhlmann
nodes.summary: Patrick R. Uhlmann works in Buddhist studies. He was a PhD candidate at the University of California, Los Angeles (attested 2012), where he studied under Robert E. Buswell Jr.

nodes.label: Woncheol Yun
nodes.summary: Woncheol Yun works in religious and Buddhist studies, earning a PhD from Stony Brook University. He held a post as Professor of Religious Studies at Seoul National University, attested in 2012.

nodes.label: Jin Y. Park
nodes.summary: Jin Y. Park works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. Park held an appointment as Assistant Professor of Philosophy and Religion at American University (attested 2007–2012) and served as a visiting fellow at City University of Hong Kong.

nodes.label: Pema Chödrön
nodes.summary: Pema Chödrön is a Buddhist studies figure who attended Miss Porter's School and the UC Berkeley Graduate School of Education. She studied under traditional teachers Chögyam Trungpa, Dzigar Kongtrul Rinpoche, and Sakyong Mipham.

nodes.label: Dzigar Kongtrul Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Dzigar Kongtrul Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology figure who studied under teachers including Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje. In 1990, he served as a professor of Buddhist philosophy at Naropa University.

nodes.label: Geo Widengren
nodes.summary: Geo Widengren (1907–1996) was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and religious studies. He studied at Stockholm University (~1926–1930) and Uppsala University (~1930–1936), holding posts at Uppsala (~1940–1973) and Stockholm University (attested 1990).

nodes.label: Benoît Vermander

nodes.summary: Paul Mendes-Flohr (1941–2024) was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who studied at Brooklyn College and Brandeis University. He held academic posts at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1975–2006) and the University of Chicago (~1999–2024).

nodes.label: Zhiyi Yang
nodes.summary: Zhiyi Yang specializes in Sinology. She studied at Peking University, the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg, and Princeton University (PhD) under Martin Kern, and held posts at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg and Goethe University Frankfurt (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Kazuharu Mizuno
nodes.summary: Kazuharu Mizuno (born 1958) studied at Nagoya University (~1978–1982), Hokkaido University (~1982–1985), and Tokyo Metropolitan University (~1985–1988). He served as professor of geography at Kyoto University's Graduate School of Letters (~2009–2024).

nodes.label: Guge Tsering Gyalpo
variants: Gu ge Tshe ring rgyal po

nodes.label: Martha Nussbaum
nodes.summary: Philosopher Martha Nussbaum studied at New York University (~1965-1969) and Harvard University (~1969-1975). She held academic posts at Harvard (~1975-1983), Brown University (~1983-1995), and the University of Chicago (~1995).

nodes.label: Yiu-ming Fung
nodes.summary: Yiu-ming Fung is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD from The Chinese University of Hong Kong in 1984. He served as Acting Head of the Division of Humanities at HKUST (attested 2008–2009).

nodes.label: Yasuo Yuasa
nodes.summary: Yasuo Yuasa (1925–2005) was a philosopher and scholar of religious studies and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Tetsuro Watsuji, later holding posts at Yamanashi, Osaka, Tsukuba, and J. F. Oberlin University, where he became professor emeritus.

nodes.label: Inyoung Chung
nodes.summary: Inyoung Chung is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at the University of Virginia under the supervision of Paul Groner, attested in 2008.

nodes.label: Seunghak Koh
nodes.summary: Seunghak Koh is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA from Seoul National University and a PhD from UCLA in 2011 under Robert E. Buswell Jr. Koh has served as an Appointed Researcher at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche is a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje (~1987–1999), Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche, and Trulshik Rinpoche, and has taught Cortland Dahl and Adam Pearcey.

nodes.label: Lars Fogelin
nodes.summary: Lars Fogelin works in archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan (1995–2003) under Carla Sinopoli, and held posts at Albion College, Southern Illinois University Carbondale, and the University of Arizona.

nodes.label: Lilla Russell-Smith
nodes.summary: Lilla Russell-Smith specializes in history and archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. She studied under Anna Eörsi and Pál Miklós, and completed her PhD at SOAS University of London.

nodes.label: Pál Miklós
nodes.summary: Pál Miklós was a scholar of Sinology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University (~1946–1950) and Peking University (~1950–1954), and later taught Lilla Russell-Smith.

nodes.label: Wenjie Duan
nodes.summary: Wenjie Duan was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the Central Academy of Fine Arts (~1940–1943) and served as director of the Dunhuang Academy in 1991.

nodes.label: David A. Hall
nodes.summary: David A. Hall specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied under Shoshin Ichishima in 1976 and earned his doctorate at UC Berkeley by 1990. He was a visiting scholar at Taisho University (1977) and department chair at Montgomery College (attested 2019).

nodes.label: Guy G. Stroumsa
nodes.summary: Guy G. Stroumsa is a scholar of religious studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at Lycée Voltaire, Hebrew University of Jerusalem, and Harvard, later holding posts at Hebrew University (around 1978–2009) and the University of Oxford (around 2009–2013).

nodes.label: John Daishin Buksbazen
nodes.summary: John Daishin Buksbazen is active in Buddhist studies. He studied at the Zen Center of Los Angeles and under Taizan Maezumi and Bernie Glassman.

nodes.label: Bernie Glassman
nodes.summary: Bernie Glassman was active in Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at NYU Tandon School of Engineering (~1956–1960), he studied under traditional teacher Taizan Maezumi (~1967–1995) and founded Zen Peacemakers (attested 2002).

nodes.label: Zen Center of Los Angeles
variants: Buddha Essence Temple, the Zen Center of Los Angeles

nodes.label: Soiku Shigematsu
nodes.summary: Soiku Shigematsu studied at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1961–1965) and under traditional teacher Kiju Shigematsu (attested 1981). Active in Buddhist studies, he taught American literature at Shizuoka University (~1975–2008) and held a post at Kansai Medical University.

nodes.label: Nguyen Thi Tuyet
nodes.summary: Nguyen Thi Tuyet works in Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at Punjabi University, attested in 2012 under doctoral supervisor Inder Mohan Singh, and also studied under traditional teacher Thich Nu Bao Nguyet.

nodes.label: Punjabi University
variants: Guru Gobind Singh Department of Religious Studies, Punjabi University, Patiala

nodes.label: Wei Lin
nodes.summary: Wei Lin is an archaeologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Nanjing University, Peking University, and Ohio State University under John C. Huntington. Her career includes posts at Nanjing Municipal Museum and Transylvania University (attested 2007).

nodes.label: Dagmar Schwerk
nodes.summary: Dagmar Schwerk is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her doctoral studies at the University of Hamburg (~2012–2017) under the supervision of Dorji Wangchuk.

nodes.label: Julie A. Gifford
nodes.summary: Julie A. Gifford specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Chicago under the supervision of Frank E. Reynolds and held a post at Miami University.

nodes.label: Scott A. Mitchell
nodes.summary: Scott A. Mitchell specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the Graduate Theological Union under Richard K. Payne (attested 2008) and became a professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Marybeth White
nodes.summary: Marybeth White works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She earned a double major honors degree from York University and was a doctoral candidate at Wilfrid Laurier University (attested 2006).

nodes.label: Hiroshi Araki
nodes.summary: Hiroshi Araki works in Japanology and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from Kyoto University (~1983–2013) and held posts at Aichi Prefectural University (~1990–1994), Osaka University (~1994–2010), and the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (~2010).

nodes.label: Tao Jiang
nodes.summary: Tao Jiang is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Temple University under doctoral supervisor Shigenori Nagatomo, and was an associate professor of religion at Rutgers University (attested 2011).

nodes.label: Margarita Kleibel
nodes.summary: Margarita Kleibel is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her master's studies under Klaus-Dieter Mathes and also studied under Karin Preisendanz.

nodes.label: Siu-tong Kwan
nodes.summary: Siu-tong Kwan works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned a PhD from the University of Hong Kong under doctoral supervisor K. L. Dhammajoti, and also studied under Zhihua Yao in 2005.

nodes.label: Marc-Henri Deroche
nodes.summary: Marc-Henri Deroche is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under doctoral supervisor Matthew T. Kapstein as well as Fernand Meyer, Samten Gyaltsen Karmay, Katsumi Mimaki, Heather Stoddard, and Franz-Karl Ehrhard.

nodes.label: Heather Stoddard
nodes.summary: Heather Stoddard is a scholar of Tibetology, history, and archaeology. She studied at SOAS University of London (~1966–1970) with D. C. Lau, and was also supervised by Nicole Vandier-Nicolas (~1977–1982) and taught by Samten Gyaltsen Karmay.

nodes.label: In-gun Kang
nodes.summary: In-gun Kang works in Buddhist and religious studies. Kang studied at the Jesuit School of Theology of Santa Clara University, the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies under several scholars, and earned a doctorate at Heythrop College under Michael Barnes.

nodes.label: Stanley Abe
nodes.summary: Stanley Abe specializes in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He held an academic post at Duke University, attested in 1995 and 2004.

nodes.label: Rafał Jan Felbur

nodes.label: Vincent Lefèvre
nodes.summary: Vincent Lefèvre specializes in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at École Nationale des Chartes and Sorbonne Nouvelle University, and has served as a curator at Musée Guimet.

nodes.label: Jean-François Jarrige
nodes.summary: Jean-François Jarrige was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at Lycée Claude Fauriel and the École du Louvre (~1961–1964). He served as the head of the Musée Guimet from approximately 1986 to 2008.

nodes.label: Namita Das
nodes.summary: Namita Das is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at Gauhati University under doctoral supervisor Sibnath Sarma (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Alexander Coburn Soper

nodes.summary: Alexander Coburn Soper specialized in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Japanology. After studying at Hamilton College and Princeton University, he held academic posts at Bryn Mawr College (circa 1939–1960) and New York University (circa 1960–1993).

nodes.label: Kang-yuan Sung
nodes.summary: Kang-yuan Sung works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA at the University of Calgary (attested 1999) under supervisor A. W. Barber, also studying under Leslie S. Kawamura.

nodes.label: Edwin F. Bryant
nodes.summary: Edwin F. Bryant specializes in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at Columbia University (~1990–1997) and held academic posts at Harvard University (~1999–2003) and Rutgers University (~2003).

nodes.label: Koenraad Elst
nodes.summary: Koenraad Elst (born 1959) is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He completed an MA at KU Leuven and studied at Banaras Hindu University around 1988 to 1992.

nodes.label: Braj Basi Lal
nodes.summary: Braj Basi Lal (1921–2022) was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at the University of Allahabad (~1939–1943). He served as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1968–1972) and Director of the Indian Institute of Advanced Study (1976–1986).

nodes.label: Diane A. Lichtenstein
nodes.summary: Diane A. Lichtenstein earned her PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1977. She has served as Adjunct Professor of Anthropology at Baldwin Wallace University and the Cleveland Institute of Art.

nodes.label: Jim G. Shaffer
nodes.summary: Jim G. Shaffer (born 1944) is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Arizona State University (~1964–1968) and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1968–1972).

nodes.label: Chris Clark
nodes.summary: Chris Clark works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his PhD under Mark Allon at the University of Sydney by 2015, where he was attested as an honorary associate in 2019.

nodes.label: Amod Lele
nodes.summary: Amod Lele is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He earned his PhD at Harvard University under the doctoral supervision of Parimal G. Patil.

nodes.summary: Jan Peter F. Hintelmann works in Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at the University of Hamburg under Marianne Pieper and also studied under traditional teachers Thupten Nyandak, Tenzin Kunga, Sonam Senge, and Geshe Sonam Rinchen.

nodes.label: Eviatar Shulman
nodes.summary: Eviatar Shulman works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1998–2008), where he later held posts in 2009 and as a Mandel postdoctoral fellow at the Scholion center (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Chaisit Suwanvarangkul
nodes.summary: Chaisit Suwanvarangkul is a scholar of buddhist studies and philosophy. He conducted research at Kyoto University and the University of Delhi, and he served as a Lecturer in Buddhist Studies at the University of Otago (attested 2015).
