nodes.label: Bhikkhunī Dhammadinnā
nodes.summary: Bhikkhunī Dhammadinnā is a scholar in Buddhist studies. Her academic career includes posts at Dharma Drum Buddhist College, where she was an assistant researcher in 2012, and the Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts.

nodes.label: Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah
nodes.summary: Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah was a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Ceylon, Cornell, and Harvard, he held posts at the University of Cambridge and Harvard University, serving as Professor of Anthropology from circa 1976 to 2001.

nodes.label: Linda Penkower
nodes.summary: Linda Penkower works in Buddhist studies and sinology. She was a research fellow at Taisho University (attested 1983) and earned her PhD from Columbia University in 1993.

nodes.label: Don A. Pittman
nodes.summary: Don A. Pittman works in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed doctoral studies at the University of Chicago and served on the faculty at Texas Christian University, attested in 2001.

nodes.label: Chun-min Yen
nodes.summary: Chun-min Yen specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Yen earned a PhD at the University of Arizona (attested 2004) under Robert M. Gimello, also studying under Todd Brown, Chanyun, and Sheng Yen.

nodes.label: Colin Leslie Dean
nodes.summary: Colin Leslie Dean works in philosophy and Indology, having studied under supervisors Peter Fenner and Purushottama Bilimoria (attested 2002).

nodes.label: Masamichi Sakai
nodes.summary: Masamichi Sakai is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his doctorate at the University of Vienna under supervisor Helmut Krasser (attested 2006, 2010).

nodes.label: Martina Draszczyk
nodes.summary: Martina Draszczyk works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed an MA under Lambert Schmithausen and earned a Dr.phil. at the University of Vienna (attested 2012), where she also held a post.

nodes.label: Dragana Majhen
nodes.summary: Dragana Majhen is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who earned a Master's degree at the University of Manitoba under the supervision of Albert Welter (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Takami Inoue
nodes.summary: Takami Inoue is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He was a doctoral candidate at the University of California, Santa Barbara (attested 2003) and served as Professor of Shin Buddhist Studies at Otani University.

nodes.label: Imre Hamar
nodes.summary: Imre Hamar (born 1967) is a Sinology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University and National Taiwan Normal University, later becoming a professor at Eötvös Loránd University (~2002, ~2008) and visiting professor at Otani University (~2009–2010).

nodes.label: Mónika Kiss
nodes.summary: Mónika Kiss is a scholar in Japanology and Buddhist studies. Kiss pursued doctoral studies in Japanese Studies at Eötvös Loránd University under advisor Masanori Yamaji (attested 2016) and studied under teachers Robert F. Rhodes and Nozomu Saito.

nodes.label: G. V. Aston
nodes.summary: G. V. Aston is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. Aston earned a PhD in philosophy at the University of Canterbury (1986–2004), studying under Paul Harrison.

nodes.label: Nguyen Van Hoa
nodes.summary: Nguyen Van Hoa is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his PhD at Savitribai Phule Pune University, attested in 2009, under the doctoral supervision of Shailaja Bapat and Lata Chhatre.

nodes.label: Nam-lin Hur
nodes.summary: Nam-lin Hur works in Japanology, religious studies, and history. He studied at the University of Tokyo and earned his PhD at Princeton University under Helen Hardacre. He was a Harvard postdoctoral fellow and became a professor at the University of British Columbia.

nodes.label: Pori Park
nodes.summary: Pori Park works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. Having studied under Robert E. Buswell Jr., she served as an assistant professor of religious studies at Arizona State University.

nodes.label: Cornelis Jan Kuiken
nodes.summary: Cornelis Jan Kuiken specializes in Sinology and Buddhist studies. Kuiken earned a PhD at the University of Groningen in 2002 under Timothy H. Barrett and Jan N. Bremmer, having also studied under Jaap den Hollander.

nodes.label: Jan N. Bremmer
nodes.summary: Jan N. Bremmer is a religious studies and history scholar. He studied at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam (~1962–1970) and the University of Bristol (~1974–1979), and held posts at Utrecht University (~1974–1990) and the University of Groningen (~1990–2009).

nodes.label: Colette Sciberras
nodes.summary: Colette Sciberras is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. She studied at Durham University under David E. Cooper and Simon P. James, as well as under traditional teachers Yungdrung Nyima and Chamtrul Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Winston Kyan
nodes.summary: Winston Kyan is a scholar in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under doctoral supervisor Wu Hung, attested in 2006.

nodes.label: Jay Holt Valentine
nodes.summary: Jay Holt Valentine specializes in Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Delaware, Naropa University, and the University of Virginia, completing his PhD under Kurtis R. Schaeffer.

nodes.label: Nicole Vandier-Nicolas
nodes.summary: Nicole Vandier-Nicolas worked in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. She held positions at École nationale des langues orientales vivantes (~1958-1971), École du Louvre (~1966-1976), and Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales (~1971-1976).

nodes.label: D. C. Lau
nodes.summary: D. C. Lau was a scholar of Sinology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Hong Kong (~1939–1946) and held posts at SOAS University of London (~1950–1978) and University College London (1970–1978).

nodes.label: Jeannine Auboyer
nodes.summary: Jeannine Auboyer worked in history, archaeology, and Indology, studying at Académie Julian, École du Louvre (1929–1934), and the EPHE (~1931–1935). She held positions at the Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique and the Musée Guimet (1965–1980).

nodes.label: Mauli Chand Prasad
nodes.summary: Mauli Chand Prasad is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He wrote a doctoral dissertation at Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar Bihar University supervised by B. Jinanand and U. Dharmaratna, and served as a Lecturer in Pali at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara.

nodes.label: Daniel Amadé Scheidegger
nodes.summary: Daniel Amadé Scheidegger is a scholar in the fields of Tibetology and religious studies. He completed his doctoral degree at the University of Bristol under the supervision of Paul Williams.

nodes.label: Mark Teeuwen
nodes.summary: Mark Teeuwen specializes in Japanology and religious studies. He earned his PhD from Leiden University (~1991-1996) and became Professor of Japanese Studies at the University of Oslo around 1999.

nodes.label: Martino Dibeltulo
nodes.summary: Martino Dibeltulo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan (attested 2015) under the supervision of Donald S. Lopez Jr. and mentoring of Ester Bianchi.

nodes.label: Gary Urton
nodes.summary: Gary Urton (born 1946) is a scholar of history and archaeology. He studied at Eastern New Mexico University, the University of New Mexico, and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, and held academic posts at Colgate University (1978–2002) and Harvard University (2002–2020).

nodes.label: Yawen Yang
nodes.summary: Yawen Yang is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned an MA at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Yongdong Shi (attested 2009).

nodes.label: Cynthia Col
nodes.summary: Cynthia Col is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. She studied Chinese religion at the Graduate Theological Union (attested 2003) under Mark C. Elliott and Steven D. Goodman.

nodes.label: Yongshan He
nodes.summary: Yongshan He specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at McMaster University under the doctoral supervision of James A. Benn, and also studied with Shayne Clarke and Mark Rowe.

nodes.label: Brad Warner
nodes.summary: Brad Warner (born 1964) is a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar who attended Wadsworth High School and Kent State University. He studied under traditional teacher Tim McCarthy (~1983) and teacher Gudo Wafu Nishijima (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Joseph Marino
nodes.summary: Joseph Marino is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Washington (attested 2017) under doctoral supervisor Richard Salomon and also studied under Collett Cox.

nodes.label: Hank Glassman

nodes.label: Ryan Matthew Jacobson
nodes.summary: Ryan Matthew Jacobson works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He completed an MA in Religious Studies at Naropa University, studying under Judith Simmer-Brown, David Phillip Stanley, Sarah Harding, Amelia Hall, Acharya Lama Tenpa Gyaltsen, and L. S. Summer, among others.

nodes.label: Sarah Harding

nodes.label: Elijah Ary
nodes.summary: Elijah Ary is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Sera Monastery, INALCO, and Harvard University (PhD ~2000–2007) under Geshe Karma Sonam, Janet Gyatso, Leonard van der Kuijp, and Charles Hallisey.

nodes.label: Cynthea J. Bogel
nodes.summary: Cynthea J. Bogel is a scholar of history, archaeology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. She studied under Keizaburō Mizuno and doctoral supervisor John M. Rosenfield, and held a post at the University of Washington (attested 2009).

nodes.summary: Amber D. Carpenter is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied under M. M. McCabe, Verity Harte, and others. She has held posts at the University of St Andrews, University of York, Einstein Forum, and Yale-NUS College.

nodes.label: Rachael Wiseman
nodes.summary: Rachael Wiseman is a philosopher who studied at the University of York from circa 2005 to 2009. She held a post at the University of Liverpool around 2013.

nodes.label: Bronwyn Finnigan
nodes.summary: Bronwyn Finnigan, a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies, studied at Auckland, Sydney, and Melbourne. She held posts at Auckland (~2008–2013), Marquette (2012–2014), and the Australian National University (2014) as continuing lecturer and deputy head of philosophy.

nodes.label: Christopher Kelley
nodes.summary: Christopher Kelley is a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar who founded the Columbia Society for Comparative Philosophy. After earning his PhD at Columbia University, he taught there, at The New School, and at Brooklyn College.

nodes.label: Heidi I. Koppl
nodes.summary: Heidi I. Koppl specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed an MA at the University of Copenhagen under Christian K. Wedemeyer and also studied under the traditional teacher Khenpo Sherab Zangpo.

nodes.label: Eugen Pander
nodes.summary: Eugen Pander (1854–1894) was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied at Polytechnikum Riga (~1873–1876) and served at Tongwen Guan in 1881 as a professor of economics and lecturer in Russian and German.

nodes.label: Qiang Ning
nodes.summary: Qiang Ning works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied under doctoral supervisors Wu Hung and Irene Winter, and held posts at the Dunhuang Academy, San Diego State University, Yale University, and the University of Michigan.

nodes.label: Shuhong Chang
nodes.summary: Shuhong Chang (1904–1994) worked in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Zhejiang Sci-Tech University (~1919–1923) and Zhejiang University, and served as director of the Dunhuang Academy (~1944–1982).

nodes.label: Ives Waldo
nodes.summary: Ives Waldo worked in philosophy, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Oxford, studied under Chögyam Trungpa between 1970 and 1988, and taught David P. Jackson.

nodes.label: Tracy Franz
nodes.summary: Tracy Franz works in Buddhist studies and other fields. Attested in 2018, she held teaching posts at Dalhousie University and Shokei University, where she was an English teacher.

nodes.label: Starr King School for the Ministry
variants: Starr King School for the Ministry

nodes.label: Brandon J. Harwood
nodes.summary: Brandon J. Harwood is a scholar in religious studies. Harwood earned a PhD at the University of Louisville (attested 2015) under advisor Patrick Pranke.

nodes.label: Patrick Pranke
nodes.summary: Patrick Pranke is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his Doctor of Philosophy from the University of Michigan (attested 2004) under the supervision of Luis Oscar Gómez and Victor B. Lieberman.

nodes.label: Andree Dominique Messent
nodes.summary: Andree Dominique Messent is a Buddhist studies scholar. She earned her PhD from the University of Bristol under Paul Williams, having also studied under Rupert Gethin and Ulrich Pagel.

nodes.label: Poh Beng Tan
nodes.summary: Poh Beng Tan is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at the International Buddhist College (attested 2015) under Charles Willemen and Tilak Kariyawasam. He also studied under teachers Sumanasiri and Shengshou.

nodes.label: Chatsumarn Kabilsingh
nodes.native: ฉัตรสุมาลย์ กบิลสิงห์
nodes.summary: Chatsumarn Kabilsingh studied at Visva-Bharati, McMaster, and Magadh universities. A Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who founded the Sakyadhita International Association of Buddhist Women, she served as Professor of Philosophy at Thammasat University circa 1973–2000.

nodes.label: Thích Thiện Châu
nodes.summary: Thích Thiện Châu (1931–1998) was a scholar in Buddhist studies. He completed his studies at Paris-Sorbonne University (circa 1967–1971) and Sorbonne Nouvelle University (circa 1973–1977).

nodes.label: Elizabeth J. Harris
nodes.summary: Elizabeth J. Harris is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at the University of Kelaniya and earned her doctorate from the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies under Ananda W. P. Guruge and Y. Karunadasa (~1988–1993), later holding a post at the University of Birmingham (~2017).

nodes.label: Hla Pe
nodes.summary: Hla Pe was a scholar of linguistics who studied at the University of Yangon (~1930–1935) and the University of London (~1938–1944). He taught Gustaaf Houtman.

nodes.label: Dungkar Lozang Trinlé
nodes.summary: Dungkar Lozang Trinlé (1927–1997) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Gyuto Monastery. He was a full professor at Minzu University of China (~1960–1965), Director of the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences, and taught at Tibet University (~1985–1997).

nodes.label: Mingyu Fu
nodes.summary: Mingyu Fu is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under MA supervisor Shi Huifeng (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Rob Nairn
nodes.summary: Rob Nairn is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Zimbabwe (~1957–1960) and the University of London/King's College London (~1960–1964). He held posts at the University of Zimbabwe (~1965–1970) and the University of Cape Town (~1970–1980).

nodes.label: Joey Hung
nodes.summary: Joey Hung (b. 1991) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the Hong Kong Academy for Performing Arts and held a post at Dharma Drum Buddhist College around 2008.

nodes.label: Vidya Dehejia
nodes.summary: Vidya Dehejia works in history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Cambridge (~1965–1968) and held a post at Columbia University (~1982).

nodes.label: James Miller
nodes.summary: James Miller works in Sinology and religious studies. He studied at Cambridge (MA, 1997) and Boston University (PhD, 2000), later serving as Professor of Chinese Studies and Religious Studies at Queen's University Belfast (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Emily T. Yeh
nodes.summary: Emily T. Yeh (b. 1971) is a Tibetologist who studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (1993, 1995) and the University of California, Berkeley (2003). She held a post at the University of Colorado Boulder (~2003).

nodes.label: Surendra Man Bajracharya
nodes.summary: Surendra Man Bajracharya is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Tribhuvan University under doctoral supervisor Bhadra Ratna Bajracharya and co-supervisor Ranjana Bajracharya.

nodes.label: Bhadra Ratna Bajracharya
nodes.summary: Bhadra Ratna Bajracharya is a scholar in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. His main posts include Dean at Lumbini Buddhist University and Chairman at the Lotus Research Centre.

nodes.label: Yungfen Ma
nodes.summary: Yungfen Ma is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned a PhD at Columbia University under the doctoral supervision of Chun-fang Yu (attested 2011).

nodes.label: Jeffrey K. Riegel
nodes.summary: Sinologist Jeffrey K. Riegel held posts as Professor of Chinese at the University of California, Berkeley (~1982–2007) and at the University of Sydney (~2007–2017).

nodes.label: Hari Shankar Prasad
nodes.summary: Hari Shankar Prasad works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Banaras Hindu University and was taught by Ramakant Tripathi, with Jan Willem de Jong serving as his doctoral supervisor.

nodes.label: Mark A. Nathan
nodes.summary: Mark A. Nathan is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history. He earned his PhD at UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr. and held appointments at Kangwon National University, UCLA, and the University at Buffalo (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Harold Conklin
nodes.summary: Harold Conklin (1926–2016) worked in linguistics and other fields. He studied at the University of California, Berkeley (~1947–1950) and Yale University (~1949–1955), and held an academic post at Columbia University (~1954–1962).

nodes.label: Mirjan Damaška
nodes.summary: Mirjan Damaška studied at the University of Ljubljana (~1955–1960) and served on the faculty at Yale Law School (~1976–2023).

nodes.label: Jan Julius Lodewijk Duyvendak

nodes.label: Helena Blankleder
nodes.summary: Helena Blankleder is a scholar in the fields of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under the traditional teachers Pema Wangyal Rinpoche and Jigme Khyentse Rinpoche, both attested in 1999.

nodes.label: Marek Zemánek

nodes.label: Yun-shan Tan
nodes.summary: Yun-shan Tan worked in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. Educated at Wenjiang Shuyuan, Mijiang Academy, Chuanshan Academy, and Hunan Normal University, he studied under several mentors including Taixu, taught at Lida Academy, and served as Professor of Chinese Studies at Visva-Bharati University.

nodes.label: Yukteshwar Kumar

nodes.label: Jerzy Bańczerowski
nodes.summary: Jerzy Bańczerowski (1938–2026) was a linguist who studied at Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań (~1956–1961). He held an academic post there from ~1961 to 2008, serving as Professor from ~1983 to 2008.

nodes.label: Linda Learman
nodes.summary: Linda Learman specializes in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She completed her doctoral work under Robert P. Weller and undertook postdoctoral mentorship under Peter N. Gregory (attested 2005).

nodes.label: Hajime Tanabe

nodes.label: Cuma Ozkan

nodes.label: Suk Fun Ng

nodes.label: Sarat Sarma
nodes.summary: Sarat Sarma specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD at Manipur University, attested in 2006, where he studied under doctoral supervisor S. Shyamkishore Singh and teacher S. Lokendrajit Singh.

nodes.label: Wulstan Fletcher

nodes.label: Ng-Fung Yuen

nodes.label: Tsoknyi Rinpoche

nodes.label: Ling Ji

nodes.label: Kang-nam Oh

nodes.label: Filippo Marsili

nodes.label: Jane Bunnag

He held posts at the School for International Training, Middlebury College, and the University of Vienna.

nodes.summary: Chamnong Adivadhanasit is a scholar of religious and buddhist studies. He earned a BA at Chulalongkorn University, where he was a part-time instructor (attested 2012), and served as a professor in the Faculty of Social Science at Kasetsart University (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Le Manh That
nodes.summary: Le Manh That is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his BA at the University of Saigon (ca. 1961–1965), his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (ca. 1965–1974), and held a post at Van Hanh University (ca. 1974–1975).

nodes.label: Pataraporn Sirikanchana
nodes.summary: Pataraporn Sirikanchana is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. She earned her Ph.D. at the University of Pennsylvania and served as a professor at Thammasat University (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Ryoshin Nakao
nodes.summary: Ryoshin Nakao is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University. He held positions as a researcher at the Soto Zen Administration Research Institute and as a professor at Hanazono University (attested 1998).

nodes.label: Nobumi Iyanaga
nodes.summary: Nobumi Iyanaga specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He held a lecturer post at the University of Tokyo (attested 2003) and a research post at the École française d'Extrême-Orient Tokyo Centre (2008-2014).

nodes.label: Phillip E. Bloom
nodes.summary: Phillip E. Bloom is a scholar of Sinology, art history, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Harvard University under the doctoral supervision of Eugene Y. Wang, Yukio Lippit, and James Robson.

nodes.label: John Corrigan
nodes.summary: John Corrigan is a religious studies and history scholar who studied at the University of Chicago (~1978–1982). He held posts at Harvard (~1982–1984), University of Virginia (~1984–1990), Arizona State University (~1990–2001), and Florida State University (~2001).

nodes.label: Françoise Robin
nodes.summary: Françoise Robin is a Tibetologist who studied under Heather Stoddard from ~1996 to 2003. She took up a post at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales in ~2005.

nodes.label: Maurice Wiles
nodes.summary: Maurice Wiles (1923–2005) was a religious studies scholar. He attended Tonbridge School and studied at Christ's College, Cambridge from circa 1945 to 1948.

nodes.label: David Fiordalis
nodes.summary: David Fiordalis works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. Educated at Carleton College, the University of Chicago, and the University of Michigan (PhD attested 2008 under Luis Oscar Gómez), he became associate professor and department chair at Linfield University (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Burton Watson
nodes.summary: Burton Watson specialized in Sinology and Japanology. He studied at Columbia University (~1946–1956), and held posts at Kyoto University (~1952–1960), Stanford University (~1960–1961), and Columbia University (~1961–1973), where he served as Professor.

nodes.label: Victor Forte
nodes.summary: Victor Forte is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He earned his Ph.D. from Temple University in 2004 and served as Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at Albright College (attested 2007).

nodes.label: Robert Magliola
nodes.summary: Robert Magliola is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who earned his Ph.D. at Princeton University (~1966–1970). He was Distinguished Chair Professor at National Taiwan University (~1990–1998) and professor at Assumption University (~1998–2003).

nodes.label: Rinzin Thargyal
nodes.summary: Rinzin Thargyal worked in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He completed his Magister degree at the University of Oslo in 1985, studying under supervisor Fredrik Barth and temporary supervisor Arne Martin Klausen.

nodes.label: Fredrik Barth
nodes.summary: Fredrik Barth (1928–2016) studied at Chicago and Cambridge under Edmund Leach. He held posts at the universities of Bergen (~1961–1972) and Oslo (~1974–1985), as well as Harvard (~1989–1996), Emory (~1989–2008), and Boston University (~1997–2008).

nodes.label: John Buescher
nodes.summary: John Buescher is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his doctoral dissertation at the University of Virginia in 1982 and served as Director at Voice of America, attested in 2001.

nodes.label: James Duerlinger
nodes.summary: James Duerlinger is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1964–1968) under Sheldon Pollock and held a post at the University of Iowa.

nodes.label: Jinping Liao
nodes.summary: Jinping Liao is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He earned his Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Jurievitch Solonin, attested in 2009.

nodes.label: Gary D. DeAngelis
nodes.summary: Gary D. DeAngelis works in religious studies and philosophy, having studied under mentors Masatoshi Nagatomi and William J. Johnson. He served as Associate Director of the Center for Interdisciplinary Studies at the College of the Holy Cross (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Thomas Borchert
nodes.summary: Thomas Borchert specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He conducted PhD research at the University of Chicago under numerous faculty and became Associate Professor of Religion at the University of Vermont (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Hsiao-Lan Hu
nodes.summary: Hsiao-Lan Hu works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. Hu earned a PhD from Temple University and served as associate professor of Religious Studies and Women's and Gender Studies at the University of Detroit Mercy (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Sam Harris
nodes.summary: Sam Harris works in philosophy. He graduated in philosophy from Stanford University (~1986–2000), studied at UCLA in 2009, and studied under teachers Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche (~1988–1996) and Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje (~1992–1999).

nodes.label: Mei Ching Hsuan
nodes.summary: Mei Ching Hsuan is a Tibetologist who earned a PhD at the University of Bonn (attested 2009), where she studied under Dieter Schuh and doctoral supervisor Peter Schwieger.

nodes.label: Richard Rorty
nodes.jawiki: リチャード・ローティ
nodes.summary: Richard Rorty was a philosopher who studied at the University of Chicago (~1946–1952) and Yale University (~1952–1956). He held academic posts at Wellesley College (~1958–1961), Princeton University (attested 1987), and Stanford University (~1998–2005).

nodes.label: Matthieu Ricard
nodes.summary: Matthieu Ricard is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He completed a PhD at the Pasteur Institute under François Jacob and studied under traditional teacher Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche from circa 1972 to 1991.

nodes.label: Levi McLaughlin
nodes.summary: Levi McLaughlin works in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Tokyo and Princeton University (PhD 2009), his career includes posts at Kokugakuin University, Wofford College, National University of Singapore, University of Iowa, and North Carolina State University.

nodes.label: Takashi Nakao
nodes.summary: Takashi Nakao studied Buddhist studies and history/archaeology at Rissho University (~1950–1957). He later served as an emeritus professor at Rissho University (~2002–2020).

nodes.label: Michael J. Tetreault
nodes.summary: Michael J. Tetreault is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He earned a Master of Arts at San Diego State University under the supervision of Sandra A. Wawrytko, attested in 2011.

nodes.label: Natasha Reichle
nodes.summary: Natasha Reichle works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She completed her dissertation at the University of California, Berkeley, where she was supervised by Joanna Gottfried Williams and studied under several other scholars.

nodes.label: Luboš Bělka
nodes.summary: Luboš Bělka specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He studied at Masaryk University (~1978–1983) and later held a post there (~1989).

nodes.label: Solomon George FitzHerbert
nodes.summary: Solomon George FitzHerbert is a Tibetologist who completed a doctorate at the University of Oxford. He has served as Departmental Lecturer in Tibetan and Himalayan studies at Oxford and as a researcher at the CNRS (attested 2019).

nodes.label: Kathleen McDonald
nodes.summary: Kathleen McDonald works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied under traditional teachers Tenzin Gyatso, 14th Dalai Lama, Thubten Yeshe, Thubten Zopa Rinpoche (~1974), Ngawang Dhargyey, Jampa Tegchok, and Ribur Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Adam Pearcey
nodes.summary: Adam Pearcey is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at SOAS University of London under the supervision of Ulrich Pagel, Nathan W. Hill, and Vincent Tournier.

nodes.label: Raimon Panikkar
nodes.summary: Raimon Panikkar (1918–2010) worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at Barcelona, Complutense, Bonn, Mysore, BHU, and Lateran universities. He taught at Harvard (~1966–1971) and UC Santa Barbara (~1987–2010), where he became professor emeritus.

nodes.label: Victor B. Lieberman
nodes.summary: Victor B. Lieberman (born 1945) is a historian. He studied at Yale University (~1963–1967) and SOAS University of London (~1972–1976), and took up a post at the University of Michigan around 1984.

nodes.label: Christopher Jon Jensen
nodes.summary: Christopher Jon Jensen works in religious studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Saskatchewan, Kyoto University, and McMaster University (PhD), supervised by James A. Benn and taught by Tōru Funayama, Shayne Clarke, Mark Rowe, and Noel Salmond.

nodes.label: Kathrin Holz
nodes.summary: Kathrin Holz works in Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Würzburg under Ingo Strauch and held a research affiliation at the Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

nodes.label: Eva K. Neumaier
nodes.summary: Eva K. Neumaier is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She served as Professor Emeritus and Department Chair of East Asian Studies at the University of Alberta and as Numata Professor of Buddhist Studies at the University of Calgary (both attested 2006).

nodes.label: Hammalawa Saddhatissa
nodes.image: Most Venerable Hammalawa Saddhatissa Maha Thera (1914–1990).jpg
nodes.summary: Hammalawa Saddhatissa worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at Vidyodaya Pirivena, Banaras Hindu University, and the University of Edinburgh (PhD). His posts included London Buddhist Vihara (1957–1990), Vikramashila Pirivena, Mahabodhi College, and the University of Toronto.

nodes.label: B. R. Ambedkar
nodes.jawiki: ビームラーオ・アンベードカル
nodes.description: Indian jurist, economist, and social reformer (1891–1956)
nodes.summary: B. R. Ambedkar was a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Elphinstone College, Columbia University, LSE, University of London, and University of Bonn, and served as professor of economics at Sydenham College (~1918–1920).

nodes.label: Jingkong
nodes.summary: Jingkong (1927–2022) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Thomé H. Fang (~1953–1958) and Bingnan Li (~1958–1968).

nodes.label: Cheng Yen
nodes.summary: Cheng Yen is an active figure in Buddhist and religious studies who studied as a disciple under Yin Shun circa 1963–2005 and founded Tzu Chi.

nodes.label: Shenghai Li
nodes.summary: Shenghai Li specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. Li earned a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Donald R. Davis Jr., also studying with Charles Hallisey, Gudrun Bühnemann, Ram Shankar Tripathi, H. V. Nagaraja Rao, and several Tibetan traditional teachers.

nodes.label: Bradley L. Herling
nodes.summary: Bradley L. Herling specializes in religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. He has held posts as Assistant Director at Boston University and at Marymount Manhattan College (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Sumi Lee
nodes.summary: Sumi Lee is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She earned an MA at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign under Alexander L. Mayer and a PhD at the University of California, Los Angeles, supervised by Robert E. Buswell Jr.

nodes.label: Alan Watts
nodes.image: Alan Watts UVM 15 June 1958 Hon. D.D (cropped).jpg
nodes.summary: Alan Watts was a writer and thinker in religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He received his education at St Hugh's School and The King's School, Canterbury (~1928–1932).

nodes.label: Michael von Brück
nodes.description: German Protestant theologian and pastor, religious scientist and author, and Zen and yoga teacher
nodes.summary: Michael von Brück (born 1949) is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He held academic posts at the University of Regensburg (~1988–1991) and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1991–2015).

nodes.label: Jeffrey Mehlman
nodes.summary: Jeffrey Mehlman is a scholar of philosophy. He held academic posts at Cornell University (~1968–1974), Johns Hopkins University (~1974–1983), Boston University (~1983), UC Berkeley, Harvard University, and Washington University in St. Louis.

nodes.label: Tim Dean
nodes.summary: Tim Dean studied at the University of East Anglia under Robert Clark, Brandeis University, and Johns Hopkins University. He held academic posts at the University of Washington, the University at Buffalo, and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign.

nodes.label: Stephanie Kaza
nodes.summary: Stephanie Kaza worked in religious and Buddhist studies. Educated at Oberlin, Stanford, Starr King School for the Ministry, and UC Santa Cruz, she served as Professor of Environmental Studies at the University of Vermont (~1991–2015).

nodes.label: Nguyen Thi Xinh
nodes.summary: Nguyen Thi Xinh specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She pursued doctoral studies at Punjabi University under the supervision of Gurjit Singh Mann, attested in 2013.

nodes.label: Kathleen D. Morrison
nodes.summary: Kathleen D. Morrison is an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at Notre Dame, the University of New Mexico, and UC Berkeley. She was Assistant Professor of Anthropology at Northwestern University (~1993–1996) and held a post at the University of Pennsylvania (~2017).

nodes.label: Joseph Walser
nodes.summary: Joseph Walser is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He pursued his education under the instruction of Isshi Yamada, Adolf von Wuertenburg, and David S. Pacini.

nodes.label: Khenpo Dazer
nodes.summary: Khenpo Dazer worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, studying under traditional teacher Bötrül Dongak Tenpé Nyima. He served as a teacher at both the Ngagyur Nyingma Institute and Dzogchen Monastery.

nodes.label: Hisao Kanaseki
nodes.summary: Hisao Kanaseki was a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied at Doshisha University (~1937–1941) and held a post at Tokyo Metropolitan University (~1966–1982).

nodes.label: King Chung Lo
nodes.summary: King Chung Lo specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. Lo completed a PhD at Leipzig University, studying under doctoral supervisor Eli Franco in 2009.

nodes.label: Jinling He
nodes.summary: Jinling He works in the field of Buddhist studies and earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Koki Okumura.

nodes.label: Natalie Depraz
nodes.summary: Natalie Depraz is a philosopher who studied at the ENS de lettres et sciences humaines, Paris Nanterre University, and St. Sergius Institute. She held posts at the Collège international de philosophie, Paris-Sorbonne University, and the University of Rouen-Normandy.

nodes.label: Karma Sonam Palmo
nodes.summary: Karma Sonam Palmo works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. She studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies before earning a PhD at the University of Tasmania under doctoral supervisors Lucy Tatman and Sonam Thakchoe.

nodes.label: Yui Suzuki
nodes.summary: Yui Suzuki works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. Suzuki completed doctoral studies at UCLA under William M. Bodiford, Lothar von Falkenhausen, and Donald F. McCallum, and held a post at the University of Maryland, College Park.

nodes.label: Jeffrey Davis Schoening
nodes.summary: Jeffrey Davis Schoening is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Washington in 1991, studying under advisor Sanghasen Singh and doctoral supervisor Collett Cox.

nodes.label: Chönyi Drolma
nodes.summary: Chönyi Drolma works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Drolma studied under Thinley Norbu Rinpoche, Lama Tharchin Rinpoche, and Ngawang Zangpo (all attested 2011).

nodes.label: Tsering Gyaltsen
nodes.summary: Tsering Gyaltsen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and was traditionally trained under Dudjom Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Mark Owen
nodes.summary: Mark Owen specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Leeds, where he was supervised by Anna King and Elizabeth Stuart.

nodes.label: Jürgen Renn
nodes.description: German physicist, historian of science and university professor
nodes.summary: Jürgen Renn works in history, archaeology, and philosophy. He studied at the Free University of Berlin (~1975–1982) and TU Berlin (~1983–1987), later holding posts at the Max Planck Institute for the History of Science (~1994–2023), FU Berlin (~1995), and Humboldt University (~2006).

nodes.label: Yulian Zeng
nodes.summary: Yulian Zeng is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Jurievitch Solonin (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Graham E. Clarke
nodes.summary: Graham E. Clarke (died 1998) was a scholar of Tibetology. He held posts at the Institute of Development Studies and as a Senior Member at the University of Oxford (attested 1998).

nodes.label: Gelek
nodes.summary: Gelek is a scholar in Tibetology and other fields. He served as a researcher at the China Tibetology Research Center (attested 1998), a visiting lecturer at the University of California, and a visiting scholar at the University of Oxford.

nodes.label: Angela Manderscheid
nodes.summary: Angela Manderscheid is a scholar of Tibetology who held posts at the Free University of Berlin and the University of Oulu, where she was a researcher attested in 1998.

nodes.label: Rong Ma
nodes.summary: Rong Ma specializes in Tibetology. He earned a doctorate in social geography from Brown University, served as a visiting scholar at Harvard University, and was Director of the Institute of Sociology and Anthropology at Peking University (attested 1998).

nodes.label: Ronald D. Schwartz
nodes.summary: Ronald D. Schwartz is a scholar in Tibetology and sociology. In 1998, he was attested as Professor of Sociology at Memorial University of Newfoundland and as an Honorary Research Fellow at the University of Hong Kong.

nodes.label: Gesellschaft für europäisch-asiatische Kulturbeziehungen
variants: Gesellschaft für europäisch-asiatische Kulturbeziehungen in München

nodes.label: Chuan-ying Yen
nodes.summary: Chuan-ying Yen specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Harvard University, where she studied under doctoral supervisor John M. Rosenfield, tutor Chu-tsing Li, and teacher John Hay.

nodes.label: Chu-tsing Li
nodes.summary: Chu-tsing Li was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Sinology. He studied at the University of Iowa from circa 1948 to 1955 and later held a post at the University of Kansas from circa 1966 to 1990.

nodes.label: Kenneth J. Saunders
nodes.summary: Kenneth J. Saunders (1883–1937) was a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied under Wagiswara. He served as Professor of the History of Religion at the Pacific School of Religion (circa 1921–1935) and as a lecturer at UC.

nodes.label: Takamaro Shigaraki
nodes.summary: Takamaro Shigaraki studied at Ryukoku University (~1948-1957), later serving there as professor of Shin Buddhist Studies (1970) and president (1989-1995). A Buddhist studies scholar, he was also chairman of Bukkyō Dendō Kyōkai (~2007-2014).

nodes.label: Kuno Lorenz
nodes.summary: Kuno Lorenz (born 1932) is a philosopher who studied at the University of Kiel (~1956–1961). He held positions at the University of Hamburg (~1970–1974) and served as a professor at Saarland University (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Claus Oetke
nodes.summary: Claus Oetke (1947–2019) was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Hamburg (~1968–1976). He worked as a wissenschaftlicher Assistent at Hamburg (~1977–1989) and held a post at Stockholm University (~1989–2012).

nodes.label: Rolf Scheuermann
nodes.summary: Rolf Scheuermann is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Vienna (attested 2010) under MA supervisor Helmut Tauscher, and also studied under traditional teacher Khenpo Chodrak Tenphel.

nodes.label: Edward H. Schafer
nodes.summary: Edward H. Schafer was a sinologist who studied at UCLA (~1931–1934), UC Berkeley (~1937–1947), and Harvard (~1940–1941). He served as a professor at UC Berkeley from ~1947 to 1984.

nodes.label: Soen Shaku
nodes.summary: Soen Shaku was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under Kosen Imakita (~1878–1892) and at Keio University (~1882–1885). He served as chief abbot of Engaku-ji (1892) and held a post at Hanazono University.

nodes.label: Paul Carus
nodes.summary: Paul Carus was a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Hermann Grassmann, held a post at Open Court Publishing Company (~1887–1919), and taught Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki.

nodes.label: Dirk H. A. Kolff
nodes.summary: Dirk H. A. Kolff is an Indologist and historian who earned an MA at Leiden University (~1960-1967). He served at Leiden as Professor of Modern Indian History in 1967 and held a post there from 1991 to 2003.

nodes.label: Susanne Hoeber Rudolph
nodes.summary: Susanne Hoeber Rudolph (1930–2015) was an Indology scholar who studied at Sarah Lawrence College, Radcliffe College, and Harvard University. She held academic posts at Harvard University (~1954–1964) and the University of Chicago (~1964–2002).

nodes.label: Eiki Hoshino
nodes.summary: Eiki Hoshino specializes in religious studies and Buddhist studies. After studying at Taisho University (~1962–1970), he served there as a professor in the Faculty of Humanities and director (~1984–2014).

nodes.label: Phanit Jetjiravat
nodes.summary: Phanit Jetjiravat specializes in Buddhist studies, earning a Master of Arts in the field at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University under the academic advisement of Phra Suthithammanuwat, Veerachart Nimanong, and Paetpong Worapongpichet.

nodes.label: Francis N. J.
nodes.summary: Francis N. J. is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. Attested in 2002, he earned a Master's in Ancient History at the University of Calicut and completed doctoral studies supervised by M. R. Raghava Varier.

nodes.label: M. R. Raghava Varier
nodes.summary: M. R. Raghava Varier (born 1936) is a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Calicut and later served there as Reader in Epigraphy from circa 1974 to 1996.

nodes.label: Rajan Gurukkal
nodes.summary: Rajan Gurukkal (born 1948) is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Calicut and held posts as Director of the School of Social Sciences at Mahatma Gandhi University (~1996–2008) and at IISc Bengaluru (~2010–2015).

nodes.label: Harold Scheub
nodes.summary: Harold Scheub (1931–2019) studied at the University of Michigan (~1954–1960) and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1965–1969). He held a post at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from around 1970 to 2013.

nodes.label: Thomas James Mazanec
nodes.summary: Thomas James Mazanec is a sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Calvin University, the University of Colorado Boulder, and completed doctoral work under Anna M. Shields, Stephen F. Teiser, and Wang Ping.

nodes.label: Jeff Dolven
nodes.summary: Jeff Dolven studied at Worcester College (~1988–1990) and Yale University (~1990–1997). He founded Princeton University and held a post there around 2001, where he taught Thomas James Mazanec.

nodes.label: Joshua T. Katz
nodes.summary: Joshua T. Katz is a linguist who studied at the Dalton School, Yale University (~1987–1991), the University of Oxford (~1991–1993), and Harvard University (~1993–1998). He served as a faculty member at Princeton University from 1998 to 2022.

nodes.label: Nalini Bhushan
nodes.description: Andrew W. Mellon Professor in the Humanities at Smith College

nodes.label: Will B. Miller
nodes.summary: Will B. Miller works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Miller earned a PhD at Harvard University under doctoral supervisor Janet Gyatso, and also studied under Lopen Chorten in 2012.

nodes.label: Wilburn Hansen
nodes.summary: Wilburn Hansen works in Japanology and religious studies. Hansen studied at the University of Colorado Boulder and at Stanford University under Bernard Faure and Carl Bielefeldt.

nodes.label: Yu-kwan Ng
nodes.summary: Yu-kwan Ng is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at The Chinese University of Hong Kong under Zongsan Mou and earned a Ph.D. from McMaster University under Yun-hua Jan, Graeme MacQueen, and Koichi Shinohara.

nodes.label: Bruce Charles Williams
nodes.summary: Bruce Charles Williams is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He was taught by Edward H. Schafer, Michael Rogers, Michel Strickmann, Barend A. van Nooten, Padmanabh S. Jaini, Akira Fujieda, and Noritoshi Aramaki.

nodes.label: Sodo Yokoyama
nodes.summary: Sodo Yokoyama was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Eiko Hashimoto and Kodo Sawaki (~1940–1965). He later taught Joko Shibata.

nodes.label: Elena France Hanson
nodes.summary: Elena France Hanson is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at Harvard University, where she studied under Charles Hallisey.

nodes.label: Katherine Anne Narraway
nodes.summary: Katherine Anne Narraway is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies. She earned a Master of Arts at McGill University, where she studied under supervisor G. Victor Sōgen Hori (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Cheryl A. Crowley
nodes.summary: Cheryl A. Crowley works in Japanology. She studied under William R. LaFleur, Philip B. Yampolsky, and Ryuichi Abe.

nodes.label: Roland Wenzlhuemer
nodes.summary: Roland Wenzlhuemer is a historian who studied at the University of Salzburg (~1996–2002). He held academic posts at Heidelberg University (~2008–2017) and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~2017).

nodes.label: Dörte Kamarid
nodes.summary: Dörte Kamarid is a scholar of Tibetology and Indology. She studied at Savitribai Phule Pune University, the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and the University of Vienna, where she earned a BA and completed an MA supervised by Helmut Tauscher.

nodes.label: U Dhammissara
nodes.summary: U Dhammissara is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (attested 2017), supervised by Sanu Mahatthanadull with committee member Walmoruwe Piyaratana.

nodes.label: Asen Balikci
nodes.summary: Asen Balikci studied at Columbia University (~1957–1962) and held a post at the Université de Montréal from circa 1968 to 1994.

nodes.label: Bo-gwang Han
nodes.summary: Bo-gwang Han specializes in Buddhist studies and held a professorship at Dongguk University (attested 2004, 2015). Han also taught Silwon Suk.

variants: Regent Hotel and Technical School in Ostend

nodes.label: Anne Nishimura Morse
nodes.summary: Anne Nishimura Morse specializes in Japanology and history and archaeology. She earned her PhD from Harvard University under John M. Rosenfield and Yutaka Hirata, holding posts at Smith College, Tokyo National Research Institute, Nara National Museum, and Kyoto National Museum.

nodes.label: Yutaka Hirata
nodes.summary: Yutaka Hirata specialized in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at Kyushu University (~1950–1954), later becoming Professor Emeritus there (~1995–2013), and also held a post at Nagasaki Junshin Catholic University.

nodes.label: Seiji Nemoto
nodes.summary: Seiji Nemoto works in Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Meiji University and served as a professor at the University of Tsukuba from around 1998 to 2014.

nodes.label: Martin T. Adam
nodes.summary: Martin T. Adam specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and McGill University, where he earned his PhD under Richard P. Hayes (attested 2002), alongside teachers including Kameshwar Nath Mishra.

nodes.label: Bruno Galasek
nodes.summary: Bruno Galasek is a scholar in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at the University of Bonn under the supervision of Konrad Klaus (attested 2016).

nodes.label: Palmo Kyi
nodes.summary: Palmo Kyi is a scholar in the field of Tibetology. She studied under Hanna Havnevik, Rinzin Thargyal, and Per Kvaerne.

nodes.label: Hsiu-hui Ji
nodes.summary: Hsiu-hui Ji is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed an MA at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin, attested in 2009.

nodes.label: David Patt
nodes.summary: David Patt is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 1993) under the doctoral supervision of Geshe Lhundub Sopa.

nodes.label: Ngan-che Chan
nodes.summary: Ngan-che Chan is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD from the University of Hong Kong under Jing Yin, attested in 2007, and also studied under K. L. Dhammajoti.

nodes.label: Tenzin
nodes.summary: Tenzin is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under MA supervisor Hanna Havnevik and completed a Master of Philosophy at the University of Oslo (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Meiping Li
nodes.summary: Meiping Li is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University (attested 2009) under the supervision of Kirill Jurievitch Solonin.

nodes.label: Tao Jin
nodes.summary: Tao Jin is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who earned a PhD from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign in 2008 under doctoral supervisor Alexander L. Mayer.

nodes.label: Karl-Heinz Brodbeck
nodes.summary: Karl-Heinz Brodbeck studied philosophy and Buddhist studies at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1970–1980). He held posts at the Ifo Institute, LMU Munich, and as professor at both Würzburg-Schweinfurt and the Munich School of Politics and Public Policy.

nodes.label: Technical University of Applied Sciences Würzburg-Schweinfurt

nodes.id: I:Munich School of Politics and Public Policy
nodes.label: Munich School of Politics and Public Policy
Ashby Butnor
nodes.summary: Ashby Butnor is a scholar in philosophy and Japanology who completed a Ph.D. at the University of Hawaii under Vrinda Dalmiya in 2009. She was a Visiting Assistant Professor at Metropolitan State University of Denver (attested 2011).

nodes.label: Carlo Jamelle Harris
nodes.summary: Carlo Jamelle Harris works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Arts in Philosophy at National Chengchi University under the supervision of Chen-kuo Lin.

nodes.label: Carl Shigeo Yamamoto
nodes.summary: Carl Shigeo Yamamoto specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia, where he was supervised by Jeffrey Hopkins and David Germano, and also studied under Sonam Germano, William Magee, and Tsering Wangchuk.

nodes.label: Richard P. Boyle
nodes.summary: Richard P. Boyle studied at the University of Washington and under traditional teacher Joshu Sasaki. He taught at the University of California, Los Angeles, and held an affiliation with the University of New Mexico attested in 2015.

nodes.label: Tenshin Tanouye
nodes.summary: Tenshin Tanouye (1938–2003) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under traditional teacher Sogen Omori and founded Chozen-ji.

nodes.label: Sogen Omori
nodes.summary: Sogen Omori was a Buddhist studies and philosophy figure. He held positions at Kōho-in Temple (~1970–1994) and Hanazono University (~1978–1982), and he taught Tenshin Tanouye.

nodes.label: Eduardo Francisco Freyre Roach
nodes.summary: Eduardo Francisco Freyre Roach studied Buddhist studies at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2014), earning a Master of Buddhist Studies under the supervision of Y. Karunadasa and Georgios T. Halkias.

nodes.label: Johannes Beltz
nodes.summary: Johannes Beltz is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He earned doctorates in 1999 from the University of Lausanne and the École Pratique des Hautes Études, supervised by Marie-Louise Reiniche and Johannes Bronkhorst.

nodes.label: Esben Andreasen
nodes.summary: Esben Andreasen is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Copenhagen and was a visiting researcher at Otani University in 1992.

nodes.label: Daniel Borengasser
nodes.summary: Daniel Borengasser is a scholar in the fields of history, archaeology, and Japanology. He earned a Master of Arts degree at the University of Oregon under the supervision of Akiko Walley (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Akiko Walley
nodes.summary: Akiko Walley is a scholar of Japanology, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Aoyama Gakuin University (~1994–2001) and Harvard University (~2001–2009), and held a post at the University of Oregon (2009–2016).

nodes.label: Sonam Tsering
nodes.summary: Sonam Tsering is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under doctoral supervisor Gray Tuttle, as well as teachers Khenzur Dawa, Drepung Khenzur Gyatso, Samdhong Rinpoche, Janet Gyatso, Leonard van der Kuijp, and Gyumé Khenzur Lobzang Trinlé.

nodes.label: Sudhir Kakar
nodes.summary: Sudhir Kakar, educated at St. Edward's School, Shimla, worked in religious studies and related fields. He served as a lecturer at Harvard (~1971–1972), professor at IIM Ahmedabad (~1972–1977), and department head at IIT Delhi (~1977–1980).

nodes.label: Naman P. Ahuja
nodes.summary: Naman P. Ahuja is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He earned his doctorate at SOAS University of London and served as Professor of Indian Art and Architecture at Jawaharlal Nehru University (attested 2018).

nodes.label: Jens Schlieter
nodes.summary: Jens Schlieter specializes in religious studies, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Bonn (~1987–1999) and the University of Vienna, and became Professor and Institute Managing Director at the University of Bern (~2009).

nodes.label: Chi Chen Ho
nodes.summary: Chi Chen Ho specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned a PhD from UCLA in 2010 under Robert E. Buswell Jr., studied under traditional teacher Hsuan Hua, and served as a teaching assistant at UCLA.

nodes.label: K. Venkata Ramanan
nodes.summary: K. Venkata Ramanan worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy, studying under Yongtong Tang, Sentian Wang, and Prabodh Chandra Bagchi at Peking University and Visva-Bharati University. He was a Professor of Philosophy at Visva-Bharati and a visiting scholar at the Harvard-Yenching Institute.

nodes.label: Satyendra Nath Bose
nodes.jawiki: サティエンドラ・ボース
nodes.summary: Satyendra Nath Bose studied at Hindu School, Presidency University, Kolkata, and the University College of Science, Technology & Agriculture. He held academic posts at the University of Dhaka, the University of Calcutta, and served as Vice-chancellor of Visva-Bharati University (~1956–1958).

nodes.label: Walter Liebenthal
nodes.summary: Walter Liebenthal was a scholar in Buddhist studies, sinology, and Indology. He held positions at the University of Paris, Visva-Bharati University (around 1952–1959), and the University of Tübingen (around 1960–1965).

nodes.label: Norman Fischer
nodes.description: American Soto Zen roshi, poet and Buddhist author practicing in the lineage of Shunryu Suzuki

nodes.label: Kichinosuke Ito
nodes.summary: Kichinosuke Ito (1885–1961) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1906–1909). His career included posts at Hokkaido University (~1921–1935), the University of Tokyo as professor (~1935–1946), and Chuo University.

nodes.label: Anna Madelyn Hennessey
nodes.summary: Anna Madelyn Hennessey works in religious studies and Sinology. She earned her PhD from the University of California, Santa Barbara (attested 2011), where she studied under doctoral supervisor William F. Powell.

nodes.label: Huynh Thi Ha Vy
nodes.summary: Huynh Thi Ha Vy is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts degree at the International Buddhist College (attested 2015) under the instruction of Kapila Abhayawansa.

nodes.label: Douglas Matthew Gildow
nodes.summary: Douglas Matthew Gildow is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Princeton University under the supervision of Stephen F. Teiser and Qi Zhou, attested in 2016.

nodes.label: Ülo Valk
nodes.summary: Ülo Valk is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied at Miina Härma Gymnasium and the University of Tartu (~1980–1986). He held a post at the University of Tartu (~1995) and served as an editor for Numen (~2007).

nodes.label: David Gonsalez
nodes.summary: David Gonsalez is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He pursued traditional studies under Gen Lobsang Choephel, Lati Rinpoche, Kirti Tsenshab Rinpoche, and Denma Lochö Rinpoche.

nodes.summary: Haeju Sunim is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a visiting lecturer at Harvard University (1996–1997) and as an associate professor of Buddhist studies at Dongguk University (attested 1999).

nodes.label: Dietmar Rothermund
nodes.summary: Dietmar Rothermund was a historian and Indologist who studied at Marburg, Munich, and the University of Pennsylvania, where he earned his PhD in 1959. He was affiliated with Heidelberg University, attested in 2004.

nodes.label: Lama Palden Drolma
nodes.summary: Lama Palden Drolma is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology practitioner who studied under traditional teachers including Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, Jamgön Kongtrül III, Bokar Rinpoche, Situ Rinpoche, Dudjom Rinpoche, Druptop Rinpoche, Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima, and Khenpo Tsültrim Gyamtso Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Amar Singh
nodes.summary: Amar Singh is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his doctoral studies under Anthony Kennedy Warder and was also taught by Bimal Krishna Matilal, T. Venkatacharya, Alasdair Urquhart, and Rahul Sankrityayan (1960–1963).

nodes.label: Alasdair Urquhart
nodes.summary: Alasdair Urquhart is a philosopher who studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1963–1967) and the University of Pittsburgh (~1968–1973). He held an academic post at the University of Toronto beginning in ~1973.

nodes.label: Tianshu Zhu
nodes.summary: Tianshu Zhu specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Northwest University (MA) and Ohio State University (PhD under John C. Huntington), holding posts at Northwest University, Shaanxi History Museum, Ohio State University, and Korea University.

nodes.label: Jacob N. Kinnard
nodes.summary: Jacob N. Kinnard is a scholar in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He has held academic appointments at William & Mary as Assistant Professor of Religion and at the Iliff School of Theology.

nodes.label: Bryce Ryan
nodes.summary: Bryce Ryan held academic posts at Cornell University and the University of Ceylon.

nodes.label: Nguyen Van Thuong
nodes.summary: Nguyen Van Thuong works in Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Delhi under MA supervisor K. T. S. Sarao.

nodes.label: Xinru Liu
nodes.summary: Xinru Liu studied at the University of Pennsylvania (~1980–1985), working in Indology, history, archaeology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. She held positions at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (attested 2010) and The College of New Jersey (~2000–2021).

nodes.label: Janet R. Goodwin
nodes.summary: Janet R. Goodwin works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and history. She studied at UC Berkeley under Delmer M. Brown and Britten Dean, and held academic posts at the University of Southern California and the University of Aizu.

nodes.label: Lawrence William Nelson
nodes.summary: Lawrence William Nelson specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed a Doctor of Philosophy and Religion at the California Institute of Integral Studies (attested 2012), having also studied at Butler, Indiana, NYU, Northwestern, College of Santa Fe, and St. John's College.

nodes.label: Bryan D. Lowe
nodes.summary: Bryan D. Lowe is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who studied at Otani University and with Jacqueline I. Stone. He held a post at Vanderbilt University (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Ben Joffe
nodes.summary: Ben Joffe is a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies. He earned his Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Colorado Boulder under the supervision of Carole McGranahan.

nodes.label: Winnifred Fallers Sullivan
nodes.summary: Winnifred Fallers Sullivan is a religious studies scholar who studied at Cornell (~1967–1971). She held posts at Washington and Lee University, the University of Chicago (~2000–2005), and Indiana University (~2012).

nodes.label: Martin Riesebrodt
nodes.summary: Martin Riesebrodt was a religious studies scholar. He studied at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1973–1978) and Heidelberg University (~1978–1980), and held a post at the University of Chicago (~1990–2014).

nodes.label: Mark I. Wallace
nodes.description: author, minister, and theologian who teaches in the department of religion at Swarthmore College

nodes.label: Joanne Punzo Waghorne
nodes.summary: Joanne Punzo Waghorne specializes in religious studies and Indology. After studying at the University of Chicago (~1969–1976), she held posts at UMass Boston (1975–1983), Bowdoin College (1983–1985), UNC Chapel Hill (1987–2002), and Syracuse University (2002).

nodes.label: Takahiko Kameyama
nodes.summary: Takahiko Kameyama works in Buddhist and religious studies. In 2015, he was attested as a professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies and a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University.

nodes.label: Wes Borton
nodes.summary: Wes Borton works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Borton studied at East Carolina University under Derek F. Maher and at the University of Michigan (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Margarita Angelica Delgado Creamer
nodes.summary: Margarita Angelica Delgado Creamer is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Pittsburgh under Linda Penkower and completed postdoctoral work under Xiuping Hong.

nodes.label: Humberto Maturana
nodes.jawiki: ウンベルト・マトゥラーナ
nodes.summary: Humberto Maturana worked in philosophy and other fields. He studied at Liceo Manuel de Salas, University College London (~1954–1956), and Harvard University (~1956–1958), later holding a post at the University of Chile (~1960).

nodes.label: Yangdon Dhondup
nodes.summary: Yangdon Dhondup is a Tibetology scholar who completed a PhD at SOAS University of London (~2000–2004) under the supervision of Henry Y. H. Zhao.

nodes.label: Christopher Byrne
nodes.summary: Christopher Byrne specializes in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from McGill University, studying under doctoral supervisor Grace S. Fong, MA supervisor G. Victor Sōgen Hori, and teacher Robin D. S. Yates.

nodes.label: Alexander James O'Neill
nodes.summary: Alexander James O'Neill is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He is a PhD candidate at the University of Toronto and a research fellow at Taisho University.

nodes.label: St Antony's College, University of Oxford
Chatral Sangye Dorje Rinpoche
nodes.image: Tulku Sangay Yonten Gyatsho and HH ChatralSangyeDorje Rinpoche.jpg
nodes.summary: Chatral Sangye Dorje Rinpoche was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Sera Khandro and Dorje Dradul, and taught Keith Dowman and Khetsun Sangpo Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Kenneth J. Guest
nodes.summary: Kenneth J. Guest is a scholar of religious studies and Sinology. He studied at Columbia University, Peking University, Union Theological Seminary, and CUNY (PhD) under Aloysius Pieris, and held posts at Hunter College and Baruch College.

nodes.label: Vishwanath Prasad Varma
nodes.summary: Vishwanath Prasad Varma is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied under Dhirendra Mohan Datta, Ganga Nath Bhattacharya, Kalikinkar Datta (~1947–1950), and Joachim Wach (1950).

nodes.label: Dhirendra Mohan Datta
nodes.summary: Dhirendra Mohan Datta was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at the University of Calcutta from circa 1917 to 1923. He held posts at Patna College in 1928 and the University of Minnesota from 1951 to 1952.

nodes.label: Joachim Wach
nodes.summary: Joachim Wach (1898–1955) was a religious studies scholar and philosopher who studied at Leiden University. He held academic posts at Leipzig University (~1924–1935) and as a professor at the University of Chicago (~1945–1955).

nodes.label: Don Handelman
nodes.summary: Don Handelman is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at McGill, Pittsburgh, and Manchester (~1967–1971), and served as Professor of Anthropology at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1972–2007).

nodes.label: Charles Malamoud
nodes.description: French historian of religion and orientalist
nodes.summary: Charles Malamoud, a scholar of Indology and religious studies, studied at the University of Paris (circa 1948–1954). He held posts at the University of Lyon (circa 1968–1979) and École Pratique des Hautes Études (circa 1979–1999).

nodes.label: Mikio Otsuki
nodes.summary: Mikio Otsuki works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He has held positions as a research fellow at Manpuku-ji (attested 2007) and as a professor at Hanazono University (attested 2007).

nodes.label: M. M. McCabe
nodes.summary: M. M. McCabe is a philosopher who studied at the University of Cambridge (~1967–1978). She subsequently held a post at King's College London from ~1990 to 2014.

nodes.label: Verity Harte
nodes.summary: Verity Harte (born 1968) is a philosopher who studied at the University of Cambridge (~1989–1996). She held an academic post at King's College London (~1997–2005) before joining the faculty at Yale University (~2005).

nodes.label: Raimond Gaita
nodes.summary: Raimond Gaita (born 1946) is a philosopher who studied at St Patrick's College, Melbourne High School, the University of Melbourne, and the University of Leeds. He held academic posts at King's College London (~1989–2011) and Australian Catholic University (~1999–2011).

nodes.label: Jonathan Lear
nodes.summary: Jonathan Lear (1948–2025) was a philosopher who studied at Yale University (c. 1965–1969), the University of Cambridge (c. 1969–1971), and The Rockefeller University (c. 1973–1978). He held a post at the University of Chicago from c. 1996 to 2025.

nodes.label: Susan Neiman
nodes.description: American philosopher, essayist and cultural commentator (born 1955)
nodes.summary: Susan Neiman (born 1955) is a philosopher who studied at Harvard and the Free University of Berlin. She held academic posts at Yale University (~1989–1996) and Tel Aviv University (~1996–2000), and joined the Einstein Forum around 2000.

nodes.label: Jonathan Glover
nodes.summary: Jonathan Glover is a philosopher who attended Tonbridge School and Corpus Christi College, Oxford (c. 1960–1964). He held a post at King's College London from c. 1998 to 2013 and taught Amber D. Carpenter.

nodes.label: Songeun Choe
nodes.summary: Songeun Choe works in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. Choe studied under MA supervisor Myung-dae Moon and completed a PhD at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign under Kiyohiko Munakata (attested 1991).

nodes.label: Michael W. Meister
nodes.summary: Michael W. Meister (born 1942) is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Pennsylvania (~1964–1967) and Harvard University (~1968–1974), and served as Professor at the University of Pennsylvania (~1976–2020).

nodes.label: Melissa R. Kerin
nodes.summary: Melissa R. Kerin specializes in art history, archaeology, and Buddhist and Tibetan studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under Michael W. Meister and Deborah Klimburg-Salter, and joined Washington and Lee University as a professor (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Manfred Steger
nodes.jawiki: マンフレッド・スティーガー
nodes.summary: Manfred Steger is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who studied under Robert Aitken and at Rutgers University (~1991–1995). He held a post at RMIT University from around 2003 to 2012.

nodes.label: Keenan W. Cox
nodes.summary: Keenan W. Cox specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Cox earned an MA from McMaster University, studying under supervisor James A. Benn (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Brian Bocking
nodes.summary: Brian Bocking is a scholar in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at the University of Leeds, where he studied under Michael Pye.

nodes.label: André Couture
nodes.summary: André Couture is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at Laval University (~1965–1971), EPHE (~1971–1977), and Paris-Sorbonne University (~1971–1977), and held a post at Laval University (~1979–2012).

nodes.label: Xianda
nodes.summary: Xianda studied Buddhist studies, earning a BA at the University of Kelaniya and a PhD at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2016). His teachers included K. L. Dhammajoti and Toshiichi Endo.

nodes.label: Seung-yeon Lee
nodes.summary: Seung-yeon Lee works in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. Lee completed doctoral studies under Sang-hae Lee and held posts at Sungkyunkwan University and the Gyeonggi Cultural Foundation.

nodes.label: Jampa Mackenzie Stewart
nodes.summary: Jampa Mackenzie Stewart is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Jamgon Kongtrul Lodro Chokyi Senge and Khenpo Karthar Rinpoche (attested 1995).

nodes.label: Yukihiko Asayama
nodes.summary: Yukihiko Asayama is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. Asayama served as a professor at Hokkaido University of Education (attested 1986) and as an overseas researcher for the Ministry of Education at South China Normal University (attested 1991).

nodes.label: Tadashi Inoue
nodes.summary: Tadashi Inoue was a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1949–1953). He held posts at Kyoto University of the Arts, Bukkyo University, and Nara University (professor, ~1985–2004).

nodes.label: Tetsuo Suzuki
nodes.summary: Tetsuo Suzuki is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at Shizuoka University (~1953–1957) and served as an assistant professor at Otani University from ~1969 to 1980.

nodes.label: Leonard Bloomfield
nodes.jawiki: レナード・ブルームフィールド
nodes.summary: Leonard Bloomfield was a linguist who studied at Harvard, Wisconsin, Chicago, Leipzig, and Göttingen. He held academic posts at Cincinnati (ca. 1909–1910), Illinois (ca. 1910–1921), Ohio State (ca. 1921–1927), Chicago (ca. 1927–1940), and Yale (ca. 1940–1949).

nodes.label: Kaigen Noritake
nodes.summary: Kaigen Noritake is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Kenyu Mitomo. He held a post as an assistant professor (助教授) at Rissho University (attested 2007).

nodes.label: Carl Wilhelm Vollgraff
nodes.summary: Carl Wilhelm Vollgraff worked in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He held posts at the University of Groningen from 1908 to 1916 and at Utrecht University from 1917 to 1946.

nodes.label: William L. Smith
nodes.summary: William L. Smith (born 1942) is an Indology scholar. He held appointments at Hampton University, the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, the University of Wisconsin-Madison, and Stockholm University (~1980–2009).

nodes.label: Fumio Masutani
nodes.summary: Fumio Masutani (1902–1987) worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He held posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1949–1953), Shizuoka University (~1953–1960), Taisho University (~1961–1977), and Tsuru University (~1977–1983).

nodes.label: Kumataro Kawada
nodes.summary: Kumataro Kawada (1899–1981) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Tokyo Imperial University (~1920–1923). He held posts at Tokyo University of Literature and Science (~1932–1950), the University of Tokyo (~1950–1960), Komazawa University, and Japan Women's University.
