nodes.label: Gnanawimala Chandima
nodes.summary: Gnanawimala Chandima is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He studied at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara under Uma Shankar Vyas.

nodes.label: Jogendra Singh
nodes.summary: Jogendra Singh is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara under the instruction of Uma Shankar Vyas.

nodes.label: Shingo Einoo
nodes.summary: Shingo Einoo is an indologist who earned his PhD at the University of Marburg under Wilhelm Rau (~1976–1983). He held an assistant post at the National Museum of Ethnology (~1984–1989).

nodes.label: Hartmut Scharfe
nodes.summary: Hartmut Scharfe (1932–2020) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He completed his doctoral studies under Paul Thieme and held a position at the University of California, Los Angeles.

nodes.label: Carl Friedrich Gauss
nodes.jawiki: カール・フリードリヒ・ガウス
nodes.summary: Carl Friedrich Gauss studied at Collegium Carolinum (1792–1795), the University of Göttingen (1795–1798), and the University of Helmstedt (~1798–1799). He held a post at Göttingen from ~1807 to 1855.

nodes.label: Daijo Tokiwa
nodes.summary: Daijo Tokiwa was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. After studying at the University of Tokyo (~1896–1899), he held a post at Toyo University from approximately 1904 to 1939.

nodes.label: Yuishin Ito
nodes.summary: Yuishin Ito (1931–2023) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Bukkyo University and Doshisha University. Ito held posts at Bukkyo University (~1959–2002), Kyoto Bunkyo Junior College, Kyoto Bunkyo Gakuen, Shōjōke-in Temple, and Chion-in Temple.

nodes.label: Johann Gottfried Eichhorn
nodes.summary: Johann Gottfried Eichhorn worked in religious studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Göttingen under Christian Gottlob Heyne (~1770–1774), was professor of Oriental languages at Jena (~1775–1788), and served as Professor of Philosophy at Göttingen (~1788–1827).

nodes.label: Keiki Yabuki
nodes.summary: Keiki Yabuki (1879–1939) worked in Buddhist and religious studies, studying at Tohoku Fukushi, Taisho, and Tokyo universities. He founded Miwa Gakuin and taught at Shukyo University (~1913–1926), University of Tokyo (~1924–1935), and Taisho University (~1926–1939).

nodes.label: Shigeru Matsumoto
nodes.summary: Shigeru Matsumoto (1933–2010) was a religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1953–1957) and Harvard University (~1963–1968). He held academic posts at Tenri University (~1970–1989) and the University of the Sacred Heart (~1989–2004).

nodes.label: Bernhard Kölver
nodes.summary: Bernhard Kölver was an Indology scholar who held positions at the University of Cologne (1966–1970), the Nepal Research Centre (~1970–1972), the University of Kiel (1977–1993), and Leipzig University (1993–2001).

nodes.label: Antoine Meillet
nodes.jawiki: アントワーヌ・メイエ
nodes.summary: Antoine Meillet (1866–1936) was a linguist and scholar of Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated in Paris under Saussure, Bréal, and Lévi, he held posts at EPHE, ENLOV, and the Collège de France (1906–1936).

nodes.label: Émile Benveniste
nodes.jawiki: エミール・バンヴェニスト
nodes.summary: Émile Benveniste was a linguist, Indologist, and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar who studied at the University of Paris under Antoine Meillet. Benveniste held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1927–1972) and the Collège de France (1937–1972).

nodes.label: Theodore Dwight Woolsey
nodes.description: American jurist; president of Yale University (1801–1889)
nodes.summary: Theodore Dwight Woolsey worked in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He received his education at Hopkins School and Yale College (~1816–1820).

nodes.label: Sures Chandra Banerji
nodes.description: born:1917-08-04|died:2000|; Sureśa Candra Bandyopādhyāya 1917-; Banerji, Sures Chandra; Banerji, Sures Chandra 1917-2000

nodes.label: Toru Takahashi
nodes.summary: Toru Takahashi (1878–1967) worked in Sinology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies, and founded the Koreanology Association. He was a professor at Keijo Imperial University (~1926–1945), Fukuoka University (~1947–1950), and Tenri University (~1950–1965).

nodes.label: Seok-hyeong Kim
nodes.summary: Seok-hyeong Kim is a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Taisho University and held appointments as a part-time lecturer at Seoul National University and as a professor at Dongguk University.

nodes.label: Tsutomu Kubo
nodes.summary: Tsutomu Kubo was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1904–1908). He later held an academic post at Tohoku University (~1926–1944).

nodes.label: Pierre Amédée Jaubert
nodes.description: French diplomat, academic, orientalist, translator, politician, and traveler (1779-1847)
nodes.summary: Pierre Amédée Jaubert was a scholar of linguistics who studied at the École nationale des langues orientales vivantes (~1796–1798). He served as president of the Société Asiatique (1834–1847) and held posts at the Collège de France and his alma mater.

nodes.label: Ernest Renan
nodes.summary: Ernest Renan worked in religious studies, philosophy, and linguistics. He studied at Saint-Sulpice Seminary and Collège de France, where he studied under Eugène Burnouf. He held posts at the Bibliothèque nationale de France (1851–1860) and Collège de France (1861).

nodes.label: Gyoei Fukuda
nodes.summary: Gyoei Fukuda (1867–1954) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tendai Sect University. He served as president of Taisho University (~1926–1944) and held posts at the University of Tokyo (1928) and Toyo University.

nodes.label: Charles de Harlez
nodes.summary: Charles de Harlez worked in sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He served as Professor and Professor of Oriental Languages at KU Leuven circa 1871–1899, where he taught Louis de La Vallée Poussin.

nodes.label: Victor Henry
nodes.summary: Victor Henry was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He held academic posts at École Centrale de Lille and the University of Paris (1888).

nodes.label: Anna Seidel
nodes.summary: Anna Seidel was a scholar in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. Between approximately 1961 and 1968, she studied under teachers Maxime Kaltenmark and Rolf Alfred Stein.

nodes.label: Götz von Selle
nodes.summary: Götz von Selle (1893–1956) was a historian. He studied at the Humboldt University of Berlin, the University of Kiel, and the University of Göttingen, where he later held a post from around 1929 to 1938.

nodes.label: John Borthwick Gilchrist
nodes.image: John Borthwick Gilchrist, cropped from UCL portrait by Blanconi.jpg
nodes.jawiki: ジョン・ギルクリスト
nodes.summary: John Borthwick Gilchrist worked in linguistics and Indology. Educated at Royal High School, George Heriot's School, and the University of Edinburgh, he held posts with the East India Company (~1782–1804), Fort William College (~1800–1804), and East India Company College (1806).

nodes.label: Claudius Buchanan
nodes.summary: Claudius Buchanan (1766–1815) worked in religious studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Glasgow (1782) and Queens' College, Cambridge (~1791–1795), later serving as Vice-Provost at Fort William College (1801).

nodes.label: Bruno Petzold
nodes.jawiki: ブルーノ・ペツォルト

nodes.label: Seiichiro Ono
nodes.summary: Seiichiro Ono was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tokyo Imperial University (~1914–1917). He held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1926–1952) and Aichi Gakuin University (~1956–1968).

nodes.label: Haya Akegarasu
nodes.summary: Haya Akegarasu (1877–1954) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar. He studied at Otani University from around 1899 to 1902 and at the Tokyo School of Foreign Languages.

nodes.label: Edwin Arnold
nodes.jawiki: エドウィン・アーノルド
nodes.summary: Edwin Arnold worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. His education included studies at King's School, Rochester, King's College London (~1847–1850), and University College, Oxford (~1850–1854).

nodes.label: Siddharth College
variants: シッダールタ女子大学

nodes.label: Poerbatjaraka
nodes.summary: Poerbatjaraka worked in linguistics, Indology, and history and archaeology. He studied at Leiden University (~1921–1926) and held a post at the University of Indonesia (~1950–1964).

nodes.label: Herman Kellgren
nodes.summary: Herman Kellgren (1822–1856) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Hermann Brockhaus, Eugène Burnouf, and Philippe-Édouard Foucaux. He held a post at the University of Helsinki from ~1849 to 1856.

nodes.label: Francis Gladwin
variants: フランシス・グラッドウィン
nodes.description: British scholar of the Persian language
nodes.summary: Francis Gladwin was a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological studies. A founding member of the Asiatic Society (~1784–1812), he served as professor of Persian at Fort William College from circa 1801 to 1805.

nodes.label: William S.-Y. Wang
nodes.summary: William S.-Y. Wang is a linguist and sinologist. He studied at Columbia University and the University of Michigan before holding posts at the University of California, Berkeley (~1966–1994) and Hong Kong Polytechnic University (~2004).

nodes.id: I:Grundriss der indogermanischen Sprach- und Altertumskunde
nodes.label: Grundriss der indogermanischen Sprach- und Altertumskunde
variants: Grundriss der indogermanischen Sprach- und Altertumskunde

nodes.label: Albert Thumb
nodes.image: Professor Albert Thumb 18.05.1865 bis 14.08.1915 Sohn von Ida Schanzenbach und Albert Alois Thump.jpg
nodes.summary: Albert Thumb was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Freiburg (circa 1884–1888). He later held academic posts at Freiburg (circa 1889–1909) and the University of Marburg (circa 1909–1915).

nodes.label: James Charles Colebrooke Sutherland
nodes.summary: James Charles Colebrooke Sutherland (1792–1844) was an Indology scholar. He studied at East India Company College and Fort William College under Thomas Roebuck, and later served as professor of law at Presidency University, Kolkata.

nodes.id: I:Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters
nodes.label: Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters
Richard Bowring
nodes.summary: Richard Bowring (born 1947) is a scholar in Japanology and Buddhist studies. He was educated at Blundell's School from circa 1960 to 1965 and Downing College from circa 1965 to 1973.

nodes.label: Muzaffar Alam
nodes.description: historian at the University of Chicago
nodes.summary: Muzaffar Alam (born 1947) is a historian and Indologist. After studying at Jamia Millia Islamia, Aligarh Muslim University, and Jawaharlal Nehru University, he held posts at JNU (~1973–2001) and the University of Chicago (~2001), as well as Wisconsin-Madison, Leiden, and Collège de France.

nodes.label: Benkyo Shiio
nodes.summary: Benkyo Shiio was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1902–1905). He held posts at Waseda University, Taisho University (~1926–1947), and Sanko Library (~1960–1968).

nodes.label: Sanko Library
variants: 三康文化研究所附属三康図書館

nodes.label: Karl Ferdinand Johansson
nodes.summary: Karl Ferdinand Johansson was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Uppsala University in 1880. He later served there from around 1893 to 1925 as University Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology of the Indo-European Languages.

nodes.label: Louis H. Gray
nodes.summary: Specializing in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies, Louis H. Gray studied at Princeton (~1892–1896) and Columbia (~1896–1900). He held posts at Princeton (~1900–1902) and the University of Nebraska–Lincoln (~1920–1921).

nodes.label: Sangay Dorji
nodes.summary: Sangay Dorji is a scholar of Tibetology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tengtho Monastery and Simtokha Dzong, later teaching at Simtokha Dzong and serving as Secretary of the Dzongkha Development Commission.

nodes.label: Ugyen Pelgen
nodes.summary: Ugyen Pelgen specializes in history, archaeology, and Tibetology. He earned a master's degree from Aligarh Muslim University and served as a lecturer of history at Sherubtse College.

nodes.label: John A. Ardussi
nodes.summary: John A. Ardussi specializes in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He completed an MA under Turrell V. Wylie, earned a PhD attested in 1977 from Australian National University, and served on a CNRS research team.

nodes.label: Phuntshok Tashi
nodes.summary: Working in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Phuntshok Tashi earned a BA from Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and an MA from the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies. He held a post at the National Museum of Bhutan.

nodes.label: George van Driem
nodes.jawiki: ジョージ・ヴァン・ドリーム
nodes.summary: George van Driem is a linguist and Tibetologist who completed his doctorate at Leiden University (~1983–1987). He held posts at Leiden University (~1987–2009), the University of Bern (2010–2022), and the Indian Institute of Technology Guwahati (2020).

nodes.label: Lungten Dubgyur
nodes.summary: Lungten Dubgyur is a scholar in Tibetology and other fields. He completed his studies at Sherubtse College, Government Law College, Mumbai (LL.B), and the University of Edinburgh (LL.M).

nodes.label: Kees W. Bolle
nodes.summary: Kees W. Bolle (1927–2012) was a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied at Leiden University (~1946–1953). He served as a fellow at the Netherlands Institute for Advanced Study and Professor Emeritus of History at UCLA (both attested 2005).

nodes.label: Thinley Dorji Bhutia
nodes.summary: Thinley Dorji Bhutia worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as Tibetan Teacher and Boarding Superintendent at Darjeeling Government High School, and in 1994 was Director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and Chief Editor of Bulletin of Tibetology.

nodes.label: Georg von der Gabelentz
nodes.jawiki: ゲオルク・フォン・デア・ガーベレンツ
nodes.summary: Georg von der Gabelentz (1840–1893) was a scholar in sinology and linguistics. He studied at the universities of Jena and Leipzig, later serving as professor of East Asian languages at Leipzig University and at Humboldt University of Berlin.

nodes.label: Alexander Cunningham
nodes.jawiki: アレキサンダー・カニンガム
nodes.description: British army engineer and amateur archaeologist (1814-1893)

nodes.label: Aloys Sprenger
nodes.summary: Aloys Sprenger (1813–1893) was an Indologist who studied at the University of Vienna (~1832–1836). He served as principal of Delhi College (~1845–1848), Hooghly Mohsin College (1851–1854), and Aliah University (~1850–1856), later holding a post at the University of Bern (~1858–1881).

nodes.label: Robert Hyde Colebrooke
nodes.description: British infantry officer and surveyor in India (1762–1808)

nodes.label: John Herbert Harington
nodes.description: British administrator in India and Persian scholar
nodes.summary: John Herbert Harington was an Indologist and historian/archaeologist. He served as secretary at the Asiatic Society from circa 1794 to 1798 and later was a professor at Fort William College from circa 1801 to 1823.

nodes.label: Amaranatha Jha
nodes.summary: Amaranatha Jha (1897–1955) studied at Muir Central College (~1913–1917), where he became Professor of English in 1917. He later served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Allahabad (~1938–1946) and Banaras Hindu University (~1947–1948).

nodes.label: Charles Elliott
nodes.summary: Charles Elliott worked in Indology. He served at the East India Company circa 1795–1826 and was Treasurer of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland circa 1837–1856.

nodes.label: Edmund Nathaniel Snyder
nodes.summary: Edmund Nathaniel Snyder was an Indologist who graduated from Harvard University in 1886. He studied under Albrecht Weber and Hermann Oldenberg.

nodes.label: James Irving Manatt
nodes.summary: James Irving Manatt (1845–1915) worked in history, archaeology, and linguistics. Educated at Grinnell and Yale under William Dwight Whitney, he held posts at Denison, Marietta, the University of Nebraska–Lincoln, the United States, and Brown University (~1892–1915).

nodes.label: James Hadley
nodes.summary: James Hadley (1821–1872) was a linguist who studied at Yale College (~1840–1842) and under Edward Elbridge Salisbury (1849). He held posts at Middlebury College (1844–1845) and Yale University (1845–1872).

nodes.label: Francis Robinson
nodes.summary: Francis Robinson is a historian and scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied at Bexhill College (~1956–1963) and became a professor at Royal Holloway, University of London, circa 1973.

nodes.label: Gordon Johnson
nodes.summary: Gordon Johnson (born 1943) is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Trinity College, Cambridge (~1961–1967) and held a post at the University of Cambridge (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Kurfürst-Ruprecht-Gymnasium Neustadt
variants: Gymnasium at Neustadt an der Haardt

nodes.label: Don Martino de Zilva Wickremasinghe
nodes.summary: Don Martino de Zilva Wickremasinghe was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He studied under Wilhelm Geiger at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg from around 1894 to 1897.

nodes.label: Shridhar Ramkrishna Bhandarkar
nodes.summary: Shridhar Ramkrishna Bhandarkar (b. 1859) was an Indologist. He served as Assistant to the Professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College (1884), Professor of Sanskrit at Elphinstone College, and permanent Professor of Sanskrit at Wilson College, Mumbai.

nodes.label: Rewata Dhamma
nodes.native: ဦးရေဝတဓမ္မ

nodes.label: Narada Mahathera
nodes.image: Portrait Of Most Venerable Narada Maha Thera (1898-1983).jpg
nodes.summary: Narada Mahathera (1898–1983) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Ceylon University College and trained under traditional teacher Pelene Siri Vajirañāṇa (~1917–1955).

nodes.label: C. R. Krishnamacharlu
nodes.summary: C. R. Krishnamacharlu was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist. He completed his F.A. studies at Madras Christian College and earned his university degree from Pachaiyappa's College.

nodes.label: James Gibbs
nodes.summary: James Gibbs (1825–1886) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Mumbai (1870–1879) and President of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (~1876–1881).

nodes.label: Oliver Codrington
nodes.summary: Oliver Codrington (1837–1921) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Secretary of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (attested 1878) and Honorary Librarian of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland (attested 1892).

nodes.label: Dermot Killingley
nodes.summary: Dermot Killingley is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Oxford and SOAS University of London. He held a post at the University of Malaya (1967-1970) before serving as Senior Lecturer and Reader at Newcastle University (circa 1970-2000).

nodes.label: Institute of Economic Growth
variants: Institute of Economic Growth (University of Delhi)

nodes.label: Vasudha Narayanan
nodes.summary: Vasudha Narayanan (born 1953) is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. She studied at the Universities of Madras and Mumbai before completing her education at Harvard (~1974–1978). She was appointed Distinguished Professor of Religion at the University of Florida (~1982).

nodes.label: Sumathi Ramaswamy
nodes.summary: Sumathi Ramaswamy is a historian and Indologist who studied at Delhi University, JNU, and the University of Pennsylvania. She held academic appointments at the University of Pennsylvania (~1991–2000) and the University of Michigan (~2000–2007).

nodes.label: Declan Quigley
nodes.summary: Declan Quigley is an Indologist who has held teaching positions at the University of Cambridge, the University of St Andrews, and Queen's University Belfast.

nodes.label: Henry Herbert Dodwell
nodes.summary: Henry Herbert Dodwell (1879–1946) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Lord Williams's School and St John's College (~1899–1902). He served in the Indian Educational Service (1908–1922) and was Professor of History of India at SOAS (~1922–1946).

nodes.label: Madan Mohan Malaviya
nodes.image: Madan Mohan Malaviya 2011 stamp of India.jpg
nodes.summary: Madan Mohan Malaviya (1861–1946) was an Indology scholar who founded Banaras Hindu University. He completed his studies at the University of Calcutta (circa 1879–1884) and the University of Allahabad (circa 1889–1893).

nodes.label: Suzanne Karpelès
nodes.summary: Suzanne Karpelès worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études from circa 1917 to 1922 and held a post at the French Information Bureau from circa 1945 to 1949.

nodes.label: Henry Sullivan Jarrett
nodes.summary: Henry Sullivan Jarrett (1839–1919) was an Indologist, historian, and archaeologist. He served as Secretary and Member of the Board of Examiners, Calcutta (~1870–1894), succeeding Heinrich Blochmann.

nodes.label: Heinrich Blochmann
nodes.summary: Heinrich Blochmann (1838–1878) worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and history and archaeology. He pursued studies at Leipzig University from around 1855 to 1857 and at the University of Calcutta from around 1860 to 1861.

nodes.label: Ian James Coghlan
nodes.summary: Ian James Coghlan specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a doctorate in Asian Studies from La Trobe University by 2004 and served as a research fellow at Monash University's Monash Asia Institute (attested 2005).

nodes.label: Holly Gayley
nodes.summary: Holly Gayley is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She completed doctoral studies at Harvard University (~2001–2009) and held a post at the University of Colorado Boulder (~2008).

nodes.label: Heinz Mode
nodes.description: German art historian, orientalist and indologist (1913-1992)
nodes.summary: Heinz Mode (1913–1992) worked in archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under George Peiris Malalasekera, Otto Fischer, and completed a doctorate at the University of Basel, later serving as Professor of Oriental Archaeology at Halle-Wittenberg (~1948–1978).

nodes.label: Otto Fischer
nodes.description: German art historian, director of Kunstmuseum Basel (1886–1948)
nodes.summary: Otto Fischer specialized in Sinology, Japanology, and history and archaeology. He held a post at the Kunstmuseum Basel in 1927 and taught at the University of Basel from circa 1927 to 1937.

nodes.label: Willem Bollée
nodes.summary: Willem Bollée (1927–2020) was an Indologist. He studied at Utrecht University and completed his Habilitation at the University of Hamburg (1975). He was an assistant professor at Münster (1971–1978) and professor at Heidelberg from 1979.

nodes.label: William Frederic Sinclair
nodes.summary: William Frederic Sinclair (1847–1900) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the Royal School, Armagh, and held a post in the Indian Civil Service beginning in 1866.

nodes.id: I:Oriental Translation Fund of Great Britain and Ireland
nodes.label: Oriental Translation Fund of Great Britain and Ireland
Dilli Raman Regmi
nodes.summary: Dilli Raman Regmi was an Indologist and historian who completed an M.A. at Patna University and an M.Litt at the University of Madras.

nodes.label: William Rainey Harper
nodes.summary: William Rainey Harper (1856–1906) worked in linguistics and religious studies. He studied at Yale under William Dwight Whitney and held academic posts at Denison University and the University of Chicago.

nodes.label: Daniel Coit Gilman
nodes.summary: Daniel Coit Gilman (1831–1908) studied at Yale, Harvard, Cambridge, and Humboldt University. He served at Yale (~1856–1872), UC Berkeley (~1872–1875), and was president of Johns Hopkins (1875–1901), the American Oriental Society (1893–1906), and Carnegie Institution (~1901–1904).

nodes.label: Toshio Horiuchi
nodes.summary: Toshio Horiuchi specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He completed his PhD at the University of Tokyo (~2002–2008) and held researcher appointments at Toyo University (~2013–2021) and Zhejiang University (~2017).

nodes.label: Thomas Jülch
nodes.summary: Thomas Jülch (born 1975) works in sinology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~2006–2011) and served as a research fellow at Ghent University (attested 2019).

nodes.label: Klaus Pinte
nodes.summary: Klaus Pinte works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. Pinte studied at Ghent University under Pol Vanden Broucke and served there as a teaching assistant in 2006.

nodes.id: I:Singapore University of Technology and Design
nodes.label: Singapore University of Technology and Design
variants: Singapore University of Technology and Design

nodes.label: Jacob Samuel Speyer
nodes.summary: Indologist Jacob Samuel Speyer studied under Hendrik Kern (~1868–1872). He held academic posts at the University of Amsterdam (1877–1889), the University of Groningen (1889–1903), and served as Professor of Indology at Leiden University (1903–1913).

nodes.label: Lionel Obadia
nodes.summary: Lionel Obadia is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD from Lille University of Science and Technology in 1997. He has held academic posts at INALCO, KU Leuven, EPHE, Lille 3 University, and Lumière University Lyon 2.

nodes.label: Lille 3 University
variants: Charles-de-Gaulle University of Arts and Social Sciences

nodes.label: Richard Hughes Seager
nodes.summary: Richard Hughes Seager worked in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Wisconsin System, Harvard Divinity School, and Harvard University (PhD ~1981–1987), later serving as Associate Professor of Religion at Hamilton College (~1994–2014).

nodes.label: Michelle Spuler
nodes.summary: Michelle Spuler (born 1971) specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Queensland and taught at Colorado College and in the Department of Religious Studies at Victoria University of Wellington.

nodes.label: Robert Maclagan
nodes.description: British Army officer and military engineer (1820–94)
nodes.summary: Robert Maclagan was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1836–1837) and Addiscombe Military Seminary (~1837–1839). He served as Principal of the Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee from 1847 to 1860.

nodes.label: Erberto Lo Bue
nodes.description: Italian indologist, tibetologist, translator and university teacher
nodes.summary: Erberto Lo Bue (1946–2022) was a Tibetologist and historian who earned his PhD from SOAS University of London in 1981. He lectured at the University of Milan (attested 1996) and held a post at the University of Bologna (~2002).

nodes.label: Jean-Luc Chevillard
nodes.summary: Jean-Luc Chevillard is a scholar in the fields of Indology and linguistics. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure in 1975 and served as a researcher at the Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique (~1989).

nodes.label: Monika Horstmann
nodes.summary: Monika Horstmann is an Indology and religious studies scholar. She held posts at Australian National University, the Free University of Berlin, the University of Bonn, the University of Cologne, EPHE, and Heidelberg University, where she became emeritus professor around 2007.

nodes.label: Rudolf Aernoud Kern
nodes.description: civil servant in the Dutch Indies (1875-1958)

nodes.label: Rajendralal Mitra
nodes.summary: Rajendralal Mitra (1824–1891) worked in Indology, history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Hindu School and the University of Calcutta, and served as president of the Asiatic Society (~1885–1886).

nodes.label: Francis Buchanan-Hamilton
nodes.jawiki: フランシス・ブキャナン＝ハミルトン
nodes.summary: Francis Buchanan-Hamilton worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1779–1783), served in the Indian Medical Service (~1794–1815), and succeeded Henry Thomas Colebrooke.

nodes.label: Mona Schrempf
nodes.summary: Mona Schrempf specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. After completing a doctorate in anthropology at the Free University of Berlin in 2001, she held posts at Humboldt University of Berlin and Heidelberg University, both attested in 2006.

nodes.label: Jogindra Nath Samaddar
nodes.summary: Jogindra Nath Samaddar (1884–1929) was an Indologist and historian educated at Presidency University and Bangabasi College. He taught at Pramatha-Manmatha College, St. Columba's College, and served at Patna College (1912) and Patna University (1923).

nodes.label: Winfred Robert Martin
nodes.summary: Winfred Robert Martin (d. 1915) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He served as Professor of Oriental Languages at Trinity College and as Librarian at the Hispanic Society of America.

nodes.label: Daniel John Gogerly
nodes.summary: Daniel John Gogerly (1792–1862) was a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. He served as chairman of the Wesleyan Methodist Missionary Society (~1838–1862) and president of the Royal Asiatic Society of Sri Lanka (~1845–1862).

nodes.label: Graves Champney Haughton
nodes.summary: Graves Champney Haughton (1788–1849) studied at East India Company College (~1814–1816), later serving there as Professor of Hindú Literature, and the History of Asia (~1817–1827). He also served as secretary of the Royal Asiatic Society (~1831–1832).

nodes.label: Netherlands Institute for Advanced Study
variants: Netherlands Institute for Advanced Studies in the Humanities and Social Sciences

nodes.label: Parul Dave-Mukherji
nodes.summary: Parul Dave-Mukherji works in Indology, philosophy, and history/archaeology. She completed her DPhil at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson (1988–1991) and served as professor of Visual Studies and Art History at Jawaharlal Nehru University (attested 2020).

nodes.label: Kazuaki Komine
nodes.summary: Kazuaki Komine (born 1947) is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies. He held a post at Tokushima University (~1978–1991) and served as professor emeritus at Rikkyo University (attested 2015–2019).

nodes.label: Hermann Sauppe
nodes.summary: Hermann Sauppe (1809–1893) was a scholar in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He held posts at the University of Zurich (~1838–1845) and the University of Göttingen (~1856–1893).

nodes.label: Gottlieb Wilhelm Leitner
nodes.summary: Gottlieb Wilhelm Leitner (1840–1899) was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at King's College London in 1858, held a post there in 1861, and later worked at the Oriental Institute in Woking (~1889–1899).

nodes.label: Addiscombe Military Seminary
variants: Hon. East India Company's Military Seminary, Addiscombe
Honourable East India Company's Military Seminary, Addiscombe

nodes.label: Henry George Keene
nodes.description: English employee of the East India Company and Persian scholar
nodes.summary: Henry George Keene was a scholar of Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He served in the East India Company (~1798–1811) and was Professor of Arabic, Persian, and Hindústání Literature at East India Company College (~1824–1834).

nodes.label: David Ruddell
nodes.summary: David Ruddell was a scholar in Indology and linguistics who studied at Laval University and held a post as Secretary at Fort William College.

nodes.label: Emil Rödiger
nodes.jawiki: エミル・レーディガー
nodes.summary: Emil Rödiger (1801–1874) was a linguist who studied at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1821–1825). He held posts at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1830–1860) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1860–1874).

nodes.label: Alfred Master
nodes.description: Master, Alfred (1883-1978) Lecturer in Indian Philology

nodes.label: Manudeva
nodes.summary: Manudeva is an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied under traditional teacher Bālakṛṣṇa Pāyaguṇḍa and was a disciple of Bāla Śarman Pāyaguṇḍe.

nodes.label: William Erskine
nodes.summary: William Erskine (1773–1852) was a scholar in the fields of history, archaeology, and Indology. He was educated at the Royal High School and studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1788–1792).

nodes.label: James Atkinson
nodes.description: English surgeon, artist and Persian scholar (1780–1852)
nodes.summary: James Atkinson (1780–1852) specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1798–1802) and served as Assistant Persian Professor at Fort William College in 1818.

nodes.label: Dayong
nodes.summary: Dayong was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Wuchang Buddhist Institute, where he taught in 1923, under Taixu, Palden Tenzin Nyendrak, and Bai Puren, and founded the Tibetan Language School of Beijing.

nodes.label: Pabongkha Dechen Nyingpo
variants: Pha bong kha pa dbe chen snying po

nodes.label: Buddhist Academy of China
variants: Institute of Buddhist Studies of Beijing

nodes.label: John Thompson Platts
nodes.jawiki: ジョン・トンプソン・プラッツ
nodes.summary: Platts was a scholar in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Balliol College (~1881–1884) and served as Teacher of Persian at the University of Oxford (~1880–1904).

nodes.label: Finnian M. M. Gerety
nodes.summary: Finnian M. M. Gerety is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. After completing his doctorate at Harvard University by 2015, he held a postdoctoral fellowship at Yale (2017–2018) and a post at Brown University (attested 2020).

nodes.label: Andrea R. Jain
nodes.summary: Andrea R. Jain is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. She studied at Southern Methodist University and Rice University, later becoming Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Indiana University–Purdue University Indianapolis (~2017–2021).

nodes.label: Hidehiko Kurita
nodes.summary: Hidehiko Kurita works in religious studies and Japanology. He completed a PhD at Tohoku University and served as a lecturer at Aichi Prefectural University (attested 2020).

nodes.label: Kwangsoo Park
nodes.summary: Kwangsoo Park is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies who earned an MA at the University of Iowa and a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison. He is attested as a professor at Wonkwang University in 2020.

nodes.label: Samani Pratibha Pragya
nodes.summary: Working in religious studies and Indology, Samani Pratibha Pragya completed her PhD at SOAS University of London and served there as a research assistant (attested 2020).

nodes.label: Julian Strube
nodes.summary: Julian Strube is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied at Heidelberg University and the University of Amsterdam. He held posts at Heidelberg (2015–2019), Amsterdam (2016–2017), the University of Münster (2019–2021), and the University of Vienna (~2021).

nodes.label: Edward Clive Bayley
nodes.summary: Edward Clive Bayley worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Haileybury and Imperial Service College / East India Company College (~1840–1842) and entered the Indian Civil Service in 1842.

nodes.label: Justus Olshausen
nodes.summary: Specializing in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies, Justus Olshausen studied at Kiel, Berlin, and under Silvestre de Sacy, Langlès, and Kieffer. He held posts at the University of Kiel (~1827–1853) and the University of Königsberg (~1853–1858).

nodes.label: Christopher André Holmboe
nodes.summary: Christopher André Holmboe was a scholar in linguistics, Indology, and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Oslo and under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy and Armand-Pierre Caussin de Perceval, later serving as reader and professor at Oslo.

nodes.label: Hokkaido University of Education
variants: 北海道教育大学岩見沢分校
北海道教育大学函館分校

nodes.label: Tetsuo Otani
nodes.summary: Tetsuo Otani is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University (~1959–1965) and Komazawa University (~1965–1969). He held positions at Komazawa University (~1979–1990, 2002–2006), Tomakomai Komazawa (2006–2007), Tsuru (2013–2016), Tohoku Fukushi (2015–2019), and Peking University.

nodes.label: Asahikawa University Junior College
variants: 旭川大学女子短期大学部

nodes.label: Doranne Jacobson
nodes.summary: Doranne Jacobson is an Indology scholar who earned a doctorate in anthropology at Columbia University, where she also served as a seminar associate at the Southern Asian Institute.

nodes.label: McKim Marriott
nodes.jawiki: マッキム・マリオット
nodes.summary: McKim Marriott (1924–2024) was an anthropologist and Indology scholar. He earned his doctorate at the University of Chicago (~1947–1953) and served there as a professor of anthropology and social sciences from ~1953 to 1998.

nodes.label: S. Sankaranarayanan
nodes.summary: S. Sankaranarayanan was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and history and archaeology. He served as an Honorary Professor at the Adyar Library and Research Centre (~1986–1999) and held a post at the Chinmaya International Foundation in 1999.

nodes.label: Chinmaya International Foundation
variants: Adi Sankara Nilayam, Chinmaya International Foundation

nodes.label: R. Thangaswami Sarma
nodes.summary: R. Thangaswami Sarma (1924–2000) studied at The Madras Sanskrit College and Annamalai University. An Indologist and philosopher, he held posts at Presidency College, the University of Madras, Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, ICPR, and Adyar Library and Research Centre.

nodes.label: Sri Sarada Education Society Research Centre
variants: Sri Sarada Education Society Research Centre

nodes.label: Camillo Alessio Formigatti
nodes.summary: Camillo Alessio Formigatti is an Indologist who studied at the University of Milan. He worked on the Sanskrit Manuscripts Project at Cambridge (2011–2014), taught Sanskrit at SOAS University of London, and served as Sanskrit Librarian at the Bodleian Libraries (attested 2019).

nodes.label: Geoffrey Goble
nodes.summary: Geoffrey Goble works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. He earned an MA from the University of Virginia and a PhD from Indiana University, and was appointed Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Oklahoma (attested 2019).

nodes.label: Alastair Gornall
nodes.summary: Alastair Gornall specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He completed a PhD at the University of Cambridge (~2008–2013) and held posts at SOAS University of London (~2015) and Singapore University of Technology and Design (~2016).

nodes.label: Max Leopold Margolis
nodes.summary: Max Leopold Margolis (1866–1932) was a linguistics and religious studies scholar. He studied at Columbia University (~1889–1891) and later held posts there (~1891–1892), at the University of California, Berkeley (~1897–1905), and at Dropsie College (~1909–1932).

nodes.summary: Soshuku Shibatani specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at Waseda University and served as a commissioned researcher at Koyasan University, attested in 2015.

nodes.label: Yuka Otani
nodes.summary: Yuka Otani is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts as a part-time lecturer (非常勤講師) at Ryukoku University and Hanazono University, both attested in 2015.

variants: Wiener Zeitschrift für die Kunde des Morgenlandes

nodes.label: Frederik David Kan Bosch
nodes.summary: Frederik David Kan Bosch (1887–1967) was an Indologist and archaeologist who headed the Archaeological Service in the Netherlands East Indies (~1916–1936). He later held posts at Utrecht University (1938–1945) and Leiden University (1946–1957).

nodes.label: George Cœdès
nodes.summary: George Cœdès (1886–1969) was a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1903–1906) and served as president of the Société des Amis du Vieux Hanoi (attested 1934).

variants: Ceylon Branch of the Royal Asiatic Society

nodes.label: Arthur Christensen
nodes.summary: Arthur Christensen was a Danish scholar of Iranian philology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Copenhagen from circa 1893 to 1903 and was appointed professor extraordinarius of Iranian philology there in 1919.

nodes.label: Henrik Samuel Nyberg
nodes.summary: Henrik Samuel Nyberg was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, religious studies, and linguistics. He studied at Uppsala University in 1908 and later held a post there from ~1919 to 1956.

nodes.label: Otto Höfler
nodes.summary: Otto Höfler was a scholar of linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Vienna (~1921–1926) and Lund University (~1928–1934), later holding posts at the University of Kiel, Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich, and the University of Vienna.

nodes.label: George Shirt
nodes.summary: George Shirt was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He earned a B.A. from the University of Cambridge by 1864 and studied at the Church Missionary Society College, Islington (~1864–1866).

nodes.label: Jean Humbert
nodes.description: academic (1792 - 1851), member of the Accademia delle Scienze di Torino since 1832

nodes.label: Syed Ali Bilgrami
nodes.summary: Syed Ali Bilgrami worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Lucknow, IIT Roorkee (~1873–1876), and the University of London (~1876–1879), before serving in the Government of Hyderabad (~1879–1901) and as Reader in Marathi at Cambridge (~1902–1911).

nodes.label: Sukumari Bhattacharji
nodes.summary: Sukumari Bhattacharji was an Indologist educated at the University of Calcutta and Jadavpur University. She held a post at Lady Brabourne College in 1945 and served as a teacher at Jadavpur University from 1957 to 1986.

nodes.label: Walter Ewer
nodes.summary: Walter Ewer was an Indology and history scholar who studied at Fort William College around 1801 to 1803 and served in the Indian Civil Service from around 1801 to 1839.

nodes.label: Edward Albert Gait
nodes.summary: Edward Albert Gait was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at University College London (~1880–1882) and founded the Bihar Research Society in 1914.

nodes.label: Leedom Lefferts
nodes.summary: Leedom Lefferts is a scholar of religious studies and anthropology. He served as Professor of Anthropology, Emeritus at Drew University (attested 2011) and as a Research Associate in the Department of Anthropology at the Smithsonian Institution (attested 2011).

nodes.label: Kavita Singh
nodes.summary: Kavita Singh (1964–2023) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied at Lady Shri Ram College for Women (~1982–1985) and Panjab University (~1985–1987).

nodes.label: Jules Michelet
nodes.description: French historian; popularized the historical concept of the Renaissance
nodes.summary: Jules Michelet (1798–1874) was a historian who studied at Lycée Charlemagne (1812–1816). He held posts at Collège-lycée Jacques-Decour (1822), École Normale Supérieure (1827), Archives nationales (1830–1852), and the Collège de France (1838–1852).

nodes.label: Raghu Ananthanarayanan
nodes.summary: Raghu Ananthanarayanan studied engineering at IIT Madras and trained under Tirumalai Krishnamacharya and T. K. V. Desikachar. Active in philosophy, he taught at Krishnamacharya Yoga Mandiram and was a visiting faculty member at IIM Ahmedabad (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Manshi Kiyozawa
nodes.summary: Manshi Kiyozawa was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Toyo University, and at the University of Tokyo (graduated 1887) under Ernest Fenollosa. He founded the Philosophical Society of Japan and served as president of Otani University (~1901–1903).

nodes.label: Ernest Fenollosa
nodes.jawiki: アーネスト・フェノロサ
nodes.summary: Ernest Fenollosa worked in philosophy and Japanology. He studied at Harvard College and the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, later holding posts at the University of Tokyo (~1878–1890), the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston (1890–1896), and the University of Tsukuba (1897).

nodes.id: I:Kyoto Prefectural Rakuhoku High School and Junior High School
nodes.label: Kyoto Prefectural Rakuhoku High School and Junior High School
variants: Jinjō Middle School 尋常中学校

nodes.label: Gembo Dorji
nodes.summary: Gembo Dorji is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Tango Buddhist College, the East-West Center, and the University of Tokyo, and trained under several traditional teachers including Tenzin Dhendrup, Dongyud Nyima, and Sendrak Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Jigme Choedra
nodes.image: The Spiritual Leader of Bhutan Walking to the festival.jpg

nodes.label: Norihisa Baba
nodes.summary: Norihisa Baba is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Hanazono University and the University of Tokyo, where he later held posts at the Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia.

nodes.label: Khakyab Dorje
nodes.summary: Khakyab Dorje (1871–1922) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo (~1885–1892) and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thayé (~1885–1899), and later taught Kalu Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Laeticia Söderman
nodes.summary: Laeticia Söderman is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who studied at the University of Helsinki, earning an M.A. by 2010 and continuing as a graduate student (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Karuna Kusalasaya
nodes.native: กรุณา กุศลาสัย
nodes.summary: Karuna Kusalasaya worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He was a research scholar and Assistant to the Director at Visva-Bharati University and Professor of Sanskrit at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University.

nodes.label: Fafang
nodes.summary: Fafang was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Taixu. He served as a Research Fellow in Indian Buddhism at Visva-Bharati University.

nodes.label: Satiranjan Sen
nodes.summary: Satiranjan Sen worked in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Peking University, founded Cheen Bharat Sanskriti, and served as a research scholar and junior research fellow at Visva-Bharati University.

nodes.label: Rongtha Damcho Gyatso
variants: Rong tha Dam chos rgya mtsho

nodes.label: Yuexia
nodes.summary: Yuexia (1858–1917) was a scholar in Buddhist studies who founded Huayan University and served there as a teacher.

nodes.label: Dixian
nodes.summary: Dixian was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Mingzu and served as abbot of Guanzong Temple from around 1913 to 1932.

nodes.label: Nicholas Roerich
nodes.jawiki: ニコライ・リョーリフ
nodes.description: Russian painter, writer, archaeologist and philosopher (1874–1947)
nodes.summary: Nicholas Roerich was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the Imperial St. Petersburg University (~1893-1898) and the Higher Art School at the Imperial Academy of Arts (~1893-1897).

nodes.label: Xifan Xue
variants: School of the Tibetan Language (Xi fan xue zong guan)

nodes.label: Constantin François de Chassebœuf, comte de Volney
John Lockwood Kipling
nodes.image: John Lockwood Kipling és Rudyard Kipling.jpg
nodes.summary: John Lockwood Kipling was a history and archaeology specialist who attended Woodhouse Grove School. He served as Curator of the Lahore Museum from circa 1875 to 1893.

nodes.label: Alfonsa Ferrari
nodes.summary: Alfonsa Ferrari (1918–1954) worked in Indology and Tibetology. She studied at Sapienza University of Rome (c. 1936–1941) under Carlo Formichi and Giuseppe Tucci, and later conducted post-graduate research there.

nodes.label: Jacques Bacot
nodes.image: Tchraker lama, Jacques Bacot et moines.png
nodes.summary: Jacques Bacot was a scholar in Tibetology and linguistics. During his career, he held academic appointments at the University of Paris and at the École Pratique des Hautes Études from circa 1936 to 1948.

nodes.label: Daoquan Yu
nodes.summary: Daoquan Yu (1901–1992) was a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at Cheeloo University (~1920–1924) and under Jacques Bacot (~1938–1947), and served as professor of Tibetan language and literature at Minzu University of China (~1953–1992).

nodes.label: Lorna Dewaraja
nodes.summary: Lorna Dewaraja (1929–2014) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She held posts at St Anne's College and at the University of Ceylon, where she was Associate Professor of History.

nodes.label: Senarat Wijayasundara
nodes.summary: Senarat Wijayasundara is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. In 1999, he was attested as a teacher at the University of Kelaniya and as a visiting lecturer at the Buddhist and Pali College of Singapore.

nodes.label: Walter Simon
nodes.jawiki: ヴァルター・ジーモン
nodes.summary: Walter Simon specialized in Sinology, Tibetology, and linguistics. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Otto Franke, taught there from 1926 to 1934, and subsequently held posts at the University of London and SOAS (circa 1938–1960).

nodes.label: Tibetan Language School of Beijing
variants: Institute of Tibetan Studies (Zangwen Xueyuan 藏文學院)

nodes.label: Bronislaw Malinowski
nodes.jawiki: ブロニスワフ・マリノフスキ
nodes.description: Polish anthropologist and ethnographer based in England and the USA (1884–1942)
nodes.summary: Bronislaw Malinowski studied at the Jagiellonian University, Leipzig University, and the London School of Economics under Charles Gabriel Seligman. He held academic posts at the LSE (~1913–1938), Cornell University (~1933), and Yale University (~1939–1942).

nodes.label: Dedong Wei
nodes.summary: Dedong Wei specializes in religious studies, sinology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Renmin University of China (~1995–1998) and became an associate professor of religious studies there around 1998.

nodes.label: Claude Jacques
nodes.summary: Claude Jacques (1929–2018) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied under George Cœdès (~1960–1969). He served as director at the École française d'Extrême-Orient (~1963–1973) and taught at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Amy Paris Langenberg
nodes.image: Amy Paris Langenberg in the video 'Accomplished women Female leadership and reproductive health in the Bhikṣuņī-Vinaya'.png
nodes.summary: Amy Paris Langenberg specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD from Columbia University (~2002–2008) and served as assistant professor of religious studies at Eckerd College (~2014).

nodes.label: Benedetta Lomi
nodes.summary: Benedetta Lomi focuses on Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned her PhD from SOAS University of London (~2008–2012) and held teaching posts at the University of Virginia (~2013–2018) and the University of Bristol (~2018).

nodes.label: Yoshiko Shimabukuro
nodes.summary: Yoshiko Shimabukuro (born 1911) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She completed studies at Kyoto Chuo Bukkyo Gakuen through 1936 and at Kyoto Women's University from 1936 to 1940.

nodes.label: Gangru Tsultrim Gyaltsen
variants: sGangs ru tshul khrims rgyal mtshan

nodes.label: Marsha Weidner
nodes.summary: Marsha Weidner specializes in sinology, history, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of California, Berkeley, and held posts in art history at the University of Virginia (attested 1990) and the University of Kansas (attested 2001).

nodes.label: Bidya Dandaron
nodes.description: Russian Buddhist writer and Tibetan studies scholar (1914–1974)

nodes.label: Regbi Pubaev
nodes.summary: Regbi Pubaev (1928–1991) was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at St. Petersburg University. He worked at the Institute of Mongolian, Buddhist and Tibetan Studies (~1958–1991) and Buryat State University.

nodes.label: Damdin Badaraev
nodes.summary: Damdin Badaraev is a scholar in Tibetology and linguistics who studied under Bidya Dandaron and George Roerich.

nodes.label: Adhémard Leclère
nodes.description: French diplomat, economist, politician and ethnologist (1853–1917)

nodes.label: Giovanni Gentile
nodes.jawiki: ジョヴァンニ・ジェンティーレ
nodes.description: Italian philosopher, educator, fascist theoretician and politician (1875-1944)
nodes.summary: Giovanni Gentile (1875–1944) was an Italian philosopher. Educated at Liceo Ximenes, Scuola Normale Superiore, and the University of Florence, he held posts at Palermo, Pisa, Rome, Scuola Normale Superiore, Bocconi University, and served as president of IsMEO.

nodes.label: First Zen Institute of America
variants: Kyoto branch of the First Institute of America
First Zen Institute of America in Kyoto

nodes.label: Christopher Framarin
nodes.summary: Christopher Framarin specializes in philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. He earned an MA at the University of Hawaii and a PhD at the University of New Mexico, later becoming an associate professor at the University of Calgary.

nodes.label: Tao Pan
nodes.summary: Tao Pan is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He completed a BA at Fudan University in 2010 and earned a Magister Artium at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich.

nodes.label: Nicholas Witkowski
nodes.summary: Nicholas Witkowski specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at Stanford University (until 2015) and held a research fellow post at the University of Tokyo, attested in 2017.

nodes.label: Yingguang Qu
nodes.summary: Yingguang Qu was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Nordan Hutuktu in 1926 and Bai Puren in 1929.

nodes.label: Yuanxing Guo
nodes.summary: Yuanxing Guo (1920–1982) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Gongga Rinpoche. Guo held a position at Jinling Sutra Publishing House and served as a researcher at the Chinese Buddhist Culture Research Institute.

nodes.label: Chinese Buddhist Culture Research Institute
variants: Research Institute of Chinese Buddhism (Zhongguo Fojiao Wenhua Yanjiusuo 中國佛教文化研究所)

nodes.label: Nianzu Huang
nodes.summary: Nianzu Huang was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Beijing Institute of Technology (~1932-1936) and under Nordan Hutuktu, Gongga Rinpoche, Hsu Yun, Lianju Xia, and Jiaqi Wang. He held posts as head at Central People's Broadcasting Station and professor at Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications.

nodes.label: Voice of America
variants: Tibetan Broadcast Service for Voice of America

nodes.label: Pieter Hendrik Pott
nodes.summary: Pieter Hendrik Pott was a scholar of Tibetology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He served as a curator at Museum Volkenkunde (~1947–1965) and held a post at Leiden University in 1973.

nodes.label: Constantin Regamey
nodes.summary: Constantin Regamey (1907–1982) worked in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies, studying at Warsaw (~1927–1931) and Paris (~1932–1936). He held posts at the University of Warsaw (~1936–1941) and as professor at the universities of Lausanne (~1945–1977) and Fribourg (~1946–1977).

nodes.label: Louis Ligeti
nodes.summary: Louis Ligeti was an Iranian/Central Asian, sinology, and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University (~1921–1925) and the University of Paris under Paul Pelliot (1925–1928).

nodes.label: Chogye Shabdrung
nodes.summary: Chogye Shabdrung (1981–) is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Sakya College in 2003 under Khenchen Sonam Gyatso.

nodes.label: Krisztina Teleki
nodes.description: (1978–) Hungarian literary translator, linguist, orientalist, tibetologist and mongolist
nodes.summary: Krisztina Teleki (born 1978) specializes in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Eötvös Loránd University (~1997–2009) and later served there as a research fellow around 2009.

nodes.label: August Conrady
nodes.jawiki: アウグスト・コンラーディ (中国学者)

nodes.label: Berthold Laufer
nodes.image: Annual report of the Director to the Board of Trustees for the year .. (1933) (17811378703).jpg
nodes.jawiki: ベルトルト・ラウファー
nodes.summary: Berthold Laufer worked in Sinology, Tibetology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He earned his doctorate at Leipzig University (~1896–1897) under August Conrady, later working at Columbia University (~1904–1906) and the Field Museum of Natural History (~1908–1934).

nodes.label: Friedrich Weller
nodes.summary: Friedrich Weller specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied under August Conrady (~1912–1915) and served as Ordinarius for Indology at Leipzig University from 1928.

nodes.label: Johannes Schubert
nodes.summary: Johannes Schubert, a scholar of Tibetology and sinology, studied under August Conrady (~1922–1925) and August Hermann Francke. He held posts at the Ahnenerbe (~1939–1945) and served as professor of Tibetan at Leipzig University (~1952–1961).

nodes.label: Jan Jaworski
nodes.summary: Jan Jaworski was a scholar of Sinology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Warsaw (~1922–1928) under Stanisław Schayer, and later studied under Jean Przyluski (~1928–1930).

nodes.label: Ludwik Skurzak
nodes.summary: Ludwik Skurzak was an Indologist who studied under Stanisław Schayer. He held a post as a lecturer at the University of Breslau.

nodes.label: Maryla Falk
nodes.description: Polish indologist and historian of religions

nodes.label: Eugeniusz Słuszkiewicz
nodes.summary: Eugeniusz Słuszkiewicz (1901–1981) was a Polish scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at Lviv University (~1919–1924) and held posts at Lviv University (~1934–1939), Nicolaus Copernicus University (~1945–1969), and the University of Warsaw (~1953–1971).

nodes.label: Somchai Kusalacitto
nodes.summary: Somchai Kusalacitto is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who received a Ph.D. from the University of Madras. He served as dean and deputy rector for foreign affairs at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (attested 2003).

nodes.label: François Jacob
nodes.jawiki: フランソワ・ジャコブ
nodes.description: French biologist and geneticist, winner of the Nobel Prize in 1965
nodes.summary: François Jacob (1920–2013) studied at Lycée Carnot and the Paris Medical Faculty (~1938–1947). He held a post at the Collège de France from 1964 to 1991.

nodes.label: Stephen Addiss
nodes.summary: Stephen Addiss specialized in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and art history. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan (~1973–1977) and held professorships at the University of Kansas (~1977–1992) and the University of Richmond (~1992–2013).

nodes.label: Juan Wu
nodes.summary: Juan Wu is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed her PhD at Cardiff University under the doctoral supervision of Max Deeg, attested in 2012.

nodes.label: Laurence Austine Waddell
nodes.summary: Laurence Austine Waddell worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies after studying medicine at the University of Glasgow (ca. 1873–1878). He held posts in the British Army (ca. 1880–1908), Medical College Kolkata (1896), and University College London (1906–1908).

nodes.label: Bötrül Dongak Tenpé Nyima
nodes.summary: Bötrül Dongak Tenpé Nyima was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Dzogchen Monastery under Thubten Nyendrak and Khenpo Genam, and later taught Jigme Phuntsok, Tarthang Tulku, Khenpo Chökhyap, and Khenpo Dazer.

nodes.label: Seán McLoughlin
nodes.summary: Seán McLoughlin is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who completed a Ph.D. at the University of Manchester. In 2005, he was attested as Lecturer in South Asian, Islamic and Religious Studies at the University of Leeds.

nodes.label: Eric J. Sharpe
nodes.summary: Eric J. Sharpe (1933–2000) studied at the University of Manchester (~1955–1958) and worked in religious studies and Indology. He held posts at Manchester (~1966–1970), Lancaster (~1970–1977), and the University of Sydney as First Chair of Religious Studies (1977–1996).

nodes.label: Phra Brahmagunabhorn
nodes.native: พระราชวรมุนี
nodes.summary: Phra Brahmagunabhorn is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University and Sukhothai Thammathirat Open University. He served as Dean of Buddhist Studies and Deputy Vice Rector at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University.

nodes.label: Liqian Liu
nodes.summary: Liqian Liu (1910–2008) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. During his career, he held posts at West China Union University, the Ethnic Publishing House, and the translation administration department of the State Council of the People's Republic of China.

nodes.label: West China Union University
variants: Border Area Institute of Research of the West China University

nodes.id: I:State Council of the People's Republic of China
nodes.label: State Council of the People's Republic of China
Genzao
nodes.summary: Genzao (1891–1993) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Dzogchen Monastery until 1950 and trained under traditional teachers Gyang mdzod Rinpoche (in 1948) and Kalu Rinpoche.

nodes.id: I:Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications
nodes.label: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications
variants: Beijing Institute of Post and Telecommunications

nodes.label: Basil Gould
nodes.summary: Basil Gould worked in tibetology and linguistics. After studying at Winchester College (~1896-1902) and New College (~1902-1906), he served in the Indian Civil Service (~1907-1947).

nodes.label: John Claude White
nodes.description: British engineer, civil servant and photographer in India (1853–1918)
nodes.summary: John Claude White was active in Tibetology and history and archaeology. He was educated at Rugby School (~1867–1870) and the Royal Indian Engineering College (~1873–1876).

nodes.label: Józef Kowalewski
nodes.summary: Specializing in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Buddhist studies, and linguistics, Józef Kowalewski studied at Vilnius University and Kazan Imperial University. He held posts at Kazan Imperial University (~1828–1860), serving as rector in 1855, and at the University of Warsaw (~1862–1878).

nodes.label: Khangsar Tenpe Wangchuk
nodes.summary: Khangsar Tenpe Wangchuk (1938–2014) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He pursued his traditional studies under Jampal Gyepe Dorje and Lodro Gyatso.

nodes.label: Longlian
nodes.summary: Longlian (1909–2006) was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Tibetology. She studied under Fazun in 1939 and under Nenghai as her traditional teacher from ~1941 to 1967.

nodes.id: I:Tibetan School of the Buddhist Academy of China
nodes.label: Tibetan School of the Buddhist Academy of China
Guankong
nodes.summary: Guankong (1903–1989) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He taught at the Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Institute and was appointed professor at the Buddhist Academy of China in 1957.

nodes.label: D. Neil Schmid
nodes.summary: D. Neil Schmid is a Sinology and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed doctoral studies at the University of Pennsylvania under Victor H. Mair, and also studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and Waseda University.

nodes.label: Rachel H. Pang
nodes.summary: Rachel H. Pang works in Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Virginia and was attested in 2019 as the Lester D. Coltrane III Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at Davidson College.

nodes.label: Sangseraima Ujeed
nodes.summary: Sangseraima Ujeed works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She earned her doctorate at the University of Oxford (~2013–2018) and held a postdoctoral fellowship at the University of California, Santa Barbara (~2019–2021).

nodes.label: Mother Sayamagyi
nodes.summary: Mother Sayamagyi was a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure who studied under and subsequently succeeded Sayagyi U Ba Khin as his disciple.

nodes.label: Sayagyi U Ba Khin
nodes.description: Burmese civil servant and Vipassana meditation master

nodes.label: Seiko Hirata
nodes.summary: Seiko Hirata was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University (~1947–1950) and under Shin'ichi Hisamatsu (~1948–1951), and held a post at Hanazono University from around 1970 to 1994.

nodes.label: Shigetsu Sasaki
nodes.summary: Shigetsu Sasaki (1882–1945) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at the Tokyo Academy of Fine Arts and under disciple master Sokatsu Shaku (~1905–1919). In 1931, he founded the First Zen Institute of America.

nodes.label: Peter Connolly
nodes.summary: Peter Connolly is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He completed his BA, MA, and Ph.D. at Lancaster University and held a post as Lecturer in Religious Studies at the University of Chichester in 1980.

nodes.label: Lynn Thomas
nodes.summary: Lynn Thomas is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at Lancaster University and completed a D.Phil at the University of Oxford in 1987. She served as a lecturer in Hinduism at the University of Roehampton (attested 1997).

nodes.label: Theodore Gabriel
nodes.summary: Theodore Gabriel worked in religious studies and Indology. He earned an M.Litt from the University of Aberdeen and served as a Lecturer in Religious Studies at the University of Gloucestershire.

nodes.label: Agvan Dorjiev
nodes.jawiki: アグワン・ドルジェフ
nodes.description: Russian Buddhist monk and diplomat, envoy and Finance Minister of Tibet (1853–1938)

Pratap Kumar Penumala
nodes.summary: Pratap Kumar Penumala works in religious studies and Indology. In 2010, he was attested as a Professor at the University of KwaZulu-Natal and as a Visiting Professor at Colorado College.

nodes.label: Ashok Vajpeyi
nodes.summary: Ashok Vajpeyi is an Indologist who completed an MA while studying at St. Stephen's College, Delhi, circa 1961–1963.
